# deepamp-audio - CHANGELOG

This file carries the record of the plugin this package holds, continued from the tree this copy was made from.
The cards below that line are that record: they name the older package and its paths where those were the names of
the day, and history is not rewritten to hide that. **One dated exception, 2026-11-18 (the private-data sweep,
`TODOS.md` part one item 38, classes (b) and (d)): a card's private literals were re-expressed in place — this
machine's absolute path became `<home>/…`, the backup location became "the workspace backup directory", and the two
captured engine pages appear under the names they carry in the tree today. The operator's word on this was to
re-express them, because a tracked file must not carry them once the package is published and pushed. What a card
SAYS is untouched: its measurements, its numbers, its state words and its dates all stand exactly as written —
with one further exception of the same day, at the operator's word ("can we just drop the disk references - i do not
think we need those as history for now"): the free-space and memory figures of this machine and of the nodes were
dropped, because a volume measurement of a named machine is private under the same rule. What stands is every
measurement that belongs to the work rather than to a machine — a byte sum, a package size, a duration, a count, an
assertion total — and the sentence each dropped figure was carrying as evidence still reads, re-expressed as its point
("nearly full", "gained room back once the superseded builds were cleared"). `T-887` item 5 names what was dropped and
what was deliberately kept. **A third exception of the same day, at the operator's word (classes (c) and (d) of that
sweep, `T-887` item 10): the machine names in these records became neutral tokens — `cpu1`, `cpu2`, `gpu1` for the
three boxes the audio lane runs on, `node1`–`node3` for the vision nodes, and `10.0.0.N` for their addresses, taken
from a reserved private range so they route nowhere and still sit inside the private class the plugin's own LAN check
accepts. The token-to-box mapping lives in `LOCALHOSTS.md`, which git never tracks, and it is the same map the test
suites use.** Two shapes were left standing deliberately: the loopback form `127.0.0.1`, which names no machine, and
the words `192.168` inside a sentence about address *ranges*, which names a class and not an address. The same day's
third pass took out the account handles and the machine words embedded inside path-like tokens, and left the package
scope where it must stand — `T-887` item 11 states which files keep the real name and why.**

Closed cards moved out of `TODOS.md` on 2026-10-16 under the rule the user approved on T-512: a card moves when
its state word is BUILT / DONE / COMPLETE / CLOSED / RESOLVED / SUPERSEDED / REVERSED, and it moves TRIMMED -
the user's own word: "OK, try to trim clutter we do not need while moving into changelog". What is kept is the
ruling, the measured before/after and the state word; what is dropped is development history, superseded
intermediate notes and repeated measurements. A card that EXPLAINS a test pin stays in `TODOS.md`, and so do
the fleet, meter and registry rulings - those are current work, not history. Every moved id keeps a one-line
pointer where the card used to be, so an id cited in a code comment still resolves, and a pointer says plainly
when the change still needs a browser refresh or a harness restart.

Nothing was deleted. The full text of everything moved here is in `the workspace backup directory/backup_20261016_*.tar.gz
and in a working copy at `audio-play-cordis/scratch/TODOS_before_t512.md`.

## The origin door becomes a declared setting: `allowed_origins`, read-only from the panel (T-935)

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "our same origin protection against others accessing the api will need an options in settings, so that if some user is using a different host ip to access it can still use the plugin, right ? ... (no everybody forwards to local 127.0.0.1)" — then the ruling on how to take it: "start with the origin setting - and highlight that it's a security setting", and the shape chosen from the options put: **an allow-list plus a `*` value**. `TODOS.md` part one item 126.
2. **Measured before designing, because the premise needed checking.** Reaching the panel at another address **already works today** when the page and the API share that address: the T-931 gate compares the request's `Origin` with the `Host` it was addressed to, and a browser fills both from the same URL. What the rule actually refuses is a page from a **different origin** calling the API. And measured on our own surface: `Access-Control` appears **0** times in `lib/`, and `OPTIONS` is not handled as a method at all — so a cross-origin page that passed the gate would still be stopped by its own browser. Both facts are in `docs/FACTS.md` item 8 rather than assumed.
3. **What the harness itself recommends, read rather than guessed (the operator asked for exactly this).** `dsh-host-webserver/README.md` names it a route-owner job ("**No server-wide authentication or origin policy** — route owners … enforce their own request policy. Binding a non-loopback address still exposes unprotected routes and static assets to that network"), and `dsh-client-connection/src/api-request-trust.ts` is the reference: a Host fence on every request (loopback | the listener's bind literal | a declared `trustedHosts` authority, "exact on `host:port`, any port on port-less entries"), a `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` refusal, and an Origin fence — with malformed configured authorities **failing the load**, and the instruction that a plugin keys request policy on the listener's own configuration "instead of inspecting sockets or trusting forwarded headers". Whether a browser can reach the host at all is the webserver's `host` Config, and "`dsh web --host 0.0.0.0` is unsupported". The whole reading, with quotes, is now `docs/FACTS.md`, "What the harness itself runs as a request policy".
4. **What was built.** A Config field `allowed_origins`: bare `host` or `host:port` authorities, or the single value `*`; **an empty list is not a declaration** and the door stays closed. The gate asks one function now (`originAdmitted935`), which keeps the T-931 fence as the first answer and consults the list only after it. `GET origin_policy` reads the live policy — same-origin-only or not, the list, the wildcard, what was refused at boot, the source, and the listener facts taken from `ctx.webServer` (reported as *unanswered* when a carrier does not supply them, never guessed from the request). The boot audit names the door beside the rest of what was declared, and the 403 names the setting and the read.
5. **Why it is a security setting, and what that decided.** The operator declares it in the patch file and **nothing writes it** — no POST verb, no panel control: a page must not get to widen the boundary that decides whether the page may ask. **One entry that is not a bare authority in canonical form refuses the whole list** (a half-applied allow-list is a door nobody intended) and the bad entry is named verbatim in the audit and on the read. A port-less entry answers its host on any port; an entry naming a port answers that authority only. And what it is **not**: not authentication (a caller that sends no `Origin` is not gated at all), and not a Host fence — this lane still has none, and that gap stays open on item 126.
6. **Two faults found and fixed in the pass, both recorded rather than smoothed over.** (a) A T-786 source pin located the Config-key list by its **last entry**, so adding a key made the locator blind; the locator is re-cut to find the list by its own declaration — a stronger locator, the same claim (AGENTS 8.5). (b) The first draft of tracker item 124 named a fleet machine; the `T-926` sweep caught it, and the line now carries a role word and points at `LOCALHOSTS.md` §2.
7. **Measured.** `lib/index.js`: one Config field, the policy block, the gate consult, one read verb, the boot-audit field. `docs/VERBS.md`: one row → the contract reads **104 routes, 104 rows, 0 gaps, 0 extras** (was 103/103). `AGENTS.md`: the §6 row and the paragraph that says what kind of setting it is. **12 new assertions** (the AGENTS 8.6 cap; a behaviour contract, not plumbing). Host suite **2 783 pass, 0 fail** — 2 771 before, plus these 12, nothing else moved. Full run **26 suites, 6 359 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0** — 6 347 before this card plus exactly these 12, nothing else moved. Logs: `scratch/t935_host_run2.log`, `scratch/npm_test_20261127_post_origin_setting.log`. Pre-change copies: `scratch/pre_origin_setting_20261127/`.
8. **Open on item 126, in the order it bites.** (a) **the CORS half**: until `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and an `OPTIONS` answer exist, the list admits an origin it cannot actually serve to a page — this card makes the door correct, not the browser round trip work. (b) the **Host fence** (DNS rebinding), which this gate has never had. (c) showing the live door read-only in the panel's Settings section. `docs/DETAILS_SETTINGS.md` was left untouched, since there is nothing in the panel to describe yet.
9. **State: BUILT and GREEN, host half.** **RESTART HARNESS NOW** to put the gate, the read and the refusal wording live. Nothing changes for anyone who declares no `allowed_origins`: the default is the T-931 behaviour, and the only visible difference is a 403 that now names the door.

## No document pointer leaves this package, and the retired workspace files are named nowhere (T-934)

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "i copied over the old files into … i want them not used anymore, i need you to consolidate all docs accordingly, and put all relevant and current deepamp references within the git repo folder, the 'local harness' information and todos for other projects should NOT be pulled in". Then the shape asked for: "…so that we will end up with a ../PROJECTS.md file and ../DSH.md instead of having multiple AGENTS.md and TODO.md files … but no confusion anymore between ./AGENTS.md and ../AGENTS.md".
2. **What was wrong, measured before the change.** 114 lines cited `../AGENTS.md`, `../TODOS.md` or `../audio-play-cordis`; 60 of them are `CHANGELOG.md` cards and were left as written. The rest were live instructions, and **the same string meant different files depending on which file it was written in**: a `../TODOS.md` citation in `AGENTS.md`, `lib/index.js` or a suite named the retired workspace tracker while that path resolves to *this package-s* tracker; a `../AGENTS.md` citation in `docs/` named this package-s guide while its own sentence called it "the author-s workspace file". Nothing runtime-side was broken: no suite and no runtime code reads a file outside the package (the one cross-project read prints that it skipped).
3. **The mechanism the rule is written against, read in the installed harness rather than assumed.** The instruction loader walks up to the **first directory containing `.git`** and loads only `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (with an `AGENTS.local.md` overlay in the same directory); the candidate names are configurable. This package **is** a git root, so no parent guide can reach a session here — the ambiguity lived only on the page. A project index or a harness fact sheet beside the repository is therefore never injected: reference material, read on demand, authority for nothing inside.
4. **The rule as it now stands** (`AGENTS.md` 1 and 8.10): a citation inside this package is written **from the package root**; no file outside it is named as authority; a `WM-` id inside a card is a dated citation and not a path to open; a decision no file of this package carries is asked of the person in front of the session. A markdown link inside `docs/` keeps its parent-directory prefix, because that is how a link renders.
5. **What was pulled in — two records, and only two, where this package was the only party that needed them and the retired tracker was the only holder.** `docs/FACTS.md`, "Records the retired workspace tracker used to hold": the separation pass and the request wall (one separator at 434.9 s for 180.00 s of audio, about **2.4x realtime**; the other cut by **this plugin-s own 3 600 s request limit** at that length — a wall on one path and none on the other), and the operator-s word on one model-s quality with the measured row kept beside it so the judgement and the seconds are not read as one thing (6.06 s audio, 290 924 B, `elapsed_load 1.6 s`, `elapsed_gen 157.4 s`, **26x realtime**). Other projects- cards, the workspace plans, and this machine-s harness facts were **not** pulled in.
6. **Counts, before → after.** `AGENTS.md` 12 → 0. The ten section guides: 13 backticked `../AGENTS.md` citations → 0 (their "Also:" markdown links resolve inside the package and stay). `docs/PROMPT_CODING.md` 6 and `docs/PROMPT_DOC_UPDATE.md` 5 → 0, including nine `../scratch/`-style citations now written as `scratch/`. `docs/FACTS.md` 4 pointers + 5 "it lives in the old source tree" claims → 0. `docs/MODELS_TABLE.md` 2 → 0. `docs/MODELS_TEST_MATRIX.csv` 4 record citations → `docs/FACTS.md`. `lib/index.js` 2 and `tests/host.test.cjs` 2 code-comment citations → the internal `docs/FACTS.md` section. `docs/PROMPT_FIRST_SETUP.md` read-order item 2: the parent-guide step is gone, replaced by "there is no guide above this package". `CHANGELOG.md` cards: untouched, and its standing note about reading this file now says plainly that the tracker is retired.
7. **The ratchet** (`tests/host.test.cjs`, the T-934 block, beside the T-926 private-data sweep it follows): 26 reader-facing files scanned; three patterns refused — a backticked `../` citation, any `../../`, and the retired source tree named as a place to go. **4 new assertions** (within the AGENTS 8.6 cap). Host suite **2 771 pass, 0 fail** — the previous 2 767 plus these 4, nothing else moved. Full run **26 suites, 6 347 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0** — 6 343 before this pass plus exactly these 4. Logs: `scratch/t934_host_run.log`, `scratch/npm_test_20261127_post_docs_consolidation.log`. Pre-change copies of all 20 touched files: `scratch/pre_docs_consolidation_20261127/`.

## The README-s own hero frame was not in git and not in its manifest (T-932)

1. **Found while measuring the tree for the freeze, not while looking for it.** `README.md:6` renders `docs/screenshots/v0.1.0/hero_player_music.png` as the landing-page hero. That file was **untracked in git** and **absent from `docs/screenshots/v0.1.0/manifest.json`** - measured: the manifest lists 17 shots, the version directory holds 18 files. A clone or a tag of this package would have shown a broken image on its first line, and the record of the frame round would have been short by one frame with no note saying so.
2. **What was added.** The PNG into git, and one manifest row for it: `px [743, 955]`, `bytes 191192`, and the digest. Its `from` says plainly that it is the README hero frame added by hand on 2026-11-25 and was **not** produced by the capture round that named the other frames - the record does not pretend it came from a round it did not come from.
3. **The method, measured before writing it.** The manifest key is `sha12`, and it is **not** a sha1 of the file: checked against four rows already listed, it is **`sha256(file)` truncated to 12 hex characters** (`bytes` is the plain file size, which also checked). The key name is the older word; the method is what the rows carry, and the row added here follows the rows. Nothing was renamed - the fix was to write the right digest, not to relabel the field.
4. **State: done, and committed with the rest** (see `TODOS.md` item 13). No document line was changed: `README.md` was left exactly as the operator left it.

## A page in the browser can no longer drive the lane: the route owner takes an origin rule (T-931)

1. **The decision, verbatim** (the operator, 2026-11-26, from four scopes put to them with the surface measured): **"Origin rule only - no script breaks"**. What the measurement said first: the surface is **103 route rows — 24 GET-only, 56 POST, 23 GET-or-POST**, so "gate the writes" would have meant 79 write paths; and the harness-s own seam (`ctx.connection.requestRejection`, which applies the Host/Origin checks **and** browser authentication) would have asked every script and every hand-run `curl` for a per-process launch token — `$DSH_WEB_URL` carries none (21 characters, no token parameter).
2. **Built.** A `sameOrigin931(origin, host)` helper and one gate at the top of `handleApi`, **before the body is read**: a request that carries an `Origin` must carry the authority the request was addressed to (default ports normalised, so `http://host` and `http://host:80` are one origin); anything else is answered **403** naming the Origin it refused and saying plainly that a caller with no `Origin` is unaffected. A malformed Origin is refused, not treated as same-origin.
3. **What is untouched, and that was the point.** The panel: `lib/client.js:15334` builds a **relative** `/api/deepamp/<verb>`, so its `Origin` equals the `Host` it addressed. Every script and hand-run `curl` in this package and in every session: they send no `Origin` at all. The four agent tools: host-internal, never HTTP. The **audio prefix `/deepamp` is deliberately not gated** — a foreign page reading a rendered WAV costs the lane nothing, and the panel plays those files.
4. **What this is not.** It is not authentication and the refusal says so. A program on this machine can still drive the lane; that is the accepted shape while the port is loopback. The stronger mechanism stays recorded on `TODOS.md` item 117 — including `admit()` and `allowsRemoteAuthorities` — for the day the port leaves loopback, where it is a decision to revisit, not a defect to find again.
5. **Tests.** `host` **2 771 / 0** (was 2 764; seven new pins, two of them about ordering and scope: a foreign write whose body would have answered 400 answers 403, so the gate is before the read; and one gate only, with `serveAudio` untouched). Full run **26 suites, 6 347 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0** (was 6 340). Logs: `scratch/fullrun_T931_20261126.log`, `scratch/host_T931_20261126.log`.
6. **Documents.** `docs/VERBS.md` §11 gains item 14 — the first 4xx on this surface that is not about the body. `docs/FACTS.md` mismatch 1 now carries the decision and the correction that the seam is callable. `TODOS.md` item 117 **CLOSED**.
7. **One thing not papered over:** no pre-change copy of `lib/index.js` was taken before this edit. The copy in `scratch/` is the one from before T-930, one card older; this change is two additive hunks (the helper before `handleApi`, the gate before the body read), which is why the before-state can be re-derived — but it is not claimed as a copy.
8. **State: BUILT and GREEN, not live** — this is a host half. **RESTART HARNESS NOW**: what becomes live is a 403 to any page that is not this one, and nothing else changes for any caller this package uses.
9. **LIVE, verified at the operator-s restart of 2026-11-26 ~19:58 Berlin, five checks against the running server** (all through `curl`, which is also the no-`Origin` case): no `Origin` → 200 and the answer unchanged; `Origin: http://elsewhere.example:3080` → **403** carrying the refused value and the sentence about a program with no `Origin`; `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:3080` with that same `Host` → 200; `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:80` with `Host: 127.0.0.1` → 200, the default-port normalisation working; and `/deepamp/…` with a foreign `Origin` → **404, not 403**, the audio prefix staying open by design. One real take was rendered through the agent tool after the restart (`ap-1944`, a `clone_sample` of a registered voice, model read from the primary-s own catalog at the moment of the ask — the first attempt named a model the primary does not list and was refused with the placement list, which is the capability bar answering correctly and costing no id). The same read showed why the explicit-wall parameter of T-930 was not cosmetic: **this profile runs `job_timeout_sec` at 7 200 s** (`GET job_timeout`), so the old default form would have timed a stuck capture download at two hours instead of its own 900 s.

## The capture leg carried the same wall fault T-912 closed for engine requests. It is closed, and the tool definitions were trimmed (T-930)

1. **The instructions, verbatim** (the operator, 2026-11-26): **"3.4 do as recommended"** on the shell-timeout question, and **"2.2 ok"** on the ruling *cut only the duplication, not the warnings*. Item 120 was closed at **"1.7, ok, then keep as is"** and no code was written for it.
2. **What "as recommended" resolved to, and why.** The two options were: exempt the long local calls from the executor's deadline, or keep it and add a bound plus a doc line. Measured first: every shell call in the host half names its own ask (the only one that names none is a `mkdir`), and the largest named ask besides an engine request is **`YTDLP_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 900000` ms — above the transport's documented default clamp of 600 000 ms** (`dsh-bash-local`, the `maxTimeoutMs` default). So the claim that `AGENTS.md` 6 and `docs/PROMPT_FIRST_SETUP.md` 5.5 made — that non-engine calls "sit far below" that clamp — was true of the ffmpeg legs (max 300 000 ms) and **false of the capture download**: on a profile that had not raised the cap, a long capture was cut at 600 s by a wall this lane never set. That is the T-912 fault in a second leg, and it is why the answer is both halves: exempt that one leg, and make the claim for the rest unbreakable.
3. **Built (host half).** `engineWall912` takes an optional wall and an optional label; the capture download runs with **no executor deadline and this plugin's own wall at the 900 s the file asked for**, and its abort names `capture download wall`, not `job_timeout_sec`. The engine path is untouched — the five T-912 drives pass exactly as they were written. Three new source assertions hold the claim honest: the own-wall minimum equals the documented 600 000 ms; no call in the host half asks at or above it except that one constant; the download site is wrapped.
4. **Built (tool half).** Eight clauses cut out of `audio_render`: the per-kind model-refusal table (now one sentence), the staging mechanism in `convert` and `voice`, the capability-bar sentence in `kind`, "a row with no finished audio is refused", "this tool sends no path and no sample". Six source assertions that pinned the removed sentences were **re-cut with dated notes, not deleted** (`AGENTS.md` 8.5); one of them, T-852 B, is now carried by the host-side clauses plus the one sentence.
5. **Measured, including a correction to a number this package published yesterday.** The authoritative measure is the schema an agent is handed, read from `Tool.listTools` on the live host: **`audio_render` 5 105 bytes, `audio_status` 1 419, `audio_voices` 1 606, `audio_control` 1 418 — 9 548 bytes, 21.0 % of the 45 487 bytes of tool schemas that agent carries (43 tools)**. The 8 649 "characters" in T-929 and `docs/FACTS.md` was a flawed source scan (one tool's window ran into the next) and is corrected there. Source-side delta of this pass: 5 676 to 5 314 description characters (−362). **Re-measured after the operator's restart the same day: `audio_render` 4 083, the other three unchanged — 8 526 bytes, 19.2 % of the 44 465 bytes that agent carries. The delta is −1 022 bytes (−10.7 % of our four).** The source-side estimate of −362 characters was the wrong method a second time: a scan of source string literals under-counts concatenated multi-line descriptions. The live schema is the only authority for this number, and the method that produced it is now named wherever the number is.
6. **Documents.** `docs/PROMPT_FIRST_SETUP.md` 5.5 now names the documented default, the measured bound, and the capture exception. One edit to `AGENTS.md` 6 (the same sentence corrected; the session's single AGENTS edit). `docs/FACTS.md` mismatch 9 corrected and mismatch 10 carries the fault found. Tracker: 120 closed, 121 measured and half built, 103 extended, **117 rewritten** — the operator was right that the harness protects its own surface: `ctx.connection.requestRejection` applies the Host/Origin checks and browser authentication to another Web route, and `allowsRemoteAuthorities` reads `trustedHosts`; our routes simply do not call it. That stays a decision, and no code was written for it.

Logs: `scratch/fullrun_T930_20261126.log`, `scratch/host_T930_20261126.log`, `scratch/audio_tools_T930_20261126.log`. Pre-change copies: `scratch/lib_index.js.bak_20261126_pre_T930_capture_wall`, `scratch/tools_index.js.bak_20261126_pre_T930_definition_trim`, `scratch/PROMPT_FIRST_SETUP.md.bak_20261126_pre_T930_wall_number`.

## The kind list and the model list stop being one slot's answer: an unserved kind is pickable and the panel reads the other slot, 2026-11-26 (Berlin) (T-924)

1. **Instruction** (operator, verbatim): **"The available ui-selections should actually never result from a single endpoint's feature set as user might want to set other endpoint ... ---> convert into an overall fix on all fronts and do so"**, with the fallback half named on the same card: **"we could implement a fallback to the single model of this 'section/type' if there is at least one shown (currently we have 0 displayed!) and 'none' set thus far"** and **"it must be prevented to send the music prompts to the speech lanes on accident -bad user xp"**. The shape was ruled as one pass: *"do as recommended in 6"* — the panel half of `TODOS.md` item 108 (host half built as T-922) together with item 109.
2. **The measured fault.** The kind list, the model list and the fallback were all read off ONE slot (`get_models?fn=`), and a kind with no model there was **traded**: `resolveTtsSelection` fell back to `kinds[0].id`, and a preset pick whose kind was unserved returned null and never moved the form. The panel already received the registry answer naming the lane's other slots and threw it away. Consequence on the live panel: a music preset picked against a slot with no generator landed the words on a speech model, which is the accident the operator named.
3. **Built (client only, one pass).** (a) `get_models` from the panel carries `&id=` when a slot is named — the verb half the host added in T-922; (b) a kind the read slot does not serve is a **pickable** option labelled "no model on this slot" (it was a disabled option), and picking it keeps the kind and lands **no** model; (c) when the kind has nothing to serve here and the lane has another registered slot, one control beside the model select reads that slot — both views of its lane, the pair the refresh control already asks — through `get_models?fn=&id=`, lands its rows labelled "… · read from e-N" off the row's `served_by`, and moves the lane pin to that slot in the same press; (d) `resolveTtsSelection` keeps a valid kind token instead of trading it, and only a string that is not a kind token is replaced; (e) the tool press refuses naming the kind and the read that would settle it — "the prompt was not sent to a model of another kind"; (f) a preset pick moves the form to its own field even when nothing serves the kind here, and says that no model was selected rather than landing one of another kind. A held slot stays held: a read is allowed, a job is not, and the option says which. (g) The same read runs at boot when the browser store restores a lane pin to a named slot — without it the panel comes back offering models the restored pin will refuse, the list and the pin disagreeing until a hand press. That boot half reuses the read path the pins below exercise; it has no pin of its own (it needs a mount fixture whose store carries the pin, and that fixture is not in this pass). (h) The transcription lane is covered on the same front: its model lines carry the slot they were read from, and a slot that lists no transcription model offers the read of another registered slot instead of an empty "(no models)". That control is the same code path with `fn=stt` and has no pin of its own in this pass — said, not hidden.
4. **Measured.** Three new pins in `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` in the live panel that registers a second tts slot: the read control and what its line declares; the press -> `get_models?fn=…&id=e-1` plus the option labelled with the slot it came from plus the lane pin moved; and the run that follows carrying `"endpoint_id":"e-1"` with that model in the body. One new pin that the unserved kind option is not disabled. Two pins re-cut, not deleted, with dated notes: `ui_state` "the form keeps the model it has" (the model slot is now EMPTY rather than carrying a model of another kind) and `render` "listed DISABLED … never selectable" (now selectable, still labelled, still never a silent kind trade); and two in `selection_memory` — "the kind selector lists the SERVED kinds only" (now: the served set in order, plus the unserved ones as pickable lines that say so) and "a saved kind no model serves falls back to a served kind" (now: the kind is kept with an empty model slot, stored and restored as that kind — that fallback was the accident). The shared-box / input-style control counts moved 19 / 37 -> 19 / 39 because the panel gained two controls wearing the same style as the controls beside them, not a style of their own. Client suites after the change: `ui_state` **1 166**, `render` **235**, `flow` **113**, `transport` **115**, `model_library` **49**, `tooltips` **13** — 0 fail, 0 throw; the tooltip ratchet did not move. Full run after the change: **26 suites, 6 301 pass, 0 fail, exit 0** (`scratch/npm_test_T924e_20261126.log`; the run before the `selection_memory` re-cuts went red on exactly those two pins, which is what found them — `scratch/npm_test_T924d_20261126.log`).
5. **State: BUILT — client half, live on a browser refresh; no harness restart owed** (the host half of this shape went live with T-922). The section guides (`docs/DETAILS_*.md`) do not describe the new control yet — a guide pass with fresh screenshots is a separate pass and the operator-s call, not something to slip into a code card. ## The batch flag is no longer a thing an endpoint can be off, 2026-11-25 (Berlin) (T-921)

1. **Instruction** (operator, 2026-11-25, verbatim): "the 'batch' option is to complicated… keep it in code, but set
   it to true for all TTS endpoints, remove the buttons, we can pin ttsd jobs to endpoints now, so that is actually not
   really needed anymore … and we can get rid of the risk". The trigger was a real one: the operator made a CPU node
   the TTS primary to render music, the row showed **batch ON**, and the scene still would not place — "although it
   displayed batch as ON (display bug) it was actually off … this is a problem in the 'make promary'".
2. **What the flag was, and why the display could lie.** `batch_allowed` gated ONE thing: whether a `dispatch_batch`
   part could be placed on an endpoint. The panel painted a green `batch on` from the stored value, while the value that
   a promotion left behind came from the entry the demoted machine carried, so a row could read ON for a lane that
   refused parts, and the refusal named a flag the user had never set. The pin (`endpoint_id`) already decides where a
   part goes, which is what made the flag a risk with no remaining use.
3. **Built, host (`lib/index.js`).** The flag is kept in the data model and in every answer, and it is always true:
   `cleanEndpointFlags` sets `true` and REFUSES `false` naming the ruling ("batch_allowed is always true since T-921 —
   a batch part is placed like any other job, and the control over where it goes is the endpoint_id pin"); the primary
   flags and a registry-entry load normalise to `true`, so a state file that still carries the old `false` cannot come
   back barred; `endpoint_add` and `endpoint_update` both refuse it, and a refused field rejects the whole update, so
   nothing is half-applied. The placement bars that READ the flag were kept in code, per the operator's word — they
   simply never fire.
4. **Built, panel (`lib/client.js`).** The `batch on` / `batch off` control is off every endpoint row (both lanes), the
   two `batch_on` / `batch_off` action routes are gone, and the fall-through notify that echoed a batch value is gone.
   The state colour rule was re-stated: the green is read by one control, the state control.
5. **Measured.** The re-cut was the work: **18 host assertions and 14 panel assertions** named the old contract, and
   none was deleted — each was re-expressed with a dated `(T-921 contract change)` note and now asserts the new one (a
   stored `false` reads back `true`; a batch is placed where it used to be refused; a pin takes it; no row of either
   lane carries a batch control; a panel handed an older host's `false` renders no control for it). Two of them needed
   their ORDER changed, not their claim: the ordinary-dispatch placement check runs before the batch now, because the
   batch occupies the endpoints it used to be refused on. Full run after the pass: **26 suites, 6 288 pass, 0 fail**
   (`scratch/npm_test_T921_20261125.log`; the intermediate host run was 2 720 pass / 18 fail).
6. **Not touched:** `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/`. Pre-change copies: `scratch/{index.js,client.js}.bak_20261125_pre_T921_batch_always_true` (and the same names in the workspace `scratch/`).

## The wall on an engine request is this plugin-s own, not the transport-s, 2026-11-23 (Berlin) (T-912)

1. **Instruction, verbatim:** "having to raise the value harness-wide is the wrong direction, please investigate
   alternative options ... is there no possibility for the plugin to set a different timeout on a per call basis ?"
   — and on the direction chosen, "ok, do as recommended".
2. **The change.** An engine request whose ask reaches the stock transport clamp (600 000 ms, the shell
   executor-s `maxTimeoutMs` default) is now run with `onExpiry: 'none'` plus this plugin-s own `AbortController`,
   which is the shell seam-s own documented shape for a caller that bounds its wait. The wall is
   `job_timeout_sec`, honoured at the number it names (30 … 7200 s) on any profile, and **no profile setting has
   to be raised to make a long take payable**. One helper, asked once per engine attempt inside `runEngine`;
   the short calls — probes, model loads, ffmpeg, capture — keep the executor-s deadline, their numbers sit far
   below it. Re-armed against the time actually left, so an early clock is not a cut; a cancel the row carries is
   chained in, so a hand cancel stays a cancel; `unref`-d, so an hour-long wall never holds the process open. When
   our wall ends a call the result is reported in the shape every consumer already reads for a wall.
3. **Wording and documents.** The below-wall sentence no longer tells anyone to raise a profile number (one T-908
   clause re-expressed with a dated contract-change note). `docs/PROMPT_FIRST_SETUP.md` §5 item 5 and §6 item 6,
   `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` 6 rewritten for it. On this machine the profile override is **reset to the shipped
   defaults** (`timeoutMs 60000`, `maxTimeoutMs 600000`) so the stock wall is live here and the fix is verifiable
   locally — the operator-s word: "about C - we should reset it to the defaults locally, so our fix we use can be
   verified locally, too".
4. **Measured.** host suite 2723 → **2731** (+8: one spec-shape pin at the speech door, seven driving the helper
   on a fake clock). Full run on this tree: the client scope suite answered **496 pass / 1 fail** once and
   **497 / 0** standalone — a time-boundary flake in a hue walk (`T-542`, four colour schemes sampled against a
   clock), the class the T-784 ruling named ("Make the fixture deterministic"). It is unrelated to this card and
   it is recorded here rather than hidden. Host half — **RESTART HARNESS NOW**.

## A name and a type are not what the engine says a parameter IS: the clone channel is read from the engine's own description, 2026-11-20 (Berlin) (T-901)

1. **The question the operator asked, verbatim:** "but we have used the model before - where is the problem resulting
   from ? it is something we need to fix now and verify against other models, too", and after the analysis was read
   back: "I do not understand why we messed with the cloning path in the first place, this has been proven and tested
   code before so why was it changed ? I want the fixed result fully tested and the change reason analysed and the
   current solution sanity checked". Both choices on the card were the operator's: all three moves, into v0.1.0, tag
   moved again.
2. **What was proven before, and it was not what was changed.** The clone route this lane has always used — stage the
   registry sample on the endpoint that renders the take, send it as `voice_ref` (or `voice_samples` for a cast) plus
   `reference_text` — serves the eleven families whose own record names one of those three keys (the sweep the T-895
   card states, 44 families asked on one CPU slot). The family the T-895 fault was measured on (`docs/FACTS.md` item
   16, 2026-11-19) names none of them: it names `target_voice` (`audio_path`) and answered `unknown <Family> request
   option: reference_text` at 0 bytes after paying a model load. That family had never worked on this lane. The proven
   route was not regressed; a family outside it was failing, expensively.
3. **Where the inference went wrong, read in the engine.** The two cards consulted one source — the request-options
   parameter table — and matched a parameter's NAME against `voice|reference|clone|prompt` and its TYPE against
   `audio_path|path|file`. The engine's own model specs and the descriptions on those same parameters say what each
   one is. `dramabox-s target_voice`: "Reference voice WAV path for voice cloning" — the channel T-898 built is right
   for it. `chatterbox-s target_voice`: "Voice conversion target WAV path; overrides the speaker reference" — a
   conversion input, and writing the clone sample there is what made both CPU slots answer that the family-s prepare
   requires a speaker reference (measured 2026-11-20, one row per slot). `pocket_tts` names `voice_embedding_file`
   ("Precomputed voice-state embedding path") and `export_voice_state_file` ("Export the prepared voice state") — a
   derived cache and an OUTPUT — while its spec declares `capabilities.clone = [speaker_reference]` and its session
   refuses a voice-less job outright; the mode reader had been answering "a stored voice has no route onto this
   family" for a family that renders with a stored voice in 2.8 s. Sweep of the whole engine catalog (130 spec files):
   19 families declare `speaker_reference` and name no key of ours, and the name-and-type reading also catches a noise
   file, a pre-encoded codes file and a model checkpoint. The analysis with every family and description is
   `scratch/CLONE_CHANNEL_ANALYSIS_20261120.md` (not tracked).
4. **The fix, three moves and one clause.** `cloneRefParamIsReferenceVoice(p)` (beside `cloneChannelFault`) reads the
   engine-s own sentence about the parameter: it must affirm a reference voice / voice cloning / speaker reference /
   reference audio, and a description that names a conversion is never a clone reference. `cloneChannelFault` counts
   only those, so a family whose file parameters describe an embedding and a noise file is no longer called
   unhandable and is offered `clone_sample` again. `cloneAudioRefKey` refuses to write a conversion-named key, so a
   clone request keeps `voice_ref` and `dispatch_mode:"upload"` and writes nothing under the conversion parameter,
   while the family whose description names a clone reference keeps the channel it was built for. Both clone legs of
   `capVoiceModesOf` now name the channel the reference actually rides where the family names no reference parameter
   of its own (one shared clause, computed once beside the channel fact, so the two answers cannot disagree).
5. **What stays exactly as ruled.** A parameter typed plain `path` is still never written (T-895, T-898). A family
   that names one of the three channels keeps its route untouched. A record that is unreadable or silent about a
   reference says nothing — no claim, no refusal (AGENTS 5.9). The refusal leg is not removed: it fires on a family
   whose own description calls a non-audio file its reference voice, and the sentence it writes still names that
   parameter, the count of parameters read, and the consequence. The drop-undeclared-options leg — the thing that
   actually prevents the `unknown request option` 500 the fault was — is untouched, and `force:true` still steps over
   the channel rule where one exists.
6. **Tests: 5 new assertions, 7 existing ones re-expressed with dated contract notes, none dropped.** The fixtures
   now carry the three real shapes as the engine describes them: a clone reference (`Reference voice WAV path for
   voice cloning`), a conversion pair (`Voice conversion target WAV path; overrides the speaker reference`), and a
   clone-task family whose only file parameters describe a precomputed embedding and a noise file. The override
   record is paid by the family the bar still refuses. `tests/host.test.cjs` 2 695 → 2 700; full tree **26 suites,
   0 fail, RC=0, 6 258 → 6 263 counted assertions** across the 25 suites that print a count (`tests/handler.test.cjs`
   prints its own OK line and no number), one suite moved: `tests/host.test.cjs` +5. Logs
   `scratch/host_901_run3.log`, `scratch/full_901_run1.log`.
7. **Sanity check of the build the operator is testing, live lane, 2026-11-20.** A stored voice renders on `pocket_tts`
   (2.8 s, `dispatch_mode:"upload"`, the row dropping `reference_text` because the family does not declare it) and the
   same text with no voice is refused by the engine for want of a session voice. A stored voice renders on
   `moss_tts_local` (3.84 s, one CPU slot) and on `voxcpm2` (3.84 s, the other). A stored voice on `chatterbox` fails
   on both slots with the row naming `clone_ref_key:"target_voice"` — the fault this card fixes. `dramabox` clone is
   ACCEPTED on the built channel (no option fault) and produced 8.33 s of audio, 1 599 404 bytes, after 2 669 364 ms
   of generation on 4 CPU threads — the channel works, the model is too slow for this lane, and the operator ruled it
   out of the test set the same day. `vevo2` refuses on a model file the shared store does not hold
   (`vevo2-f16.gguf`; `vevo2-q8_0.gguf` is there). `rvc` is refused at the door, unchanged by this card.
8. **Fleet reading behind it, since the config was blamed.** Both CPU nodes run `audio-cpp-cpu.service` with the same
   options and a server JSON of the same name on each machine, and every entry compared is identical — `chatterbox`
   declared `task:"clon"` on both, 59 entries each, and both nodes' `model_specs/chatterbox.json` declare
   `tasks ["tts","clone","vc"]` with `speaker_reference` on clone and vc. The live `/v1/models` still answers `vc` on
   one slot and `clon` on the other for the same id with both `loaded:false`, so the difference is in the two engine
   checkouts, not in the operator-s config, and nothing in the config was changed.
9. **State: CLOSED, inside v0.1.0.** The tag moves again for the third time — `v0.1.0` is re-cut from the object it
   named at `6251d80` onto the commit carrying this card, so the tree the operator tests is the tree that carries the
   fix and the suite that pins it. Pre-change copies: `scratch/lib_index.js.bak_20261120_pre_T901`,
   `scratch/host.test.cjs.bak_20261120_pre_T901`. Open on this line, unchanged: the engine-side question of why two
   builds answer one entry differently stays a measurement in this package-s own records and goes nowhere else.

## The pre-freeze sanity pass the operator asked for found one sentence that was never finished, and the freeze line is drawn on the tree it repaired, 2026-11-20 (Berlin) (T-900)

The instruction, verbatim: "after Your implementation and tests and checks, run an additional sanity check on all
your latest changes after our last big code review a few days back - in the code and address any resulting problems
from the latest changes.... I finally want to have a solid code freeze version for solid testing and closed all
v 0.1.0 cards".

**1. What the pass covered.** The last big review is the client round of 2026-11-14; its last code commit is
`5bca62d`. The range walked is `5bca62d..HEAD` — 15 code-touching commits, 2 309 added lines across 12 files
(`lib/index.js`, `lib/client.js`, `tools/index.js`, seven `scripts/`). The scan is `scratch/sanity_scan_20261120.py`
(range as an argument), its wide output `scratch/sanity_wide_20261120.txt`: every function defined in the added
lines and how often the current file names it, duplicate declarations, markers and prints and loose comparisons and
swallowed catches, a `/g` regex held in a variable or `.test` on a `/g` literal, private literals in added text,
the new tool parameter names counted where they appear, and a syntax check of every changed code file.

**2. The one real defect, and why nothing had ever seen it.** In `capVoiceModesOf`, the closing brace of the
record leg sat in the MIDDLE of a string concatenation: `… appears among its ' + chanFault895.params + ' declared
parameters; }` then the consequence clause was concatenated on and thrown away. The statement was valid JavaScript,
the suite was green, and the caller received `clone_none_reason` cut off at "appears among its ". The part that
named the consequence — that a stored voice has no route onto that family — had never reached a caller or an
assertion since T-895 wrote it. The sentence is one string again (the leg at `lib/index.js:7552`), its sibling leg
above was re-indented to match, and the stray blank line left by the repair was removed. A scan for the same shape
(a `}` followed by `+ `, or a `+` followed by `}`) across `lib/index.js`, `lib/client.js` and `tools/index.js`
found no other instance.

**3. The fixture gap that hid it, closed.** No family in the suite ever reached that leg: the five the T-895 block
carries are stopped before it by a plugin-side `clone_required` record, by a task the mode reader does not treat as
speech, or by a parameter the reader does not count as a reference. The block carries six now — `path_fam` /
`path-clone-one`, a clone task the record itself declares with only `path`-typed parameters. Two things were needed
to land it on that leg. It had to be on BOTH fixtures — a model the CATALOG does not list is answered
`known:false / unknown family on this endpoint` before any capability record is read, which is the honest answer for a
model this slot does not serve. And the catalog has to name it under the ACCEPTED spelling `clone` (T-808), not the
wire word `clon`: the wire word routes a family through this plugin-s own "a clone model needs a reference" fallback,
which is the leg above the one that reads what the record actually names. Both facts are said in the fixture comment.

**4. What the pass found while pinning the precedence.** The channel branch lets the plugin write a family-s own
reference parameter. That precedence is now pinned rather than assumed: a caller that names the family-s own key
itself loses to the sample this lane staged, because the merge does not overwrite a key the plugin already wrote —
the same rule the dialogue cast already follows for `voice_samples`. Reading the door to make that assertion honest
surfaced a fact this package had not stated: **an `options` value is shape-gated (T-885), and that gate-s grammar
contains no slash** — a caller cannot name a path there at all. So the key a family names for its reference voice
is a key only this plugin writes, and the assertion carries a value the gate does accept.

## The agent-facing door onto voice exchange: `audio_render` gains a conversion kind 2026-11-20 (Berlin) — T-899: `convert` joins the render kinds

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "usually 1 - explain in more detail and tag for current - still v0.1.0" — option 1 of the question this session filed as `TODOS.md` part one item 83(a), and one of the three cards the same answers moved back inside v0.1.0.
2. **What already worked, measured live the same day** (`docs/FACTS.md` item 18): the task route drives voice exchange end to end — it stages the registered voice-s own sample onto the endpoint that renders the take, places the row, honours a pin, records the target voice on the row, and refuses **before the row exists** on a family that cannot read a speaker reference. What had no door was the **tool half**: `audio_render` offered six kinds and none of them was a conversion, so an agent reached the route only through a raw verb — and a raw verb leaves to the caller exactly the things this plugin already knows how to do.
3. **Built, tool half.** `kind:"convert"` takes `source_job_id` (the row holding the audio) and `target_voice` (a registered voice name), with `model` and the optional pin, and maps onto the same `dispatch_task { task_kind:"vc" }` the verb takes. **No new request path, no staging code, no placement code, no second capability bar** — that absence is the design: one door onto one route, so the bar, the staging and the family-s own reference channel cannot drift from what the verb does.
4. **Three refusals at the door, each naming the read that answers it, none carrying a default:** no source row (names `audio_status (recent)`), no target voice (names `audio_voices (list)` and says this tool sends no sample of its own), no model (names `audio_status (slot_models)`). The tool deliberately does **not** resolve a model for a conversion: it cannot know which family a model name belongs to, and a guessed conversion family is the fault the host bar exists to stop. This is the shape T-890 and T-892 settled for a take and for a transcription, kept here unchanged.
5. **What the door does not gain, stated because a later session might "complete" it.** No path or row form of the target voice (the verb keeps those), no `voice` / `text` / `file_path` riding a conversion body (pinned: the body carries exactly five keys), no model default, no client change, and no second voice-conversation with the family table — the per-family channel rules stay the host-s and are still open on item 83. The scene guard is untouched and stays keyed to `kind:"scene"`: a conversion is one voice over audio that already exists, not a batch of takes, so the operator-s-call rule that covers a scene does not reach it and no new ask was invented for it.
6. **Measured.** `tests/audio_tools.test.cjs` **71 → 78** (+7: the route and its body, the five-key body, the three door refusals, the two descriptions, and a refusal that names neither a model nor a voice). Two assertions re-cut with dated notes, neither weakened: the kinds pin (six → seven, the new one appended where a new kind belongs) and the model-facing-text ratchet (9 000 → 10 000 bytes — counted from the definitions actually registered; measured on this card 9 512 bytes of definitions plus 1 653 of scoped section, 11 165 per agent). Full run **RC=0, no FAIL line**, and the only suite that moved is this one — 71 → 78 — every other suite byte-identical to the T-898 run (`scratch/regress_npm_test_899.log` beside `scratch/regress_npm_test_898.log`). The tools suite was re-run once more after a wording smoothing of the tool description: 78, 0 fail.
7. **State: BUILT — host-side like every other half of this component, so it goes live on the same restart press `T-895`, `T-897` and `T-898` are waiting on.** The live proof owed after the press: `audio_render { kind:"convert", source_job_id:<a finished row>, target_voice:<a registered voice>, model:<a model the slot lists>, endpoint_id:<a slot> }` answering with a row id and a take the same length as its source.


## A stored voice now rides the reference parameter a family names for itself, instead of being refused for not having one 2026-11-20 (Berlin) — T-898: the clone channel `TODOS.md` item 80 asked for

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "yes, now" — the operator-s answer to the CHANNEL half of `TODOS.md` part one item 80, the half `T-895` refused to guess at on the same day and filed instead.
2. **Where the channel is, read in the engine and not inferred.** A family of this class takes its reference out of the request-s **options** map: its own session code calls `find_option(request.options, {"target_voice"})` and then opens that path from its own disk. The engine-s type word for "a WAV I open out of the request" is **`audio_path`**, and the same option table registers the parameter under that word. So the shape this lane can write is: stage the plugin-s sample onto the endpoint that renders the take — the staging `voice_ref` and `voice_samples` already use, one `POST /v1/ui/upload` — and name the staged path under the family-s own `audio_path` parameter.
3. **Built, host half.** `cloneAudioRefKey(fam)` answers the first parameter the record declares as `audio_path`, with a reference-shaped name, that is not one of the three keys this lane already writes; the payload writes the staged path into `options[<that key>]`, the row reports `dispatch_mode: "ref_option"` and **`clone_ref_key`**, and `voice_modes` offers `clone_sample` again for such a family and names the key the reference will ride. `capsOf` and the bar consult ONE channel fact, so the modes and the gate cannot disagree about whether a route exists.
4. **What is not claimed, and stays refused.** A parameter typed plain **`path`** is not audio: the same engine records use that word for a precomputed voice embedding and for a noise file, and writing a WAV into one of those would be this lane inventing a channel the record never named — those families keep T-895-s refusal, now carrying the sentence that says what it looked for. A family that already names one of the three channels keeps its route untouched (`voice_ref`, `dispatch_mode:"upload"`, no key claimed for it). A record that was never read says nothing: no route, and no refusal — the bar-s UNKNOWN rule, unchanged.
5. **Two things kept deliberately.** The channel is chosen from the **cached** record at payload time, so a render pays no extra engine read (pinned on the source). And the caller-s own options still merge last and never overwrite the plugin-s key: the plugin owns the knob, exactly as it owns `voice_samples`.
6. **Measured.** `tests/host.test.cjs` **2 687 → 2 692** (+5). Eight `T-895` assertions were re-cut with dated `(T-898 …)` notes quoting the ruling, none dropped: the refusal of a WAV-named family became the assertion that the take RUNS and names the key it rode; the "a refusal spends nothing" count moved onto the family that is still refused; the capability-object claim moved onto that family too; `force:true` is now asked on that family, because stepping over a rule that no longer exists proves nothing; one source-read bound grew 13 000 → 18 000 (a bound, not a claim); the mode reader-s offer-site count moved 2 → 4, with the exclusivity that count guarded still pinned by the same `!cloneFromCaps475` guard. Full run **RC=0, no FAIL line** (`scratch/regress_npm_test_898.log`).
7. **State: BUILT — host half, not live until the operator presses the restart** (the same press T-895 and T-897 are waiting on). The live proof owed after it: a registered voice on a family of this class, on a slot whose catalog lists such a model — the take should run with `dispatch_mode:"ref_option"` and `clone_ref_key` naming that family-s own parameter, and render audio.


## A stored file can now be decoded back INTO the format this plugin works in, and the container list is written once 2026-11-20 (Berlin) — T-897: `convert_item` reads the containers the upload door accepts

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "Yes - teach convert_item the containers the upload door accepts" — the answer to the question filed this session as `TODOS.md` part one item 83(b), and one of the three cards the same answers moved back inside v0.1.0.
2. **Measured on the live lane before anything was written.** A dictation recorded into the panel arrived in the browser-s own container; the transcription lane read it and answered; the same file was taken as a voice-conversion source and rendered into another voice; and `convert_item` refused it — `does not name a container this plugin knows (…webm), so there is nothing to convert FROM`. One store, two lists: the upload door accepts 11 extensions, this door knew 3. The gap was not cosmetic — it decided whether a person-s own dictated audio could be re-used inside the lane at all, and the workaround was a step outside the lane.
3. **Built, host half.** `convSrcExt468(path)` answers the source container **derived from the upload door-s own extension table, at call time** (`UPLOAD_EXT` is declared further down the file, so the read has to be call-time, and the comment says why rather than leaving it to be rediscovered); one container-s two spellings are canonicalised (`oga` → `ogg`, `aif` → `aiff`). `CONV_CODECS468` supplies the one leg the new direction needs (`-c:a pcm_s16le`) and `ffmpegToFormat468` takes an optional codec leg: the convert door names its map, the download door passes nothing and keeps `DL_CODECS468`. The blanket refusal of `format:"wav"` is gone, and the case it existed for — a row already stored as wav — is refused by the same-container check that was already there, now pinned in that form.
4. **What a row now says.** `converted_from_container`: the container the source actually claimed, beside `converted_format`. A decode into wav and a transcode down to a smaller container are different acts, and the row states which one ran rather than leaving a reader to infer it from a file name.
5. **What was deliberately NOT widened, stated because it is the half a later session might "finish" by mistake.** The delivery door still serves wav, ogg and mp3 and nothing else: widening what a conversion may READ is not widening what a delivery may BE. The tagging rule is untouched — only the mp3 and ogg copies are tagged, a decoded wav carries no tags, and no verb over an existing file was built. A container neither door knows is still refused, and that refusal now carries the upload door-s list so the caller can see what would have worked.
6. **Measured after.** `tests/host.test.cjs` **2 677 → 2 687** (+10: the webm decode; the ffmpeg leg naming the wav codec and landing beside the row it copies; the new row naming both containers; a second container proving the read set is a list and not one exception made for one browser; the `oga` spelling refused as the same container; wav→wav refused as the same container; the unknown-container refusal carrying the list; the delivery door still refusing a fourth format; and two source pins — the derived list, and the download door-s call still passing no codec). Two existing T-468 assertions were re-cut with dated `(T-897 contract change)` notes quoting the ruling: the pinned refusal of converting INTO wav became the assertion that it RUNS and names both containers, and the pinned absolute ffmpeg-leg count became a before/after difference, which is the claim that assertion was always guarding. Full run **RC=0 with no FAIL line**; the 25 suites that print a count line move **6 232 → 6 242**, and the only suite that moved is the host suite — every other suite byte-identical to the T-895 run (`scratch/regress_npm_test_897.log` beside `scratch/regress_npm_test_895.log`).
7. **State: BUILT — host half, and NOT live until the operator presses the restart.** The live proof this card owes after the press is the chain it had to do by hand while measuring: `upload_audio` → `convert_item {format:"wav"}` → `dispatch_task {task_kind:"vc"}`, with no ffmpeg step outside the lane.

## A stored voice needs a CHANNEL the family actually reads, and the bar now asks before the row exists 2026-11-20 (Berlin) — T-895: the refusal names the parameter the family does take, and `voice_modes` stops offering a mode the engine will punish

1. **The fault, in one line.** Measured 2026-11-19 (`TODOS.md` part one item 80, `docs/FACTS.md` item 16): a registered voice named on a family whose own engine parameter table names its reference voice as a FILE it reads under a fourth key went out carrying `reference_text`, paid a model load, and came back `500 unknown <Family> request option: reference_text` at 0 bytes — and this plugin-s own outcome record already classified it `cls:"capability"`, after the row existed. The order the operator set for this card: **"Build the door refusal first, then freeze"**.
2. **What was built, in one place.** `cloneChannelFault(fam)` in `lib/index.js`, beside the voice-mode vocabulary: it reads the parameters that family-s own record declares and answers one question — does the family name its reference voice as a file the engine reads (`audio_path` / `path`, named for a reference: `target_voice`, `source_audio`, `voice_embedding_file`) while naming none of the three channels this lane writes (`voice_samples`, `voice_ref`, `reference_text`)? A path-typed parameter that says nothing about a speaker (`noise_file`), or carries the word "voice" under another shape (an enumerated `voice_id`, a `do_sample` switch), is not a channel and is not counted. `null` means "nothing to say", and it covers three different facts: no record, a record that declares no parameters, and a family that names one of the three.
3. **Consulted in three places, so the two host answers cannot disagree.** (a) The clone-required leg of `capVoiceModesOf`: where the plugin requires a reference and the family cannot be handed one, NEITHER mode is offered and both absences are stated. (b) The record-declared-clone leg of the same function (the leg this package-s own dated family table feeds for a self-voicing model): `clone_sample` is not offered and `clone_none_reason` names the parameter the family DOES take. (c) A new branch (2c) of `capGateVerdict`, taken on the `dispatch_tts` door: a voice named on such a family is refused **before a row exists** — no id spent, nothing counted against any ceiling, no model load paid — with `capability.why:"no_clone_channel_for_family"`, `capability.clone_channel` naming that parameter, and the sentence giving the two ways out (render the model on its own voice, or aim the take at a model whose record names one of the three). `GET voice_modes` carries `clone_channel` and `clone_none_reason` on its answer, on the model leg and on the family-only leg.
4. **What stays exactly as it was.** A family whose record is unreadable or silent about a reference is not evidence: the bar stays permissive on an unknown (AGENTS 5.9). A family that names one of the three channels keeps its route untouched. A built-in family is still answered by the T-884 membership branch above this one. The two families this plugin answers from its own empirical rows are settled before the branch is reached, exactly as T-877 keeps them. `force:true` steps over and leaves one `cap_override` record, and it still pays no capability page read — on a cold record the override is simply absent, which is the T-248b rule kept and is now pinned by a test. The pre-existing refusal of a voice-less take on a clone-required family is untouched.
5. **Measured sweep, before writing the rule (one CPU slot, the primary).** 44 families answer with a parameter table. Eleven name at least one of the three channels this lane writes — the families the clone path serves today. Of the rest, the ones that name a reference at all name it as a file under a fourth name; the rest name nothing about a reference and stay permissive. `docs/FACTS.md` item 17 carries the numbers and the two catalog-read shapes beside them.
6. **Tests and state.** 13 assertions added to `tests/host.test.cjs` on a five-family fixture (the measured shape, the same parameters under the clone task, a family naming `reference_text`, a record silent about a reference, a second file-shaped family): refusal before the engine is asked, nothing spent, the capability object carrying the record-s parameter, the same model with no voice still rendering, the control family untouched, a silent record permissive, the second shape refused with its own parameter named and a non-speaker path not counted, the clone-task form refused the same way with its old voice-less refusal kept, both mode absences stated, `force:true` recorded, and one source pin that both clone legs of the mode reader consult the one channel fact computed before either is offered. Suite 2 664 → 2 677; full pass **26 suites, RC=0, 6 236 assertions, 0 fail**, every other suite identical to the T-893 baseline (`scratch/regress_suites_895.txt`). **Host half built and green, not live until the operator presses the restart.** The CHANNEL half of the fault — writing the key such a family reads — is not built: it is filed for v0.1.1 at `TODOS.md` part two item 10(f), inside the freeze this card closes v0.1.0 against.

## Built 2026-11-17 (Berlin) — T-884: the capability bar asks whether a voice is one of the model-s speakers, and a built-in-speakers-only family never rides the clone channel

1. **The finding and the words.** `TODOS.md` part one item 67, measured live as `ap-1728`: a voice take on a 54-speaker built-in family carrying a plugin voice name passed the bar and the engine answered `500 unknown Kokoro TTS request option: reference_text`. Asked what to do, the operator said: "this sounds like something we should analyse right now", and of the shapes put chose **"D: A + B + C"**, filed **"v0.1.0 now, unfiled"**.
2. **What the analysis found — two defects, not one.** (a) The bar checked that a voice was **named**, never that the name was one of the speakers the record names (its own comment said so: "one with a list passes the moment a voice is named"). (b) The wire **channel** was chosen by `voiceDispatchMode` from whether **this plugin-s store** holds a WAV for that name — not from what the model accepts. So a name that IS a real engine speaker but also sits in the plugin store was routed to the clone channel (`voice_ref` + `reference_text`) that a built-in-only family does not have. A membership refusal alone would have fixed (a) and left (b). The line also carried a claim that is now corrected on it: the panel **can** produce the pick — its dropdown offers stored names on a model whose speakers are known whenever the host says nothing about cloning.
3. **Host half.** Three named helpers, one source of truth for both doors: `builtinVoicesKnown67` (the engine-s own page first, this plugin-s dated mirror second — the same order the bar already reads), `builtinOnlyFamily67` (speakers known, no clone leg in `capsOf`, not a `voice_samples` family), `builtinNameListed67` (exact, then case-folded). New bar block 2b: a named voice that is not on the known list of a built-in-only family is refused before any row exists, with the list counted and printed, its source named, and the `force:true` step stated (`capability bar T-248b`, why-word `voice_not_a_built_in_speaker`). The channel correction runs at all three decision points so the pre-row answer and the payload cannot disagree: `voiceDispatchMode` (now asked about the family and the slot), `stageJobSamples` (no sample staged, no `voice_ref` built — such a take pays no staging round trip it could not use), and the payload-s `name` leg, which sends no `reference_text` for such a family and says so on the row (`reference_text not sent: <family> renders on its built-in speakers and has no clone leg on this endpoint`). Families with a clone leg, `voice_samples` families and unknown families are unchanged, and the existing option gate (T-447) is left exactly where it was — this is the half it could not reach, a record that is optimistic about an option the family-s session cannot read.
4. **Client half, and the first form of it that was wrong.** The panel hides the stored-voice group on a model whose family the host names as clone-less — a new catalog field `no_clone_leg`, projected in `modelsOf` off the same `capsOf` derivation the bar refuses from (`familyHasNoCloneLeg67`), false for a family this plugin has no record of, since unknown stays permissive on this door too. The first form built was wider — hide the stored group whenever the model's own speakers are known — and it was measured wrong the same day: six pins in three suites went red (`render` one throw, `selection_memory` five), and the reason was not the pins, it was the rule. A model's speakers say nothing about whether its family can also take a stored sample; the panel must hide exactly what the host refuses, no more. With the field driving it, those six pins are untouched and still pin what they pinned (a family the host says nothing about keeps both groups, labelled as unconfirmed). The withheld names are still named and counted on the disabled line, and its wording moved from "this host reports it takes no stored clone sample" to "this host does not offer a stored clone sample on it", which is true in both cases.

The fixture needed a real read to carry the new field, so the block now walks the panel's own door for it (the model library's reload, after asking that pane for the TTS lane) and names in its payload which read landed — measured in this session: with the library left on another lane, the reload asked for `fn=stt` and nothing reached the form. ## Built 2026-11-16 (Berlin) — T-879: the lane-call grace is one named number and a suite now holds it, before any v0.1.2 card moves it

1. **The ask, verbatim.** "please track for v 0.1.2+ that we implement better timeouts for the tool calls on the plugin side to prevent stuck agents" — tracked as `TODOS.md` part one item 65 and version-targets item 24. When that line was written it stated a fact: the 120 000 ms lane-call grace was pinned by **no** suite. Asked whether to close that half now, the operator said "ok, go ahead with your recommendation". This card is that half, and only that half.
2. **What was read, and it is what the card ratchets.** No tool declares a `timeoutMs`, and the reason is the component's own comment (`tools/index.js:53-57`); every call reaches the host half through the `audioPlay` service it provides itself (`lib/index.js:25314`), same process, no HTTP hop. 1. **The ruling.** `TODOS.md` part one **item 64** put the gap forward with three shapes: (a) refuse it in the bar before a row exists, (b) give the tool a bounded `options` object, (c) have the panel name a missing required option on the form. 2. **The measured fault this closes** (`docs/FACTS.md`, "What the GPU node cannot run…" items 7-8): a music package loaded in **1.07 s**, then its render refused in **0.010 s** with the engine-s own `{"error":{"message":"MiniMax Music 3 requires lyrics","type":"server_error"}}`. Structure tags such as [verse] and [chorus] are supported.",required:!0}`. The engine documents `[verse]` / `[chorus]` structure tags — so the ordinary shape of a lyric is exactly the shape this lane cannot carry, and until now the only answer for it was the engine-s. **Two refusal forms now say which of the two happened**: the request carried nothing, or it carried a value this lane cannot send.
5. **What was built, in four parts.** (i) `optionSpecOf` carries the flag through, from either half of the record, and a name either half marks required stays required. (ii) One pure function, `requiredOptionBlock777(spec, req)` — no I/O, no closure state — so both doors that use it can be exercised without an engine. (iii) The capability bar gained its **fourth item**, inside `capGateVerdict` (after the lane, built-in-voices and stated-mode items), and the two bar calls now receive **one** request shape built once in `capabilityGate` instead of two inline literals, so both calls describe the same request. A record that declares nothing, or declares everything optional, refuses nothing: **UNKNOWN stays permissive**, unchanged (`AGENTS.md` 5.9). And a family this plugin answers from its own empirical rows — the hot families of `capGateHotFamily` — never reaches the new item and keeps its `capsOf` and voice gates as they were. 1. **The ruling.** The model this lane cannot finish was put as a question with three shapes (keep such models off the lane; widen the Config range; carry a per-model timeout). The number it widened to — 7 200 s — is the one their own test used as a client wall the same day.
2. **The range, in one place.** `JOB_TIMEOUT_MIN766 = 30` / `JOB_TIMEOUT_MAX766 = 7200` (`lib/index.js`, beside the `jobTimeoutSec` default). The three places that enforced the old ceiling read the pair now: the `job_timeout` route gate and its refusal text, the state-file load clamp, and the declared-Config clamp that the boot audit names in `adjusted`. The Config door-s description says 7200. **The default stays 3600** — widening what may be asked for is not the same as asking for it, and the comment above the constant says so in those words.
3. **The panel-s half, because the two gates are one promise.** The Settings box now accepts 30…7200 (`min`/`max` read the same named pair), its own commit gate and its refusal line moved with it, and its hover says 2 h. The hover-s length is unchanged, so the `tests/tooltips.test.cjs` ratchet did not move. One stale claim was corrected on the way: a client comment had been asserting "the host-s accepted range is 30..7200" while the host gate refused 3601 — the number became true on this card, and the line now says when.
4. **What this card does not change, and says out loud.** An engine request in this plugin is a curl handed to the harness shell executor with `timeoutMs: genTimeoutMs()`; that executor is capped at `maxTimeoutMs: 3600000` ms in the live profile patch (the schema default is 600000). **A plugin wall above 3 600 s is a wall this side cannot keep — the transport stops waiting first.** That file is the operator-s composition, changed only on their explicit request, and moving it needs a harness restart; it was put as a question and the answer was **"Yes, raise it to 7200000 ms"**, so the line is raised in the same pass and takes effect on the same restart as this card (`TODOS.md` **item 63**, pre-change copy `scratch/cordis.patch.yml.bak_20261116_pre_t877_transport_cap`). `generation_ceiling_s` (0…3600) is deliberately untouched: it gates the length of a take, and the ruling was about how long this side waits.
5. **The history is named in the code, not just here.** This ceiling was 7200 before. T-646 item 3 lowered it to 3600 on 2026-10-25 with a reason: 1 h was the wall the transport enforced, and six perf_log records sit at 3 600 0xx ms with "curl exit null: server returned no error body" — a run killed locally while the engine kept going. Both reasons now sit in the comment above the constant, so the number is not moved a third time by someone who has read neither.
6. **The measurement that made this a live question** (`TODOS.md` item 55 carries it in full): a 30 s take on a 32 GB music package on a CPU node, the package loaded by id with the task named in 0 s, was cut at 7 200 s with **0 bytes back**, and about six hours later that node was still generating the same take — 197 % CPU, 25.7 GB resident. A plugin-s cut does not stop an engine.

Each carries a dated `(T-876 contract change)` note quoting the ruling. `AGENTS.md` section 6 carries the new range with its date and a pointer to item 63.
