## Measured pass 2026-11-16 (Berlin) — T-874: the 32 GB music test the operator asked for is reachable by package id and blocked by the 64-name cap, and a load that names no task is answered by the engine's `tts` default

1. **What was asked, and what this pass did with it.** The words are on `TODOS.md` item 55 ("…is downloading a 30GB music model i want to test … later, too", "as 30GB+ model, i guess only [the primary node] should be able to handle it VERY slowly - track for later test" — the bracket is the role word for the machine named in that line, per `AGENTS.md` 8.10). This pass took that test as far as it goes without a new ruling. **No take was generated and none is claimed: nothing was dispatched.**
2. **The library read did what it was built to do.** `GET endpoint_library` on the primary speech slot answers `library_state: complete` with **10** loadable packages, the first of them `minimax_h3_q4_k`, family `minimax_h3`, `size_bytes 32 443 213 394`, its `model_path` naming the package's own `dit.gguf`. T-870's read, on a model no slot lists.
3. **The load through this plugin was refused, and the missing half is the session the family wants, not the package.** `load_model {fn, model, package_id, endpoint_id}` answered in **663 ms** (`ms_catalog 178`, `ms_engine 485`) with the engine's own sentence `load failed: MiniMax-H3 supports offline audio generation sessions`. `loadBodyFor` (`lib/index.js:10556`) puts `task` and `mode` in the body only when the slot's catalog carries an entry for that model; this model has none, so the request arrived naming no task and `ServerModelConfig`'s default `task = "tts"` answered for it (`app/server/config.h:49-50` on the tree that node builds) against the family's own gate, which requires an offline audio-generation session (`src/community_models/minimax_h3/session.cpp:83-85`). The vocabulary is `src/framework/runtime/task_vocabulary.cpp:19`: `AudioGeneration` is spelled `gen`, aliases `music | sfx | edit | audio_generation`. Read the whole of it at `docs/FACTS.md` item 18.
4. **The same package loaded once the task was named, asked of the engine directly:** `{"id":"minimax_h3_q4_k","package_id":"minimax_h3_q4_k","task":"gen","mode":"offline"}` → `{"id":"minimax_h3_q4_k","loaded":true,"reconfigured":false}`, in under a second. That engine then lists the row `configured:false, loaded:true, task:"gen", mode:"offline"` and its `/health` model count moves 65 → 66, while the server's resident set stays at ~425 MB and the machine's available memory does not move. **A load is not a read of the weights** — a 32.4 GB package is read at the first run, not at the load.
5. **The dispatch was refused, and the reason is item 51.** That engine's `/v1/models` answers **66** rows; `endpoint_models {fn:"tts", id:"primary"}` stores **64** names for the same slot; the two it drops are `kugelaudio` and `minimax_h3_q4_k`, sitting at **positions 64 and 65 of the engine's own order** — so a model the engine has just made listable is the model this plugin drops, every time it is the newest thing on the slot. `dispatch_task {task_kind:"gen", model:"minimax_h3_q4_k", text:<a saved music preset>, options:{duration_seconds:5}, endpoint_id:"primary", force:true}` answered "… is pinned but its own /v1/models catalog does not list model minimax_h3_q4_k — a pinned endpoint never falls back to another host. Nothing was dispatched", with `placement[0].hard_reasons` naming exactly that. **`force:true` does not reach this gate**: the override of `AGENTS.md` 5.9 belongs to the capability bar, and catalog membership is a different gate. No row, no id spent, nothing queued.
6. **T-867's verb re-verified live on the way out.** `unload_all_models {fn:"tts", endpoint_id:"primary"}` answered `unloaded: ["minimax_h3_q4_k"], unloaded_count: 1, loaded_after: [], loaded_after_source: "primary_read"` in 397 ms, and that engine's `/health` still reports 66 model entries — the unconfigured row stays listed after an unload, which is `docs/FACTS.md` item 17. The slot was left holding nothing: the state it was found in, and the state the operator's preference about that machine asks for.
7. **State: MEASURED, NOTHING BUILT, and what the pass produces is a blocker named rather than a fix taken.** Two things it settles. A package-id load is only half of making a model usable: the session the family requires has to be named too, and this plugin has no way to name it — the load route hard-codes `loadBodyFor(fn, model, null, pkg870)` at `lib/index.js:14074` and no caller of it supplies a task. And **item 51's cap is what stands between this plugin and the test the operator asked for**, which moves that item from a reporting defect to a load-bearing one. Neither is decided here: the cap is the operator's word plus a harness restart, the task half carries no ruling, and starting a 32.4 GB first run on that machine is the operator's call, not this pass's. ## Fixed 2026-11-16 (Berlin) — T-871: a load that names a package_id no longer sends the catalog path beside it, and the listing check says which catalog it was read from

1. **Why this card exists: it is what testing T-870 on the lane found.** The operator restarted the harness at ~00:3x Berlin and T-870 was read live: `endpoint_library` on a CPU speech slot answered `library_state:"complete"`, 453 packages / 84 installed / 328 382 990 732 B, with **`loadable_by_package_id` 10 rows, `count:10`, `truncated:false`**, every row carrying the engine's own `model_path` and family, `minimax_h3_q4_k` (32 443 213 394 B) at the top and `firered_vad_f32` (2 368 640 B) at the bottom; and a `load_model {fn, model, package_id, endpoint_id}` for an unlisted model returned `ok:true` in 22 265 ms (engine leg 21 821 ms) with `load_via:"package_id"`, `model_listed_before_load:false`, and the engine's own `loaded_after` naming the model. The slot was restored with `unload_all_models` (`unloaded_count:1`). **T-870's state word is now LIVE**, and its item 7 — which said the engine-side proof was missing — is superseded by items 4 and 5 below.
2. **The defect, measured as a sequence, not inferred.** That first load made the engine LIST the model: the same `/v1/models` went 65 → 66 entries and the new row reads `configured:false, loaded:true`. So the **second** load of the same model found a catalog entry, copied its `path` as this verb has always done for a listed model, added `package_id` on top of it — and the engine refused the body in 131 ms with its own sentence: `load failed: send either path or package_id, not both`. A door that works once and refuses on the second press is the shape of this defect.
3. **The engine's rule, read where the code runs.** `ui_model_load_package_id` (`app/server/server_ui.cpp:280-296`) 400s a body that names both; `resolve_ui_package_model_load` (`:298-346`) sets `path` from the package **unconditionally** and refuses a caller-sent `family` that is not the package's own, while `load_options` / `session_options` are merged with the caller's keys winning. Those line numbers are of **the node's own checkout** (its git HEAD `6b0260ec`, read over ssh); this host's own checkout is a different commit (`4efa3959`) and **does not contain these functions at all** — a fact worth knowing before anyone greps the wrong tree for them. So: a named package_id means the file and the family are the package's. `loadBodyFor` now keeps `id`, the session `mode` and the task and leaves out the catalog's `path`, `family` and `load_options` when a package is named; with no package named the body is byte-for-byte the one this verb has always built.
4. **The second defect, found by the same live test.** `model_listed_before_load` / `model_listed_after_load` are read through `findRaw`, and `findRaw` reads the catalog `fetchModels(fn)` fills — which asks **the primary engine's** `/v1/models`, not the endpoint a named load talked to. Measured: the target engine listed the model at once (`loaded:true`, read at +0 s, +2 s, +5 s) while this verb answered `model_listed_after_load:false`. Both statements were true of different things, and the answer did not say which one it was making. The answer now carries **`model_list_source`** (`lane_catalog:primary`, or `lane_catalog:primary_not_the_target` for a named endpoint) and, for a named endpoint, a note that points at `endpoint_models {fn, id}` as the read that answers the engine the call actually talked to. A load with no package named carries neither key, and the existing note rules are unchanged.
5. **The engine-side proof, made without this plugin in the path** — the proof T-870's item 7 said it did not have: `POST <engine>/v1/models/load {"id":…,"package_id":…}` answered `{"id":"index_tts2_5_q8_0","loaded":true,"reconfigured":false}`, and the entry was in that engine's list at the first read after the load and stayed there as `configured:false` after the unload. And the same door refuses a family that does not fit the lane: a VAD package asked on the speech lane answered `load failed: FireRed VAD supports the VAD task` in 167 ms. **A package-id load is not a lane change.**
6. **What it cost, measured on the same slot, and it lands on item 51.** The engine now lists 66 entries on that slot; this plugin stores 64 (`MAX_ENDPOINT_MODELS`); the two names it drops are `kugelaudio` **and `index_tts2_5_q8_0`** — the model the package load had just made listable is the one the cap drops, and nothing on the slot read says so. That is why `TODOS.md` item 51 is now written as the blocker of item 56's auto-import half rather than a reporting nuisance beside it.
7. **Tests.** `tests/host.test.cjs` 2 589 → **2 593, 0 fail**. One existing assertion re-cut with a dated note (the one that said a package load keeps the catalog fields beside the package id — it was written before the engine's own sentence was measured, and the substance it protected, "a named package loads and the file is the package's own", is kept in its place); three new assertions (a package load on a **listed** model sends no `path`, no `family`, no `load_options` and keeps `mode`; a load aimed at a named endpoint names the catalog its listing check read and points at `endpoint_models`; a load aimed at the primary says so plainly and a load with no package named carries neither key) and one on the log record (a load aimed at a named endpoint names both the package and the endpoint it talked to). The T-625 source window went 1 400 → 3 400 for the same reason T-498's was widened in the last card — this card's comment sits inside that function and pushed the two pinned lines past the old prefix; the order that assertion exists for is still checked by the `indexOf`, not assumed. The first run after the change was **2 588 / 3 fail** (`scratch/host_t870b_run1.log`) and all three failures were mine: two of the card's own count assertions broke because I put a new load call **before** them, and one because of the window above; the new block was moved to the end of the card's sequence so a later card cannot move an earlier card's numbers. Whole-tree run of all 26 suites: every `--- rc=0`, `RC_ALL=0`, **6 120 `  PASS ` lines, 0 `  FAIL ` lines** (`scratch/suite_full_20261116_t870b.log`, runner `scratch/run_full_20261116_t870b.sh`).
8. **State at the time this item was written: BUILT AND TESTED, NOT YET LIVE** — superseded by item 9, which is the live reading. Host half: it goes live on a harness restart, and that per-restart OK is the operator's press — asked here, not taken. **One bookkeeping fault, stated because a baseline a later session cannot re-derive is not a baseline:** the runner I copied from the last card still named that card's log in its `OUT` line, so this run truncated `scratch/suite_full_20261115_package_load.log` — the file the T-870 card points at. Its numbers are in that card; the file is not. The new content was renamed to `scratch/suite_full_20261116_t870b.log` so no file describes a run it does not contain, and the runner's `OUT` line was fixed. Copies before this card's code changes: `scratch/index.js.bak_20261116_pre_t870b_body_fix`, `scratch/host.test.cjs.bak_20261116_pre_t870b_tests`. Nothing was committed or pushed.
9. **LIVE 2026-11-16 ~05:4x Berlin — the operator restarted the harness at ~05:38 Berlin and both halves were read on the lane in the same minute.** On a CPU speech slot, two consecutive `load_model {fn:"tts", model:"index_tts2_5_q8_0", package_id:"index_tts2_5_q8_0", endpoint_id:"e-11"}` calls: the first answered `ok:true` with `load_via:"package_id"` in 27 091 ms (`ms_engine` 26 715 — the engine actually reading the 3.5 GB file), the **second answered `ok:true` in 496 ms** (`ms_engine` 118, the model already resident). The second call is the case this card exists for: before the fix it copied the catalog `path` beside the package id and the engine refused the body with `send either path or package_id, not both`. The listing check now answers `model_listed_before_load:true`, `model_listed_after_load:false`, **`model_list_source:"lane_catalog:primary_not_the_target"`**, and the note carried on the row names `endpoint_models {fn, id}` as the read that answers the engine a load talked to — the second half of this card, and what makes those two flags readable instead of misleading. The slot was restored with `unload_all_models {fn:"tts", endpoint_id:"e-11"}` → `unloaded:["index_tts2_5_q8_0"], unloaded_count:1, loaded_after:[]`. **State: LIVE, both halves verified.** What this card does not settle is `TODOS.md` item 51: a model this fix makes loadable is still not dispatchable, because the load appends it to the engine's list at a position this plugin's 64-name cap drops — measured on two slots the same day, and it is what stands between this plugin and the test at item 55. **The next card id at the time item 8 was written was `T-872`; that id and `T-873`, `T-874` have since been used, and the next is `T-875`.**

## Built 2026-11-15 (Berlin) — T-870: a package an engine has installed but does not list can be loaded by its package id, and the library gap is stated as a load

1. **The ask, and which half of it this card is.** `TODOS.md` part one item 56, the operator's words: **"New models should show up and be auto-imported into our model registry"**, asked while six music models were downloading, with the intent that what lands in the shared store becomes usable through this lane **without a person editing a node's server config**. The card chosen from the options put was **"Item 56 (card B): engine package catalog plus package_id on the load verb"**. Item 56 itself had already measured the mechanism end to end on the engine side; what it named as blocking was on this side, and that is what this card changes.
2. **What was already here, stated so this package does not grow a second door.** A first draft of this card added a read verb — `endpoint_packages`, one engine read of `GET <engine>/v1/ui/models/package-sizes` beside that engine's own `/v1/models`, answering counts plus the installed-but-unlisted gap. It was measured against the live lane **before it was cut**, and it duplicated a verb this package has had since T-641: `GET endpoint_library` already makes those two engine reads per endpoint, with a 5-minute per-endpoint cache, a byte cap and a truncation check, a named 403 sentence for an engine started without `--ui-management`, and `installed_not_configured` naming up to eight **package ids** beside each directory. Two verbs answering one question from two places is the drift this package's rules exist to prevent, so the verb was removed and the finding comment was left where the function had been (`lib/index.js`, above the dispatch routes). The engine's answer shape — `{data, message, state}`, per-row `load_target`, `package`, `size_bytes`, `version_state` — is recorded in `docs/FACTS.md`.
3. **Measured on the lane before a line of plugin code was written.** Both CPU-class slots answered their own package catalog with **453 entries, 84 of them installed**, while the same engine's `/v1/models` lists **65** models; comparing the two by the engine's own `load_target.model_path` against the engine's own listed paths gives **24 installed packages that this engine does not list — the same 24 on both nodes**, which is what one shared store under two different unit configs looks like. The largest of them is `minimax_h3_q4_k` at 32 443 213 394 bytes (`TODOS.md` item 55's model: the package is installed, it is only absent from both configs); the smallest is 2 368 640. Id list: `scratch/t870_gap_ids.txt`. **And the catalog is a job with a state, not a snapshot:** the CPU unit, minutes after its own unit restart, answered `state:"running"` / "Checking package sizes" with the same 453 rows carrying `state:"pending"`, `size_bytes:null` and `version_state:"unknown"`; the same unit answered `state:"complete"` a few minutes later. A null size is not a zero size and a pending read is not an empty catalog — which is how `endpoint_library` already treats it (`library_state`, `retry_after_ms`).
4. **Built, host half, two regions.** 1: `load_model` may name a **`package_id`** (`lib/index.js` — the route gate validates it with the same token rule it uses for every other name, `loadBodyFor` adds the field, `loadUnload` takes it as an optional fifth argument). The engine's load route already reads that field and, **when it is empty, falls through to the ordinary load unchanged** (`handle_package_model_load`, `app/server/runtime.cpp:442-465`, `app/server/parallel_runtime.cpp:495-519`), and when it is present the engine looks the package up in its own installer and resolves `path`, `family`, `load_options` and `session_options` from the package with the **caller's keys winning** (`resolve_ui_package_model_load`, `app/server/server_ui.cpp:298-346`) — so this plugin sends both and changes nothing about what a listed model gets. The answer now says which path a load took (`load_via`, `model_listed_before_load`, `model_listed_after_load`) and the one log record the model verbs already write carries `package_id` — an empty string being the old shape. The two unload verbs refuse the field **in words** rather than ignoring it. 2: the library join reads each census row's own `load_target` (`pkgTarget870` in `libraryJoin641`), adds `model_path` to the installed rows it already publishes — additive, nothing that read that list before reads it differently — and publishes **`loadable_by_package_id`**: the same gap it already named, each entry carrying the package id, the engine's own model path, the family and the size, biggest first, bounded at 24 with the count beside it and never cut. The note that used to say a gap needs a person's hands now names the third way and **keeps both sentences it had**, so the two assertions pinned on it still pass unchanged.
5. **Not touched, on purpose.** No new verb (item 2). No change to the capability bar: `loadable_by_package_id` is a read of what could be asked for, not a dispatch candidate, and a model reaches the bar only after a load the engine then lists. `installed_not_configured`, `configured_not_installed` and `installed_default_quant_not_configured` keep their shapes and their separation. `MAX_ENDPOINT_MODELS = 64` is not touched (item 51 stays open). **And the honest limit of the new list, measured rather than assumed:** it covers the packages this plugin's spec catalog can place — of the 24 gap packages, **21 are named in the spec catalog and land in the list; three are not** (`nemotron_transcribe_iq4_nl`, `realtime_reuse_f32`, `soulx_flashhead_lite_q8_0`) and stay named only as `installed_dirs_without_catalog_entry` / `rogue_packages`, with no load handle. A second gap definition built from engine paths alone would have given this answer two meanings of "not configured", which is the drift item 2 exists to avoid. **Neither the panel nor the four agent tools reach `load_model` today** — zero references in `lib/client.js` and `tools/index.js` — so the field is reachable through the verb only, and both halves are named as open on the TODOS line.
6. **Tests.** Twelve new assertions in `tests/host.test.cjs` (four on the census half: the gap stated as loadable with the engine's own path; the loadable set being exactly the gap, with a configured package not offered and a catalog-unknown one not invented; a path that is the engine's field or nothing at all; the note keeping both old sentences while naming the new one and the read issuing no load; eight on the load half: the old body byte-for-byte with the new key **absent rather than present-and-empty**, a package load keeping the catalog fields, the answer naming the path it took, an unlisted model loadable with a body of `id` + `package_id` and nothing invented, no claim made about what the engine did after, a bad shape refused at the gate with no engine call, both unload verbs refusing, and the log record naming the path). One opt-in mock seam, `auditLoadTargets870` — real census rows carry `load_target`, the fixture rows never had one, and `rogue_shelf_pkg` deliberately gets none so "no load target, no claim" is testable. **Three existing source windows were widened, none moved or weakened:** the T-498 call-shape pin now accepts a further argument after `mEid498`, the T-625 load-body pin accepts the widened signature while still checking the order it exists for, and the `loadUnload` source window went 6 500 → 13 000 because this card's comments pushed one pinned line past the old prefix — every pattern in that block now reads more source than it did. `tests/host.test.cjs` 2 577 → **2 589, 0 fail**. Whole-tree run of all 26 suites: **6 128 pass, 0 fail, `RC_ALL=0`**, every suite `rc=0` — `scratch/suite_full_20261115_package_load.log` (runner `scratch/run_full_20261115_package_load.sh`); the twelve new assertions are `PASS` lines 1122-1133. The two runs before it are kept and they name my own faults as they happened: `scratch/host_t870_run1.log` 2 578 / 11 fail, which found **a real bug in my own code** — `pkg870` declared inside the catalog leg of `loadUnload` and read in the answer leg, a ReferenceError that made **every** `load_model` answer `ok:false` and is exactly what the existing T-207 and T-642 assertions caught; `scratch/host_t870_run2.log` 2 588 / 1 fail, which found the source-window cut. Copies: `scratch/index.js.bak_20261115_pre_t870_package_load`, `scratch/host.test.cjs.bak_20261115_pre_t870_tests`, `scratch/t870_diff.txt` (249 lines added, 7 replaced).
7. **State: BUILT AND TESTED, NOT YET LIVE.** This is host-side, so it goes live on a harness restart, and that restart is the operator's per-restart OK — it has not been taken. **The engine-side attempt I made while writing this was refused and I am not claiming it as proof:** a `POST <engine>/v1/models/load` naming `firered_vad_f32` and its package id on a CPU slot answered `cannot load model 'firered_vad_f32': max_loaded_models=1 and every loaded model is busy; retry later` in 11-15 ms, because a row of ours was running on that slot at that moment; the package-resolution half was never reached, so the load claim in this card rests on the engine source and the catalog reads above, not on that attempt. What that attempt did surface is a live condition worth its own line in `TODOS.md`: that same engine refused the unload that would have freed the slot with **`model 'controlfoley' is busy: current inference has run 694 727 ms (busy_timeout_ms=300000); the previous request has likely wedged and cannot be cancelled`** — and the reading I made from that sentence was wrong and is corrected where it belongs: the run was live, it belonged to a row of ours on that slot at that moment (`ap-1714`, 706 604 B, ended `ok`), and the engine calls anything past its own `busy_timeout_ms` of 300 000 ms "likely wedged" while it is still producing. That is `docs/FACTS.md` item 15, and the lesson it carries for this package is the order of the reads: a row read (`job_status`, `queue_status`) before an engine sentence is called a wedge. Nothing was committed or pushed. **The next card id is `T-871`.** **(Dated correction 2026-11-16, made by `CHANGELOG.md` T-871 and written here rather than by rewriting this card: this card's state word and its item-7 disclaimer are superseded. Item 4's sentence "the caller's keys winning … so this plugin sends both" is the part that was wrong where it matters: the engine sets `path` from the package unconditionally and answers 400 on a body that names `path` and `package_id` together, which is the defect T-871 fixes and what its tests now pin.)**

## Built 2026-11-15 (Berlin) — T-869: the speech lane reads the engine's own held-slot sentence and parks, instead of running the busy ladder

1. **The ruling.** The operator's choice of which half of `TODOS.md` part one item 48 to build first, verbatim: **"A first: the speech lane parks a busy engine"**. The measurement is their own read-aloud of 2026-11-15: one text split into 39 chunk rows, **34 placed on one node and every one rendered**, **5 placed on a CPU node — `ap-1651`, `ap-1659`, `ap-1669`, `ap-1677`, `ap-1685` — every one ended `error` with `cls: busy`**, each after four engine attempts 20 / 40 / 60 s apart, each answered by the engine in 116-135 ms with `cannot load model 'kokoro-tts': max_loaded_models=1 and every loaded model is busy; retry later` — the answer T-649 / T-763 / T-767 / T-773 already class as capacity and park. Row dump: `scratch/ap1659_chunk_split_20261115.json`.
2. **The cause, read out of the code before a line of it was changed — and it is neither of the two candidates item 48 had named.** `speechSpec` writes its response with `-o '<out>.part' && mv '<out>.part' '<out>'`, and `--fail-with-body` puts the body of a 4xx/5xx **inside the file the `-o` names**. stdout stays empty, so `serverErrorOf` can only return curl's own line — `curl exit 22: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 503` — and `isSlotWedgedRejection` / `SLOT_LOAD_REFUSE_RE` are never given the sentence the engine said. `sweepPart` and `capturePartBody` do recover it, but they run after the whole retry ladder, so it arrived only as text on the row's error. The task route passes no `-o`, its body is on stdout, its classifiers see it, and the same engine sentence parked there one hour later (`ap-1689`). Same engine, same slot, same sentence: the difference is where curl writes the body.
3. **What changed** (`lib/index.js`, one region, narrow on purpose): `runEngine` takes an optional fifth argument naming the `.part` a request writes into, and the one speech call site passes `outPath + '.part'`; on an HTTP-failure exit the existing bounded reader runs **before anything is classified**, and what it returns is given to those two classifiers **and to nothing else** — `isWedgeLike`, `isDeviceLostFailure`, `isBootWindowEmptyReply`, `isBusyRejection`, `isEngineRefusal` and `isTransientEngineError` all still read `err`, byte for byte; `sweepPart` reuses the text that read already produced instead of reading the file a second time; the new flag is cleared per attempt in the same block as every other attempt flag. **Nothing else moved:** `ENGINE_TRIES` 4, `ENGINE_BACKOFF_MS` 20000, `SLOT_PARK_MAX763` 3, `ENGINE_SLOT_HOLD_MS` 300000, `SLOT_WAIT_MAX_ARMS763` 10, `MACHINE_WAIT_RETRY_MS` / `BOOT_WAIT_RETRY_MS` 15000, `PART_ERR_MAX_BYTES` 2048 and `PART_ERR_MAX_CHARS` 200 are unchanged, no new constant was introduced, and `capturePartBody` itself is untouched — three occurrences in the file: its definition and its two readers. The other nine `runEngine` call sites pass no part path and behave exactly as before.
4. **Two harness findings explain why three cards of slot-classifier tests were green through all of this**, and a third came out of writing the new shape. 1: the `speechFail` seam answered the engine's body **on stdout and in the `.part`** at once — a shape the real `-o` route cannot produce — so the existing T-767 assertion that expects `capacity_slot` was measuring the mock, not the lane. 2: the two legs `capturePartBody` needs (`stat -c %s`, then `head -c 200`) are gated behind the session-identity engine options, so no `speechFail` instance could reach that reader at all. Both are now opt-in: `speechFail { partOnly:true, body:'…' }` and `partReadSeam869:true`, and every expectation written before this card answers the shape it answered before. 3: the seam's `.part` regex expected `'<path>'\.part'` — the suffix **outside** the quotes — while this curl quotes the whole path, so the write under it has never matched this command. The old two lines were left as they were; the new branch matches the shape the route really sends.
5. **Tests.** Six new assertions under `T-869` in `tests/host.test.cjs`. Behaviour: a slot refusal on the speech route is one engine attempt and no ladder, `cls: capacity_slot`, one `engine_capacity_park`, one `no_brake_capacity_refusal`, zero `auto_pause`, the endpoint still enabled; the parked row carries `park_reason: slot`, `capacity_parks: 1` and `endpoint_slot_wait.engine_hold` naming the engine's own sentence; the attempt record still carries only what came back on stdout while the park record carries the sentence read off the file. Contracts: the call site passes the part path; only the two slot classifiers read the captured text; the flag is cleared before it is set; no new constant or ceiling; the bounded reader is byte-for-byte unchanged. `tests/host.test.cjs` 2 571 → **2 577, 0 fail** (`scratch/host_t869_run4.log`). The three runs before it are kept and they name my own faults as they happened: `_run1` a quote inside a test name, `_run2` and `_run3` the two harness findings above — caught as failures, not absorbed. Whole-tree run of all 26 suites, 2026-11-15 22:0x-22:5x Berlin: **6 116 pass, 0 fail, `RC_ALL=0`**, every suite `rc=0` — `scratch/suite_full_20261115_slot_body.log` (runner: `scratch/run_full_20261115_slot_body.sh`); the six new assertions are `PASS` lines 3823-3828 of that log, and the suites that carry the order contracts this card had to leave alone came through unchanged: `engine_boot` 99, `endpoint_exclusivity` 125, `flow` 113, `stream_overlap` 141, `pause_resume` 67, `shut` 68, `transport` 115, `ui_state` 1 159, `scope` 497, `verb_contract` 25, `tooltips` 13 with its ratchet unraised. ## Built 2026-11-15 (Berlin) — T-868: an option value this plugin cannot carry is named on the row instead of vanishing between the row and the engine

**The finding this answers is `TODOS.md` part one item 57**, found on the `minimax-music3` test. `cleanOptions` keeps a key only when the key matches `OPTION_KEY_RE` **and** the value matches `OPTION_VAL_RE` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9._:,%\- ]{0,120}$/`), and a value that fails the pattern is **not** added to `dropped` — so the caller's field vanished between the row and the wire without a word anywhere, and the engine then refused a field the caller had sent (`ap-1647`, `ap-1648`: `MiniMax Music 3 requires lyrics` on a row that carried only `duration_seconds`). Every other option path in this file is fail-closed with a name; this one was silent.

1. **Built, host half.** `optionValueShapeNotes(o, family, model)` beside `cleanOptions` in `lib/index.js`. It re-reads the same two patterns and nothing else, reads the same 20-key window `cleanOptions` reads, skips the keys the option-deny set already owns so a denied key is never named twice, caps its notes at 8, and for each value it cannot carry says what is wrong with it **in the terms of the rule** — its length against the 120 the rule allows, that it carries a line break, that it carries characters the rule does not allow — and for a bad key, that the name is not one this plugin can put on the wire. **`cleanOptions` is byte-for-byte unchanged:** the T-258 pinned signature and its single call site still match, and what gets carried did not change at all.
2. **Where the words land.** At the task-dispatch site, beside the note the dropped-keys path already writes: the row's `note` gains `option value dropped: <key> (<reasons>)`, and one `option_value_dropped` record goes to the performance log naming the job, the model, the family, the keys and the sentence "the value did not fit this plugin option shape and never reached the engine". A row whose values all fit is silent, exactly as before.
3. **Measured before and after, on the lane.** Before: `ap-1648` came back carrying `options: {"duration_seconds":"30"}` and the engine answered its own contract refusal. After the operator's harness restart of ~21:00 Berlin, the first row through the changed path — an effects row on a CPU speech slot carrying one option value of 158 characters — was accepted, placed, and **carries on itself `option value dropped: prompt_extra (158 characters, the option value rule allows 120)`**, with the `option_value_dropped` record sitting beside the engine-capacity records that slot was already holding. The row was not refused and spent no brake: the drop is now said, and the take behaves as it did before this card. **Two things that row also showed, both of them other cards working:** it is parked, not failed — `park_reason: slot`, `endpoint_slot_wait` carrying `engine_hold` with the engine's own sentence, because the model slot on that node is held by a generation this plugin ended an hour earlier (`TODOS.md` items 48 and 52, and `AGENTS.md` 5.7 as written) — and its note names a length fill: `length filled from the stable_audio record (params duration_sec default 120 s): this request named none`. **That second half is my own call, not a defect:** I put the length in the body of the verb call, and the task path reads `body.options.duration_seconds` (`lib/index.js:18791`), so the number never reached the options channel and the T-837 fill did exactly what it is specified to do, naming the record it came from. **And the render half, which is the half that says nothing about a take changed:** `ap-1690`, dispatched at 21:27 with the length in `options` and the same 158-character value beside it, answers **`ok` — 5.0 s of audio, 882 044 B**, `elapsed_load` 1 380 ms (cold, the first request after the unit restart recorded on `TODOS.md` item 52) and `elapsed_gen` 15 396 ms, its options carrying `{"duration_seconds":"5"}` and nothing else, its note carrying **only** `option value dropped: prompt_extra (158 characters, the option value rule allows 120)`. A value this plugin cannot carry is now named where the caller will read it, and the take is the take it always was.
4. **Tests.** Five new assertions in `tests/host.test.cjs`, ahead of the T-652 block: the helper exists and the cleaner is untouched; the note and the log record are both there; the real 222-character lyric of item 57 is named with all three reasons at once; carried values stay quiet (a tags string, a numeric length, a deny-list key not named twice); a bad key is named and 40 unusable values produce at most 8 notes. `tests/host.test.cjs` 2 566 → **2 571, 0 fail**. Whole-tree run, 2026-11-15 21:1x Berlin: 26 suites, **6 110 pass, 0 fail, `RC_ALL=0`** — `scratch/suite_full_20261115_option_value_note.log`; the run before it was 6 105 (`scratch/suite_full_20261115_t867.log`). The earlier runs of this block are kept, not overwritten, including the three that carry my own test's faults as they happened (`scratch/host_option_value_note_20261115.log` through `_run4.log`). **Stated because the rule asks for it: no pre-change copy of `tests/host.test.cjs` was taken before this block was added.** The nearest one, `scratch/host.test.cjs.bak_20261115_pre_t867`, is the state before T-867 and is not the state this change started from; the copy taken for the source half is `scratch/index.js.bak_20261115_pre_option_drop_note`.
5. **Not touched.** The text-shaped option and the field that carries it — `TODOS.md` part two item 22, filed to v0.1.2 at the operator's word. Nothing was committed or pushed.

## Built 2026-11-15 (Berlin) — T-867: the plugin can tell one engine to hold nothing, and the idle-unload value was read off the unit instead of inferred from the config

**The operator's words:** "if the unload functionality for models is not wired in accordingly, its a fix to make now that the unload button actually works with the right remote verb!" then "go for 2 - implement now, let me know when to restart and i will do it , for 1 - you can use node cpu2 AND gpu1 now for the tests of the edits and restart cpu2 services - delay the work on cpu1 while downloads are in progress".

1. **Measured before anything was written.** `POST /v1/tasks/unload_all_models` with an empty body answers `{"unloaded":[]}` on an engine that holds nothing, and the dispatch switch calls that handler with no `ui_management` gate around it (`app/server/request_dispatch.h:148-152`). The list form refuses `{"ids":[…]}` with **"request requires a 'model_ids' string array"** — the key is `model_ids`, and it answers `{"unloaded":[…],"not_found":[…]}`. `last_activity_ms_`, the clock the idle pass measures, is written only by the load and run paths (`parallel_runtime.cpp:755, 914, 942, 1538, 2188`): **a catalog read and a `/health` probe do not reset it**, so this plugin's own reads never keep a model resident.

## Built 2026-11-15 (Berlin) — T-866: the effect starter prompt is a caption that names one event, not one word — measured on ten renders

**The operator's word:** "ap-1572 and ap-1573 are 'lama-like' - sounds ok, should be a little shorter, maybe test 5 seconds so we know it's not the short duration at fault … maybe we need to restart cpu1 host later after the downloads, … and it seems we have to expand the startup preset for the 'llama call'".

1. **Measured.** Ten renders, one CPU slot, one model (`stable_audio_sfx`), one file. The single word `lama` answered with music in four takes. Captions naming one event answered with that event — a dog, a steam-train horn, a llama in two wordings — at 10 s and at 5 s. The row table, the load and generate timings, the ms-per-audio-second figures and the sound-coverage measurements are in `docs/FACTS.md`, "What an effect prompt has to say for the stable-audio family to answer it".
2. **The rule that came out of it.** Name one event, name the room if you want it, and say what must not be there (`no music`, `no drums`, `no instruments`). A keyword is not a caption and returns the family's music prior. **5 s is the length for a single event:** the two captions that worked at 10 s left 1.0 s and 4.4 s of silence in the file, and neither carried a silence note at 5 s.
3. **What was ruled out before the rule was written.** Both alternative explanations were tested and both failed. The file is the effects package, not the music one — its own header records its conversion source, and it carries 1 024 tensors where the medium package carries 1 336. And the text encoder is **embedded in the model file** (the `t5gemma-b-b-ul2` tokenizer set travels inside it), so there was no missing tokenizer to blame. Both packages carry a **byte-identical embedded model spec** naming tasks `music, sfx, edit`: nothing in the metadata names a side, which is `AGENTS.md` 5.18 measured in the files.
4. **Changed.** The effect starter preset's prompt: `lama` → the caption that filled the window at both lengths (a store file, not a tracked file; copy `scratch/preset_lama.json.bak_20261115_pre_caption_expanded`). `docs/PROMPT_FIRST_SETUP.md` §3 item 2, which told an installing agent that the effect prompt "is deliberately one word", now carries the caption rule and the length, with the measurement pointed at (copy `scratch/PROMPT_FIRST_SETUP.md.bak_20261115_pre_effect_prompt_rule`). **This reverses T-833 (2026-11-13: "prompt set to one word … at the operator's word")**; the reversal is the operator's word of 2026-11-15, stated here so the two cards are not read as a contradiction.
5. **Not touched.** No code, no suite, no node config, no capability record. The two units on the second node were restarted at 09:23:08 before the control renders — unit, node, cost and the re-read health and catalog are in the chat of that morning. The primary node's restart after its own model downloads is the operator's timing and is not this card's to take.

**State: DONE.**

`TODOS.md` part-two item 14 — the read the operator asked for on 2026-11-12 ("**no scheduler, remind me as open todo prior to release**") — run today, and ruled at their card answer today: **"Build T-852 now."** **Agent-component half only (`tools/index.js`). A harness restart carries it, and this card owes one.** No verb, no route, no parameter name, no enum value and no tool name was changed, so nothing any existing session has already been told about how to call these tools moved.

1. **The read is a document:** `scratch/TOOL_DEFINITIONS_20261114.md`. It measures what the set costs, records ten claims that hold with the host line that proves each, and names seven drifts. The 9 022 B the tracker line carried had no method recorded with it; the method is recorded now (`scratch/tool_def_measure_20261114.cjs`), so a later pass compares against a like measure and not against a number nobody can reproduce.
2. **One claim was proved live, at no cost to the lane.** A `plan` dispatches nothing, so it was asked with a dialogue line naming no speaker, and answered `{"ok":false,"error":"line 1 has no voice/name — every batch line must say who speaks"}` (`lib/index.js:14481`). The tool had said the opposite: "or empty to let the model invent that speaker". That is the sentence that cost a model a refused call.
3. **The finding the read actually turned up** was bigger than that one. `model` is optional on all six kinds, and leaving it out is five different behaviours: a voice take reaches the engine with no model on it (`:14003` carries no gate; `:13025` builds the payload from `job.model`); a generated take is refused before a row exists, with the words `invalid model name` (`:18578`); a scene or a plan is filled with `moss_ttsd` (`:14804`); a transcription is filled with `qwen3_asr` (`:17267`); a speaker analysis is filled with `nemotron_asr` while its separation half is filled with `nemotron_3_diar` (`:17991-17992`). One optional parameter, five outcomes, none of them stated anywhere a model could read them.
4. **What was written, and where each fact was put.** A: a batch line must name its speaker — on `dialogue.items.voice`. B: the five outcomes of an omitted `model` — on `model`, in one sentence. C: on `analysis` the parameter names the transcription model and the separation model is not named here — on `model`. D: `analysis` is the chain it is, speakers separated then each one's words transcribed — on `kind`. 5. **The client half.** `isMusicRow603` (`lib/client.js:2214`) is asked about the side BEFORE it is asked about the kind. `loadPresets572` (`:12675`) carries the reported pairing into the picker. `presetModelMove841` (`:12781`) is the acting half: a pick whose folder names a generator side moves the panel-s generator selection to the model its preset was recorded with, through `modelsForKind` membership and `resolveTtsSelection` — the same selection every generator path reads — and `usePreset572` (`:12831`) says in the pick-s own sentence either that it moved, or why nothing moved. ## Built 2026-11-14 (Berlin) — T-837: a generated take that names no length takes the length the model-s own record declares — the fill, the name bridge, and the five cases where nothing is filled

1. **What the operator asked, verbatim.** On `TODOS.md` item 26 the card answer to "How firm should the duration requirement be on the agent side?" was **"Instruction plus fill-with-note"**; at this card-s own question the ruling was **"Fill from the model's own record"**. That is the whole of it. Everything below is what that one sentence touched.
2. **What was read before anything was written.** The two captured engine pages the suites read (`tests/fixture/t631_voice_capable_20261023/fixture/engine_index_20261023.html`, 1 909 030 B, and `tests/fixture/t248a_capability_reader_20261007/fixture/engine_index_20261007.html`, 1 650 872 B): **no family declares `duration_seconds`** — the name every engine carries is `duration_sec`. Its declared defaults differ by family: the `stable_audio` music entries `default:120`, the sfx entry `default:8, minimum:.64, maximum:60`, other families `default:20`, `default:0`, `default:""`, and one `default:-1` whose own description is "Target seconds; non-positive lets the planner choose". The live read of both enabled slots on 2026-11-14 answered the same two numbers this card cites (120 across the `stable_audio` family, 8 for `controlfoley`). A third thing was read: `optionSpecOf` (index.js:18094) builds its entries from a fixed key list — name, type, min, max, values, source — and **never carries `default` at all**, so the panel-facing option list is not a source a length could be read from.
3. **The name bridge, which is most of the work.** The record spells the parameter `duration_sec`; the runner-s option reader is exact-key over its own aliases and accepts `duration_seconds` — measured on the live store, where `ap-1504`, `ap-1505`, `ap-1507`, `ap-1508`, `ap-1509` and `ap-1510` each carry `{"duration_seconds":"5"}` on their rows and rendered `ok`. So the fill reads under the record-s name and writes under the wire-s name, and it sends **one** spelling: a request carrying both spellings of one knob is the engine throwing at two values for the same thing, and that is the risk this card carried and handled.
4. **Where it runs, and why there.** `fillGenDuration837` is one step in the `runTask` chain (index.js:13626), between the stage step and the request builder — the first point at which the row-s node is known, so the record read is **that node-s** record and not the plugin-s idea of a model. At dispatch the node is not chosen yet; a fill there would read a slot the row may never run on. The helpers sit beside `markVoiceCapable631`, which already reads the same cache for the same reason, and they take the cached answer when it is fresh and start one read when it is not.
5. **What is filled.** A `gen` row carrying no length under either spelling, on a family the option gate does not refuse, against a record that declares a positive number for that parameter: the number is written to `job.options.duration_seconds` as a string, exactly as a caller-s own option would arrive, and the row-s note says `length filled from the <family> record (params duration_sec default N s): this request named none`. One `duration_filled` record goes to the lane log with the model, the family, the seconds, the parameter name and which list it was read from, so a later reader can see why a row carries a length nobody asked for. The panel needed no change: `client.js:7920` prints the row note in the hover, and the options a row carries are already printed on the row.
6. **The five cases where nothing is filled — each one the old behaviour kept, not a new refusal.** (a) a caller named a length under either spelling: a person-s number outranks a record-s, and nothing is read for that row at all; (b) the family-s option gate already refuses the key — `controlfoley` (`OPTION_DENY`), where filling it would only buy a drop note; measured today, `ap-1506` carries `note "dropped duration_seconds: controlfoley does not accept it"` and rendered at the engine-s own 8.01 s; (c) the record is unreadable or names no entry for that parameter — no record, no claim; (d) the declared default is not a length: zero, negative, or not a number — the `-1` whose own sentence says the planner chooses is the engine-s decision and not a number to copy; (e) the declared default is above the generation ceiling.
7. **The ceiling keeps its meaning.** The gate at index.js:18361 refuses a length a **CALLER** asked for. A record-s default is not a caller-s ask, so the fill never walks through that gate, and a default over the ceiling is **skipped, not clamped into it**: the row carries `no length filled: <family> declares N s, over the generation ceiling of M s — the engine keeps its own default` and one `duration_fill_skipped` record is written. The sentence at the gate saying this plugin does not invent a length for a request that did not ask for one is still true where it stands — it is about a request reaching the gate with nothing on it — so it was left in place and given a dated pointer to the fill beside it, not deleted.
8. **The row this changes, named by its id.** `ap-1503` (`stable_audio_sfx`, `opts {}`, `dur 120`, `note ""`) is exactly the shape this card changes: it rendered at the engine-s own 120 s and nothing on the row said why a take nobody sized came out at two minutes. After this card the same dispatch carries `"120"` on its row and a note naming the record it came from. Nothing was re-rendered to prove it; the before-half is that row-s own record.
9. **Tests.** Thirteen new assertions at the end of `tests/host.test.cjs`, run against a synthetic parameter table in the shape the capability reader reads today (the T-781 form) whose parameter **names, defaults and sentences are the measured ones** and whose family names are test names, so a live catalog change cannot move this card; `controlfoley` keeps its real name because the gate that refuses it is keyed on it. They pin: the raw record carries the default the projection drops; the fill reaches the engine request as `"options":{"duration_seconds":"120"}` and lands on the row-s own options; the note names the family, the list, the parameter, the number and that the request named none; the lane-log record; a caller-s 7 is not overruled by a record-s 120 and no fill note is written; controlfoley is not filled; a `-1` default fills nothing; a declared parameter with no default fills nothing; a record that spells the wire name is filled and only one spelling reaches the request; a ceiling lowered to 60 s skips a 120 s default and says so on the row and in the log; no capability page means no fill, no note and no log record; the call site sits before the request object is built; and the projection `optionSpecOf` builds carries no `default` key at all. One existing pin was re-cut, not dropped: `T-456 (c)` at `tests/host.test.cjs:13800`, with a dated `(T-837 contract change)` note quoting "Fill from the model's own record". Its meaning — the ceiling never fires on a length nobody asked for — is unchanged, and the label now says which half it pins, because that fixture reads no capability record at all.

The first run, `scratch/t837_host_run1.log`, answered 2 537 / 1 FAIL, and the one failure was this card-s own assertion (m): it named a statement (`delete out.default;`) that does not exist in `optionSpecOf`, which never copies `default` rather than removing it later. ## Built 2026-11-14 (Berlin) — T-838: a take is only crossfaded when it is long enough for the fade, and the floor is asked of the side that moves

1. **What the operator asked, verbatim.** "we have to \"not\" crossfade between the short sfx jobs - crossfade should be skipped for sfx, voice, clone (spoken text) - while muic generations should be crossfaded if enabled … i guess the easy protection would be that duration of generation has to be at least 3xcrossfade-suration to actually use it".
2. **What was read before anything was written.** The crossfade lives entirely in the panel. The decision is one table, `crossfadePair603` (client.js:2250), fed by `isMusicRow603` (client.js:2206), which answers "is this row music" from the row's own task token. The spoken half of the ask was already that table's property since T-603 — a voice, a clone, a design render, a voice-convert, a scene line and a stem are not a music side and nothing about them moves — and the only length test in the file was at play time, in `tailFadeFor603`, where it refuses to fade a take whose element reports no duration. It never asked how short a take was.
3. **Why this is a length gate and not an sfx gate.** A generated row cannot name which side of the generator made it: `task_kind` is `gen` for an effect AND for a piece of music, and the family record cannot tell them apart either. The host met that exact gap and refused to guess (index.js:11337, `tagGenre606`: "A generated row records task_kind \"gen\" for BOTH music and effects, and its family record (stable_audio: \"music sfx edit\") cannot tell them apart. No genre frame rather than a guessed one."). What the row DOES carry is the length the engine reported for that take, and that is the one fact here that separates a 5 s effect from a 3-minute piece without inventing a kind.
4. **The gate.** `CROSSFADE_MIN_TAKE_RATIO603 = 3` (client.js:2228) with `takeFloorSec603` (client.js:2238) and `takeClearsFloor603` (client.js:2244). The floor moves with the length a person sets, across the panel's whole range: 0.25 s → 0.75 s, 1 s → 3 s, **the built-in 2.5 s → 7.5 s**, 12 s → 36 s. At the default a 5 s effect is not faded in any shape of handover, which is the case the operator named; a person who sets a short fade is asking for a short fade and gets it.
5. **The floor is asked of the side that MOVES, and only of that side.** This is the correction the first draft needed: gating both sides would have refused a music-into-speech fade because the spoken clip it hands over to happened to be short, and in an `out` or `in` handover that short side is started at full level and touched by nothing. A crossfade where both sides move asks it of both. Asserted both ways.
6. **"Not readable" is not "short".** `takeClearsFloor603` answers yes for a row that reports no duration, and the play-time guard in `tailFadeFor603` stays the one place that refuses to fade a take whose element cannot report its own length. Two places, one fact each, neither one guessing a number the lane did not report.
7. **One decision, two call sites.** The plan builder hands the decision the fade length at both halves of a handover (client.js:13385-13386) and nowhere else in the file calls it that way; the length is not read from inside the decision, because the decision is pure and testable without a browser.
8. **The controls say it.** The crossfade switch's hover now states that a short take is never faded, what the floor is at the default, and why it is measured rather than guessed; the fade-length field states the arithmetic of the floor beside the length it sets. Both were extended, nothing was removed from what they already said.
9. **Tests.** Fourteen new assertions in `tests/crossfade603.test.cjs`. Ten are the decision itself: the ratio is one number in the panel and is the one the operator named; the 5 s case in all five handover shapes; the floor is asked of the side that moves, so a short spoken take does not veto a fade it is not part of; a long handover still moves together; the floor is met AT the line (7.5 s at 2.5 s) and not only above it; the floor moves with the length a person sets; a spoken take is never faded with a long duration on it or without one; no fade length asked for is not a floor; a row with no duration is not read as a short one; the rule is stated in both hovers; the call sites. Four are the panel: a mounted walk of three 5-second generated rows with the crossfade on and the built-in length keeps every take at the level the person put it and starts no overlap, the arriving 5-second take is not faded in either, and the same three rows carrying 30 seconds on their rows DO overlap at the same built-in length — which is what says the wiring is untouched and the length is the only thing that moved. The media element is held at 20 s by the suite's own helper in both cases, so nothing but the row length is deciding. The ratio is read out of the panel's own source rather than restated in the test, so this file cannot drift from the number the panel uses — run against the pre-change client it throws instead of passing. One T-603 wiring assertion was re-cut with a dated `(T-838 contract change)` note quoting the operator: it pinned the two-argument call text, and its meaning — a handover needs a real neighbour on both sides, a walk's first row gets no fade-in and its last row no fade-out — is unchanged.
10. **Measured.** `crossfade603` **86 PASS / 0 FAIL, rc=0** (72 before this card). Whole-tree pass: `scratch/run_full_20261114_t838.sh` → `scratch/suite_full_20261114_t838.log`; its crossfade section reflects the suite as it stood when that suite ran (83), and the suite's final form is the run above. Logs: `scratch/t838_crossfade{,2,3}.log`. The hover sweep measure is **unchanged** before and after this card — 334 hovers read, 81 longer than 3 lines, longest 13 lines / 197 words / 1016 chars at the auto-generation control — measured against the pre-change copy (`scratch/t838_hover_before.log`) and the current one (`scratch/t838_hover_after.log`): the two hovers were extended and none of them became a wall of text. Copies before the change: `scratch/{client.js,crossfade603.test.cjs}.bak_20261114_0950_pre_T838_crossfade_length_floor`.
11. **The rows that show what the old rule did.** The four 5 s `lama` takes dispatched on this card's test run — `ap-1507`, `ap-1508`, `ap-1509`, `ap-1510`, all 5.00 s, 44.1 kHz stereo 16-bit, distinct renders — are four short generated rows in a row. Under this card every one of those pairs answers `none`, and a 180 s piece handing over to a 120 s piece still answers `cross`.

## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-827: why the player jumped from ap-1444 to ap-1446 — the walk's order key had no tie, and a chunked read mints its rows inside one millisecond — client + tests

1. **What the operator asked**, verbatim: "the whole play order now seems to be messed up, during normal player button usage i would expect it to play ap++ - and while deriving chunks from line, do it the same way ?!? - so playback of the message parts always stays in order …. or do we have to modify 'autoplay generated by this window' while it's already playing ?" Then the concrete case: "it jumps from ap-1444 to 1446 instead of 1445 during normal playback for example - why ?"
2. **Answered from the live lane before anything was written.** `ap-1444` carries `created 1794592691970`, `ap-1445` carries **the same value `1794592691970`**, and `ap-1446` carries `1794592691971`. All three are `kind:tts`, `status:ok`, `voice_mode:preset_speaker`, and their `text` is three consecutive chunks of one agent reply — they are one read-aloud, minted in one event-loop turn, so `Date.now()` answered the same millisecond for two of them.
3. **The mechanism.** `walkOrder299` sorted on the row's `created` stamp alone. A sort leaves tied entries in the order they arrived, and the host hands the playlist out **newest-first** — so the tied pair sat in the walk **reversed**: the order the walk actually held was `ap-1445, ap-1444, ap-1446`, and the step forward from `ap-1444` landed on `ap-1446`. Nothing was skipped by the lane; the key said the rows happened in an order the lane never used. This is also the older symptom on `TODOS.md` item 21 — "the next played item seems to jump to the next currently finished job" — at a wider scale: inside a burst the parts are walked in list order, not mint order.
4. **The rule now**, `lib/client.js`: `rowOrderCmp299` asks the stamps first (`if (ta !== tb) return ta - tb;`) and returns to the mint order only on an exact tie (`return rowMint299(a) - rowMint299(b);`). The stamp stays the primary key — it is what orders takes made at different times. Inside one millisecond the id sequence IS the order: registry ids are a global sequence and are never reused, and `rowWhen299`'s existing no-stamp fallback to that sequence is untouched.
5. **Both walks use the one comparator** — `walkOrder299` (the transport prev/next) and `ffOrder559` (the fast-forward that waits for a render). They were two sorts keyed on the stamp alone; they are now two uses of one rule about what "next" means. No third place sorts rows by stamp.
6. **What the operator's second question asked, answered as measured: no, the auto-generation chain is not what needs changing here.** The reproduction runs with `auto_gen: { state: 'off' }` in the fixture and `deepamp:agentplay = '0'`, and the jump happens anyway. The chain inserting rows while a read plays is a different question and this card does not touch it; the fault is in the ordering key the transport uses, with or without it.
7. **And it is not the read-aloud path either.** The same scenario re-proves that the read plays its own parts in the order it dispatched them (`ap-0711` is the take heard first, three dispatches, the ordered inserter intact from T-824). What was broken is only what the transport buttons walk when a person presses them.
8. **Tests.** `tests/flow.test.cjs` **106 pass, 0 fail** (`scratch/t827_flow_after.log`), up from 100. Six new assertions in a scenario built in the live shape — two rows sharing a stamp, one a millisecond later. Run against the pre-change copy (`scratch/t827_flow_before.log`) the three forward presses asked `ap-0712, ap-0711, ap-0713` and the reverse press asked `ap-0711`; run against the change they ask `ap-0711, ap-0712, ap-0713` and the reverse asks `ap-0712`. The observable is the `play_job` request the walk makes, because the read-aloud path never calls that verb — which is what makes the walk separable from the read.
9. **A claim of mine, corrected, because it is the reason this took two attempts.** The T-824 scenario `walkNextDuringReadAloud` pressed a control taken from the FIRST render of the class it wanted: `shim.rt.created` accumulates every node the shim ever built, so that closure held the playlist as it was when the panel was empty, and the press did nothing. What that scenario was measuring was the read-aloud path continuing in its own order, not the walk — and its passing result was read as proof about the walk. The control is now taken from the newest render, and the T-824 label was re-cut with a dated note saying what its measurement does and does not show. Its condition and its outcome are unchanged; only the claim about it moved.
10. **Copies, taken before the change:** `scratch/lib_client.js.bak_20261113_180722_pre_T827_walk_tie_break`, `scratch/tests_flow.test.cjs.bak_20261113_180722_pre_T827_walk_tie_break`. Probe kept as a probe: `scratch/t827_probe1.cjs` with `scratch/t827_probe1.log` (it reports that a bare mount with no boot sequence walks to nothing — that is a harness fact, not a plugin fault, and it is why the reproduction is a scenario and not a probe).
11. **Whole tree, run and clean:** `scratch/run_full_20261113_t827.sh` → `scratch/suite_full_20261113_t827.log` — **26 suites, 5 939 pass, 0 fail, `RC_ALL=0`**. The count moved 5 929 → 5 939, which is exactly this card's 6 plus the 4 from T-826 that had not yet been carried by a whole-tree run. Per suite: `tests/flow.test.cjs` 106, `tests/audio_tools.test.cjs` 40, `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` 1 113, `tests/host.test.cjs` 2 521 (the host half is untouched by this card, as it should be).
12. **State: BUILT, client half — goes live on a browser refresh; no harness restart.** `TODOS.md` part one item 21 is updated: the out-of-sequence playback it recorded as unreproduced **is** reproduced by this card, with the mechanism named. What is still open on that line is whether the operator's 16:52-16:58 Berlin run was this same fault end to end — the four `play_job` records for `ap-1374`, `ap-1375`, `ap-1376` are consistent with a walk press, and only the operator re-running a read-aloud after the refresh can say so.

## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-826: what a clear does to a row that is still waiting — the tool sentence said the opposite of what the panel does — tools half, wording only

1. **The question, verbatim:** "hmm, what happens if i clear a scheduled job without canceling it first ? that should result in a cancel prior to clear , right ?" The operator's expectation was correct, and the code already implements it.
2. **What is actually done, measured in both halves.** `clearAllRows367` (`lib/client.js:20306`) walks every `queued` row and calls `cancel_job` on it, then calls `playlist_clear` — its comment: *"A waiting row is taken out of the line first (cancel_job on a queued row is a DEQUEUE, never a kill) … A RUNNING row is never touched by either control."* The host agrees: `playlist_clear` keeps `running` and `queued` rows always and does not count them against `keep` (`lib/index.js:23935`), above the note *"'Clear' only retires FINISHED rows - an earlier version ate a running job."* The order is what makes one press enough: reversed, the row would survive the clear sitting there cancelled.
3. **What the two kinds of cancel cost.** `cancelJob` on a queued row is `finishJob(job, 'cancelled', 'cancelled before dispatch')` (`lib/index.js:21084-21090`) — nothing ran, and the endpoint cooldown gate (`err_own_timeout === true && status error|aborted`, `:6215`) does not fire, so the lane pays nothing on that endpoint. Cancelling a running row aborts the in-flight request, sets `aborted`, and takes the 300 000 ms hold; that is the one that costs, and clear never makes that choice on a running row.
4. **The fault this found.** The agent tool's own parameter description said *"clear retires finished rows — running and **queued** rows stay"* (`tools/index.js:286`), while an agent's `clear` is carried by the panel (`lib/client.js:16935` → `clearAllRows367()`), which dequeues queued rows first. The sentence described the host verb and not the path the agent's request actually takes.
5. **The corrected sentence** now says what the panel does, on the parameter where the rule belongs: *"clear retires finished rows; a row still waiting in the queue is taken out of the line first, so no queued row survives a clear, and that costs the endpoint nothing. A row the lane is running is left alone — only its own control stops it. No audio file is deleted."*
6. **Measured, because a tool definition is paid for in every prompt that carries it:** the `what` description went from 306 to 476 characters, **+170**, and `tools/index.js` by the same 170 B. A first draft also added the same fact to the tool-level description; that half was reverted, so the tool-level description is **byte-identical to before** and the fact is said once. The internal verb names were taken out of the sentence — it describes behaviour, not the mechanism behind it.
7. **Tests.** `tests/audio_tools.test.cjs` **40 pass, 0 fail** (`scratch/t826_audio_tools_run1.log`), up from 36. Four new assertions read the **registered tool definition** an agent is handed (`E.bag.byName('audio_control').parameters.what.description`), not the source text: the dequeue-first order and the zero endpoint cost are stated; the false claim appears nowhere in the component; the running-row boundary is stated beside it; and the phrase occurs exactly once across the tool description, the parameter, the scoped prompt section and the Config line that offers the tool.
8. **Copies.** `scratch/tools_index.js.bak_20261113_175326_pre_T826_clear_wording` was taken before the change. **No pre-change copy of `tests/audio_tools.test.cjs` was taken** — stated rather than repaired: the change there is one inserted block and its text is in this card's item 7.
9. **State: BUILT, tools half — `tools/index.js` runs in the host fiber, so this goes live on a harness restart, which needs the operator's explicit per-restart OK.** Nothing here changes behaviour: the panel and the host did what this sentence now describes before the sentence was written. The whole tree is unchanged by this card except `tests/audio_tools.test.cjs` (36 → 40); the tree record of 5 929 pass / 0 fail / `RC_ALL=0` stands as T-825 item 12 states it, and the next full run will carry this suite's four.
10. `TODOS.md` part one item 14 — read the four tool descriptions and the lane prompt section — is **not closed by this card**: it touched one parameter of one tool, found by a question rather than by the pass. The item stays open and now carries this finding on it.

## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-825: a slot pinned to an engine's own speaker is no longer called an orphan — the panel asks before it claims — client + tests

1. **What the operator reported**, verbatim: "if i select an angine with pre-defined voice - like kitten_tts and want to set it for an auto-play slot, voice “Kiki” is no longer in the plugin voice store — the pinned reference is gone is the error - but i selected an engine internal voice - how can we add it ?" Their second sentence is a tracking ask and it is filed: "also, track for v 0.1.2 that we want to display the engine voices in the voices section, too" (`TODOS.md` version targets item 6, new item (e)).
2. **The sentence and its whole test, measured.** `slotProblem419` at `lib/client.js:16698` answered `if (reg419 && !reg419[voice]) return "voice … is no longer in the plugin voice store — the pinned reference is gone"`. Membership in `props.voiceReg` — the plugin voice store — and nothing else. No engine asked, no host asked, and the model entry it had just looked up twelve lines above was not consulted.
3. **The name was legitimate.** The panel's own voice dropdown is *"the plugin's own registry voices + the selected model's built-in speakers"* (`:6143`, merged at `:6167` off `props.voicesBuiltin`), and those names come from `refresh_voices?fn=tts&model=<name>&caps=1`, which answers `builtins` / `builtins_source` / `default_voice` / `builtins_declared_empty` (`lib/index.js:21749-21806`) with **the model's own declaration deliberately beating the family record**. The panel offered a name and then called it gone.
4. **It was a warning, not a refusal.** The function's own rule: *"It never refuses a save … the slot stays visible and flagged."* The operator's slot was armed and would have spoken with Kiki. What was broken was the claim, and the cost of a false amber line is a slot a person stops trusting.
5. **The ruling, chosen on the card: "Ask before claiming"** — over "stay silent when it does not know" and "carry it in the model list". Nothing was added to the plugin voice store, and nothing should be: the store is the clone entity (`:6144-6148` says the engine voice list was deliberately removed from that merge for that reason), and copying an engine speaker in would give it a WAV and a reference transcript it does not have.
6. **The change, `lib/client.js`.** `askSlotModelVoices825(model825)` rides the verb that already exists — `call("refresh_voices", { fn: "tts", model })` already sends `caps=1` (`:14674`) and the host ranks model-level, then family capability, then the 2020-09-20 mirror, caching all three. The answer is remembered per model in `slotModelVoices825`; `slotModelVoicesAsked825` makes it one ask per distinct model per open panel, and a failed ask is not remembered so a later render may try again.
7. **`slotProblem419` takes a fourth argument** — the speaker answers the panel holds. Inside the existing store gate: no answer yet → ask and **say nothing** (*not looked up yet is not the same as gone*); the name is one of the model's own speakers → say nothing; the name is in neither place → one line that names both places it checked and says where the speaker list came from (`its speaker list: model | capability | mirror | none`). The other three arms of the sentence, warn-not-refuse, and the amber class are untouched.
8. **Tests.** `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` **1113 pass, 0 fail** (`scratch/t825_uistate_run4.log`), up from 1107. Six new assertions in a block beside the T-595 slot-warning block, reusing its mount shape: a slot pinned to a name the model itself serves gets no warning and the ask really happened; **eight renders after the answer landed asked zero more times**; no engine `/v1/audio/voices` listing was reached and no new route was invented; a name in neither place gets one line naming both places and its source; the ask rides the existing verb behind its guard and a failure is not cached; the sentence the operator read is gone as code.
9. **Three existing assertions were re-cut, none weakened**, each carrying a dated `(T-825 contract change)` note that quotes the operator: the T-419 signature pin (four arguments now), the T-419 call-site pins (both sites pass the speaker answers), and the T-595 item 8 source pin (the same two call-site patterns). What those pins exist to hold — one pure sentence, warn not refuse, the panel's own kind trio, no model name written into the warning — is unchanged and still held.
10. **Two test-side faults, recorded because they are why the first runs were red.** The ask counter took its baseline *after* a render had already spent the ask it was counting, and it conflated the panel's own selected-model hop — which rides the same verb — with the slot's ask; re-expressed as "zero further asks once the answer is in", which is the guard the code actually promises. And the "old sentence is gone" count matched **this card's own comment** quoting the operator's report; it now counts the returned sentence as code.
11. **Copies, taken before the change:** `scratch/lib_client.js.bak_20261113_174021_pre_T825_slot_engine_voice`, `scratch/tests_ui_state.test.cjs.bak_20261113_174021_pre_T825_slot_engine_voice`. Runner `scratch/run_full_20261113_t825.sh`, record `scratch/suite_full_20261113_t825.log`.
