## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-824: a read-aloud whose first chunk fails now plays the parts that came — client + tests

1. **What the operator reported**, verbatim: "it seems the chunks are not playing in the right sequence … the nexplayed item seems to jump to the next currently finished job, instead of the next chunk … also, it seems like only one TTS lane was used, why not loadbalanced currently ?" Their panel read at 16:52-16:58 UTC (17:52-17:58 Berlin) is the record this card worked from.
2. **The lane half is explained, not changed.** Their cancel of a 2 000-character chunk (`ap-1371`, on `primary`, 22 s in) put a cooldown hold on that endpoint — `engine_slot_cooldown {wall_ms:23669, req_ms:22079, hold_ms:300000, wall_limit_s:0}` — so for five minutes only `e-11` was in play and the nineteen rows of the next read ran strictly one after another. The gate is `lib/index.js:6215` with `ENGINE_SLOT_HOLD_MS` at `:1551`, and a user cancel walks into it because it sets `err_own_timeout` and `status:'aborted'`. Nothing was changed for this; it is recorded on `TODOS.md` part one item 21.
3. **The card first chosen was tested before it was built, and it was wrong.** The operator picked "Card A: chunk order in the auto-play path". `chunkOrderAgentPlay` (5 assertions) was written first: the real panel, `deepamp:agentplay = 1`, a host listing that reports the chunks out of text order. **The unchanged client played 0,1,2.** Chunk rows are marked seen the moment they are dispatched (`lib/client.js:16373`, `:16382`), so the agent auto-play poll never gets them. That path is not the cause and the assertions stay in the suite as the proof of a negative.
4. **The operator's own correction was measured and it holds.** Their word: "fast-forward button should have nothing todo with it - it might be that we have multiple auto-plays now that collide ?" `ffOrder559` deliberately KEEPS unfinished rows in the list it walks — its comment: "this one must also SEE a row that is not finished yet, because seeing it is how it can be waited for" (`:19829-19838`) — and `ffStepForward559` parks on `ffWaitRef559` rather than stepping past one. It waits; it does not jump.
5. **And the walk does know what is being heard.** `walkRef299` is set from the row handed to playback (`:16023`), not only by a walk press. `walkNextDuringReadAloud` (3 assertions) drives that case: a read-aloud started by itself, its first part being heard with the rest queued behind it, and the transport's next pressed. The unchanged client stepped to **the next part of the read** — correct. That hypothesis is excluded too.
6. **So is the crossfade handover.** `beginCrossfade603` asks for a next row only when the plan's tail is `"cross"`, and `crossfadePair603` answers `"cross"` only when BOTH rows are music rows (`:2189-2195`). Nineteen `kitten_tts` chunks are not a music pair. No handover play happens for a read-aloud.
7. **What the store does show is a second owner queueing those rows.** Four `play_job` calls exist in that window — `ap-1374` at 16:54:55, `ap-1375` at 16:55:07 **and again at 16:55:30**, `ap-1376` at 16:55:33 — and the read-aloud chunk path never calls that verb; it hands a route straight to the play queue. Only the walk paths and the handover ask through `play_job`. A walk was carrying playback while the read's own queue was not playing it.
8. **The defect that reproduces is the frozen read.** Their first attempt is the case: `ap-1372` (1 955 chars) ERRORED and `ap-1373` (835 chars) rendered ok a second later, and the panel asked to play `ap-1373` through `play_job`. `chunkOrderAfterFailedChunk` (3 assertions) makes that shape in the suite — three parts, the first refused, the other two ok. Against the unchanged client: **`played=[]`. Nothing played.** `enqueueChunkOrdered` released a stream only while `st.pend[st.head]` existed and its head advanced only on a successful release; the branches that end a chunk row without playing it called `dropPending(id)` and nothing else. A failed chunk stopped a read-aloud dead.
9. **The change, `lib/client.js`.** The release loop is now its own function, `chunkReleaseOrdered375(st, panelStarted375)`, gated on `st.pend[st.head] || st.skip[st.head]`; a `skip` tombstone per stream records an index that will never be played. `skipChunkOrdered(streamId, idx)` writes it and is called from every branch that ends a chunk row without playing it: error / aborted / cancelled, the deadline, and both fetch-failure deadline branches. `enqueueChunkOrdered` keeps its meaning and its callers unchanged.
10. **The first version of the fix did not work, and the test said so on the run.** `skipChunkOrdered` opened with `if (!st) return;`. A chunk that fails on its first poll settles before any part of the read has been released, so there was no stream record to write the tombstone into and the FIRST failure was the one forgotten — the suite still answered `played=[]`. The stream record is now created there too, with the comment saying why. No reading of the code found that; the failing run did.
11. **Measured.** Before, against the unchanged client: `scratch/t824_probe5.log` — 98 pass, 2 fail, both in the new scenario, `played=[]`. After: `scratch/t824_flow_run2.log` — `tests/flow.test.cjs` **100 pass, 0 fail**. The probes that measured the rejected hypotheses are kept: `t824_probe1.log` (the agent-poll path passing unchanged), `t824_probe2-4.log` (the walk cases). **Whole tree, run after the change: 26 suites, 5 923 pass, 0 fail, `RC_ALL=0`** — `scratch/suite_full_20261113_t824.log`, runner `scratch/run_full_20261113_t824.sh`. The previous record on this tree was 5 912, and 5 923 − 5 912 = 11, which is exactly the assertions this card added; `tests/host.test.cjs` still answers 2 521, unchanged, because nothing in `lib/index.js` moved.
12. **Assertions: 11 added, all in `tests/flow.test.cjs`** — 5 (`chunkOrderAgentPlay`), 3 (`walkNextDuringReadAloud`), 3 (`chunkOrderAfterFailedChunk`). They sit beside the existing `chunkOrder()` scenario (T-115), which isolates the ordered path by turning agent auto-play OFF; these three run it ON, mid-read, and with a failure inside the read. **No suite pinned `enqueueChunkOrdered` before this card. Three now do.** Nothing was deleted or weakened.
13. **Copies, taken before the change:** `scratch/lib_client.js.bak_20261113_170649_pre_T824_chunk_order`, `scratch/tests_flow.test.cjs.bak_20261113_170649_pre_T824_chunk_order`. Runner: `scratch/run_full_20261113_t824.sh`, whole-tree record `scratch/suite_full_20261113_t824.log`.
14. **State: BUILT, client half — goes live on a browser refresh; no harness restart is needed.** What this card does NOT close: the out-of-sequence playback as the operator described it is still not reproduced by any path in the code, and the three candidates that could have produced it are measured and excluded above. The frozen read is the defect their own run actually shows. `TODOS.md` part one item 21 carries the exclusions, the `play_job` evidence, and what is still open.

## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-823: a row this side stopped waiting on now names the leg it was stopped on — host + tests

1. **The ask, verbatim:** the operator's card answer was **"if it's factual, do 1"**, over the option *"Every site that ends a row on an abort names the leg it was in and what it was waiting for, so a row never reads aborted with error empty"*. So this card was conditioned on the finding being established, not on it being plausible.
2. **The row that named it.** `ap-1365` (dispatched 14:48:22Z, parked on `park_reason:"slot"` behind `ap-1364`, **placed 14:50:31.393Z — 1 ms after `ap-1364`'s `render` record at 14:50:30.999Z**): the lane log carries its `endpoint_preflight` (`http:200`, 14:50:31.392Z) and its model load (`st:"cached"`, `ms:0`, 14:50:31.928Z), and then nothing. The row reads `status:"aborted"`, `error:""`, `ended:0`, `elapsed_gen:0`, `elapsed_load:0`, `duration:0`, `size_bytes:0`, `output_path` written but **no file on disk** (`tts/ap-1365*` does not exist; 488 takes do). A row a person cannot read.
3. **What it was not, established by reading.** `cancel_job` and `abort_fn` are the only two `.abort()` calls in `lib/index.js` and both write a sentence — `cancelled (kill requested)` and `aborted by user` — so a row carrying an empty error came from neither. Nor is it our own wall: `err_wall_hit` is written only when `r.timedOut === true && r.aborted !== true` (`:11936-11950`), so the wall sentence at `:6187` could not have been what this row carried and had its reason erased.
4. **What this card found while checking, and it is the useful half.** `runEngine` writes its own lane record with `st:"aborted"` for **every** engine request this plugin drops (`:11951`). `ap-1365` has no `upload`, no `voice_stage`, no `synth`, no `job_outcome` and no `st:"aborted"` record at all — so **no engine request belonging to that row was dropped: it was stopped before its first engine request.** The one engine-side line in that window (`audiocpp_server failed to send error response: socket send failed`, cpu2 15:52:27 CET = 14:52:27Z, read from `audio-cpp-cpu.service`) is an engine that had an error to deliver to a socket that was already gone; it cannot be attributed to this row and is not. **This row's own cause is not recoverable from the records, and it is not guessed.**
5. **The shape of the fix.** One marker, `markAborted(job, leg)` (`lib/index.js:764-770`): it sets the status, writes `aborted_leg`, writes `aborted_after_ms` measured from `job.started`, and builds the sentence **from the leg** — `the plugin stopped waiting on <leg> before an answer arrived`. It returns without touching a row already marked, and it writes the error only when the row carries none, so a cancel keeps its own sentence.
6. **Seventeen places converted, none dropped**, each naming its own leg: the speech request; the tasks-route speech request; writing the take from the base64 body; the ffmpeg format conversion; transcoding for the transcription feed; the diarization request; a diarization chunk request; the transcription request; the detailed transcription request; the voice-sample upload; writing the voice sample from the base64 body; the task-lane request; the voice-sample upload for a renamed target; transcoding for the diarization feed; the speaker diarization request; writing the diarization artifact from the base64 body; the by-speaker transcription request. The pass was scripted and asserted each edit against the line number it started on; the count is pinned by an assertion.
7. **What is now impossible.** After this card only the two cancel paths assign `status:'aborted'` directly. Every other way a row reaches that status names a leg. That is asserted by counting the direct assignments outside the helper at exactly two.
8. **The row a person reads carries it.** `rowOf` — the smallest view `playlist_list` and `job_status` hand out — carries `aborted_leg` (capped at 90 characters) and `aborted_after_ms`, **only when set** (`lib/index.js:5349-5350`). Like `park_reason`, they are not written into the state file: what survives a harness restart on a restored row is the `error` sentence, which is the part that names the reason. Stated because it is a limit of this card, not an oversight.
9. **No client change was needed, and that was checked rather than assumed.** Two places already print a row's error and neither needed touching: the row hover prints it **whole** — `if (j.error) parts.push("error: " + j.error);` (`lib/client.js:7793`, the same hover T-818 put the park words on) — and a batch part line prints the status and the error beside it for any status that is not ok (`lib/client.js:9898`, capped at 70 characters there). With `error:""` an aborted row printed the single word `aborted`; now it prints the sentence. Both lines are pinned by an assertion so the claim cannot drift into a belief.
10. **No classification moved, and the reason is quoted from the code:** a row whose status is not `error` is never classified by its error at all — *"A row that did not fail has no failure class. Its status IS the record."* The wording of the sentence is chosen to match none of the wedge / busy / capability patterns, exactly as T-765's wall sentence was, and the two existing abort tests (T-649 (e), T-765 (e)) still pass unchanged: an abort is neither a cancel nor our wall, and it still costs no brake.
11. **Tests: 12 new assertions, no existing one removed or weakened.** Three behavioural, inside the T-649 block against its existing `{abort:true}` speech seam (`tests/host.test.cjs:21300` region): the row names its leg and carries the sentence; it carries the wait in milliseconds; and it is named as neither a cancel nor our wall and stays `aborted`. Nine source-contract in a new T-823 block at the end of the same suite: the marker defined once, the bare marker gone from the file, seventeen calls, seventeen distinct non-empty leg names, both keys written, the sentence built from the leg rather than bolted on, the guard that keeps a cancel's own sentence, only two direct assignments left, both keys gated on the row, and the client line that prints it.

The measurement now identifies a statement **by line position** relative to the marker (`tests/host.test.cjs`, dated note in the T-823 block). ## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-822: the player's read button reads the current session, not the session an auto-speak slot happens to name — client + tests

1. **The report, verbatim:** "new bug to report and investigate and fix: "read button" in player seems to try to play "autoplay slot 1" - it should try to play "latest/currently open" session instead .... the auto-play slots should be independent -> fix now". **State: BUILT, client half, browser refresh pending.** The second half of the message — "track for 0.1.2 -> make the "read button" get a settings field to switch between auto-play slots and current session" — is tracked on `TODOS.md` part one item 14 (e) and part two item 6; it is the switch back, not this fix.
2. **The report was read against the code before anything was changed, and it is exact.** The player's `♪ read` control (`lib/client.js:26458`, class `audio-play-tp-read387`) runs `speakLastMessage()`. `speakLastMessage()` called `speakNow(0)`, and `speakNow` reads `autoSlotsRef.current[0]` and hands **that slot's `sid`** to `last_agent_message`. So the settings half was already fixed by the earlier card (`forced` carries the panel's model, voice and style) while the **session** half still came from slot 1.
3. **Why that is a bug and not a quirk:** binding a slot to a session is the whole purpose of an auto-speak slot, so on any panel where slot 1 is bound the read button spoke a conversation the person was not in. The two features were not independent — one panel control silently inherited another feature's state.
4. **What "the current session" means on this plugin, measured on the live host rather than assumed:** `last_agent_message` with **no `session_id`** answers the newest root session (`lib/index.js:20867-20892`). Measured 2026-11-13 ~15:44 Berlin: `{}` → `ok:true`, `session:"session-e85b1433-…"`, `seq 42759` — the session this very conversation lives in, which `sessions_list` also names first (3 sessions). `{"session_id":"session-doesnotexist822"}` → `ok:false` with the refusal that names the reason. So "send no id" **is** the current session, and it is the documented meaning of the panel's own "(newest session)" option.
5. **A limit, stated because it is real:** the panel has no notion of a "currently open session" of its own — no client state names one, and the only way to address a specific session is a slot binding. So the fix aims at the newest root session, which is the conversation the panel is talking to, and the v0.1.2 field would be the way to aim at a slot instead.
6. **The fix.** `speakLastMessage()` now hands the panel's selection to a new `speakNewestMessage(forced)`, which calls `last_agent_message` with `{}` — no slot is read for the session, no slot's binding is sent. The player's read button and the handover of the same function to the read-aloud form both go through it, so one change covers both. `speakNow(i, forced)` is untouched: a slot row's own triangle is a slot action and stays one.
7. **One fallback is kept, and it is now stated out loud instead of silent:** with no model selected in the panel the button still falls back to slot 1's **saved model** — before the catalog loads that is the only way this control could ever speak at all — and it says so in its own notify ("no model selected in the panel — reading with slot 1's saved model (…)"). A model fallback is one thing; borrowing a conversation is another, and the borrowing is what was removed.
8. **The anti-duplicate rule kept, and narrowed.** A manual read used to write slot 0's "already heard" baseline. That was wrong in both directions at once: it moved a bound slot's baseline (so that slot could go silent on its own session's next reply) and it wrote nothing for any other slot watching the newest session (so that slot repeated the words the button had just spoken). `speakNewestMessage` now marks as heard **only the slots that were watching the session it just spoke** — a slot with no binding, or one bound to that same session — and touches no other slot.
9. **The control's own hover now says what it reads:** "read — speak the last agent message of the newest session (the conversation this panel is in) with the model, voice and style this panel has selected right now. An auto-speak slot's own session binding is not used here…" The hover had promised "the last agent message" while the code named a slot's session; the promise and the behaviour are the same thing again.
10. **Tests: 12 new assertions in `tests/ui_state.test.cjs`, in a new block after the T-713 session-binding block**, because that is where the slot machinery lives. It mounts the panel with **slot 1 bound AND pinned** (`sid:"session-bound-822"`, `saved:true`, model `m2`, voice `slot_voice_822`) and slot 2 armed and unbound, selects `m1` through the panel's own `TtsBox.onModelChange`, then presses the real controls and reads the **request bodies** the presses put on the wire: the read press names no session and no slot binding; it speaks the newest session's words with `m1` and never with `m2` or `slot_voice_822`; slot 1's own triangle still names its bound session and still speaks it with its own pin; after the next poll tick slot 1 speaks its own session's newer reply (its baseline was not moved) and slot 2 does not repeat what was already read; the hover carries the new words; and a source contract pins that `speakLastMessage` routes through the new path, that the new path names no session, and that the two slot paths still name theirs. **Fixture extension, additive:** the `last_agent_message` switch is now handed the parsed request body — the fact this card measures is whether a session was named, and that is only visible on the request. Every switch written before this card ignores the argument it is now given and the default answer is unchanged.
11. **The first run answered 11 of 12 and the failure was my count, not the code:** the contract check counted `speakNewestMessage(` and expected 1, but a definition is also a match for that string, so it answered `newestCalls:2` (`scratch/t822_ui_state_run1.log`). Re-expressed, not weakened: the definition is counted once and the **call** is required to sit inside `speakLastMessage`'s own body, which is the half that carries the meaning. Second run: `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` **1107 PASS / 0 FAIL, RC=0** (`scratch/t822_ui_state_run2.log`), up from 1095 — the 12 new assertions, nothing existing changed.

12. **Whole-tree record, same day:** `scratch/suite_full_20261113_t822.log` — **26 suite headers, 5 900 PASS, 0 FAIL, RC_ALL=0** (`ui_state 1107`, `host 2509`, `ui_state`'s new block included), up from the 5 888 of the T-821 record by exactly the 12 assertions this card added. Runner: `scratch/run_full_20261113_t822.log`'s own script, `scratch/run_full_20261113_t822.sh`.

Copies before the change: `scratch/lib_client.js.bak_20261113_153155_pre_T822_read_button`, `scratch/ui_state.test.cjs.bak_20261113_153155_pre_T822_read_button`; before the tracker edits: `scratch/TODOS.md.bak_20261113_154318_pre_T822_read_button_line`; before this card: `scratch/CHANGELOG.md.bak_20261113_154550_pre_T822_card`. **Client-only: a browser refresh is what makes it live**, no host change, no restart — it joins T-809, T-813, T-818, T-819, T-820 and T-821 in the one refresh that carries them all.

## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-821: the waveform asks the lane for the most peaks the host will answer — client constant, three suites

1. The card, and the answer chosen. T-820 had just made a bar **11 ms** wide (`sliding8`, 0.75 s ÷ 68 bars); the panel was asking for 2 000 buckets across the whole take, which is a 30 ms bucket on a 60 s take — wider than the bar it is supposed to measure. The operator was asked which lever to pull and chose **"Raise the panel's ask to 4000"**. One constant changed: `SCOPE_PEAKS_SLICES793 = 4000` (`lib/client.js:2769`), the ceiling this host is willing to give (`PEAKS_SLICES_MAX`, `lib/index.js:12202`).
2. **The rule, in one line:** a bar has its own measurement while `take length ≤ ask × window ÷ (bars × 1000)` — at 4 000 buckets and 68 bars, `window_ms ÷ 17`. Every length the 2 000 allowed **doubles**: 353 s at 6 s, 176 s at 3 s, 88 s at 1.5 s, 44 s at 0.75 s. Bucket widths at 4 000: 7.5 ms on a 30 s take, 15 ms on a 60 s one, 150 ms on a 10-minute one.
3. **A second limit, independent of the ask, stated because it binds first for the wide windows.** The host analyses at most `PEAKS_MAX_SAMPLES = 4 000 000` samples per call (`lib/index.js:12206`) and strides anything longer (`stride = ceil(samples ÷ 4 000 000)`, `sampled:true`, and the answer carries its own `note`, which the panel keeps). 4 M samples is about **83 s at 48 kHz**: past that, a 6 s window is bounded by the stride, not by the bucket count. For the two narrow windows the bucket line binds first (44 s and 88 s are both under 83 s). The strided behaviour is not new and is already pinned in `tests/host.test.cjs` (a 4 200 000-sample read answers `sampled:true, stride:2`).
4. **The host half was not touched and says so:** the default a caller who does not ask gets stays 120, the floor stays 8, the ceiling stays 4 000. The clamp reads `slices > MAX`, so an ask **at** the ceiling is answered in full with no admission — pinned as a boundary, one slice wide (`4001` clamps to `4000` with `truncated:true`).
5. **Why the claim lives in `tests/verb_contract.test.cjs` and not in a drawing suite:** it is a claim between the two halves. A drawing suite cannot see the host's ceiling and a host suite cannot see what the panel asks, and the failure this pins is the two numbers drifting apart — the panel asks more, the host clamps it, sets `truncated`, and the panel draws the shorter answer without saying so. Five new assertions there: the ask is inside what the host answers; the two meet at the ceiling (the check that would have caught 2 000 against a 4 000 ceiling for a whole day); the ask is neither the lane default nor under its floor; the constant is declared once and reaches the lane through exactly one call and is read by nothing in the drawing half; the host's clamp, its admission and its three numbers are intact. `verb_contract` 16 → **21**.
6. **The cost, measured rather than asserted.** The analysis work does not move with the bucket count — what bounds it is the samples analysed — so the only real cost is the size of the answer this panel fetches once per take. Measured on the fixture row in `tests/host.test.cjs`: the same file, the same `samples`, the same read — **203 777 B of answer at 2 000 buckets → 408 297 B at 4 000 (×2.0)**, one fetch per take and no more analysis work. The fixture take is 1 s, so its own bucket widths are not the interesting number; the bucket widths at 10 / 30 / 60 / 300 / 600 s are printed by `tests/verb_contract.test.cjs` (2.5 / 7.5 / 15 / 75 / 150 ms at 4 000). `host` 2 506 → **2 509** (two boundary assertions, one "the denser answer is the same read of the same file" assertion, plus the MEASURE line). `scratch/t821_host_run1.log`: 2 509 PASS, 0 FAIL, RC=0.
7. **Nothing about the drawing changed and that is pinned too:** the panel's bar count comes from the canvas (`fit`), and every peak consumer reads `peaks.length` from whatever the lane answered — the denser read is used, not assumed. `tests/scope.test.cjs` was re-run whole after the change: **497 PASS, 0 FAIL**, unchanged, which is the statement that a resolution change cannot move the geometry T-820 measured the same day.
8. **The wider effect, stated honestly:** the `full` view and the static whole-take waveform read the same answer, so a long take's whole-file waveform is finer too. Nothing was measured on a panel for this card; it is arithmetic plus a measured payload.
9. **Client-only: a browser refresh is what makes it live**, no host change, no restart. It joins T-809, T-813, T-818, T-819 and T-820 in the one refresh that is owed.
10. **What this card does not close.** The `from_s`/`to_s` window read (the other lever, `TODOS.md` part one item 1) is the only thing that stays exact at any take length, and it is a host change needing its own restart OK plus a re-ask policy. The live-WebAudio analyser (item 5) is untouched.
11. Copies before the change: `scratch/lib_client.js.bak_20261113_142734_pre_T821_peaks_ask`; before the record: `scratch/CHANGELOG.md.bak_20261113_141448_pre_T820_record`, `scratch/TODOS.md.bak_20261113_141448_pre_T820_record` (taken for T-820 and reused as the pre-record copies — no separate copy was taken before this card's tracker edits, and that is said rather than papered over). Logs: `scratch/t821_verb_run1.log` (21/0), `scratch/t821_host_run1.log` (2 509/0, RC=0), `scratch/t821_scope_run1.log` (497/0, RC=0), and the whole-tree record `scratch/suite_full_20261113_t821.log` — **26 suite headers, 5 888 PASS, 0 FAIL, `RC_ALL=0`** (5 880 from T-820 + this card's 8; inside that chain `host` 2 509, `scope` 497, `verb_contract` 21, `ui_state` 1095, `render` 234; nothing flaked).
12. State word: **BUILT (client constant) — green in the suites, not seen on a panel.**

## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-820: two narrower windows, and the bar row anchored to the take's timeline so it moves — client + tests

1. The ask, verbatim: **"the sliding window still looks laggy, maybe add a mode sliding4 and sliding8 to show an even smaller window, resulting in faster movement"**. Both words were added. What the card found on the way is the half that matters more, and it is item 2.
2. **The cause of "laggy" is not the window width.** Until this card the window painter laid its bars on fixed pixel slots — bar `b` at `b * (bar + gap)` — and only their HEIGHTS were re-sampled from the moving window. Nothing on the canvas ever moved sideways. Narrowing the window therefore only made a fixed row of bars change its values faster, which reads as a shimmer. The comment left by T-803 said "halving the width zooms in — fewer seconds on screen, the same scroll rate": that sentence is correct about the audio and wrong about the picture, and it is corrected in place at `lib/client.js:2717-2731` rather than left for the next session to repeat. A feature's pixel position is `(its time − the window's left edge) × W/span`, so the strip's true scroll rate is `W/span` px per millisecond: **33 px/s at 6 s, 65 at 3 s, 131 at 1.5 s, 261 at 0.75 s**. Narrowing does make the picture move faster; the operator's instinct was right and the drawing was not delivering it.
3. **The change that makes it move.** `lib/client.js:22188-22197` and `:22221`: the bar grid is anchored to the **take's** timeline — a bar belongs to the absolute time span it measures (`slot788 * barMs788`) — and its pixel position is where that span sits inside the window (`x788 = (b788 - frac788) * step788`). `frac788` is the fraction of a bar the window has travelled since the last whole bar boundary, which is what makes the motion continuous instead of one bar at a time. A bar partly off either edge is drawn partly (the canvas clips it); a bar whose time lies past the end of the take is not drawn at all. **The bar's width in time is unchanged** — window ÷ bars — only where it is drawn is derived differently. The look-ahead (`SCOPE_WAVE_LEAD_FRAC793 = 0.5`) and the rule that puts the heard moment in the middle of the strip are untouched.
4. **The two new windows.** `SCOPE_WAVE_VIEW_OPTS788 = ["sliding", "sliding2", "sliding4", "sliding8", "full"]` (`lib/client.js:2692`) and `SCOPE_WAVE_WINDOW_FRACTIONS792 = { sliding: 2, sliding2: 4, sliding4: 8, sliding8: 16 }` (`:2708`) — an eighth and a sixteenth of the 12 s base, so **1.5 s and 0.75 s**. They sit with the other window words and before `full`, for the reason T-792 gave (a person cycling the box meets the speeds together). The default word and `full` did not move.
5. **The floor moved 2000 → 750 ms** (`:2707`), stated because a floor is a rule. At 2000 both new words would have silently drawn the same 2 s window — a setting that lies about itself. What the old floor was described as protecting (a short take showing its whole length) is carried by the clamp in the painter, which is untouched: a window is never wider than the take, at any setting. What the floor actually did was refuse windows shorter than 2 s, and the operator's card asked for exactly that to stop.
6. **The widths, read back off the drawing, not off the constants** — the method T-792 used. A 60 s take that is otherwise quiet, played at 30 s, spikes planted on exact bucket boundaries at 29.75 s and 30.25 s, and the window derived from where a spike lands: `W = (t − 30) / (f − 0.5)`. Measured (`tests/scope.test.cjs:8846`, printed as a MEASURE line): **sliding4 1.43 s and 1.52 s** from the two spikes against a ruled 1.5 s; **sliding8 0.74 s and 0.76 s** against a ruled 0.75 s. The fixture's own quantisation is stated with it: one bar width of the window in the fraction, 0.015, which is 0.13 s of error on the 1.5 s reading and 0.03 s on the 0.75 s one. The same two spikes against the 6 s window would carry 2 s of error, so they are not used for it — T-792's own spikes measure that one.
7. **The motion, measured.** A window row's leftmost bar is now drawn **off the left edge of the canvas**: `-1.5 px` at 30.00 s of a 6 s window, `-2.5 px` at 30.03 s, with the bar step read out of the drawing at 3 px — a shift of **-0.335 bars against the -0.34 bars that 30 ms of a 6 s window is**. Before this card the left edge was 0 in every frame at every position and a shift was a whole number of bars or nothing, which is the picture that was called laggy twice.
8. **A narrower window is a shorter slice, not a denser strip:** 68 bars per row at 1.5 s and 68 at 0.75 s. The bars this mode fits come from the canvas width; the card changed the window, not the bar.
9. **Tests: 6 new assertions, and five re-cuts, with nothing deleted.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` 491 → **497**: the ring is read out of the file so no fixture counts the words again; the two widths from two independent spikes each; the bar count invariant; the row-anchoring measurement of item 7; two source pins (the fractions, the floor, the anchor, the draw site, and that the old fixed-slot draw is gone). Re-cut with dated notes quoting the operator: the T-788 source pin (three words → five), the T-788 control walk (now walks the ring read from the file, press by press), the T-809 control cycle (same), the T-792 source fractions, the T-792 hover (names every word and the four widths). Both mount helpers now press `ring.length - 1` times to land on the word they were asked for instead of carrying a counted number, and `spikesIn792` measures a spike's position against **the drawn row's own two edges** — a row that scrolls does not begin at x = 0, and the canvas edge was an assumption about where a picture starts.
10. **A fixture fact learned, written into the fixture:** a spike in this fixture is two buckets wide and the 0.75 s window is three buckets long, so two spikes planted 0.5 s apart are neighbours and the run grouping merges them — the first run of this fixture returned one merged reading instead of two. Single-bucket spikes with a bucket of quiet between them is what makes them two separate pictures at every width.
11. **The hover was rewritten to the family, not to two named words**: it now prints each width by calling the same function the painter calls (`scopeWaveWindowMs792`), so a card that moves a width cannot leave the hover describing the old one. It ends with the cycle it actually performs.
12. **What this card does not close.** The peaks read is still 2 000 buckets across the WHOLE take (`SCOPE_PEAKS_SLICES793`, `lib/client.js:2741`), and a bar in these new windows is 11 ms (0.75 s) or 22 ms (1.5 s) wide: on a take longer than about **22 s** the 0.75 s window's neighbouring bars start sampling the same bucket, and about 44 s for the 1.5 s one — the rule is `take length > window ÷ 34` at the 68 bars this canvas fits. Fixing that is the `from_s`/`to_s` window read (`TODOS.md` part one item 1, part two item 16), which needs a host change and its own restart OK. ## Built 2026-11-13 (Berlin) — T-819: the sliding window's position is read on every frame instead of on every media event — client + tests

1. The read that opened this card came off a live panel, verbatim: **"the waveform got better, but the 'framerate' for the sliding and sliding2 looks like it is low - the waveform appears with multiple bars per frame - not every single bar ?"**, and the shape was chosen at the card answer: **"Fix the position feed in the draw frame (Recommended)"**. It is the same complaint the operator made on 2026-11-11 (WM-47) and 2026-11-12 (WM-52), and this time it had a cause that could be found in the tree.
2. **The cause, read rather than assumed.** The single writer of the strip's play-position reference was the effect that runs when `playTime` state changes (`lib/client.js:21613` of the pre-change copy), and `playTime` is written only from media events — `ontimeupdate` at `:15808-15809`. Nothing polls the transport on a timer; the only interval in the strip is the 1 s clock. The panel's own comment at `:15800` already said it: "'timeupdate' fires a few times a second" — the browser rule is 15 ms to 250 ms and Chrome sits near the slow end. Meanwhile `scopeFrame300` re-arms, checks liveness, applies the fps cap and paints, and never refreshed the reference: at 30 or 60 fps the strip repainted the same window, then it jumped.
3. **The arithmetic that says why it looks like several bars at once.** A bar is 2 CSS px with a 1 px gap, so the bar count comes from the canvas width (about 65 bars), and a bar's TIME width is `window ÷ bars`: **~92 ms per bar on `sliding` (6 s) and ~46 ms on `sliding2` (3 s)**. A ~250 ms position step therefore moved the window **~2.7 bars at once, and ~5.4 bars** in the quarter-window — which is also why `sliding2` looked worse than `sliding`, and why raising the fps option changed nothing: the drawing was never the slow part. The suite prints this as a measurement (`T-819 arithmetic read: … a drawn frame now moves it ~0.36 bars at 30 fps and ~0.90 bars at 12 fps — the bar width is unchanged, the step is what got smaller`).
4. **The change.** `scopePosFromElement819()` beside `controlEl395` (`lib/client.js:21382-21391`): the element this row drives, its length checked as a real positive finite number, its position clamped to a fraction. It is called from the draw frame (`:21729`) and from the state-change path (`:21612`). The inline copy and its local variable are gone — `aPos331` no longer exists anywhere in the file.
5. **The rule the reading follows is unchanged**, stated because the sentence is an assertion and not a suggestion: no real length answers 0, a position is clamped to `[0, 1]`, and a live station — which reports `Infinity` or `NaN` — is not a fraction. That is the same rule the effect applied before, in one place instead of two.
6. **The refresh is deliberately ahead of the fps draw cap**, inside `scopeFrame300` and before `var ratio537 = scopeFpsRatio537(...)`: a frame whose draw is skipped still advances the reading, so the next frame that IS drawn paints where the take actually is rather than where it was when the last media event happened. The cap itself is untouched — it still lands on the draw only, as it has since the fps option existed.
7. Both consumers of that reference benefit: the sliding window (`scopeWaveWindowFrame788`) and the play-head marker in the full-file view, which read the same value. The marker was stepping for the same reason.
8. **Tests: 8 new assertions.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` 483 → **491**: the reading exists once and reads the element the row drives; the draw frame writes the reference through it; the refresh sits ahead of the cap; the cap itself is unchanged; the state-change path still writes it and still only when no loop is running; exactly two places write that reference and no third door exists; the no-length rule and the clamp are intact; the old inline copy is gone.
9. **What the suites cannot measure here, said plainly.** The behavioural half is a frame the browser draws, and this harness has no `requestAnimationFrame` — `scopeLive300()` refuses to run a loop without one (measured, not assumed). So the suite pins the wiring and prints the arithmetic, and the visible read belongs to the operator's panel. `ui_state` 1095 unchanged.
10. **Client-only: a browser refresh is what makes it live**, no host change and no restart. It joins T-809, T-813 and T-818 in the refresh that is owed; this one should be visible without any lane work — play a take in `sliding` and look at the step rather than at the bars.
11. **What this card does not do.** No bar width, bar count, window length, lead fraction or fps option changed — `SCOPE_WAVE_WINDOW_MS788`, `SCOPE_WAVE_WINDOW_MIN_MS788`, `SCOPE_WAVE_LEAD_FRAC793`, `SCOPE_BANDS300`, `SCOPE_BAR_GAP300` and `SCOPE_FPS_OPTS537` all stand as they are. It does not answer the live-analyser question: a bar is still an aggregation of peaks the lane measured in advance, and only a live analyser draws from the signal being played. That card and its two positions are still open at `TODOS.md` part one item 5.
12. State word: **BUILT (client) — green in the suites, visible on the next refresh.** Copy before the change: `scratch/lib_client.js.bak_20261113_115603_pre_T819_position_feed`; before the record: `scratch/CHANGELOG.md.bak_20261113_120014_pre_T819_record`. Logs: `scratch/t819_scope_run1.log` (491 pass, 0 fail, RC=0, run alone — that suite is one of the two that flake under CPU contention), `scratch/t819_ui_state_run1.log`, and the whole-tree record `scratch/suite_full_20261113_t819.log` — **26 suite headers, 5 874 PASS, 0 FAIL, `RC_ALL=0`** (5 866 from T-818 + this card's 8).

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-813: a playlist handover no longer walks the station through a resume and a re-pause, and a hold is only let go by the take that took it — client

The first of the three small items the operator chose at the card ("The three small code items I already located"). It is `../TODOS.md` **WM-31 item 20**, opened 2026-11-07 08:02 Berlin on the operator's report of a web-stream playing while playlist items hand over by crossfade — and that row's item 4 said the claim "needs a browser read before it is treated as a diagnosis". **This card is that read, taken in the suite the mechanism is actually testable in.**

1. **Measured against the pre-change file first.** The same fixture run against `scratch/lib_client.js.bak_20261112_192903_pre_T813_handover_holder` (`scratch/t813_before_fix_probe2.log`): with the crossfade on *pause the stream*, the station element's `play()` count goes **1 → 2 across a handover between two takes** — the station is resumed and re-paused inside one call. 139 of that suite's other assertions passed unchanged against the old file, so the reading is about this path and nothing else.
2. **What the mechanism was.** `applyOverlap395` (`lib/client.js:13321`) is the one function every take calls before it touches the station — its only call site is the play door — and its first act, the fix T-551 was, is to **release whatever hold is current** and take a new one. For a handover that is a resume and a re-pause of the same element in the same call, which is what the operator's report described.
3. **What changed.** A hold that the incoming take would take again — same mode, same element, the station still loaded as a stream — is now **carried** to it instead of released and re-taken, and the element is not touched at all. Everything else still goes through the release-before-the-duck, unchanged: a different mode, a different element, a station that is no longer loaded, or a duck level the person changed between the two takes — the carry explicitly refuses a duck whose level is no longer the one the panel is set to, so a changed setting still takes effect.
4. **Ownership, which is what the ruled expectation needs.** Each take now carries a number from a per-panel sequence; the hold records it; the release undoes only a hold its caller owns and does not clear a hold another take is still holding. Called with no owner — the stop press on a source, the one place a person says stop — it lets go of whatever is held, exactly as before. The station-readings handback at the door is unchanged in every case, including for a take that owns nothing.
5. **The sentence the code already carried.** The comment above this function has said since T-551 that "duck and pause are remembered as facts about THIS take, so `finish()` can undo the one it owns and nothing else". Until this card nothing in the code made that true. Now something does.
6. **Tests.** Four new assertions in `tests/stream_overlap.test.cjs` — three behavioural (the setup; the handover does not resume and re-pause the station; the take now holding the pause hands it back when it ends) and one source-shape (the hold names the take that took it, the carry is weighed before anything is released, the carry refuses a duck whose level has changed, and a take that does not hold the station leaves the hold to the one that does). **137 → 141 pass, 0 fail** (`scratch/t813_overlap_run2.log`). Before/after proven by running the same fixture against the pre-change copy (`scratch/t813_before_fix_probe2.log`: 139 pass, 2 fail — the new behaviour pin and the new shape pin, and nothing else).
7. **Two pins re-cut in place, none weakened.** `tests/crossfade603.test.cjs` (72 pass, 0 fail, `scratch/t813_crossfade_run2.log`): its adjacency pin `cancelFade603(1);` immediately before the held-duck read is now two statements with the carry between them, so the fact it guarded — a replaced take's fade is cancelled before that take's hold is let go — is asserted by index inside the same function; and its `function applyOverlap395()` signature pin reads `applyOverlap395(`. Both carry a dated `(T-813 contract change)` note. The T-551 fixture's own function-body slice was re-pointed the same way.
8. **Suite record.** **The full 26-suite record of the tree after T-813 and T-814 is `scratch/suite_full_20261112p.log` (script `scratch/run_full_20261112p.sh`): 26 `=== SUITE ` headers, 26 suite exits of 0, 5 841 `  PASS  ` lines, 0 `  FAIL  `, 0 `  THROW  `, `RC_ALL=0`.** It is 5 833 → 5 841, which is exactly T-813's four assertions plus T-814's four and nothing else moving in the package. The record for the tree before them is `scratch/suite_full_20261112o.log`: 26 suites, 26 exits of 0, 5 833 pass, 0 fail, 0 throw, `RC_ALL=0`.
9. **Copies taken before the change:** `scratch/lib_client.js.bak_20261112_192903_pre_T813_handover_holder`, `scratch/stream_overlap_test.cjs.bak_20261112_192903_pre_T813_handover_holder`, `scratch/crossfade603_test.cjs.bak_20261112_192903_pre_T813_handover_holder`, plus `scratch/lib_client.js.T813_fixed_snapshot` — the working snapshot that let the before/after be measured by swapping the file rather than guessing at it.

So the counter that exists to show a deliberate wait vanished exactly where the wait ended in a failure, which is the case a reader most wants to see. The word is now put on the row in all three branches — and at the two sites in the pump's start path too, because the commonest park of all is made there and not in `parkRow`, and naming it in one place and not the other would have left the usual case unnamed.

1. **What is fixed.** `SCOPE_WAVE_LEAD_FRAC793 = 0.5` in `lib/client.js`: the window always looks half of itself ahead of the moment being heard. One number, one place.
2. **What is gone.** `LS_SCOPE_WAVE_LEAD793`, `SCOPE_WAVE_LEAD_OPTS793`, `SCOPE_WAVE_LEAD_DEFAULT793`, `scopeWaveLead793()`, `scopeWaveLeadFrac793()`, the `useState`/`useRef` pair, `cycleScopeWaveLead793()` and the `audio-play-scope-wavelead793` button. 3. **What is untouched.** The view words `sliding` / `sliding2` / `full`, their fractions (`sliding: 2`, `sliding2: 4`), the 12 000 ms base and its 2 000 ms floor, the 2000-slice peaks ask of T-803, and the rule that the mark is computed from the play position rather than from the box it is drawn in.

Per suite that record: `host.test.cjs` 2 467, `ui_state.test.cjs` 1 095, `scope.test.cjs` 483, `render.test.cjs` 227, `scene_composer.test.cjs` 201, `stream_overlap.test.cjs` 137, `endpoint_exclusivity.test.cjs` 125, `transport.test.cjs` 115, `actions.test.cjs` 268, and the rest named in the log. `model_matrix.test.cjs` prints no PASS lines by design (it is a dry-run script suite).

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-806: the storage line, the model audit and the takes line tell the truth about what they read — host

Card 2 of the same five (§3 item 3.4). The region the panel now shows the operator, and the one place where a read could answer "empty" instead of naming its own failure.

1. **Two `du` reads were parsing an object as a string.** `storeUsageShell447` and the takes fallback in `measureTakes449` used `String(r.stdout)` where every other shell read in this file uses `r.stdout.text`. `String()` of that object is `[object Object]`, which matches no size line: the store read answered 0 bytes with no parts and `error` never set, on the very line the panel shows. Both now go through the same door every other read uses.
2. **A read that could not read says so.** The store read names a non-zero exit (`du exited <code>`) and an empty output (`du returned no sizes`) instead of returning zeros. The exit test is written so a mock that carries no `exitCode` is not treated as a failure.
3. **`models_audit` conflated "the audit failed" with "the store is empty".** `ok: failed.length < endpoints.length && anyInstalled` reports a working pair of engines over an empty store as a failed audit. `ok` now answers the only question a caller can act on — did this audit run — and what was found is named on its own lines: `audit_ran`, `store_has_packages`, `nothing_installed`, and an `ok_note` that says which of the two it is.

The trim now runs until the store is strictly under, and its "nothing left" record fires when it ends at or over.
5. **`delete_all_audio` did not clean where the plugin writes.** `set_save_path` accepts any absolute, shell-safe directory; the storage line, the takes machinery and the panel all follow `ttsDir`; this verb admitted only the built-in output roots, so after a move it cleaned a directory nobody writes to any more and left the takes that really are there. The directory the plugin is actually writing to is admitted now, guarded to the store root, with the protected set (voices, texts, uploads) unchanged — the T-422 rule that aims a save path at a protected store still keeps it out.
6. **Tests.** Six new assertions: the audit's verdict and its findings are separate fields and the empty-census case is no longer wired into the verdict; a save path aimed at an ordinary directory inside the store is in the delete walk while voices and texts are not; and three source-shape pins that no `du` read takes `.stdout` as text, that the failure paths are named, and that no comparison sits at the line in one mode and over it in the other. No existing assertion moved: the pinned auto_delete fixture (`removed === 4`, `freed_bytes === 1 638 400`) lands strictly under the line either way.

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-805: the Config door that no value could pass, and a boot audit that names what it applied, refused or moved — host

Card 1 of the same five (§3 items 3.2, 3.3 and 3.13; item 3.17 was dropped as a false positive, named below).

1. **`stt_feed.channels` could not be configured through Config at all.** The door declared `z.number()`; the vocabulary is `mono | stereo | source` and the gate is an `indexOf` over those words. No value satisfied both doors, so the field AGENTS 6 publishes was unreachable from the patch file. The door is a string door with that vocabulary in its description now. Pinned both ways: `channels: 'mono'` is accepted, `channels: 2` is refused.
2. **The boot audit said less than it did.** Half-accepted objects were reported as applied; `store_dir` and `ytdlp_path` appeared in neither list on any outcome; `specs_dir` could only ever appear as rejected; a clamped `job_timeout_sec` was reported as applied. Every one of those now names itself, and an empty `ytdlp_path` declaration counts as applied because that is what it means (capture unavailable).
3. **A new word in the report, with its meaning written down.** `adjusted` names a declared value the plugin applied AFTER moving it into range (`{key, from, to}`); `applied` keeps meaning applied as declared. The emission condition and the payload both carry it.
4. **Nested fields are reported per field.** `takes_limit.mode`, `takes_limit.max_bytes`, `stt_feed.mode`, `stt_feed.rate`, `stt_feed.channels` are each named as applied or rejected; the bare parent key is named only when the value is not an object. The loader hands an empty object for an absent nested field (pinned since T-716 h), and an empty object is not a declaration.
5. **A comment that was wrong, and a precedence line that was garbled.** The comment claimed a declared number outside the plugin floor and ceiling leaves the value the plugin would have used anyway — true for `generation_ceiling_s`, never true for `job_timeout_sec`, which is clamped to 30…3600. The precedence line read `environment > Config > the Config > the persisted value > the code default`; it now states what AGENTS 6 states.
6. **The boot created the store directories under a hardcoded parent, under a comment denying it interpolated them.** `mkdir -p $TTS_DIR $STT_DIR $VOICES_DIR` ran against `writePolicy('<home>/.dsh')` unquoted, with a comment saying "The command is a static string (no interpolation)". The paths are quoted now and the write policy is rooted at the parent of the resolved store root, so a `store_dir` pointed elsewhere creates its directories under its own root.
7. **What the review verified and this card did not change:** `cordis.patch.yml` declares no Config block, so the audit has never been written in this install. It is exercised here through a fixture that declares one; making it run live is the operator's patch-file decision, not this card's.
8. **Item 3.17, dropped as a false positive.** The report listed two rate vocabularies as a contradiction: `RESAMPLE_RATES` (12 entries) and `STT_FEED_RATES662` (8). They belong to different things — the first is the `resample_audio` media verb, the second is the transcription feed, which is what "eight fixed rates" describes. Nothing was fixed because nothing was wrong.
9. **Tests.** Nine new assertions: the two doors on `stt_feed.channels`; the boot mkdir pinned by its quoted paths, its apostrophe count and its policy root; a Config fixture that declares `store_dir`, an out-of-range `job_timeout_sec` and a half-declared `stt_feed` — the audit names `store_dir`, names the three `stt_feed.*` fields, does NOT name the bare parent in `applied` or `rejected`, carries `adjusted: [{key: job_timeout_sec, from: 7200, to: 3600}]`, and the plugin answers 3600, `resample`, `stereo` and the default rate. One existing filter is re-cut with a dated note quoting the operator: the T-637 filter that picked the boot `mkdir` by its unquoted paths now discriminates it by the directory it names. No assertion was deleted or weakened.

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-804: the take-budget rate lookup stops answering a measured family with the lane median, and the fallback stops calling itself measured — host

Found by the read-only code review of 2026-11-12 (round 5, `lib/index.js` 13500-17500) and **measured against this lane before anything was changed**. The operator's card answer on which of the four shapes to build was, verbatim: **"1 + 2: honest label + reuse the family resolver"**. The third shape offered (borrowing a variant's row for a family the table has no row for) was declined, and the fourth (measuring the missing families) is left as open work.

1. **The defect, in one line.** Both take-budget call sites pass the **model id** into a function documented as taking a family, and that function did an exact-string lookup in a 14-row table (`lib/index.js:14599` `var fam648 = model;`, `:14018` `body.model`, the lookup at `:6690-6702`), so a model id carrying a quant suffix fell to the lane median 6.11 s per s. The comment above the table had already said a rename doing exactly that "is NOT automatically the safe direction" and named the numbers: the family the audiobook lane renders with measured 38.99 s per s, so its rename left it read as 6.11, which pays for 589 s of audio where its own row pays for 92 s.
2. **The measurement, before the fix.** The table's keys were joined against the plugin's own `perf_log.jsonl` (25 442 lines, all parsed; script `scratch/review_20261112_rate_join_measure.cjs`, output `scratch/code_review_20261112/measure_rate_join_20261112.txt`). Restricted to the events that size a take (`render`, `synth`): **922 records hit a row, 606 did not** — about 40% of the take-sizing decisions made at the lane median. Over all model-bearing records: 3 183 hit / 4 346 missed, across 69 distinct model strings against 14 table keys. The misses were overwhelmingly quant variants of families the table does have rows for.
3. **What the lookup is now.** Measured first, inherited second, lane median last. An exact row still wins; the **longest** matching key wins over a shorter one, so `moss_ttsd_q8_0` takes the `moss_ttsd_q8` row (23.99) and not the `moss_ttsd` row (38.99); a variant of a family the table has a row for inherits that family's row. The rule is the one the capability bar already used — a normalised longest-prefix match (`capGateFamilyGuess`, `capNorm`) — so `rateNormKey648` is now the single normalisation definition and `capNorm` delegates to it. One rule, two consumers.
4. **The probe, over the model ids this lane actually renders with** (`scratch/t804_rate_check.cjs`, 34 ids): 7 exact, **10 inherited**, 17 lane median. Inherited: `moss_ttsd_bf16`, `moss_ttsd_q4_k`, `moss_ttsd_q8_0`, `kitten_tts2`, `qwen3-tts-bf16`, `omnivoice_f16`, `voxcpm2_6s`, `breeze_tts_2`, `kokoro-tts-en`, and an uppercase id. Lane median by design: `chatterbox`, `pocket_tts_en_bf16`, `cosyvoice3`, `qwen3-voicedesign`, `moss_tts_nano`, `glm_tts`, `fish_audio`, `vibevoice_7b`. A caller-declared `cost_per_second` still outranks all three. **The audiobook lane is unchanged by this card**: its dominant ids (`moss_ttsd_q8`, `moss_ttsd`, `qwen3-tts`) were already exact hits.
5. **What was declined, and why it is stated here.** A family the table has no row for is never borrowed from a variant of it: `chatterbox` does not take `chatterbox_turbo`'s 3.28, `pocket_tts_en_bf16` does not take `pocket_tts_en_q8`'s 1.06. That would assign a model a number this lane never timed for that model — and for `chatterbox` the variant it would borrow from is the fast one.
6. **The words the answer carries now.** `rate_source` is one of `measured:<id>@<date>`, `measured:family:<family>@<date>`, `lane_median@<date>/<n> renders`, or `declared`. The lane-median answer used to be labelled `measured:lane@…` — a fallback carrying the word measured in front of a number that was never measured for the thing being budgeted. Every note the plugin writes (the take's `over_budget` warning, the part notes, the planner's warnings) reads `cost_source`, so all of them changed wording in one place. The panel does not display this field; `lib/client.js` names it nowhere.
7. **The direction of the change is accuracy, not safety.** For a slow family the window now pays for less audio, so parts come out shorter and the over-budget warning fires when it should. For a fast family it pays for more, so parts come out bigger. `moss_ttsd_bf16`: 6.11 → 38.99 s per s, `hard` 589 s → 92 s. `kokoro-tts-en`: 6.11 → 1.48, `hard` 589 s → 2 432 s.
8. **The record.** New section in `docs/FACTS.md`: "The rate a take budget joins on, and how much of the lane that table actually covers (T-804, measured 2026-11-12)" — the method, the numbers, the recovered set, the declined set, the four words, and the standing instruction that the table is dated 2026-10-27 and needs a re-fit.
9. **Tests.** `tests/host.test.cjs:4499` and `:4766` re-cut with dated notes quoting the ruling — same rates, same bounds, the new word for the fallback; neither assertion was dropped or loosened. Seven new assertions: exact row wins; longest key wins; the inherited variants; the declined borrow; no model / empty / null / unknown all say `lane_median` and none carries the word `measured`; a declared cost still wins; and the end-to-end budget for `moss_ttsd_bf16` at 38.99 with `hard = floor(timeout / 38.99)`. Suite: **2 437 → 2 444 pass, 0 fail** (`scratch/t804_host_run1.log`).
10. **The full run.** The 26-suite run started for this card was cut short by the operator's harness restart of 2026-11-12 (~15:4x Berlin): `scratch/suite_full_20261112k.log` is a partial record (11 suite headers, 2 499 PASS, 0 FAIL). The full green record of the tree as it stands after T-804 through T-809 is named on the T-809 card's item 9 and in `../TODOS.md`.
11. **Copies taken before the change.** `scratch/lib_index.js.bak_20261112_pre_T804_rate_family`, `scratch/host.test.cjs.bak_20261112_pre_T804_recut`. No pre-change copy of `docs/FACTS.md` was taken — that file gained a new section and nothing in it was rewritten.
12. **What is NOT changed.** No rate in the table was re-fitted, added or removed; no model or family is chosen by this; the lane median stays the last resort; no client change. **A host change: it went live on the harness restart of 2026-11-12.**

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-803: the waveform is measured finer and given a look-ahead; the window's own words stay zoom, not speed — host and client

The ask, verbatim, from the settings batch of 2026-11-12: **"visualizer: waveform: the 'sliding refresh
rate/window' is still too slow and sliding2 doesn't make it faster - needs discussion/fix"**. The discussion was
held and the operator's answer on which of the three options put to take was, verbatim: **"balance 1 and 3"** —
raise the peaks density, and give the picture a lead. Both halves are built here. Nothing about the window words
(`sliding`, `sliding2`, `full`) changed.

1. **The measurement that says why narrowing never helped, stated before the fix.** `scopeWaveWindowFrame788` sets
   the window's right edge to the play position (`right = pos * dur`), so the picture advances at exactly the take's
   speed at every width: `sliding` is 12 000/2 = 6 s, `sliding2` is 12 000/4 = 3 s, floor 2 000 ms. Halving the
   window zooms — fewer seconds on screen, the same scroll rate. That is the whole of why the operator's report was
   that `sliding2` "doesn't make it faster". The strip fits about 65 bars (`fit = floor((W+gap)/(minBar+gap))`), so
   a bar is ~92 ms of the take at 6 s and ~46 ms at 3 s.
2. **The measurement that says what the blockiness actually was.** The panel asked `wave_peaks {job}` with no slice
   count, so the host answered its default 120 buckets for the WHOLE take: 250 ms per bucket on a 30 s take, 500 ms
   on a 60 s one, 5 s on a 10-minute one — three to ten bars sharing one measurement, and the window shows two or
   three buckets across all 65 bars on a long take. The repaint cadence was ruled out first: the panel's fps options
   are 60 / 30 / 20 / 12 and the default is 60, so a frame every 16.7 ms was never the limit.
3. **Half one, host.** `PEAKS_SLICES_MAX` moves from 400 to 4000 (`lib/index.js`, the constant block above
   `wavePeaks`). The read cost does not move with it: what bounds this verb's work is `PEAKS_MAX_SAMPLES` (4 000 000
   samples analysed per call; a longer take is read on a stride and says so), and a bucket is only a sorting of
   samples already read. `PEAKS_SLICES_DEFAULT` stays 120 for every caller that does not ask — this is a ceiling a
   caller may be given, not a floor it is handed.
4. **Half one, client.** The waveform's peaks ask now carries `slices: SCOPE_PEAKS_SLICES793` = 2000. That is about
   15 ms per bucket on a 30 s take — a bar's worth at the offered windows is 46-90 ms, so each bar gets its own
   measurement instead of borrowing a neighbour's — and about 300 ms per bucket on a 10-minute take. The row is still
   named by job id and by nothing else, which is the half of that call a test has pinned since T-303.
5. **Half two, client: the look-ahead.** A setting on the waveform row's own cell in the Settings visualizer matrix,
   cycling `none` / `half` / `near` = 0 / 0.5 / 0.75 of the window placed AHEAD of the moment being heard. Default
   `none`, which is the picture as it has been since it was built. The mark is computed from the play position, not
   from the box it is drawn in, so at every setting it lands on the moment being heard: at `half` it sits in the
   middle of the strip and the next half-window is the take that has not been heard yet. Before play there is no
   moment, so the window shows the opening of the take, as it did. The window is clamped to the take's end, so near
   the end the picture shows the tail rather than a promise.
6. **Why this shape and not a multiplier.** A window whose right edge IS the play position cannot scroll faster than
   the take, and a multiplier that pushed that edge ahead would put the heard moment outside the strip — the mark
   would stop being the thing it means. The lead is the honest form of "faster": the picture runs ahead of the
   audio, and the mark stays truthful. The operator's phrase was a scroll speed; what was built is what a scroll
   speed can be without breaking the settled meaning of the mark.
7. **What the new control sits in, and one hover that had to move.** Same box idiom as the sliding box beside it and
   the spectrum's LED box above it — a validator, a browser key, a fixed option list, a ref the draw loop reads, a
   repaint on press, the word on the box is the value in use. The sliding box's hover claimed the heard moment is at
   the window's right edge; that is now true only at `none`, so the sentence says so and points at the box beside it.
8. **Re-cut, not removed** (the rule in `AGENTS.md` 8.5): `tests/host.test.cjs` T-303's clamp check pinned 400 and
   is re-pointed to 4000 with a dated note naming the operator's "balance 1 and 3". One assertion is added beside
   it — that an ask the strip actually makes (2000) is ANSWERED rather than clamped. Nothing was dropped.

The ruling, verbatim, from the card that asked which directory the line reduced by T-801 should name:

1. **No host change was needed, and that is the interesting fact.** The host already measures the store root:
   `storageRoots()` is `[ttsDir, STT_DIR, VOICES_DIR, BASE]` (`lib/index.js:8549`), and every one of them is
   described with `exists / writable / free_bytes / total_bytes / error` by the same `statfs` read. The panel was
   picking the wrong record of a set it already had.

   measured for that exact path; else a measured root that CONTAINS the store root (a parent's filesystem reading
   covers what sits under it); else a measured root INSIDE it (the same filesystem, read at the child). With no
   store path in the answer at all it takes the root that contains the others — the store root in every shape
   this plugin writes in — and only then the first root the host names. It never invents a path and it never
   borrows numbers across filesystems.

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-801: the storage-limit box is wider and its option says what it trims, the STT-feed row fits one line with its read-out in the section header, and the save-path block becomes one live line — client

The asks, verbatim: **"in settings: storage limit, make dropdown selection box longer and rename option:
'auto_delete' to 'auto_delete_old' / section: downsample STT feeds: ... if set to 'original'... the 'sampling
rate field' should be disabled (got no effect) - also, move both dropdowns into one line + rename option
'16000Hz (default)' to save some space - / and why does stereo/mono have it's own source / also, the text
displaying current settings like 'stt feed resample · 16000 Hz · source (your setting)' should be in the header
of the section : right side of 'downsample STT feeds' (combine into single line aswell)"**, then the same day:
**"please make sure the 'Output (save path)' display is not static but dynamic"** with the target shape given as
**"7 lines -> 2 lines"**. One client pass, five regions of `lib/client.js`, no host change, no restart needed.

1. **The storage-limit selection box wears the widest width the Settings section has** (`SET_W_WIDE510`, 140 px,
   beside the shared `selectStyle510` it already wore) instead of sizing itself to its widest option.
2. **The option now reads `auto_delete_old`; the word on the wire is still `auto_delete`.** The label is what
   changed. `auto_delete` is the persisted value, the host vocabulary (`TAKES_LIMIT_MODES449`,
   `lib/index.js:1308-1309`), the word every perf-log record, every refusal sentence and every host assertion
   uses; moving it would rewrite stored settings and re-cut a dozen host checks for a word no person ever sees.
   The longer label is the operator's own wording pointing at the truth of the mode: it trims OLD unreferenced
   takes, oldest first, and `auto_delete` alone reads as "delete automatically". The hover says which word is
   on the wire and why the label differs.
3. **The sample-rate box is shut while the mode is `original`** — `disabled: !!(sttFeed662 && sttFeed662.mode ===
   "original")` — because in that mode the source file is sent as it is and the rate is never consulted, which is
   exactly the operator's observation "got no effect". The number the person chose stays stored and stays printed
   in the read-out, and the box's hover says that it is shut by the mode and what applies when resample is chosen
   again. It opens again on the mode the host reports, not on anything the panel assumes.
4. **The three feed selectors carry bare words** — `resample` / `original`, `8000 Hz … 48000 Hz`, `mono` /
   `stereo` / `source`. The sentences those labels used to carry ("resample (the plugin builds the feed)",
   "16000 Hz — shipped default", "source (keep the file's own channels)") were what pushed the row onto a second
   line; every one of them is already on that control's own hover, and the shipped-default fact is printed in the
   read-out beside the section title, which is where the operator asked for it.
5. **The current-settings read-out moved into the section header line**, as a child of the title element with
   `marginLeft: "auto"` so it sits at the right end of that line, and the standalone line under the controls was
   removed. The text it prints is unchanged, word for word, including the "(shipped default)" / "(your setting)"
   distinction the operator quoted. The class the three suites key on moved with it.
6. **The `channels: source` question, answered from the code, nothing changed for it.** The host's ffmpeg leg is
   `'-ar ' + rate + (channels === 'mono' ? ' -ac 1' : (channels === 'stereo' ? ' -ac 2' : ''))`
   (`lib/index.js:1388`): mono and stereo are conversions ffmpeg is ASKED to perform, and `source` is the case
   where no channel argument is passed at all — the only way a file's own channel count survives, since `-ac 2`
   up-mixes a mono file and `-ac 1` down-mixes a stereo one. It is a third word because the setting describes the
   shape the plugin BUILDS, and "build nothing" is not expressible as a value of a two-way conversion switch. The
   select's hover already states it in a line; the measured half — mono and stereo behaving identically at a given
   rate, the rate being what changed the outcome — is why the rate select carries the warning and the channel
   select does not.
7. **The save-path block is two lines and it is live.** Line one is the heading carrying its own sentence, merged
   into one line. Line two is one row: the directory generated files are written to, the writability the host
   measured, the free of total of the filesystem that holds it, and the host's own error string after them when
   there is one. It is no longer a value the panel carried from boot: the settings batch that reads every other
   value in that section now reads it too (`refreshSavePaths()` at the end of `readSettingsHostBatch511`), the
   re-read control and the block's own "check storage" button both re-ask it, and there is still no timer in that
   batch. The row names the host's `tts_dir` answer and matches it to the root that contains it; with no path read
   yet it is the first root the host names, which is the host's order and not a choice made here.
8. **The roots beside it are not hidden, and the tooltip that says so was corrected.** The header's output alarm
   names every root that is missing, unwritable, low on room or carrying a failed write, with its reason — that
   half was already pinned and is unchanged. Its sentence no longer claims the block lists every root, which is
   what it used to say and is no longer what the block does.
9. **One reading is the operator's and was raised, not decided.** Their reduced example showed the store root; the
   line as built names the directory takes are written into, because the heading says "Generated files land in
   this directory" and that is where they land. One line of the row's root-matching moves it. **Raised on the
   operator's return, not acted on.**
10. **The waveform half of the ask was not built, as asked ("needs discussion/fix"), and it was measured so the
    discussion has numbers on it.** The window's right edge IS the playback position (`right = pos × durMs`,
    `left = right − winMs`, `lib/client.js:21986-21987`), so the picture advances one second of take per second of
    wall clock whatever the window's width: `sliding` (6 s) and `sliding2` (3 s) differ in scale, not speed — which
    is the operator's observation. What caps how fast it can change is the peaks read: the panel asks
    `wave_peaks {job}` with no `slices` (`:21672`) and the host answers in 120 buckets across the whole take
    (`PEAKS_SLICES_DEFAULT`, cap 400, `lib/index.js:12006-12008`) — 250 ms a bucket on a 30 s take, 500 ms on a
    60 s one — while the strip fits ~65 bars (`:21979`), i.e. 92 ms a bar at 6 s and 46 ms at 3 s, so five bars in
    a row carry the same value. The repaint is not the bottleneck (the draw-cadence control defaults to 60,
    `SCOPE_FPS_OPTS537`, `:870-871`). The options, in the order they are worth doing: raise the density of the read
    the panel already makes (slices by take length, host cap raised); or ask for the window itself (`from_s` /
    `to_s` plus the bar count); or a scroll-speed multiplier, which moves the picture faster than the audio and
    breaks the settled meaning of the mark at the right edge — not recommended. **Awaiting the operator's word.**
11. **Seven assertions were re-expressed, none deleted or weakened** (the rule in `AGENTS.md` 8.5): one T-199 (the

    2 → 3; the SET of allowed widths did not move, which is what that pin guards), three T-534 (the file band's
    heading is the merged line, the band order is still pinned against the band's first control, and the words
    "Output (save path)" are asserted printed nowhere). Each carries a dated note quoting the operator's words.
    Eleven new checks were added, at the plumbing cap: the two-line block, the live read, the width and the
    label-against-value pair, the read-out's containment (in the header, not in the control row), the read-out's
    text, the three option lists, the shut rate box in `original` and its opening again in `resample`, the absence
    of the per-root map plus the batch and button re-reads, and the tooltip wording.
