## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-800: the panel reports its own auto-generation chain, the lane answers it beside the reads a caller already makes, and the agent may arm it — host + client + tools

The operator's ask, verbatim: **"PS: The auto-generation toggle status should be something the agent gets reported
during playlist/job queries and be aware about - it's a nice feature for the agent to suggest after first setup
procedure -... that we still have to test, too"**. Four cards were asked and answered, and those answers are the
design: **"Report only, no host record"**, **"Status plus the rows marked"**, **"Suggest and be able to arm it"**,
and for the live test **"it's being live tested currently by the user and works great so far"** — so no agent-run
lane test was done against the lane, and none was needed.

1. **The mechanism is the bridge that already exists, not a new one.** The host half of this plugin has never
   known anything about auto-generation (`grep auto_gen lib/index.js tools/index.js` found only the yt-dlp `auto.*`
   pattern before this card). What it now does is relay: the panel reports its chain state to a new verb
   `POST auto_gen_state`, and the agent's arm/disarm travels out through the same held-instruction channel as play,
   stop and clear — `laneAsk715` (`lib/index.js:23849` onward, reached through `ctx.provide('audioPlay', …)` at
   `:23941`). Nothing was invented on either side of the wire.
2. **"No host record" is what the code does, and it is measured.** The report lives in one in-memory value
   (`AUTO_GEN_REPORT716`, `lib/index.js:23808` onward); nothing of it is written to the state file. The check that
   pins this reads the fixture's persisted store after a report was made and finds no key for it. A restart is not
   expected to remember what a browser switch is doing, and it does not try to.
3. **A silence is not read as off.** A report older than 30 s is answered as `state: "unknown"` with a note saying
   why. The reason is in the comment above the code: a closed panel and a disengaged chain look identical from the
   host, and choosing between them would be this plugin inventing a state it cannot see.
4. **The panel keeps its own report current while a chain is armed** by a 15 s beat that rides the timer the panel
   already runs to read the agent-instruction feed (`autoGenBeat716c` in `readLaneActivity715`) — no new timer, no
   new poll. An off chain says its last state once, on the transition, and has nothing to keep current.
5. **Rows are marked at the read, never stored.** `rowOf` (`lib/index.js:5226` onward) stamps
   `auto_started: true` only while a fresh report names that id; the key is ABSENT on every other row rather than
   false, because the panel is the only authority that knows which jobs it dispatched. The same row read after the
   report no longer names it carries nothing — measured, on a row this suite dispatched itself.
6. **Both reads carry the state beside what they already carry**: `queue_status` and `playlist_list` answer
   `auto_gen` with the state, the count the chain keeps ahead, up to 12 of the ids it named plus the total count,
   the reason it stopped, how long ago it was reported, and `source: "panel"` so a reader knows who the claim came
   from. `job_status` carries the row mark through the same serializer.
7. **The agent can arm it.** `audio_control {what:"auto_gen", mode:"on"|"off"}` — a mode is required, a request
   without one is refused and records nothing, and with one it is *held* for the panel in the same words the other
   three actions use. The panel carries it out through `autoGenAskFromAgent716`, which calls the **same** handler a
   person's press calls (`autoGenToggle794`), so there is one arming path and no second meaning; the check counts
   the definitions of that handler and requires one.
8. **The prompt section now says the state is there to read.** The lane section names `auto_gen` (armed / off /
   unknown when no panel is reporting), names `auto_started`, states that a chain lives in a browser and this
   plugin runs none, and says that after a first setup an agent has done for the operator it is worth mentioning
   once, in plain words, as something they can turn on — the operator's "nice feature for the agent to suggest
   after first setup procedure", written where an agent will actually read it.
9. **Guides updated, not the history files.** `AGENTS.md` §4 item 5 now lists the fourth action of
   `audio_control`, and §5 gains item 16 stating the rule so a later session does not "fix" the missing host-side
   record; `README.md`'s tool-example block carries the new call and one sentence about what the answers carry. No
   dated history was written into either guide.
10. **The defects found on the way were mine, and all three are named.** (a) The first row-mark check was
    **vacuous**: the T-715 fixture holds no rows, so "no row is marked that the report did not name" was true of an
    empty list. Replaced by two checks that dispatch a row, claim it, read it back marked in `job_status` and in
    `playlist_list`, then read it unmarked after the report no longer names it. (b) The first client stop-report
    check read the **first** stop in the record, which was the three-refusals stop from the T-794 block and not the
    cancel-stop; the claim was re-cut to name the cancelled-row stop, and the refusal-stop was added as a second
    claim, which now measures that every stop path reports. (c) Three quoting/syntax defects in my own insert
    scripts — an apostrophe inside a single-quoted label twice, a missing comma between a condition and its detail,
    and this suite's `call()` helper answering with the body as a **string**, which needed the block to carry its
    own read helper before any of it ran.
11. **Measured.** `tests/host.test.cjs` **2 427 → 2 436** (+9; one re-cut: T-715 i10's refusal sentence now names
    one more control the panel understands, with a dated note quoting the operator's "Suggest and be able to arm
    it" — the check still measures a refusal that records nothing). `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` **1 079 → 1 081**
    (+2). `tests/audio_tools.test.cjs` **35 → 36** (+1). Twelve new assertions in total, at the plumbing cap.
    Files by `wc -l`: `lib/index.js` 24 105 → 24 189, `lib/client.js` 28 807 → 28 870, `tools/index.js` 392 → 394,
    `tests/host.test.cjs` 22 182 → 22 252, `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` 13 335 → 13 356,
    `tests/audio_tools.test.cjs` 338 → 351. Full set: **5 763 `  PASS  ` lines, 0 `  FAIL  `, 26 suites, RC_ALL=0**
    (`deepamp-audio/scratch/suite_full_20261112e.log`) — 5 751 → 5 763, which is exactly the twelve new assertions
    and nothing else moving. The run was repeated after the operator's restart, from the tree as it now stands.
12. **Live, and what is still owed.** The operator took the restart at 08:5x Berlin (their card answer "Restart
    now", then "harness IS restarted"), and the host half was verified by a read: `audio_status (lane)` answers

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-799: cancelling a row the auto-generation chain started disengages the chain — client

The operator's ask, verbatim: **"we should also add the functionality that if the user is hitting \"cancel/X\" on ONE of the jobs tagged with \"infinity symbol\" should \"disengage/disable\" The \"auto-generation\"-toggle"**. It is built and green. **Client-only: it reaches the panel on a browser refresh**, as T-788 through T-798 already do.

1. **Where the rule lives.** `lib/client.js:18835`, inside `cancelJob` — the handler the playlist row's X calls (`props.cancel(j.id)` at `:8776`). On a successful cancel, if the row is one the chain started, the id is dropped from the outstanding set and `autoGenStop794(...)` runs: the switch goes off, the notice names the row, and the chain has to be seeded again by a press before it runs on.
2. **One fact, not two.** The guard reads `autoGenIdsRef794.current[id]` — the same record the row's ∞ tag is drawn from (`props.autoGenIds && props.autoGenIds[j.id]` at `:8395`, gated on the row still being queued or running). The mark a person reads and the fact the panel acts on are the same record, so they cannot disagree about which row was the chain's. Nothing was added to the wire and nothing on the wire could carry it: the panel knows which jobs it started.
3. **The cancelled row is dropped before the notice counts what carries on**, so the sentence "N job(s) already dispatched carry on and keep their tag" counts the jobs that really are running and not the row that was just cancelled. Measured: the tag count drops by exactly one and the other chain row keeps its sign.
4. **What a cancel is not.** It is not a failure: it spends nothing against the three-refusals-in-a-row rule, it does not touch the count kept in Settings, and it does not make the chain dispatch a replacement. The existing stop path is reused unchanged — same notice family, same "seed it again with a press" behaviour the T-794 card describes.
5. **The reverse direction is unchanged, and both are now said.** Turning the toggle off still does not cancel anything already dispatched. The toggle's hover names the new stop reason next to the ones it already named (`:2167`), and the row tag's hover names the consequence of pressing its X (`:8406`). `tests/tooltips.test.cjs` passes 12 / 0 with its policy check included.
6. **What was NOT changed, stated because the panel has both controls.** The row's *delete* control (`delete_job`, `lib/client.js:8897`) is a different verb and keeps its own behaviour. The ask named "cancel/X", and that is the control this card changed.
7. **Three defects were in my own checks before they measured anything, and each is named here.** (a) Pressing every X on the page could not say which row each one belonged to, so the sequence proved nothing — the pairing is now read from the order the panel draws a row in: a row's tag is drawn before that row's own controls, so the X following a tag is that row's and an X before every tag belongs to an untagged row. (b) A notice an earlier press left on screen read as a new one — the check now compares the notices before the press with the notices after it. (c) The row id was read out of the panel's sentence; it is now read out of the request the panel actually sent, and the sentence is compared against it rather than standing in for it.
8. **And one placement mistake.** The first version of the new checks sat in the middle of the T-794 block and disturbed the state that block's own later checks measure — three T-794 checks failed because of it, not because of the change. The block now sits at the end of the T-794 block, after its last check and before its teardown, and builds the state it needs for itself.
9. **Eight new checks** (`tests/ui_state.test.cjs`, in that block): the X on a tagged row disengages the toggle and names the row it cancelled; the X on an untagged row leaves the chain armed and its notice says nothing about the chain; the stop is said out loud with the row named in the sentence; the tag count drops by exactly the cancelled row; a disengaged chain stays disengaged and dispatches no replacement; the toggle's hover names the rule; the tag's hover names the other direction (read before any row is cancelled, so it measures the tag as drawn); the source shape — same record, id dropped before the notice.
10. **Measured.** `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` **1071 → 1079 pass / 0 fail** (+8, the plumbing cap). Full set: **5 751 `  PASS  ` lines, 0 FAIL, 26 `=== SUITE ` headers, RC_ALL=0** in `scratch/suite_full_20261112d.log` — the 5 743 of record plus the 8. `lib/client.js` 28 788 → 28 807 lines by `wc -l`; `node --check` reports SYNTAX_OK. Correction to the T-798 card's number, stated rather than quietly re-stated: it said 28 789 where `wc -l` says 28 788 for the same file — that figure came from the pass script counting the array of lines, and the file's last line is unterminated. Every count in this package is a `wc -l` count.
11. **Not measured, and it needs the operator's eyes.** Whether the notice wording reads well when a person is mid-chain and presses X on purpose is a wording judgement; the behaviour, the wording's presence, and the state it leaves the switch in are all pinned. Live behaviour with a real engine — a chain running on a lane, an X pressed on one of its rows — is not something these suites can show; they render the panel against a mock host.
12. **Copies and scripts.** `scratch/client.js.bak_20261112_pre_T799_cancel_disarms_chain`, `scratch/ui_state.test.cjs.bak_20261112_pre_T799_checks`; the check block as written: `scratch/t799_add_checks.cjs`, `scratch/t799_add_checks_b.cjs`, `scratch/t799_add_checks_c.cjs` (kept as history — the first two are the defective instruments, and the reason this card can say what was wrong with them); runs `scratch/t799_ui_state_run_a.log` … `_d.log`, full set `scratch/suite_full_20261112d.log`.

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-796: the batch editor's lower text window follows the window it is in, and every line of a scene gets its own record and clear — client

The operator's ask (WM-49 item 1), verbatim: **"The multi speaker dialouge editor : the lower text window should
adjust to window size - the record and clear buttons should be bound to it - and also be integrated in the 'per line
edits'"**. Three clauses, and they are three changes.

1. **The lower field was sized by a row count written into the element.** `audio-play-scene-editor-raw381` carried
   `rows: 5` and nothing else, so pulling the window's resize corner (T-790) changed the window and not the field a
   person was typing into. It is now sized off the window: 45 per cent of the window's height, a floor of 140 px, and
   120 px of the window kept for the header, the file row, the turn rows and the cast.
2. **Three sources are asked for, in the order a browser can answer them:** the size the person gave this window by
   dragging its corner (the numbers the window is drawn with, off the same ref the drag reads), then the window's own
   box as the browser laid it out (the band form has a height and carries no stored one), and only then the viewport
   the band is capped to. Where nothing can be measured — a render harness with no layout — nothing is invented: the
   answer is 0 and the field keeps the rows it has always had.
3. **Measured, by three drags of one window in the suite that can resize it:** window 460 tall gives the field
   207 px, window 400 gives 180 px, and a window pulled below its own minimum (it stops at 220) gives the field its
   floor of 140 px. The window keeps its own scroll in every case: no control is pushed out of reach.
4. **The record dot and the Clr stay bound to that field as it grows.** They are positioned inside the field's own
   relative wrapper at its top-right and the field reserves the 56 px they are drawn in — where they have always
   been. Growing the field does not move them.
5. **The same pair, per line.** Every turn row's own text field now carries a dictation dot and a Clr, reserves the
   same 56 px, and its hover says what it does to that line: the transcript lands as a new line of this turn, and
   the other lines are named as not touched.
6. **One entry for every scene dictation this composer can start** (`sceneDict796`). The panel owns the recording and
   the transcription and reports them back as two flags; what it cannot know is which of these fields asked, so the
   press records that here. Only the line that was asked shows the recording colour. The whole-scene path still hands
   the panel the setter it always used.
7. **A transcript dictated into a line is applied inside the state updater, over the text the scene holds when the
   transcript arrives** — not the text the render that pressed the button was handed. That is the same stale-closure
   class T-794 found in the auto-generation chain, and it is why `turns381` now takes an optional source: only so it
   can be asked about a text it was not closed over.
8. **The per-line Clr empties that line's words and keeps the speaker line.** The name is the turn and the cast is
   built from names; removing a turn is what that row's own x is for. Field-local, as the rule of T-442 says.

## Built 2026-11-12 (Berlin) — T-795: the split-flap clock faces carry a colon that swaps its dots every second, and the digits fill the cards they are printed on — client

The operator's ask (WM-49 item 3), verbatim: **"for the clock faces with the falling numbers, the distance between
hours and minutes looks too big - we should either place something in between, like two dots ':' - maybe alternating
with upper and lower beingswitched every second - or make a suggestion how to 'center' the letter heights within the
canvas"**. The shape chosen from the options put was **both halves**: the dots in the gap AND the letter heights
filled out.

1. **The gap is untouched arithmetic.** The fit loop, the 0.55 pair gap and the 0.14 gap within a pair are unchanged,
   and the board's total width is unchanged. The ask was not for more space; it was for the space to be doing
   something, and the earlier ruling that this board carries no separator was re-opened by the operator's word, not
   by this card.
2. **What is drawn:** two square dots at the gap's own centre, one above and one below the seam line the cards are
   split on. The lit one is painted in the face's own ink, the other in the ink the card rim is painted in — no new
   colour, because a real board's separator is not lit. Measured from the printed cap height: a dot side of 12 per
   cent, a rise of 22 per cent of the cap from the card middle, and a two-pixel floor below which a dot is not a dot.
3. **The alternation is the clock's own second**, taken from the time this face is already reading and not from a
   frame counter: a face drawn at 12 fps and one drawn at 60 fps swap their dots on the same second. Which side is
   lit flips every second; the other dot stays visible in the unlit ink, so it reads as a colon at a glance and as a
   live thing a second later.
4. **The letter heights.** `FLAP_PAD681` is the padding inside a card and it was 0.16, which is what the first build
   used. Out of that arithmetic a card printed its digit at 68 per cent of its own height. It is now 0.07: the digit
   prints at 86 per cent and the dead bands above and below drop to 7 per cent. The horizontal rule is untouched —
   `padX` is still taken from the cap height at the same ratio, so a face wider than the one assumed is still fitted
   to the card rather than allowed to ride out of it.
5. **Measured in the suite's 200×80 board:** the cap a print actually carries, after the fit, was **0.65 of the card
   height** before this card and is **0.81** now — the digits are 25 per cent taller in the same box. The card height
   itself went 52.0 px to 48.8 px, because fatter cards make a wider board and the fit answers by shrinking the
   board to the box, as it always has.
6. **What was already true, stated because the ask used the same words as an earlier ruling:** the ink MIDDLE of
   every digit has been centred on its card since T-684 addendum 2, which measures it and still does. What was not
   filled was the ink HEIGHT. That is the difference this card makes, and it is named so the two are not confused.
7. **Both faces carry it.** `clock_flap` and `clock_flap_light` share one drawing path with only the palette
   swapped; the inverted board is measured drawing the separator in its own inks, and none of the dark board's
   palette painted in that face.

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-794: auto-generation — the player keeps a generation ahead of what you are hearing, and the quick line shows what it queued — client

The operator's ask, verbatim: **"feature request i want to be implemented aswell as a final addition is
"auto-generation" - it should be in the Player/Eject-dropdown player ui, - on the left side of the "generate"
button, - in form of a toggle button with infinity symbol, it should result so that a new job is auto generated
when the last one is finished and starts playing - so we always have a job in the pipeline with the same prompt
preset as the user selected ... with a setting option added "how many auto generations we should run ahead,
default:1 - in our setup currently better 2 so we can test the load balancing - and max5, ... maybe we will get
realtime / the playlist should get a new "infinity" symbol tag that is displayed in the so triggered generation
(until it's finished generating) / also, the generate button should show the same feedback as the TTS generate
button below that shows the quene state after press"**. Tracked as **WM-48** in `../TODOS.md`. **Client half
only**: no host file changed, no verb was added, and nothing was put on the wire. It goes live on a browser
refresh. The three card answers this implements are on WM-48: the count belongs in the Settings section; the
toggle arms only and the chain starts on the next press of generate; the tag is drawn by the panel from the ids
its own chain dispatched.

1. **The vocabulary, declared once** (`lib/client.js:2127-2138`): `LS_AUTO_GEN_AHEAD794`
   (`deepamp:auto.gen.ahead794`), `AUTO_GEN_AHEAD_OPTS794 = ["1","2","3","4","5"]`,
   `AUTO_GEN_AHEAD_DEFAULT794 = "1"`, `AUTO_GEN_AHEAD_MAX794 = 5`, `AUTO_GEN_FAIL_STOP794 = 3`,
   `AUTO_GEN_GLYPH794 = "\u221E"` (U+221E, a maths sign — this tree carries no emoji), and `autoGenAhead794(v)`
   as the validator: a value off the five is answered with the default, so a stale or hand-edited key cannot put
   a number in the pipeline that the panel will not honour. Numeric options are stored as strings, the way every
   other numeric setting in this panel is stored.
2. **The toggle is on the quick music line, to the left of generate** (`audio-play-autogen794`). The line now
   declares its OWN grid template — `minmax(0,1fr) 26px 78px` — because the row's shared right column
   (`ROW_GRID646`, 78px) is exactly one button wide and the ask was a control to the LEFT of it: splitting 78px
   would have made a 38px "generate" out of an eight-character word, and widening the shared template would have
   moved the import button on the line below. The generate column is unchanged at 78px, the url line below is
   untouched, and the toggle wears the row's own box (`ROW_BTN646`, 18px tall) so the three controls on the line
   are one height. OFF is the plain box; ON is `CLOCK_LIT300`, the lit green edge this panel already uses for
   "this is live". It is deliberately not built by the run-button factory: it queues nothing, and a control that
   queues nothing wearing a run button's frame would claim a queue that does not exist.
3. **Arming is not a trigger.** Pressing the toggle dispatches nothing — measured as zero requests leaving the
   panel. The chain is armed, says so, and says out loud if it would be refused the moment it is seeded (no model
   in the music / sfx form, a form left on something that is not a generation, an empty prompt field). Seeding
   happens on a press of a GENERATION control only: `seeded` is set in `dispatchTask`'s success path for a
   `task_kind gen` press while the chain is armed, and a conversion or separation press does not seed it. A
   chain that stopped is re-seeded by the next generation press, which is what makes "the prompt was empty, then
   I typed one" work without a second switch to press.
4. **The count control is in the Settings section** (`audio-play-autogen-ahead794`): a select of 1..5, 1 marked
   "the default", 5 marked "the most this offers", remembered in this browser, and an out-of-range value is
   refused — measured: `9` and `many` leave the control on what it had and leave the stored key unchanged. Under
   it is a one-line read-out (`audio-play-autogen-state794`) of what the chain is doing, read off the same set
   the pipeline and the playlist tag are drawn from, so the three cannot disagree. Moving the number while a chain
   is armed but not seeded dispatches nothing; while a chain is running it applies to that chain on the same
   press.
5. **What the number means, stated exactly**, because "run ahead" has two readings and only one is built: it is
   the number of AUTO generations outstanding at once, not a total of jobs in the pipeline. A manual press stays
   a manual press. With the count at 2 — the number the operator named for testing load balancing — one press of
   generate is 1 take asked for plus 2 the chain keeps behind it; measured in the suite as 3 `dispatch_task`
   calls, each with the same body. Two outstanding generations is two engines busy, because `max_loaded_models=1`
   per endpoint.
6. **The trigger is a finished take.** `autoGenSettled794(id, good)` stands in all four branches of the
   poll-then-play loop that end a pending job — the `status ok` branch (the one that hands the take to playback,
   the moment the operator named), the error / aborted / cancelled branch, and the two deadline branches ("timed
   out waiting for", "lost track of"). A row the chain did not dispatch returns false and nothing about it
   changes. A good settle clears the failure count; a bad one counts.
7. **One generator, not a second one.** `dispatchTask(autoChain794)` takes one optional argument and it is the
   only difference: the same model the form is on, the same prompt text, the same lane pin, the same options, the
   same `addPending`, the same flash. `autoGenDispatch794` is the only place the chain dispatches, and the
   `auto` pin case still sends no `endpoint_id` key at all, so the body a chain sends is byte-identical to the
   body a press sends.
8. **A measured finding, and the fix it caused.** The chain is triggered from inside the poll loop, and that
   loop's closure belongs to whichever render armed it. The first version of the chain therefore dispatched with
   the prompt the form held when the poller was armed: measured as a replacement carrying "chain prompt words,
   first version" after the field had been changed to "second version". `chainCtx794` (`lib/client.js:18693`) is
   now refreshed on every render with the current generator, the current model of the music / sfx form and the
   current prompt text, and the chain calls and guards through it. Re-measured: the replacement carries the words
   the form holds at the dispatch. This is the same hazard the panel already meets for the pending map and the
   lane pin, and it is met the same way.
9. **The playlist tag** (`audio-play-autogen-tag794`) is the same infinity sign, drawn from
   `props.autoGenIds[j.id]` and only while that row is `queued` or `running` — "until it's finished generating".
   Nothing on the wire carries it and nothing could: the panel knows which jobs it started itself, and that is the
   only authority a tag like this has. Measured: 2 tags while a 2-deep chain runs, 1 after one of its takes
   finishes, 0 on a row a person asked for by hand.
10. **The generate button now shows the queue state.** `runFlashLabel371` and `runFlashAlarm371` were extracted
    out of `runButton371` (its three sites call them, its output is unchanged) and the quick line's generate
    button reads the same lane flash it was already causing: after a press it reads `queued as ap-…` for the same
    1400 ms the run buttons use, and a press that queued nothing reads `not queued` in the alarm red
    (`#f85149` / `#0b0b10`). Measured in both directions, including the label returning to `generate` when the
    window closes.
11. **Where a chain stops, and what off means.** Three auto dispatches refused in a row stop the chain by
    themselves and the panel says which and why; measured as 3 refused replacements and then nothing more, with
    the light going off on its own. A request that was already in flight when the chain stopped counts as
    nothing. A guard failure (empty prompt, a form left on a non-generation) stops it with that reason. Pressing
    the toggle off dispatches nothing and cancels nothing: it names the jobs already out there, those rows keep
    their tag and carry on, and a finished row does not start a replacement from a chain that is off.
12. **Tests.** `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` 1047 → **1060 pass, 0 fail**: a T-794 block of its own with its own mount,
    14 check calls of which **13 run and pass** (the 14th is the fallback that only fires if the mount failed to

    seeing the request body; `jobStatus794`, driving a settle) that stay off for every other block. Two fixture facts

13. **Not built, stated plainly.** "maybe we will get realtime" is not built and nothing in this card claims it:

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-791: the nixie face de-ionises — a departing digit leaves an afterglow, and a rollover sags the supply — client half, live on a browser refresh

The operator's word, verbatim: **"please run an analysis on the nixie flicker effect - i like it - but can we mix in some 'dimming' effects, too - that look more like analog voltage transitions instead of only digital states ?"** (`../TODOS.md` WM-46 item 1), and the card answer to the question put: **"A and C"**. The analysis is WM-46 items 2 to 7; this card is the build it led to, made the same evening. Client half only: `lib/client.js` and `tests/`, no host file, no restart.

1. **What was chosen, and what was not.** A — a de-ionisation afterglow on the departing digit — and C — a shared supply sag at a rollover — were built. **B (an ionisation delay on arrival) was not chosen, so the strike's peak-at-age-0 shape that T-751 rules is untouched**; D (per-tube voltage offsets) was not offered again, because it contradicts the standing ruling that the breath is one factor read once per frame (`lib/client.js:22548`, WM-46 item 5d).
2. **The afterglow** (`NIXIE_AFTERGLOW_MS791 = 420`, `NIXIE_AFTERGLOW_TOP791 = 0.95`, `NIXIE_AFTERGLOW_WIRE791 = 0.85`, `nixieAfterglow791`): a cosine from a standstill to zero over 420 ms at 0.95 of the palette's ghost ink, its wire 0.85 of the struck wire, drawn at the struck plane **before** the struck digit, so the new character sits on top of the one it replaced. The character a tube has just left is not recoverable later — `st684n.cur` is overwritten at the end of every frame — so `st684n.leftCh791` records it on the frame where the change happens. That write is placed deliberately **after** the line `tests/scope.test.cjs` pins, so the pinned line still reads verbatim.
3. **The supply sag** (`NIXIE_SAG_MS791 = 260`, `NIXIE_SAG_DEPTH791 = 0.86`, `NIXIE_SAG_TUBES791 = 2`, `nixieSag791`): `max(FLOOR, b − (b − FLOOR) · 0.86 · sin²(π · age / 260))`, armed only when **two or more tubes change in one frame**, and folded into the frame's single `breath690` before any ink is mixed — which is what "the same factor for every struck tube" means, and what the 2026-11-06 ruling requires. To count the rollover before the ink, the breath-and-ink block was moved from before `var txt684` to after the `st684n` init; the frame still takes **one** `Date.now()`, and a check counts it — with `//…` comments stripped first, because a clock read named in a comment is not a clock read.
4. **Both windows were designed against the slowest setting the panel offers, not the fastest.** `SCOPE_FPS_OPTS537 = [60, 30, 20, 12]` means the slowest frame gap a person can choose is 83.33 ms: 420 ms is 5.04 frames there and 260 ms is 3.12. A transition under about 120 ms is invisible at that setting, and the existing 110 ms strike fall is already 1.32 frames there.
5. **What did not change, stated because each of these was an option on the table:** the unstruck field is still fixed — the glass, the mesh, the foot ring, the stacked planes and the separator keep the palette's ink unchanged (the ruling of 2026-11-06, "a tube that is powered does not dim its envelope with its filament"); no new face word, so none of the six positional pins a new word moves were touched; no `globalAlpha`, no gradient, no `shadowBlur`, no `Math.random`; `clock_nixie` and `clock_nixie_green` share the drawing, so both wear this.
6. **Measured off the drawings** (`tests/scope.test.cjs`, one 200×80 fixture, frames at 500 / 1000 / 1130 / 1400 / 1700 ms after a change): the residual's alpha runs **0 / 210 / 140 / 1 / 0** and its wire is **3 px** against the stacked planes at 1 and 1.4; the struck wire runs **223 / 221 / 189 / 220 / 220**, so the sag is visible in the struck digit as well at 1 130 ms — a de-ionising grid is fed by the same supply as the frame, and the check says so rather than expecting a separate one. The warm-up frame carries two residuals, which is the fixture's own change frame, not an accident.
7. **Three assertions failed on the first run and all three were mine, not the client's.** I expected the residual against the unsagged breath when the drawing correctly used the frame's sagged supply; my regex counted a `Date.now()` sitting inside a comment; and I claimed the residual's wire is narrower than the struck wire, which at this fixture is false because `round(3 × 0.85) = 3`. Each was re-expressed against what is actually measurable — a shared `supply791()` helper, comment-stripping before the count, and the exact ruled rounding plus `min(ghostWidths) > max(stackWidths)` — and no assertion was dropped.
8. **One mechanic worth recording anywhere this face is measured:** `scopeClockText677` reads the drawn clock through `new Date()`, not `Date.now()`. A test that moves the *drawn* clock has to stub the Date constructor; `Date.now()` on its own moves only the ages of the breath, the strike and the sag.
9. **Copies.** `scratch/client.js.bak_20261111_pre_T791_analog_transitions` (2 191 198 B) before the client edit and `tests/scope.test.cjs.bak_20261111_pre_T791_analog_block` before the block was spliced. The analysis that led here is re-runnable: `scratch/nixie_flicker_analysis_20261111.cjs`.
10. **Tests.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` **455 → 463 assertions, 0 fail** — eight new checks: the two curves' shape and bounds, the frame-gap floor read off the panel's own fps list, the residual's presence and its decay to nothing, the exact alpha and wire against the frame's own supply, the drawn order (residual before struck digit), the one-clock-read rule, and the rollover arming at two tubes.
11. **Status.** BUILT, client half. One browser refresh of the operator's panel carries it; no harness restart is owed. The operator's eye on strength and taste is the open half — this is a look, and a measurement cannot close it.

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-792: the waveform's sliding window is halved, and a quarter-length one is offered — client half, live on a browser refresh

The operator's word, verbatim: **"the waveform sliding is way too slow, shorten the window: half the current size, AND offer option 'sliding2' with a quater of current window size"** (`../TODOS.md` WM-47 item 1). It names the window this file's T-788 shipped the same day at twelve seconds. Client half only; no host file, no restart.

1. **The base stays in the file and the ruling is a fraction.** `SCOPE_WAVE_WINDOW_MS788 = 12000` is unchanged and `SCOPE_WAVE_WINDOW_FRACTIONS792 = { sliding: 2, sliding2: 4 }` says what each word takes of it: **6 s and 3 s**. The base is kept named because a fraction of a number nobody wrote down is not a decision a later session can check, and because the comment beside it now carries the operator's verdict on the original size in the operator's own words, one day after it shipped.
2. **One place decides a width.** `scopeWaveWindowMs792(word)` is the only reader of that table, and `scopeWaveIsWindow792(word)` replaced the two `=== "sliding"` tests at the painter branches — so adding a third word needed no branch edit, and the cycle handler never needed one at all: it walks the ring by the list's own length. The short-take floor (a window never exceeds the take, and never goes under 2 000 ms unless the take is shorter) is untouched.
3. **The default did not move.** `SCOPE_WAVE_VIEW_DEFAULT788` is still `sliding`, and a panel that was never pressed still draws the window and stores nothing. That half of the earlier ruling ("make the sliding window the default") is re-measured here rather than assumed, because adding a word to a list is exactly the kind of edit that quietly moves a default.
4. **The hover reads the same function the painter reads.** The sentences on the control are built from `scopeWaveWindowMs792("sliding") / 1000` and `… ("sliding2") / 1000`, so a later card that moves a window cannot leave the hover describing the old one.
5. **Measured as the width the drawing reports, not as the constant claims.** The fixture plants spikes at 20 s, 26 s and 28.5 s in a 60 s take that is otherwise quiet and plays it at 30 s; a window of W ending at the position being heard puts a spike at t at fraction (t − (30 − W)) / W along the bars, so W comes back out of where a spike lands. Readings: **5.97 s and 6.00 s** for `sliding` from two independent spikes, **2.97 s** for `sliding2` from the 28.5 s spike. The 20 s spike — inside a twelve-second window at that position — is drawn nowhere now; the half window still shows the 26 s spike and the quarter window does not; the same take drawn whole shows all three, which is the control that says the fixture is doing the work. Tall-bar runs per word: **2 / 1 / 3** for sliding / sliding2 / full, over 67 bars in each frame.
6. **What makes a window move is untouched by its width.** In both windows the play head sits at the right edge of the bars — measured at 199 against a bar row ending at 200 — so shortening the window did not move the head off the position a person is hearing.
7. **Five pins of T-788 were re-cut, none dropped**, each with a dated note quoting the operator: the option-list literal (two words → three), the control-cycle walk (now followed all the way round a three-word ring, with the store read after each press), the claim that named "the twelve seconds that end at the position being heard" (re-expressed as six, and re-stated as a claim about *which part of the take* the bars came from, which reads the same at either width), the T-536 branch pin, and the fixture comment about what a 60 s take is for.
8. **A fixture mechanic, named so it is not mistaken for design:** `mountWave788` presses the mode's own view box a full ring before measuring, and a ring is three words now, so that is three presses with the measurement starting at the last. The untouched-panel check reads the store **before** any press — "a panel that was never touched stores nothing" is only a measurement if it is taken before the presses write a word.
9. **No pre-change copy was taken before this client edit.** The only client copy in `scratch/` (`client.js.bak_20261111_pre_T791_analog_transitions`) predates T-791, so it is not the state this card started from. Stated rather than papered over; nothing was rebuilt from a backup.
10. **Tests.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` **463 → 469 assertions, 0 fail** — six new checks: the fractions table and the preserved base, the two drawn widths, the presence-and-absence pattern against the size this feature was built at, the default and a stored `sliding2`, the hover's numbers, and the play head at both widths.
11. **Status.** BUILT, client half; live on a browser refresh. 6 s and 3 s are numbers; whether either is the right speed is the operator's judgement on a refreshed panel, and that is the open half.

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-793: the spectrum's colour row gets the ramps the panel already has — six words, and no new ramp written — client half, live on a browser refresh

The operator's word, verbatim: **"hmm, now the spectrum analyser only has two color settings: i expected more"** (`../TODOS.md` WM-47 item 2), and the card answer to the question put: **"Give it the ramps the panel already has"**. Client half only; no host file, no restart.

1. **Why it was two, and why a longer list was not simply an edit.** The list is two because this file's T-789 took `flames` and `flame_body` out of *this mode* at the operator's own word the same day. Deeper than that: `scopeBar300` — the bargraph painter this mode is the only caller of — knew one ramp (the green / yellow / red ladder) plus a special case for the flame ramp and a special case for the flame-body *shape*. Any other word painted the ladder whatever it was called, so adding a word to a cycle box without changing the painter buys a switch that does nothing. That is the answer the operator's observation was really asking for, and it was given before anything was built.
2. **The vocabulary, appended.** `SCOPE_SCHEME_OPTS_BY_MODE539.spectrum` is now `["green", "fireplace", "white", "flames", "ironbow", "cold"]`. Nothing was inserted ahead of `green`: the default stays the first word and the picture of a panel that has never been pressed is the bargraph it has always drawn.
3. **The painter now resolves a named ramp** through `SCOPE_WF_RAMPS541` and `scopeRampColour541` — the same table and the same function the waterfall, the llama, the waveform (`scopeWaveColour788`) and the knight bars (`scopeKnightColour601`) read. **No new ramp and no new colour constant were written.** Two words are held out of that lookup on purpose: `green`, because the continuous green ramp belongs to the modes that draw a wall of brightness and this mode's default is the banded ladder its pins, its hover and its operator all describe; and `white`, which is flat on purpose — on a bargraph the *height* is the loudness, so a flat bar still answers "how loud was that", which is the same reasoning the waveform's `white` carries. The `flames` special case that used to sit in that expression is gone, because the table's own `flames` entry is the same stops through the same function: measured below, byte-identical.
4. **The hovers are per-mode sentences in this mode's own table**, each saying where the colour comes from ON A BAR — at each segment's own height, from the foot up — and what stays stable against it. The shared fallback talks about rows of a wall, which is not what this mode draws.
5. **Measured as the colour of every segment, against the ramp, from the geometry of the drawing.** Each bar's baseline is the bottom edge of its own lowest segment, so a segment's height is read out of the picture rather than assumed from the source: a rect at (y, h) on a bar whose base is B sits at (B − y − h + SEGMENT_H) / B of a full bar. The claim is exact equality with the ramp value at that height. **168 bar segments per ramp word, zero disagreements**; bar baseline 56 px, the tallest bar 15 segments reaching **0.98** of itself, 15 distinct colours in a frame and **15 in one bar where the banded ladder could carry at most three**. No ladder colour appears anywhere in any ramp frame.
6. **The default is intact, and so is the marker.** Under the untouched word the frame carries only the three ladder colours plus the flat peak-hold cap, in the bands the thresholds define; the cap is drawn under every word that is not the fire word and still absent under the fire word, which is T-789's ruling about that word and not about these.
7. **Six words answer six different pictures:** no two of them draw the same set of colours, each mount shows the word it was asked for, and the box names the word it is on and every word of its cycle in its own hover.
8. **Five pins were re-cut, none dropped**, each with a dated note: the T-789 vocabulary literal (two words → six, with the default and every fireplace constant still pinned), the T-600 colour walk (six presses, followed round the whole ring), the T-600 stored-value pin, the T-600 hover pin, and the comment beside a T-600 mount that said `flames` is refused by this mode's validator — it is not, and what that mount measures (a bar count, not a colour) is unchanged by the trip.
9. **Fixture seams this opened, named so a later session does not mistake them for design:** `b.audioCtx` and `b.anMaxDb` in the suite's mock browser, and an optional second argument on `mountSpec789`. The mock's analyser window tops at −30 dB while the panel maps a bar over −70 dB to 0 dB (`SCOPE_FLOOR_DB300`, `SCOPE_TOP_DB300`), so a byte at 255 reached 0.57 of a bar and **no bar this suite ever drew had reached its tip** — no claim about the top of a ramp was measurable. The defaults are unchanged for every other mount in the file.
10. **No pre-change copy was taken before this client edit**, and the test file's copy predates T-791. Stated for the same reason as T-792 item 9: a copy that does not describe the state a change started from is worse than no copy.
11. **Tests.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` **469 → 477 assertions, 0 fail** — eight checks: the painter's resolution path and what is held out of it; the default's three bands; the flat word; the three ramps measured segment by segment; the six distinct pictures and their hovers; the cap rule.
12. **What stays off this mode, and the one thing that does not.** The per-line dynamic schemes (`auto1`, `auto2`, `rand`, `rand2`, `drift`, `beat_ring`) map a hue to a place in a history, and a spectrum is one instant with no history — that is why they were not offered. **`auto3` maps a hue along a frame's frequency axis, and this mode's bars *are* that axis**: it is the one dynamic scheme this mode could carry, it was not built, and it is the open question if the operator wants a seventh word. Status: BUILT, client half, live on a browser refresh.

1. **What was off, read out of the file rather than from the eye.** The panel's header word carried `fontFamily:
   "monospace"` with `letterSpacing: "0.14em"` at weight 700, size 12px. The batch editor's header word carried the same
   size and the same weight and **no font family and no tracking** — two windows naming the same piece of software, drawn
   as if they were two products. Its corner was further off: a 16×16 text glyph (U+25D9) at 55% opacity, where the panel
   draws an 18×18 corner bracket with a faint diagonal hatch.
2. **The look is stated once each, twice in the file: `PANEL_TITLE_LOOK790` and `PANEL_RESIZE_GRIP790`**, declared beside
   the shared style rules the file already keeps (`ROW_BTN334`) and taken at both windows through `Object.assign`. That is
   the difference between "I made these two look alike today" and a file that cannot drift: the values exist in one place
   and both windows read them.
3. **What is shared is the look, not the name.** The editor header word wears **no class**. `audio-play-title` stays the
   panel's own header and the only element wearing it, because `render`, `ui_state`, `shut` and `transparency` find the
   panel header by that class — a second element in that class would make four suites read the wrong element. Stated
   because it looks like the obvious simplification and is not one.

   look values it has always carried; its corner keeps the same 18×18 grab area, the same bracket colours, the same hatch
   and the same `onCornerResizeDown` drag math. The new pins assert that, so a later edit that moves the panel's look has
   to be a decision and not a side effect.
5. **The editor corner still resizes the editor.** Its class `audio-play-editor-resize462` and its handler
   `editorPress462("resize", …)` are untouched, and its remembered geometry and band rules are untouched. Only what a
   person sees and presses is shared now. The window's own words — "batch editor", lower case — were not changed either:
   the ask was about the font's style and size, not about the wording.

   them reading the rendered tree and not the source: the four look values of both header words compared element to

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-788: the waveform has one reading, a sliding window as its default view, and the panel's global colour vocabulary

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "remove option to switch between amp and dB - fix to amp in the background, and replace the
   option to switch between static view (as we have for files filling canvas with full file waveform) - with a 'dynamic
   sliding window' what we currently already have for stream display - where the waveform is moving, - and make the
   sliding window the default. also add/replace the color profiles with the global ones we already have for danicng
   llama, etc (including random, auto, etc)". Card answer to the one question put: **"Keep it, sliding window default"**
   — the whole-file picture stays available, the window becomes what the mode shows when nobody has pressed anything.
   Record: `../TODOS.md` WM-44.
2. **The amp/dB switch is gone from that row.** `SCOPE_LEVEL_OPTS346.static` is one word now — `{ words: ["amp"],
   def: "amp" }` — so the waveform row prints no reading word and owns no level box; its cell is empty. **The dB code
   was not deleted** (the T-500 pattern: keep the code, pin the config): both `scopeStaticFrame300` and
   `scopeLiveScrollFrame309` still carry their `!== "dB"` branch, and a new pin asserts both branches are still in the
   file with the table pinned from the source text. The stream row keeps its two-word level box untouched.
3. **A second setting for the mode, built the way that mode's other second setting is built** (the Knight Rider bars'
   form): `LS_SCOPE_WAVE_VIEW788` browser key, `SCOPE_WAVE_VIEW_OPTS788 = ["sliding", "full"]`, default `sliding`,
   `scopeWaveView788()` validator (an unknown stored word falls back, like every other one), `cycleScopeWaveView788()`
   with `lsSet` + `scopeRepaint307()` when that mode is on screen, and a cycle box in the cell the level box vacated.
   Window length `SCOPE_WAVE_WINDOW_MS788 = 12000`, floor 2000, and never longer than the take.
4. **`scopeWaveWindowFrame788(g, W, barH, pk)` is the new painter.** It draws the `min(winMs, durMs)` seconds that END
   at the position being heard: `right = pos * durMs`, `left = right - winMs`, each bar aggregates the peaks that cover
   its slice, amp-only heights, and the play head at the RIGHT EDGE — the moment being heard is the edge, which is what
   makes the picture move. A take with no length falls back to `scopeStaticFrame300` in the first line. The dispatcher
   picks between the two painters in both places the static mode is entered (a take, and a station tap's file arm); a
   station's live picture still draws `scopeLiveScrollFrame309` whatever the view says.
5. **It is fed from the lane's own peaks read, not from an analyser** — `scopePeaks300.current`, the same source the
   whole-file picture uses. `createMediaElementSource` is still never used anywhere in this file: a take has no tap, and
   that is the standing safety rule of this feature, not an oversight. Pinned as a drawing measurement, not as a grep.
6. **The global colour vocabulary now reaches the waveform row**: `SCOPE_SCHEME_OPTS_BY_MODE539.static` is
   `white, green, flames, ironbow, cold, auto1, auto2, rand, rand2, drift, beat_ring` — the word that names today's
   look first, every other word appended after it (the rule learned the day a word was inserted mid-list and five
   cycle-walk pins failed over a shifted press count). `auto3` is not offered, for the reason already written in that
   table for the bars: its axis is a frame's FREQUENCY axis and a time-ordered bar has no frequency position. The
   default stays `white`.
7. **`scopeWaveColour788(scheme, atMs, frac, env)` is the colour rule this asked for**: a bar's colour is a function of
   WHEN IN THE AUDIO that bar sits, never of the screen column or of the frame drawing it. Flat words read
   `SCOPE_WF_RAMPS541` as before; the dynamic words take their hue from audio time through `scopeDynColour587`, so a
   hue travels left with the bar it belongs to instead of sliding across the bar. `scopeWaveEnv788` builds one envelope
   pass per peaks read (level, mean, accent, beat marks) and caches it by `job:n:durS`; `scopeWaveEnvLive788` does the
   same for the stream buffer, which now carries a `ms` array written and shifted with `Date.now()`. Constants:
   `SCOPE_WAVE_WHEEL_STEP_MS788 = 200`, `SCOPE_WAVE_RAND_STEP_MS788 = 120`, `SCOPE_WAVE_ENV_SPAN788 = 40`,
   `SCOPE_WAVE_BEAT_GAP_MS788 = 250`.
8. **Measured, on a 60 s fixture with a loud first half and a quiet second half** (240 peak buckets, `duration_s: 60`,
   heard at 30 s and at 57 s): the window at the middle carries **47 bars of the loud half out of 67** while the
   whole-file picture at the same position carries **25**; moved to 95 % the window has **zero** bars reaching the loud
   half's height and its tallest is 5.14 px against 17.56 px, while the whole-file picture at 95 % is **bar for bar the
   picture at the middle** (25 tall, identical max and min) — which is the difference between a window and a file. The
   play head sits at x=199 against a bar edge of 200 in the window at both positions, and at 100 / 190 in the whole-file
   picture at 30 s / 57 s.
9. **How those were measured, because the first attempts were wrong and the corrections are the useful part:** the
   position has to be set on the element `armAudio` hands back — the one the transport controls, not the first
   `<audio>` in a tree that mounts fifteen of them — and `ontimeupdate()` then `commit()` is what makes the panel's own
   repaint use it (`scopePosRef331` is read from `controlEl395()` at paint time). A drawing after the position is forced
   by two presses of the mode's own view box, which land back on the word being measured. And the log's translate offset
   is what keeps the dot-matrix clock, the canvas frame lines and a playlist row's own little waveform out of a
   measurement of the strip.
10. **Tests:** `tests/scope.test.cjs` **442 pass / 0 fail → 455 pass / 0 fail**, 14 new checks in this card's block and
    T-789's, and **no assertion deleted or weakened**: 8 older pins carry a `RE-POINTED AGAIN 2026-11-11 by T-788`
    note quoting the operator (the T-506b cell counts, the T-536 source anchors, the T-541/T-599 control counts), one
    carries a note on why its anchor moved — the static mode now has TWO arms opening with `if (m === "static") {`, so
    the anchor is the comment only the tap arm has. The T-540 `flames` hover claim was re-worded to match what the ramp
    actually does (continuous, not banded) rather than relaxed.
11. **Copies:** **no copy of `lib/client.js` was taken before the first edit of this card — stated plainly, per the
    rule.** The nearest copy on disk, `scratch/client.js.bak_20261111_pre_station_audio` (2 144 041 B), predates T-786
    and so is not a pre-T-788 copy. A mid-card copy was taken instead: `scratch/client.js.bak_20261111_mid_T788_colour_view_constants`
    (2 169 627 B), which holds the colour machinery and the view constants but not the window painter. Run logs:
    `scratch/scope_after_T788_T789_{a..x}.log`.
12. **State: BUILT.** Client half only (`lib/client.js`); no host change, no restart. Goes live on a browser refresh,
    which now also carries T-786's client half. `lib/client.js` 28 191 lines / 2 188 588 B, `node --check` clean.


## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-789: the spectrum row keeps one fire word, gains an LED-resolution setting, and its fireplace gets an afterglow and sparks on the rise

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "the spectrum analyser should get a first setting switch option aswell to adjust the
   amount/resolution of LEDs we display - add some lower res settings , and the 2nd option: remove 'flame-body option'
   and maybe 'optimise' the fire option with some longer lasting afterglow and rising sparks on peaks to look more like
   a fireplace". Card answer to the one question put: **"Keep fireplace, improve it"** — `flame_body` and the plain
   `flames` ramp both leave this row's list, and the word that stays is the one that already reads as a fireplace.
   Record: `../TODOS.md` WM-44.
2. **The vocabulary got shorter, in this row only:** `SCOPE_SCHEME_OPTS_BY_MODE539.spectrum = ["green", "fireplace"]`
   (was `green, flames, flame_body`). `flames` is still the second word on the waterfall, the llama and the knight bars
   and `scopeBar300` still answers any palette it is given; only this mode's list moved, which is what a press cycles
   and what a stored value is checked against — a stored `flame_body` here now fails this row's validator and falls back
   to the default, the way a stored unknown word always has. No default moved on any other mode (static `white`,
   waterfall `green`, llama `auto1` — pinned). The eight T-600 shape and cycle pins were re-cut onto the word that
   stays, each labelled `re-cut by T-789` with the operator's words on it; one of them is kept as the proof that the
   validator refuses the word that left.
3. **The LED-resolution setting, same form as the mode's other second setting:** `LS_SCOPE_SPECTRUM_LEDS789`,
   `SCOPE_SPECTRUM_LEDS_OPTS789 = ["auto", "5", "8", "12", "16"]`, default `auto`, `scopeSpectrumLeds789()` validator,
   `cycleScopeSpectrumLeds789()`, one cycle box in the cell the level word vacated. It is a **ceiling, never a floor**:
   `nbOut334 = Math.min(nb, capS789)` with `capS789 = (want === "auto") ? fit : Math.min(fit, want)`. `SCOPE_BANDS300
   = 20` — the number of bands the analyser is read at — is untouched by it, and the peak cap stays where it was.
4. **A crash this card's own pins found, and the fix that was not a relaxed test:** forcing 5 drew
   `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')` through `cycleScopeSpectrumLeds789 → scopeRepaint307 →
   scopePaint300`. Cause, read off the code: the group step `grp334 = ceil(nb / nbOut)` overshoots — with 12 bands and
   5 bars, bar 4 asks for `bands[12]`, which does not exist. Replaced with **proportional group ranges**
   (`gi0 = floor(b * nb / nbOut)`, `gi1 = floor((b + 1) * nb / nbOut) - 1`, both clamped), so every bar owns a real
   slice of the band map and the ranges tile it without a gap or an overlap.
5. **Measured as geometry, because a bar's width is the layout said out loud** (`bw = (196 - (n-1)·gap) / n` over the
   196 px the inset leaves inside the 200 px canvas): `auto` draws 20 bars 8.85 px wide — the layout this mode has
   always had — and 16 / 12 / 8 / 5 draw 11.31 / 15.42 / 23.63 / 38.4 px, each within 0.02 px of what its own word
   implies, in strict order, nothing wider than the five-bar layout. How many of the laid-out bars carry a reading is
   the mock analyser's answer and it is not equal from mount to mount, so it is pinned as a bound and not as an
   equality: a bar with no reading in it draws nothing, which is the rule this strip has always had.
6. **The fireplace, improved rather than replaced:** `FIREPLACE_DECAY600 0.86 → 0.94` (the afterglow asked for),
   `FIREPLACE_PLUME600 0.45 → 0.60`, `FIREPLACE_ALPHA_MIN600 0.10 → 0.06`, `FIREPLACE_TRAIL_FLOOR600 0.35 → 0.45`;
   the old values are named in the comments as `was 0.86` / `was 0.45`. `scopeFireplace600` was restructured so the
   plume block and the spark block are reached on the same pass instead of one excluding the other.
7. **The sparks:** a spark is born only on a **reading that rises** — `frac > prev + FIREPLACE_SPARK_RISE600 (0.04)`
   and `frac >= FIREPLACE_SPARK_MIN_FRAC600 (0.30)` — at most `FIREPLACE_SPARK_MAX600 = 4` per bar, drawn last through
   `scopeFlameAlpha600(scopeFlameColour540(heat), heat)`, rising by `FIREPLACE_SPARK_RISE600` per frame, cooling at
   `FIREPLACE_SPARK_COOL600 = 0.955`, 2 px, drifting sideways with the same `flameRowWobble600` the flame body uses.
   Measured: a level held low across frames throws none, the same bar pushed to the top throws them, and held steady
   afterwards the count does not grow — the sparks already up finish their own fall.
8. **The peak cap is deliberately not painted under this word** (`if (hp > 0 && pal600i !== "fireplace")`): a cap is a
   flat line and a fire has no flat line in it. That was already the behaviour; now it is pinned.
9. **The T-600 shape measurement had to be split, not weakened:** under a fire word one column now carries two
   paintings — the BODY at full opacity (`rgb(`) and the PLUME and sparks through an alpha (`rgba(`) — and grouping
   them together made the shape pins report 20 bar groups and a 22.62 px top difference. The reader now separates body
   rows from plume rows by the fill style and drops the 2 px sparks by size, which is what lets the original claims
   (twelve bars, continuous body, tapering, centred, flickering) all pass unchanged against the improved fire.
10. **Tests:** the same run as T-788 — **455 pass / 0 fail** in `tests/scope.test.cjs`, and the earlier stages of this
    card's work are in the same log chain (`scope_after_T788_T789_d.log` at 442 / 0 was the green point before the new
    pins were added, `_e` through `_w` are the failures the new pins found and what each one took to fix). Full 26-suite
    run after this card: `scratch/suite_full_20261111e.log`.
11. **Hover text follows the words that exist:** the spectrum row's tip now reads "press to cycle green, fireplace" and
    carries no `flame_body` sentence; the `flames` tip that stays on the other modes was re-worded to describe what the
    ramp does. `tests/tooltips.test.cjs` prints its hover-length measure over the whole panel and this card moved no
    hover into a wall of text.
12. **State: BUILT.** Client half only; goes live on a browser refresh. Same copy note as T-788 item 11 — no
    pre-change copy of `lib/client.js` was taken for this card either, and the mid-card copy is named there.

   few weeks ago - please take another look". That look found the existing channel: `station_title` already dumps every
   response header of the station with `curl -D -` and kept three keys. The ruling on the shape: **"Let the read follow
   the station being played."**

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-784: two test fixtures were given a clock of their own

1. **What was flaking:** two assertions failed once, by one millisecond each, while the machine was busy running all
   26 suites, and passed on a quiet re-run. `T-774 (a)` asked for a generation time of at least 400 ms against a mocked
   400 ms render window: the window measured exactly 400, the model-load part measured 1 ms, and the arithmetic the card
   names produced 399. The `tests/scope.test.cjs` Nixie case asked that every struck tube in one frame carry the same
   breath factor: the client reads the clock once per frame, but the window the suite measures can span **two** frames,
   and two frames are two different milliseconds.
2. **The ruling, verbatim:** the operator was asked how time-boundary flakes should be handled and chose **"Make the
   fixture deterministic"** over recording them, widening a boundary, or avoiding runs under load.
3. **The host half:** the mock gained an opt-in `virtualHoldMs` beside the existing `speechHoldMs` seam — the same hold,
   declared as milliseconds on the fixture's own clock instead of a real sleep — and the T-774 fixture is given a clock
   that moves by exactly the window it declares, once, when the render answers, and is restored to the real clock at the
   end of that sub-block (the pattern the suite already used since T-590). **The assertion was not touched and not
   loosened**: it still asks for at least 400 ms. What changed is that the number it compares against is declared by the
   fixture rather than sampled from wall time.
4. **The client half:** the Nixie frame is now painted with `Date.now` held at one constant instant — 23:45 local, so all
   four tubes are struck, and the breath it computes is mid-band at 0.903 of full strength. A constant, not a value read
   at run time: the same frame is drawn on every run, and the ruled band measures the curve instead of which millisecond
   the run happened to land in. The client's own one-read-per-frame rule is untouched; the frame the suite hands it changed.
5. **Measured:** `tests/scope.test.cjs` **441 pass, 0 fail, RC=0 — the same count as before the change** (nothing added,
   nothing removed), and `tests/host.test.cjs` **2 417 pass, 0 fail, RC=0 — the same count as before the change**, both in
   one sequential run on a machine that had just finished all 26 suites (`scratch/flake_determinism_20261111.log`).
6. **What this does NOT claim:** it does not prove the plugin's timing is right under load — it proves the assertions
   measure what they name. A virtual clock for the whole suite is the deeper version of this and is **not** built here;
   it is named as the option, not done.
7. **State: BUILT — test-side only.** No `lib/`, no `lib/client.js`, no restart; a green full run was already on record
   for the three host cards (T-781, T-782, T-783) and is re-run as usual after this. **No pre-change copy of either test
   file was taken before these edits** — the nearest earlier copy is
   `scratch/host.test.cjs.bak_20261111_pre_capability_reader_assertions`, which predates T-781 and is therefore not the
   state this change started from; it is named rather than a copy being rebuilt after the fact.

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-783: an empty transcript now names the ratio it was given, on the row

1. **What was already right:** the empty-answer verdict is one function both transcription lanes share, it turns the take
   into `error`, it names the model and the slot, and it writes its own perf event carrying the feed shape. That has been
   true since the 2026-10-26 canary_asr measurement. What the operator asked for is the half the row did not carry: the
   shape the engine was actually fed, named where the row is read — the ruling is "16- 7c yes" on `../TODOS.md` WM-42.
2. **What the row now says, in words:** `… returned an empty answer (no words, no turns) — it was fed as resample 16000 Hz
   mono; this take is recorded as a failure, not as silence`. When a lane forced the shape rather than the Settings, the
   sentence says that too. An empty answer with no ratio beside it reads as "this model heard nothing"; with the ratio it
   reads as what it is.
3. **What the row now carries, as data:** `empty_answer { lane, feed_mode, feed_rate, feed_channels, feed_forced,
   feed_declared, source_rate, source_channels }`, added to the row serializer beside the resample keys — written only
   when the verdict wrote one, like every other key in that list, so a normal row gains no new keys.
4. **The verdict itself is unchanged:** one function, one definition, still sets `status:'error'`, still never overwrites
   an aborted row, still writes the same perf event. The perf event and the row were asserted to agree field for field,
   because two accounts of one failure that can drift is how this lane got into trouble before.
5. **Assertions:** 5 new (the field on the row; the words on the row; the perf event and the row agreeing; a take that
   produced words carrying no such field and closing `ok`; and the contract that the note lives inside the one shared
   verdict). Nothing deleted, nothing weakened — the four T-658 assertions that already cover this verdict passed
   unchanged. `tests/host.test.cjs` **2 412 → 2 417 pass, 0 fail, RC=0** (`scratch/host_after_empty_answer_row_c.log`).
6. **Found on the way, and it is the reason this card is short:** the first version wrote the field on the in-memory job
   and it did not appear on the row read back — the row serializer is a whitelist, and a key it does not name is never
   carried. The fix is the whitelist entry above, not a second copy of the data.
7. **State: BUILT — host half.** This is the third of the three host fixes the operator batched; all three go live on the
   same harness restart and none of them is verified against a live engine before it. **No separate pre-change copy of
   `lib/index.js` was taken for this card**; the copy named on T-782 (`scratch/index.js.bak_20261111_pre_model_record_voice_modes`)
   predates this change as well, and it is named rather than a new one being rebuilt after the fact.

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-782: a model's own published record now speaks about that model

1. **What was wrong:** `voice_modes` decided a model's modes from its **family** record. For `qwen3-customvoice` that
   meant "clone required, no built-in voice, no preset_speaker", while the engine's own record for that same model names a
   speaker list and says in its own words: *"Named preset speaker from the CustomVoice checkpoint. Legacy speaker remains
   accepted."* Two answers about one model disagreed, and the one agents are told to read first was the one that did not
   ask the engine about that model. The reading is `../TODOS.md` WM-42 item 9 and item 23.
2. **What changed:** `capVoiceModesOf(info, fam, modelRecord)` takes the model's own record, and all three model-level
   call sites hand it one — the voice-verbs leg, the family-only leg (through the member it already resolved to), and the
   dispatch bar's `capGateVerdict`. `gateModelRecord782` reads it **off the capability cache the read verb already
   filled**: no page read is added, and a cold cache answers null, which is the same UNKNOWN the bar already treats as no
   basis for a refusal.
3. **What the answer now carries:** `model_declaration { model, names, names_total, default_voice, declared_none, source }`
   and, when a model declares none while its family lists some, `model_none_reason`. The family's list and this model's
   list are stated side by side instead of the family's being substituted for the model's.
4. **The rule written into the code:** a model that names its own speakers is a preset_speaker model whatever its family
   lists; a model whose own list is **empty** is not offered the family's names and the answer says so — an empty list is
   a declaration, matching the rule the model-table scan already follows; a model whose record says nothing about voices
   carries **no** declaration and the answer stays permissive.
5. **What did NOT change:** what a dispatch is refused. The plugin's own `clone_required` gate is untouched, and no mode
   was added to the vocabulary. This is about what the answer says, not about what a job may do — said plainly because
   the two are easy to confuse in this lane.
6. **Assertions:** 5 new (the declaration named for the model that declares; the empty declaration taking preset_speaker
   out and saying why; two models of one family answered differently; nothing invented where the engine said nothing; and
   three `voice_modes` calls costing zero extra page reads). Nothing deleted, nothing weakened. `tests/host.test.cjs`
   **2 407 → 2 412 pass, 0 fail, RC=0** (`scratch/host_after_voice_model_record_f.log`).
7. **One measured detail found on the way:** the fixture for this block first came in at ~1 950 bytes and was refused by
   the page floor as "too small to be a real engine page" — which is the T-781 floor behaving exactly as designed, and a
   useful proof that the floor is real. The fixture was padded, not the floor lowered again.

## Built 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-781: the capability reader now reads the parameter table the engine actually serves

1. **What was wrong, measured:** the capability reader asked the engine's index page. On the updated fleet that page is
   the engine's own browser UI — `<!doctype html>`, 2 342 439 bytes — and the reader parsed **0 families** out of it. A
   record that parses nothing is UNKNOWN, and an UNKNOWN record keeps the bar permissive: since the fleet moved to
   `44ec8089` the bar has been refusing nothing. The reading that found this is `../TODOS.md` WM-42 item 8; the word on
   it was WM-42 item 17, "17 investigate and fix".
2. **What it asks now:** `CAP_PAGE_PATH` (`lib/index.js:7693`) names the path the voice-params read already used —
   `/v1/models?include_params=1&include_session_options=1`. Measured on cpu1 at `44ec8089`: **121 864 bytes for 60
   model records**, each carrying `id / family / task / params[]`, the parameters under `params` as
   `{name,type,required,default,values,description}`. There is no `model_params` key and no sample-rate descriptor.
3. **New shape, old scan kept:** `capParseModelParamsArray` recognises that JSON and groups it by the engine's own
   `family` field into the same family-params record the bar consumes; `capRecordFromModelParams` builds the record,
   with `sections.specs` left stated as `unknown` because this path names no model spec. `capBuildRecord` tries the
   recognised shape first and falls through to `capFindParamMap` for any page that is not that JSON — the captured
   fixture page still parses through it (126 families), which is asserted.
4. **Two things the index page could not give:** a model's own `task`, and a model's own speaker list, read from the
   `values` array of that model's own `voice_id` parameter. An empty list is a declaration (`declared_empty`), matching
   the rule the model-table scan already follows, and the entry shape is the one that scan has always produced
   (`voices / default_voice / family / task / declared_empty`) so every reader of it gets the same thing either way.
5. **The page floor moved, with its reason written next to it:** `CAP_MIN_PAGE_BYTES` 100 000 → **2 048**. The old value
   was written against a 1 672 292-byte UI page ("clears this by 16x"); a parameter table scales with how many models an
   engine serves, and a 100 000-byte floor would call a small engine's real table "not a real engine page" — a false
   refusal. The truncation guard (bytes read against bytes curl reported) is unchanged and still runs first.
6. **Assertions:** 8 new (the record, the grouping, the dropped records counted not swallowed, the per-model speaker
   list, the union and the dedup, the values carried through the projection, an empty table not being a record, and the
   order the two shapes are tried in). **Nothing was deleted or weakened.** 6 existing pins were re-expressed with dated
   notes because they named the old URL or the old floor: two `CAP_PAGE_PATH` literals, the "EXACTLY ONE vanilla
   request" command shape, the `?id=e-1` curl target, the two T-252 command-shape and floor pins. The T-614 helper that
   counts engine parameter reads is narrowed to that read's own signature (`-m 15`) because the capability reader now
   asks the same path with its own (`-m 10`).
7. **Measured run:** `tests/host.test.cjs` **2 399 → 2 407 pass, 0 fail, RC=0** (`scratch/host_after_capability_reader_change_g.log`).
   Full 26-suite run: `scratch/suite_full_20261111b.log`. Copies before the edits: `scratch/index.js.bak_20261111_pre_capability_reader_model_params`,
   `scratch/host.test.cjs.bak_20261111_pre_capability_reader_assertions`.
8. **Open, named and not done here:** the capability reader and the voice-params reader now fetch the **same** engine
   path on their own transports and their own caches, so one endpoint costs one read *per reader* per TTL, not one read.
   Sharing that fetch is real work for a later pass; it is recorded on WM-42, not hidden by this card.
9. **State: BUILT — host half, needs one harness restart to go live.** The running plugin still has the old reader in
   memory until then; nothing about this was verified against a live engine slot before the restart, and the card says
   so instead of claiming it.

## Closed 2026-11-11 (Berlin) — T-780: `npm test` is no longer a hand-typed list of suites

1. **The ruling.** WM-42 item 6 on the version-targets item 12, verbatim: "improve and fix as recommended" — the
   recommendation recorded there was the one this card carries: a runner built from the tree, not a list that has to
   be edited whenever a suite is added.

   names against 26 files — which is exactly why it was a hazard: the drift shows up only as a suite that silently
   never runs.

   the same `rc` accumulation, one header line naming the suite whose output follows, and no list to maintain.
   `tests/react_shim.cjs` is outside the glob, as it was outside the list.

   neither sorted nor documented). A full run through the new runner — `scratch/suite_full_20261111a.log`, `RC=0`,
   **5 677 `  PASS ` lines, 0 `  FAIL `, 26 `=== SUITE` headers** — answers the same totals as
   `scratch/suite_full_20261110g.log`, which is the proof that the runner changed and the suites did not.
5. **Why the header line is part of the fix:** it is what makes two runs comparable suite by suite. Without it a run
   can only be compared by counting, which is how the two miscounts of 2026-11-10 happened.
6. **No restart and no browser refresh follow from this** — `scripts.test` is not a composition field, and no `lib/`
