## Closed 2026-11-07 (Berlin) — T-749: the second animal in the visualizer is the deepseek whale, turned 180 degrees and rolling like the qwen mark

1. **The ask, verbatim, as it has stood on its card since 11:28 Berlin today:** "expand dancing lama plugin with dancing whale option - use the deepseek whale in same scale, turn it 180* and replace lama icon with whale as a visualizer setting" (`../TODOS.md` WM-34 item 1).
2. **The mark is a cell map, not a drawing.** `SCOPE_WHALE_MASK749` (`lib/client.js:973`) is 22 rows of 30-bit hex values — 30 columns, 22 rows, **334 lit cells**, painted at 2 px per cell (`:980-983`). The first row is `0x00007f00`, the last `0x00100000`. Row 0 is the top of the mark and bit `cols-1-cc` is its leftmost cell, the convention verified at theta = 0 against the qwen mask.
3. **How it was traced.** `scratch/trace_whale_749.py` reads the deepseek logo's own path data and fills it with a standard-library nonzero-winding polygon parser — this host has no SVG rasteriser, and installing one for a 30×22 bitmap is not a step worth taking. The chosen cell map is written to `scratch/whale_cellmap_749.json`; the two orientations that were compared are `scratch/whale_preview_749_rot180.png` and `scratch/whale_preview_749_mirrored.png`. The turned form is the one the ask named: body to the right, fluke lower-left, facing its direction of travel — which is also the only one of the two that rolls the way a rolling mark should.
4. **The size is decided by the roll, not by the picture.** A body rolling on a line needs `2(a|sinθ| + b|cosθ|)` inside the 76 px inner height (`SCOPE_H300 = 80` less two edge insets), so at 45° `(w + h)/√2 ≤ 76`, and at 2 px cells `cols + rows ≤ 52`. The whale at 30 × 22 measures **73.54 px** — 2.46 px of spare travel. The qwen mark at 26 × 27 measures 74.96. The llama at 60 × 68 measures 90 px, which is why it has never rolled and never will at that size. The first search minimised the aspect and got the wrong answer; what has to be maximised is the turned diagonal under that bound.
5. **Word placement.** `whale` is appended at the end of `SCOPE_MODES300` (`:465`), before `off`, which is where a new word joins this ring and is the position every earlier card used.
6. **About the word "replace" in the ask.** The whale is a selectable word in the same ring as the llama; the llama is still there and is still the mode it was. A setting that puts the whale where the llama was is what "replace … as a visualizer setting" describes. If the intent was that the llama should not be offered at all, that is a one-line change to the ring and its default, and it is the operator's call, not mine.
7. **Nothing about the mark's machinery is new.** It shares the whole-canvas gate (`scopeFullCanvas541`, `:539`), the band cache, the roll map keyed per mode, the draw path at `:22380-22427` and the colour path built in T-748. Its default scheme is uniform white, like the qwen mark's. `SCOPE_MARK_GLYPHS748` carries both marks' names so the hovers name them correctly.
8. **Measured cost.** `MEASURE T-735 mode whale`: **6 978 canvas operations in one second of panel time**, 60 of 60 offered frames drawn, 116.3 per frame, 15 ms of node time. The qwen mark is 6 435 (107.25 per frame) and the llama is 25 260 (421 per frame): the whale is 8 % over the qwen mark and about a quarter of the llama's cost, which is what drawing a traced figure in merged runs of cells buys.
9. **The test half.** Provenance pins for 22 rows × 30 columns and the 334 lit cells the trace measured; an arithmetic pin for the roll bound; a walk that steps the qwen mark to the whale and asserts the clock word does not move; the whole-canvas gate and the "arriving here opens the graph" pins extended to the new word; and the ring-cycle pins re-cut from nine presses to ten (`// RE-POINTED 2026-11-07 by T-749`), which is what a word added to a ring costs every test that walks the ring.
10. **Client-only. No restart is owed for this card.**
11. **Verification and records.** Same runs as T-750 item 10, and the same live read: the whale's control exists in the panel as rendered, two presses on its colour control reach `flames`, and the canvas answers **5 312 white device pixels and 0 chromatic** in its default scheme — 332 of its 334 cells on screen at that instant — then **white 0, chromatic 6 576, 12 distinct colours, dominant `255,127,0`** in flames, with the drawn box walking right across the three frames (`scratch/whale_colour_shot_20261107_T748_T749_T750.jsonl`, pictures in `scratch/shots_20261107_T748_T749_T750_marks/`). `../TODOS.md` WM-34 is now **BUILT** with the trace method and the turned orientation recorded, and its custom-icon half stays open. 1. **The ask, verbatim.** "wow, the rolling qwen is perfect, but, … add the different color effects we already have for dancinf llama to bring in some rainbow effects aswell as a secondary setting, try to make code reusable".
2. **"Make the code reusable" is answered by writing none.** The colour engine in this file has never been mode-specific: `scopeDynColour587(hue, frac)` paints `hsl(h, 62+26f%, 16+46f%)`, `scopeRampColour541(stops, frac)` samples a stored scheme, and `scopeDynPick587` / `scopeDynRef587` hand out the dynamic reference the llama, the waterfall and both marks read. The cycle, drift, beat-gap and slide constants are unchanged. What is new in this card is a vocabulary list and two lines that ask the existing engine for a colour.
3. **The vocabulary is defined once.** `SCOPE_MARK_SCHEME_OPTS748` (`lib/client.js:1036`) is the eleven words the marks offer — `white, green, flames, ironbow, cold, auto1, auto2, rand, rand2, drift, beat_ring` — carried into `SCOPE_SCHEME_OPTS_BY_MODE539` for both `qwen` and `whale` (`:1056-1057`). It is one list on purpose: two copies of the same eleven words in two mode rows is how a picker drifts out of step with the engine.

That choice is mine and it is reversible in one line.

The rail beside it keeps its own dim white (`SCOPE_MARK_RAIL_COLOUR748`, `:959`) unless the mode's scheme says otherwise.

It has been wrong since T-746 and nothing could show it, because the rail drew the same bars either way at the loudness the fixture produced. It is now `scopeBarLogFrac539(peak748, t748.an.minDecibels, t748.an.maxDecibels)`. The word that branch served went out of the panel the same day, under T-750.

Stated here once, for T-748, T-749, T-750 and T-751.

## Closed 2026-11-07 (Berlin) — T-747: a station a person STOPPED is the thing the play button starts again

1. **The ask, verbatim.** "one small ui bug to fix: If user is playing a stream -> stop -> play button: it should start playing the last played stream: currently it plays a playlist item (we need to remember last played item on manual stop)". The operator's own guess at the cause, in the same message: "or has it todo with: \"the browser would not start playback again - press play once more (a press is a fresh gesture)\" error message ?"
2. **The answer to that guess is no, and it is measured, not read.** That sentence exists in two places in `lib/client.js` and both are RESUME paths — `:18504` inside `togglePlaybackPause299` and `:18573` inside `resumeHeldPlayback627`, each one the rejection of a `play()` the browser refused to honour. After a station stop no resume is even attempted, so the panel could not have been saying that. Verified in a real browser the same day (item 9): with the **default** autoplay policy and real presses, the station started again and `navigator.userActivation.isActive` was `true` at the press.
3. **What was really happening.** `stopStream395()` (`:12238`) pauses the station, removes its resource (`removeAttribute("src")` + `load()`) and marks the playback stopped. `playbackIsHeld299(a)` (`:18518`) is false for an element the panel stopped, false for one that ended, and false for a fresh element with no src — so `resumePresented627()` (`:18600`), the door every play press asks first, had nothing to answer for. `playWalked()` then walked on to `walkOrder299()` and started the first playable **playlist** row. Nothing anywhere in the panel remembered the last thing it had played.
4. **The fix: the panel remembers the station it last STARTED, and a manual stop is the one case that memory outlives.** `lastStationRef747` (`:12171`, with `rememberStation747` / `dropStationMemory747` at `:12172-12173`) is written at both station starts in `playStream395` — `:12322` (the T-401 plain retry, which is a station start) and `:12354` (the normal start) — carrying the url, the **same label the station was named with** (`streamLabel395(label, host395)`, so the ticker and the hovers name it the way it was named when it began), and the row id when it has one. `stopStream395` deliberately does not clear it, and the reason is written at `:12244`.
5. **What drops it, and why each one is a different last thing played:** a take started through `startPlayback` (`:14660` — the one door every take walks through); a station that reached its own end (`:12303`); a station the plugin could not fetch twice (`:12311`, the T-401 refusal); a crossfade set to "stop the stream" (`:12408` — the setting let go of the station, and the take is what the panel played last); and the link being taken off the imported list (`:12623-12624`, matched by row id **or** by the removed row's url, because a link played from the import field carries no row id).
6. **The press asks the panel's own gate, not a private rule.** `playWalked` reads the memory at `:18401-18412`, after the resume door and before the walk, and passes the url back through `streamUrlCheck390` (`:1683`). If Stream input was turned off in between, the press names **that setting's own refusal sentence** and stops there — it does not silently fall through to a playlist row. The answer that does start says what it did: "the station this panel last played starts again — <name> · it was stopped by a press, and the link was never written to disk", the same fact the stop press stated.
7. **The gate that keeps the old meaning.** The branch only runs when the panel is not presenting a station right now (`!streamNow395`). Written without that condition the first triage broke **16** `stream_overlap` checks (`the take plays on its OWN element`, the duck and stop mode blocks, the whole T-504 block, T-551): pressing play over a live station restarted the station instead of playing the row. A station that is audible is not a station somebody stopped.

## Closed 2026-11-07 (Berlin) — T-746: a third dancing icon — the Qwen mark, traced to cells, uniform white on black, rolling along the sound rail

1. **The ask, verbatim.** "in addition to the dancing llama and dancing whale - create another \"dancing icon\" from the pattern - it's the current qwen logo - in honor to the great coder of this addon ... aka you it needs conversion from blue to uniform white on black, and maybe should \"roll\" clockwise down the \"sound rail\" — Your chance to shine - use playwright-cli to take a screenshot of the result and verify it will look cool and match dancing lama and whale in style". The mode word is `qwen`; the panel's Settings row names it "qwen mark — rolling on the sound rail".
2. **What it draws.** The logo traced into a `26 × 27` cell mask (`SCOPE_QWEN_MASK746`, 27 hex rows, MSB left, 333 lit cells) painted at the same 2 px cell the llama grid uses, so the mark is 52 × 54 px, in one white `#ffffff` on the panel's own ground `#0b0d0b`. It rolls left to right along the bottom inner edge and turns as it goes: `theta = distance / half-height`, and the centre rides at the outline's support height (`halfW|sin| + halfH|cos|`), which is what makes a mark rise and fall instead of spinning in place. The rail it rolls over is the panel's own 20-band log chain, 4 cells (8 px) tall along the bottom edge, drawn first so the mark passes over it; **the height of a rail cell carries the measurement, its colour does not** (`rgba(255,255,255,0.30)`, one colour, always). Audio drives the roll: `0.35 + energy × 3.2` px per frame through the mode's own dB / log level words.
3. **The size is a property of the box, not a choice.** A non-circular body rolling on a line needs `2(a|sinθ| + b|cosθ|)` ≤ the drawable height. On the 196 × 76 inner box of a 200 × 80 strip that limit is 76 px; 26 × 27 cells at 2 px needs 75.0 px. The llama's 60 × 68 cell map would need 90 px, so the two marks are deliberately not the same scale — the strip is the constraint, and a larger mark would be clipped at some angle.
4. **The mode has no colour vocabulary, so it has no colour cell.** The mode joins `SCOPE_MODES300` before `"off"`, the whole-canvas gate `scopeFullCanvas541`, the level row (`SCOPE_LEVEL_OPTS346.qwen`, two words `dB` / `log`), and the three gates that make a mode live (the animation-loop liveness gate, the entry arm, the flowing arm). The Settings row renders no scheme control for it, and the painter takes no scheme parameter. `SCOPE_SCHEME_DEFAULT_BY_MODE539` gained no key: a mode with no colour words needs no default colour.
5. **The defect, found by measuring rather than by reading the code.** The lit runs along a canvas row were merged with a sentinel that used the run's **start index** as the flag (`run0746 = -1`). A run beginning left of the mark's centre has a negative index, so the flush read `-14 < 0` as "no run open" and dropped it — every lit run left of the centre, every row, every frame. The mark painted **169 of its 333 cells across 28 px of its 52 px width**: half a mark, and always the left half. The mask, the constants, the geometry and the clip bounds were each measured and each cleared; the counters said `hits 334, clipped 0, rects 25`, which is what named the merge. Fixed with a separate open flag and a start number. Re-measured in the same run: `hits 334 / rects 46 / cells 334, clipped 0`, per-frame 333-337 cells, box 50-56 px wide.
6. **One comment was wrong about the code and was re-cut, not left.** It claimed the roll does not advance when nothing is measured. It does: `ROLL_BASE746 = 0.35` px per frame keeps the mark moving at its base speed and a measured band adds the gain. The comment now says that, because a mark standing still halfway across the box reads as a mode that broke. The no-tap path (no audio at all) still paints the canvas clean and drops the distance covered, as the llama does.
7. **Tests: 10 new assertions in `tests/scope.test.cjs`, plus the positional re-cuts the new entry moved.** The new pins are the mask's provenance (27 rows, 333 lit, the four named constants — the same form the llama mask is held by); uniform white with a scheme stored for the mode (`{"qwen":"flames"}` changes nothing on the canvas); the whole mark painted (37 unclipped frames, worst 324 cells, widest 56 px — a half-mark cannot pass this); nothing drawn outside the inner box; the centre advancing right in all 39 steps and covering 59 px; the drawn height taking 5 distinct values 48..56 (a rolling body, not a sticker that spins); the mark reaching the ground line at y 78; the rail standing on the bottom inner edge, never taller than 4 cells, painted under the mark; and the drive measured as 2.22 px/frame with the band at the top of the mock's window against 0.34 px/frame at its floor. The re-cuts (each with a dated `RE-POINTED 2026-11-07 by T-746` note, nothing dropped): the ring-walk block, the level-cell count 6 → 7, the Settings row count 8 → 9, the T-535 body window 3 000 → 3 600 (the body measured at 3 210 characters / 40 lines), the T-681 and T-686 press counts. One pin was found broken while it was still passing: the `scopeFullCanvas541` pattern had unescaped `||` and had matched nothing since T-681 — it now matches.
8. **Frame cost re-measured (WM-31 item 9's table).** `qwen` is **6 435 fillRect-equivalent ops per 1 000 ms at 60 fps** — between `knight` (2 520) and `waterfall` (11 880), and a quarter of `llama` (25 260). The 5 403 read earlier today was the half-mark's cost and is superseded by this number.
9. **Real-browser verification (the WM-17 harness pattern, `scratch/qwen_roll_shot_20261107_T746.mjs`).** The mode was set in the live panel and confirmed by the browser's own key (`deepamp:scope.mode = "qwen"`); one take already in the store was played (`ap-1000`, the deep-house/trance render the operator named as the music clip); the canvas pixels were read at three moments. A frame with the mark fully inside the box carries **5 296 white device pixels = 331 cells**, bounding box 33..87 × 20..70 CSS px, and `other_pixels: 0` — the frame contains nothing but white, the rail, and the ground. The rail read 1 336 px of lit rail from the real take. Pictures: `scratch/shots_20261107_T746_qwen_roll/qwen_roll_0.png`, `_1.png`, `_2.png` (the roll at three points, including the wrap where the mark is leaving the right edge), `qwen_roll_panel.png` (the mode in the panel with the Settings row beside it), `llama_same_take.png` (the same strip, the same take, the mode that has been on the panel for a year).
10. **What the style comparison actually says.** The llama is a silhouette over a coloured 3D box; this mark is a silhouette on plain black, because the ask named the conversion by hand ("uniform white on black"). What the two share is the shape of the joke: a solid traced figure, drawn in cells, moving across the strip in time with the audio. **The whale half of the comparison has no target: the dancing whale is not built** — WM-34 in `../TODOS.md` is still a card, and no whale mode exists in `SCOPE_MODES300`. If the whale is built it can use this machinery unchanged (a cell map, a roll, a support height); that is worth knowing before its card is run.
11. **Verification of the whole card.** `scope` alone: **412 pass, 0 fail** (402 before this card's pins). Full run: `npm test` form, 26 suites, **RC=0, 5 541 PASS, 0 FAIL** (`scratch/full_20261107_T746_qwen_roll.log`), read with `grep -cE '^ *PASS '`. Pre-change copy of the client: `scratch/client.js.bak_20261107_pre_qwen_roll_T746` (2 024 091 B). The mask rows are mirrored at `scratch/qwen_mask_rows_27.txt`; the tracing and the offline roll preview that settled the geometry are `scratch/trace_qwen.py` and `scratch/roll_qwen_preview.py`.
12. **Going live: a browser refresh, and no restart.** The whole change is `lib/client.js`. It was read in a real browser today, which is only possible because the client half is served from the tree, so it is live for the operator's panel at the next refresh. STATE: **BUILT, TESTED, MEASURED IN THE BROWSER — client-only, a browser refresh shows it.**

## Closed 2026-11-07 (Berlin) — T-745: WM-31 item 7's q44 half is RUN — the memory of an engine's 403 refusal of model management is cleared by the next answer that is not a 403

1. **The ruling, as recorded on the card.** q44: "the 403 memory is **cleared on any non-403 engine answer**, the operator's choice over clearing it on a read press alone; that half is host-side and needs its own restart OK before it goes live." (`../TODOS.md` WM-31 item 7.) What it fixes is the standing fact that the plugin remembered an engine's 403 refusal of model management per lane **for the life of the process** and never cleared it, so one refusal at boot silenced unload for the rest of the session.
2. **What the host does now.** `clearMgmtMemory745(fn, by)` sits beside the `mgmtDisabled` map and clears that lane's flag when an engine has answered something that is not a 403. It is called from the model load / unload path (`ensureLoaded`, on `'load_answer'` and `'load_ok'`), the model-operation path (`modelOp`, on `'model_op_answer'` and `'model_op_ok'`), the catalog audit (`fetchModels`, only when a list actually came back), and the `endpoint_models` route (`'endpoint_models_read'`). **`probeEndpointHealth` deliberately does not clear it** — a `/health` answer says the engine is up, which says nothing about whether it accepts model management. Each call names itself in the reason string, so a cleared flag can be traced to the answer that cleared it.
3. **Tests: 12 new assertions in `tests/host.test.cjs`, all passing.** Two fixture seams carry the cases: `opts.modelsAnswer745 = 'fail745'` makes the catalog read exit 7, and `opts.loadAnswer745 = 'forbid745'` answers the load / unload POST with a 403 body. The pins cover both directions — a 403 sets the flag, a later non-403 clears it — and one pins that a health probe alone changes nothing.
4. **Verification.** Full run in the `npm test` form: 26 suites, **RC=0, 5 526 PASS, 0 FAIL** (`scratch/full_20261107_T745_mgmt_clear.log`), against the 5 514 baseline T-744 left. Pre-change copies: `scratch/index.js.bak_20261107_pre_mgmt_clear_T745` (1 520 388 B) and `scratch/host.test.cjs.bak_20261107_pre_mgmt_clear_T745`.
5. **Going live: a harness restart, and it is not taken.** This is the host half. The same restart also carries T-744's environment-name rename, which was already owed; one restart serves both, and each restart still needs its own explicit OK. STATE: **RUN, TESTED, VERIFIED — restart pending.**
6. **Live 2026-11-07 14:01 - 14:02 Berlin: the operator took that restart, and the model-management path answers.** The boot's own reads are in the perf log (`~/.dsh/deepamp-audio/perf_log.jsonl`): six `endpoint_models` records at 14:01:33 - 14:01:35 Berlin — tts `primary` 60 models, tts `e-11` 60, stt `primary` 58, stt `e-13` 57, and `endpoint_models_empty` for the two held gpu1 slots (`e-10`, `e-9`) — **no 403 among them**. `queue_status` answers `mgmt_disabled: {"tts":false,"stt":false}` on both lanes, and the model census answers for both primaries with `ok:true`, `from_cache:false`, `library_state:"complete"`, `catalog_readable:true`, `endpoints_failed:0`. **The honest limit on what that read proves, stated so a later session does not over-read it:** a fresh process starts with an empty map under the old code too, so this proves the current tree is what is running and that nothing is memory-silenced — it does not prove the clearing behaviour, which is carried by the 12 assertions in item 3. No 403 has been seen on either lane since. STATE now: **RUN, TESTED, VERIFIED, LIVE.**

## Closed 2026-11-07 (Berlin) — T-744: the plugin's environment keys are renamed to `DEEPAMP_*`, and the names they carried before that date are still read, after the new ones

1. **The ruling, verbatim.** "Rename the env keys to DEEPAMP_* too" (operator, 2026-11-07, in the store-conversion discussion). The option taken keeps every old name readable **after** the new one for a dated transition, so anything set today keeps working; it is a host-side change and it rides a restart.
2. **Which keys moved.** `AUDIO_PLAY_STORE_DIR` → `DEEPAMP_STORE_DIR`, `AUDIO_PLAY_SPECS_DIR` → `DEEPAMP_SPECS_DIR`, `AUDIO_PLAY_YTDLP_PATH` → `DEEPAMP_YTDLP_PATH` (the three Config fields); `AUDIO_PLAY_MAX_JOBS_PER_HOST` → `DEEPAMP_MAX_JOBS_PER_HOST` and `AUDIO_PLAY_LOW_SPACE_BYTES` → `DEEPAMP_LOW_SPACE_BYTES` (the two knobs that are not Config fields); `AUDIO_PLAY_API` → `DEEPAMP_API` in `scripts/voice_replace.sh:24`; the test harness reads `DEEPAMP_LIB` and `DEEPAMP_TOOLS`. **Named plainly: `LOW_SPACE_BYTES` and `API` were not in the operator's list** — they are the same key family and were renamed with it; reversing that half later is a two-line change, not a redo.
3. **How the host reads a name now.** `CFG_ENV716` carries the three new Config names and a new `CFG_ENV_LEGACY744` carries the three old ones beside them. `envRaw744(name)` is the safe read; `envDeclared744(key)` returns the value **and which key answered** — new name first, old name after, `null` when neither is set. `capEnvRead744()` and `lowSpaceThresholdBytes()` use the same shape for the two knobs, and `declaredValue716(key)` now asks the environment through that pair before it asks Config.
4. **Precedence did not move, and that is the point.** env > Config > built-in default; a key answered by the environment is never written to `state.json`; the cap is still 1 … 8; the low-space threshold is still a byte count. The name of the door changed, the room behind it did not.
5. **Which key answered is now visible where the plugin already reports itself.** The boot audit's `config_declared` row carries `env_key` when the environment answered, and `cap_source` is `env:` plus the key that answered. A value set under the old spelling is therefore not invisible in a log — that is why a readable fallback was chosen over a silent alias.
6. **What was deliberately left alone.** The `GET /api/deepamp/limit_one_per_host` response keeps its existing field (`env: MAX_JOBS_PER_HOST_ENV`) and gains no new field, so the panel and every mock shape stay as they are; the legacy acceptance is documented instead of reshaped. The first attempt at that last one failed and the reason is worth keeping: the suite's own mock recomputed `cap_source` from a constant, so it could not express "the old key answered"; `tests/ui_state.test.cjs:153-158` now carries the answering key as part of the mock's shape, which is what the host actually returns.

The operator's verbatim quotes carried inside these tests were not rewritten, and no assertion was dropped: the T-458b block that checks the gate sits before the file probe and names the root and the switch still asserts all of it.

## Closed 2026-11-06 (Berlin) — T-738: the cast rows are a table now — five named columns, one column line, and the answer to "why are the text windows so long"

1. **The ruling, verbatim (operator, 2026-11-06 22:35 Berlin):** "make it more table style so the objects in the rows align in a more unified way please", in the same message as the question "Why are the text windows so long in the screenshot ? does that loog good ?" — item 2 answers that question from the code, and the picture the question was about is `scratch/shots_20261106/cast_rows_editor_closeup.png`, the cast block as it stood before this card.
2. **Why the fields were that wide.** The row was a `display:flex` line in which every part took the width its own text happened to need, and only the voice field carried `flex: "1 1 160px"` together with `width: "100%"`. Inside the pop-out editor that is the whole leftover: the editor's own band is `left: 8%` / `right: 8%` (`lib/client.js:11097`), 1210 px at the 1440 px viewport the shot uses, so the field became a banner. It does not look good, and not only as a matter of taste: a field that wide reads as "type anything here" when it means "name one voice", and the kind badge, the play control and the speaker verdict landed at a different x in every row, because nothing in the row said where a thing sits.
3. **What it is now.** One table, `audio-play-cast-table594` (`lib/client.js:10694`-`:10816`), whose columns are named in one place: `CAST_COLS594` (`:10655`-`:10661`) carries each column's key, its width, its visible label and the hover that explains it, and a `colgroup` (`:10698`) and a `thead` (`:10699`-`:10701`) are built from that same list, so the header and the rows cannot disagree. Speaker in the text 150 px, voice this cast uses 236 px, what the panel knows 190 px, the play column 28 px, and the last column — is this name a speaker? — carries no width so it absorbs whatever the window leaves over. The table is capped at 940 px (`CAST_TABLE_MAX594`, `:10654`) so a wide editor cannot stretch the field back into a banner.
4. **The long text is not a column.** What a row says about its sample's length (`audio-play-cast-dur579`), that a voice is shared by several speakers (`audio-play-cast-share581`), and the row's own note are collected per row (`:10705`-`:10742`) and, when there is any, drawn on a second line under that row in one cell that spans the table (`:10812`-`:10814`). Long text costs nothing there and pushes nothing sideways; nothing in a row is ellipsized to fit a column. Rows carry a faint stripe (`:10703`) and a note line shares its speaker's stripe, so a row and its note read as one thing.
5. **Measured, off the live page, not off the style sheet** (`scratch/cast_rows_shot3_20261106_T738.mjs`, its `scratch/cast_rows_20261106_T738.jsonl`, its shots in `scratch/shots_20261106_T738/`): the table sits at x 128 and is 940 px wide; the five column lines land at **128 / 278 / 514 / 704 / 732** with widths **150 / 236 / 190 / 28 / 336**; all nine speaker rows of the real scene match that line within 1 px, in the unmapped state and again after the scene's own cast mapping is typed in (`rows_on_the_line: true` both times, 9 speaker rows, 9 note rows). Before this card the same read was not possible: there were no columns to read.
6. **Nothing was dropped from a row.** All nine class names the panel already had are still emitted, with their text, their handlers and their hovers unchanged. Measured on the same real scene in the same state as round 2 (which is the before-record): `from594` 4, `voice638` 9, `kind594` 9, `dur579` 2, `play448` 4, `line594` 4 — identical counts before and after. One class is new: `audio-play-cast-name594` (`:10751`) carries the speaker's own name for a row that is not renamed, so every row now names its speaker in the same column; `from594` keeps its meaning exactly (renamed rows only) and still shows the name with the arrow.
7. **No assertion was re-cut, weakened or added.** The suites key on the class names, and the class names did not move, so the four suites this change touches were run and nothing else was re-expressed: `scene_composer`, `ui_state` (which pins `castBlock381()` defined once and called once, and its caption line appearing exactly once in the file), `tooltips` and `render` — **RC=0, 1497 pass, 0 fail**. Log: `deepamp-audio/scratch/scene_composer_20261106_T738_cast_table.log`. Copies taken before the change: `scratch/client.js.bak_20261106_pre_cast_table`, `scratch/scene_composer.test.cjs.bak_20261106_pre_cast_table` (unchanged by the card, kept as the pre-change copy of record).
8. **The panel's hover and caption policy was written into the new markup, and one gap in that coverage is now named.** The five column labels and their hovers, and the name cell's hover, name no route verb, no lane field, no ticket id, no storage key, no source file, no browser API and no HTTP method — checked by hand against the lists in `tests/tooltips.test.cjs`, because that suite's whole-panel policy **does not reach this block**: it renders the panel with no scene pasted, and `castBlock381()` renders only inside the pop-out editor. Its measure read the same 331 hovers before and after this card (68 longer than three lines, longest 10 lines / 139 words / 755 chars, unchanged), which is the measurement that says so. The verdict column is the one column whose text length is not known in advance, so it is the one thing allowed to shorten, and its full text is in its own hover.

## Closed 2026-11-06 (Berlin) — T-737: the clock cycle's order is the operator's order — nixie orange steps to nixie green — and the question about flickering digits is answered from the source

1. **The ruling, verbatim (operator, 2026-11-06 21:48 Berlin):** "order of clocks should be \"nixie orange -> nixie green\" while cycling". It arrived in the same message as a question — "in the nixie displays - did you implement any flickering or random dimming of digits yet ?" — and item 7 and item 8 answer that question from the code. The ruling is about the walk a press takes, which in this panel is one list.
2. **What carries the cycle.** `CLOCK_MODES681` in `lib/client.js` is the whole rule: a press on the canvas while the clock is showing (`:22427`) and a press on the clock row's own face box (`:25202`) each step to the next entry and wrap at the end, and the box's hover lists the face names in that same order and says out loud that a press on the canvas "walks these faces in the same order". So the order is one line, and the control's own wording follows it with no second edit.
3. **Before and after.** Before: `clock_led → clock_nixie → clock_flap → clock_flap_light → clock_nixie_green → clock_led`. After (`lib/client.js:478`): `clock_led → clock_nixie → clock_nixie_green → clock_flap → clock_flap_light → clock_led`. The box's own word now walks `LED dots → Nixie tube → green tube → flip board → flip white → LED dots`.
4. **What did not move.** Five faces, one direction, one wrap, the same default face (`clock_led`), the same words on the box and in the hover, the same stored keys. The pair of a variant now sits together in the walk, which is what the two split-flap boards already did. And no panel's setting moves: the browser stores a face word, not a position, so a person who had chosen a face still has it.
5. **The suite's walk assertions are order-dependent, so they were re-cut, not weakened** (`tests/scope.test.cjs`, per the rule that an assertion is re-expressed with a dated contract-change note). 1) The source pin at `:1696` now pins the walked order and quotes the operator's sentence. 2) The neon-green tube's measurement block moved to sit one press after the amber tube — that is where the walk reaches it now — and every number inside it is untouched; its header and its check text now read "the face after the amber tube". 3) The wrap claim now reads "from the inverted board back to the LED face", which is the face the walk ends on. 4) The T-689 window's stated walk reads `Nixie → neon green tube → flap → inverted board → LED`; its four presses and both its assertions are unchanged, because a five-face walk started on its second face wraps in four presses in any order.
6. **Measured after the change:** `node tests/scope.test.cjs` — **RC=0, 397 pass, 0 fail**, the same assertion count the suite carried before this change, nothing dropped. Log: `deepamp-audio/scratch/scope_20261106_T737_clock_cycle_order.log`. Copies taken before the change: `scratch/client.js.bak_20261106_pre_clock_cycle_order`, `scratch/scope.test.cjs.bak_20261106_pre_clock_cycle_order`. The T-735 frame-cost instrument ran in that same pass with its per-face numbers unchanged, because it reads the face list by name and not by position.
7. **The flickering question, answered from the code, and it is answered as a fact rather than a re-derivation** (now recorded in `docs/FACTS.md`). Yes, there is dimming, and it was built on 2026-11-06 as T-729: `nixieBreath690` (`lib/client.js:21025`, constants `:21017-21024`, applied in `scopeNixieFace684` at `:21162`). A struck digit's wire, its pale core and its three halo passes are drawn at a strength that moves on a slow curve — middle 0.915, swing ±0.055, periods 9.3 s and 13.7 s, clamped to 0.72..0.97 so a tube is never at full strength — plus a rare dip, one 4-second interval in seven, up to 0.16 deep, chosen by a bijection on the wall-clock bucket.
8. **What it is not, stated exactly.** It is not per-digit: one factor per frame is shared by every struck digit, the suite asserts that identity, and the ruling of 2026-11-06 put the fluctuation on the struck digit only — the glass, the mesh, the foot ring and the ghost stack keep the palette's unchanged ink. It is not random: the client's only two `Math.random()` calls (`:1156`, `:1170`) are the waterfall's hue scheme, and nothing on a clock face uses one. Both tube faces carry it, because the amber and neon green palettes share the drawing path; the LED matrix and both split-flap boards have none. The dimming travels as alpha in the `#RRGGBBAA` ink (`nixieInk690` `:21047`) — no `globalAlpha`, no gradient, no `shadowBlur`.
9. **Going live: a browser refresh, and nothing more** — `lib/client.js` and `tests/` only, no host file, no restart. Not closed by this card: WM-31 item 1, and item 2 (the cast rows are analysed and photographed in `scratch/shots_20261106/`, awaiting the operator's look), and the open question the WM-17 pass raised about the animation loop still asking for frames at a low fps setting.

## Closed 2026-11-06 (Berlin) — T-736: WM-17 is RUN — the panel's RAM and CPU measured in a real Chromium against the live harness, four rounds, and the T-735 mock instrument checked against the real thing

1. **Ran on the operator's word of 21:0x Berlin** (q47, verbatim): "Build it and run the first round now". The side effect was stated before it ran and the operator accepted it: a headless Chromium opens the harness GUI, so a new session appears in the operator's UI while the measurement runs; their own browser tab is untouched. This is the pass q46 named as the next step of WM-31 item 9 ("nothing yet — measure in a real browser first"), and it is also WM-17, which had been a plan with no run since it was written.
2. **What was built**: four scripts and four logs, all in `deepamp-audio/scratch/` — `wm17_round1/2/3/4_20261106.mjs` and their `.jsonl`. Nothing in `lib/`, nothing in `tests/`, so nothing here needs a browser refresh or a restart. The harness reads the GUI URL from the environment (the token is read live from the tmux pane and never written into a file), drives the page through `playwright-core` 1.63.0-alpha bundled by the globally installed `@playwright/cli`, Chromium 153.0.8010.12 headless at a 1440×900 viewport, and reads the numbers through CDP `Performance.getMetrics` plus `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage`, with process RSS taken from `ps` as a process tree. The task is always the same real take — `ap-1000`, played through the panel with the visualizer in spectrum mode — never a synthetic file.
3. **Round 1 got the wrong thing, and the reason is worth keeping.** The panel's strip is the span `.audio-play-scope` inside the row `.audio-play-scope-row`; a selector written as "class contains audio-play-scope" lands on the row, and clicking a row does nothing to a mode the span owns. Round 1 therefore played three takes with the visualizer OFF. Its numbers are not discarded — they are the control phase of the later rounds — and the client's own resolver, `root389.querySelector(".audio-play-scope")` at `lib/client.js:18827`, is what the corrected selector copies.
4. **Round 2 stopped trusting a hover.** The mode is read from the key the panel itself writes (`deepamp:scope.mode`, `lib/client.js:729`) and verified after every round, so "the visualizer was in spectrum mode" is a fact read out of the panel rather than an assumption made by the harness. At mount those keys are absent, which is itself a measurement: the panel's defaults are not written to storage until a person touches a control.
5. **The leak question, answered by twelve plays in one page** (round 3, phase F: twelve rounds of play-stop-settle, a forced garbage collection before every sample). `JSEventListeners` after every round: **1020, twelve times out of twelve**. Page nodes: 7 324 after the first round, climbing 7 a round through round 5 to 7 352, one last step of 2, and then holding at 7 354 for the remaining seven samples. JS heap after a forced GC: +883 kB over the whole phase, and the steps are front-loaded (+339, +160, +126 kB) and after that are noise inside a ±100 kB band. `<audio>` elements in the page: 3 at mount and 3 after every round. Documents: 2 throughout. The shape is a warm-up that reaches a level and stays there, not a per-take accumulation. It is not proof — one page, one browser, one machine — but the thing WM-17 was written to look for, a heap or a listener count that does not come back down, is not present.
6. **What the panel actually costs, per 20-second window of a real take playing.** Spectrum mode on the strip's own canvas (200×80): **13 760 to 13 969 `fillRect` calls a second at 57.8 to 58.8 painted frames a second — 237 to 239 rectangles per painted frame**, reproduced across four independent 20-second windows, the whole spread inside 1.5 %. The clock face at rest (visualizer off, nothing playing): 285 rectangles per drawing, one drawing a second. The clock face while a take plays: 566 a second, which is the same 285-rectangle drawing issued about twice a second by the panel's wake path.
7. **The T-735 mock instrument, checked against the real browser, is right.** The mock said spectrum 252 canvas operations per frame; the real browser draws 237-239. The mock said `clock_led` 281 operations a second; the real browser draws 285 per drawing at one drawing a second. Within 6 % and 2 %. The one place the table understates is exactly the place its rows deliberately excluded: the clock rows were mounted with nothing playing, because that is what a clock face at rest is, and a real panel repaints the clock about twice a second while a take plays. The table of record stands; this card is the note that says where its scope ends.
8. **The fps control, measured in a real browser** (round 4). The control is a `select` inside the panel's Collapsible titled "Settings" (`lib/client.js:24876`, the select at `:24935`) and it is not in the DOM until that section is opened — round 3 looked for a section head saying "visualizer", never found the control, and so measured the default 60 twice. Round 4 opened the section by its own name. Setting 60: 58.2 painted frames/s, 13 784 `fillRect`/s. 30: 29.4 and 6 977. 20: 19.8 and 4 708. 12: 12.0 and 2 864. The cost per painted frame does not move (237-239). `requestAnimationFrame` is still asked for 58-59 times a second at every setting: the control stops paintings, it does not slow the loop.
9. **What the frame-cost numbers lead to, measured rather than argued.** Drawing work saved by the control: 0 / 49 / 66 / 79 %, against the mock's predicted 0 / 50 / 67 / 80 %. The page's total task time over the same window: 1.00 / 0.99 / 0.90 / 0.86 of the 60-fps case, and script time 1.744 / 1.506 / 1.295 / 1.225 seconds per 20 s. The savings are real in drawing terms and small in wall-clock terms, because drawing is not where this page's time goes. That is the answer to the question T-735 opened, and it is a measurement, not an opinion about optimisation.
10. **Where the page's time does go, and what the browser's footprint did.** The page measured is the whole harness UI with the panel mounted in it, not the panel alone. Layout churn — about 1 350 layout passes and 0.7 s of layout time per 20 s window — is present with the visualizer off as well as on, so the DOM updates (row timers, read-outs), not the canvas, carry a large part of the cost. Process RSS: 632-634 MB over 7 browser processes at the start of a run, 707 MB over 8 after minutes of work; the renderer process itself held 94 MB and ended at 96 MB. The growth is a new browser process appearing, not the renderer growing.
11. **Going live: nothing**, because nothing in the plugin changed. Open threads this card does not close, in the order they matter: whether the animation loop should also stop asking for frames at a low fps setting (measured: it does not); the CDP method the WM-17 plan named, `Memory.getDOMCountersForSnapshot`, does not exist in this Chromium build and `Performance.getMetrics` carries the same counters instead; and none of these numbers are from a real display, a GPU compositor, or a second browser — the panel was measured headless, which is the honest limit of what was available here.
## Closed 2026-11-06 (Berlin) — T-735: the frame-cost measurement WM-31 item 9 asked for is RUN — canvas operations per visualizer mode and per clock face over one second of panel time, and the fps control's own hover claim measured true for the first time
1. **Ran on the operator's word of 19:4x Berlin** (verbatim): "3E/4 - go ahead as you suggest / 6 go ahead as suggested / ask questions one by one if you need my word" — that answer ran the two offered items it named (T-733 and T-734, cards below), and the next step I then proposed was this measurement, which the same words covered. It closes the measuring half of WM-31 item 9, which is the only place this item exists in the tracker (WM-30 carries six items and none of them is a frame-cost row; the pairs item 9 names are WM-17 and WM-30 item 4, and neither is touched by this card). It proposes no change, which is what that item asked for ("What is missing is a measurement, not a change").
2. **What was built**: an instrument appended to `tests/scope.test.cjs` (before its summary line) that mounts each of the 9 visualizer modes and each of the 5 clock faces in turn, drives 1 000 ms of panel time against a virtual clock the panel is handed, and counts what the panel issued to a 2D context. Nothing else in the file was touched. The instrument is re-runnable as `node tests/scope.test.cjs` and its output is a `MEASURE T-735` table, not a threshold.
3. **The split it had to make is the finding, not decoration.** A strip is drawn from the animation loop. A clock face is repainted by the panel's own one-second tick (`timer.interval(tick677, 1000)` at `lib/client.js:19889`, the paint call at `:19875`), and with the strip off there is no animation loop at all. An instrument that watched only the animation frame path reported every clock face as costing nothing. Both paths are now counted, separately, in every row.
4. **Two faults of the instrument, both mine, both fixed, and the first two runs failed on them.** 1) Sixty steps of 16 ms is 960 ms, so a panel that ticks once a second never ticked inside the second being measured; the step is now 1000/60 ms, which is the real frame period at the 60 Hz the panel says the display offers. 2) The static waveform is driven by the media element's own `timeupdate` events, and the panel registers that handler as an element **property** (`node.ontimeupdate`); the suite's `fire()` plays the `addEventListener` path, so driving only that path drew nothing. Both are stated in the comment above the runner, not left as a working accident.
5. **Each row is mounted in the state its own name describes.** A strip row with something playing (the only state in which a strip draws). A clock row with NOTHING playing — a paused element fires no media events, and charging a clock for repaints an idle panel never pays is not a measurement. The static row with a real take, a real duration and a position that advances, because the panel asks a lane for a file's peaks only when it knows the file has a length (`:19843`). The guard asserts exactly that: every row was really the face on screen, the peaks face had a row to play, every face that draws drew something, and `off` — the one mode whose contract is to draw nothing — drew nothing.
6. **The measured table.** One second of panel time, canvas operations issued, and per offered frame: `vu_needle` 25 260 (421 a frame, 25 080 rects + 120 strokes); `llama` 25 260 (421, 25 200 rects); `vu_led` 16 020 (267); `spectrum` 15 120 (252, 120 frequency reads and 120 time reads a second); `waterfall` 11 880 (198, 119 save/restore pairs); `oscilloscope` 11 640 (194, 120 strokes carrying 5 760 path points); `knight` 2 520 (42); `static` 856 drawn on the wake path only — 4 repaints a second at the browser's own timeupdate cadence, 214 operations each; `off` 0, exactly as its contract says. Clock faces, all on the wake path, one draw a second: `clock_led` 281 (281 rects, a dot matrix), `clock_nixie` and `clock_nixie_green` 202 each (166 rects + 36 strokes + 322 path points), `clock_flap` and `clock_flap_light` 42 each (26 rects + 4 text prints + 12 save/restore). Full output: `scratch/T735_frame_cost_table_20261106.txt` from `scratch/scope_test_20261106_T735_framecost_5.log`.
7. **What the table says about the thing the group was actually worried about.** The clock faces are the cheapest drawings on this panel per second — 42 to 281 operations. The strip costs 194 to 421 operations **per frame**, which is 40 to 150 times a second. The split-flap board that WM-31 item 8 was opened about is the cheapest thing on the panel that still draws: 42 operations in a second, because it prints four strings and draws 26 rects instead of painting a dot matrix. The cost in this panel is in the strip, and the numbers now say which mode costs what.
8. **The fps control's own hover is measured true, for the first time.** `SCOPE_FPS_TIP537` claims "60 draws every frame the display offers … 30 every second frame, 20 every third, 12 every fifth". Swept over the two most expensive strip faces: frames that drew came out 60, 30, 20 and 12 out of the 60 frames offered, and the work fell with it — 25 260 → 12 630 → 8 420 → 5 052 operations in the same second, i.e. the control saves 0 %, 50 %, 67 %, 80 % of the frames. Pinned by a new check so the claim cannot drift from the behaviour: `T-735: the fps control draws at the cadence its own hover promises`.
9. **What these numbers are, stated so nobody over-reads them.** They count draw calls the panel issues to a mock 2D context, in Node, over a simulated second; the Node time for the whole simulated second came out 5–19 ms on every row, which says the panel's own per-frame work is small and says nothing about a browser's paint time, its compositor or its memory. Wall-clock frame cost, RAM and CPU in a real browser stay WM-17, and `bad_rects` was 0 on every row, so nothing here measured a drawing that was wrong.
10. **Measured, test side.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` 5 611 → 5 707 lines, one block added, no existing check touched; `node --check` OK. **(Corrected the same evening, 21:2x Berlin: this item first said "5 611 → 5 695", which understated the result by 12 lines — the guard was re-cut and `mediaEvent735` hoisted above `node735` after the count had been written. ## Closed 2026-11-06 (Berlin) — an endpoint row with nothing it could unload no longer wears an "unload" button it can never press: the dead control is gone and the reason it used to carry now rides on the read-now control

1. **Ran on the operator’s own words** (WM-31 item 7, 2026-11-06, verbatim): “the button is disabled and can’t be pressed - model state seems irrelevant”. Read against the code the symptom is exact, and it named two different greys: one is a real refusal with a reason behind it, the other was a control with no possible press. Only the second is a defect, and only the second was changed.
2. **What the dead control was, `lib/client.js:3273-3281` as it stood before this card.** When a row held no model names from an `endpoint_models` read, the row still built `ctl("un", "unload", …, undefined, props.ctlCls, { opacity: "0.45", cursor: "default" }, true)` — handler `undefined`, `disabled: true` hardcoded — so it could never be pressed in any state, in the never-read case and in the read-answered-nothing case alike, and its own hover sent the person to a “read now” press.
3. **Why it could not have been made to work instead.** `lib/index.js:12777` reads `if (!model) return Promise.resolve(logModelOp207({ ok: false, error: ‘no model’ }))`: the verb needs a model name, and the only names a row may offer come from that endpoint’s own read. A bare “unload everything” does not exist on this lane, so a button naming nothing has nothing to send.
4. **What changed.** The placeholder is no longer built at all. The `loaded_models` / `loaded_at` read moved above the read-now control (`lib/client.js:3211-3214`) and the read-now hover carries the two cases in the words the old control used: “this endpoint’s engine reported nothing loaded on the last read … there is no model on this engine to evict” when a read answered empty, and “the panel has not read what this endpoint’s engine has loaded, and nothing here is unloaded on a guess” when it was never made (`:3224-3232`, the reasoning written into the comment at `:3256-3265`).
5. **The grey that stays is the honest one and it was not touched.** A row whose endpoint holds a running job greys the per-model controls and names the row it protects (`:3275`, `:3281`): a temporary refusal with a real reason behind it. The earlier ruling on this same control — “either work and be functional, or removed” (T-651) — was answered by making the per-model control work (T-653); this card removes the one case in which it could never work.
6. **Two live pins moved with the design, `tests/ui_state.test.cjs:8242-8252`.** One asserted the row list `unload | unload whisper_large` after an unload; it is now `unload whisper_large`, because the emptied row builds nothing. The other asserted the grey control’s hover; it now asserts that NO bare `unload` control is built and that the two truths are still told apart, on the read-now hover. Both carry dated CONTRACT CHANGE notes naming q43 and the operator’s sentence.
7. **Test run.** Full `npm test`: `FULL_RC=0`, 5 486 PASS, 0 FAIL, 26 suite summaries — the same counts the T-726 baseline produced. The first run of this pass failed exactly those two checks, and its log is kept (`deepamp-audio/scratch/npmtest_20261106_no_dead_unload.log`) because it is the evidence that the pins were live rather than decorative.
8. **The cost is named, because this group has ruled against it before.** The read-now hover grew: the panel’s longest hover measures 10 lines / 139 words / 755 chars where the baseline measured 9 / 129 / 695 (`tests/tooltips.test.cjs` prints this as a measure, not a failure). T-687 and q35 both pushed the other way — a control explains itself on hover, not by wearing a paragraph. The shorter form is to state the empty state on the row and keep the hover to one clause; that is the operator’s call and it stays open.
9. **Live status, and what is ruled but not run.** Client-only: `lib/client.js` 26 268 → 26 271 lines, `node --check` clean; a browser refresh shows it and no restart was taken. Held for its own turn: q44 — the plugin remembers an engine’s 403 “dynamic model management is disabled” per lane for the life of the process (`lib/index.js:12801`, never cleared; the live read of 04:2x Berlin showed `mgmt_disabled: {tts:false, stt:false}`) and that memory is to clear on any non-403 engine answer. That half is host-side and needs its own restart OK.

## Closed 2026-11-05 (Berlin) — the split-flap board prints one flip as two bands that meet at the moving edge: the card that showed two letters at once is gone

1. **Ran on the operator’s word, verbatim** (the WM-31 group of 2026-11-05, its item 8): “flip clock faces: fix/optimise 'drop of letters'”. The symptom as the operator named it is one card showing two letters at the same time while a digit is changing.
2. **What the board is, read before anything was touched.** `scopeFlapFace681()` draws the split-flap clock face; a digit change runs a drum (`scopeFlapDrum681()`) over `FLAP_FRAMES681 = 8` frames and may pass through up to `FLAP_MAX_FACES681 = 3` intermediate faces; `scopeFlapPrint684()` prints INK ONLY — a glyph, never a card-coloured fill.
3. **Why this is a defect and not a design question, and why it needed no ruling.** The comment above the print already stated the occlusion rule — the arriving card covers the face that is leaving — and the code carried out only half of it: the arriving face was clipped to the band it had covered, the leaving face was printed whole. Because the print carries no card fill, both glyphs stayed fully visible for the length of a flip, which is the shape the operator described. A rule the code already states is fixed, not discussed.
4. **What changed, `lib/client.js:20994-21007`.** Both prints are now bounded by one edge: `edgeH681` is the band the arriving card has covered at this frame, `edgeY681` is the moving edge itself. The face that is leaving is clipped to the band BELOW that edge, the arriving face to the band ABOVE it. The two bands meet at the edge and together tile the card, and neither glyph is stretched — a glyph that shrinks would be a lying glyph, so this is a clip and not a scale.
5. **The seam and the edge are now the same number.** The moving-edge lines at `:21009-21014` draw at the hoisted `edgeY681` — the boundary the two clips already meet at — instead of computing it a second time. Nothing else in the face moved.
6. **What was not touched, and what stays the operator’s.** The flip’s speed (`FLAP_FRAMES681`), how many intermediate faces it may show (`FLAP_MAX_FACES681`), the drum, the card geometry, both board palettes, the seam drawn at the foot of the module loop, and the other clock faces are unchanged. How fast a flip should read, and whether the drum should show more or fewer faces, is a visual judgement this card does not make; the two knobs are named so that it can be made with them.
7. **Test side, the stub in `tests/scope.test.cjs`:** the clip a drawing is under is now part of the drawing. `rect` keeps the path it was given (`:140`), `clip()` adopts it (`:141`), `beginPath` clears it (`:143`), `save` and `restore` push and pop it (`:98-99`), and every `fillText` records the band it printed under as an appended ninth field (`:129-132`). The appended field is safe because no older check indexes past index 7 of that record. Only one `g.rect(` call exists in `lib/client.js` — the flip path — so the tracking touches no other drawing.
8. **The new check, `tests/scope.test.cjs:2562-2595`, measures a real flip rather than a shape.** It reuses the window the T-684 drum-cap check already drives — a stubbed clock moved by five minutes, `b.frames(40)` — pairs the prints that share a card, and for every frame requires that the two bands meet, that they tile that card from its top edge to its bottom edge with no gap and no overlap, and that both faces are never whole at once. Measured on this run: 32 flip frames, 0 bad frames. The gate refuses a vacuous pass (`frames >= 8`), and the T-684 check that window comes from still passes.
9. **Test run.** `node tests/scope.test.cjs` 389 / 0 against a baseline of 388 plus this one check. Then the full chain: `npm test` → `FULL_RC=0`, 0 FAIL, 5 485 PASS against the previous 5 484, and 26 per-suite summaries byte-identical except the scope line 388 → 389. The only difference in the whole tree is this check and the code it measures. Log: `audio-play-cordis/scratch/npmtest_20261105_flip_occlusion.log`.
10. **Live status.** Client-only: `lib/client.js` 26 251 → 26 262 lines, `node --check` clean; a browser refresh is what shows it, and no restart was taken or claimed. Copies before the change: `audio-play-cordis/scratch/deepamp-audio_lib_client.js.bak_20261105_pre_flip_occlusion` and `audio-play-cordis/scratch/deepamp-audio_tests_scope.test.cjs.bak_20261105_pre_flip_occlusion`. Nothing was deleted anywhere.
11. **The tracker, and what this row does not close.** Root `TODOS.md` WM-31 item 8 carries this run. The thin-line half of item 7 is the next row of that group that needs no ruling; the “fix 'unload'” half of item 7 stays unrun because what is wrong with that control has not been described. Items 1-6 of the group are unchanged by this card.

## Closed 2026-11-05 (Berlin) — the manifest now names the harness it needs: an `engines.dsh` floor with no ceiling, a cordis peer, and the schemastery range moved to the harness minor

1. **Ran on the operator's word, twice.** The install contract first: "Do 1" — git-first, the repository created later in this subfolder and pushed by the operator by hand, another user's install being a git spec rather than an Update. Then the gate: "do 1 - but only gate against lower versions, higher versions should be ok usually". No repository is created by this card.
2. **Why a git-installed bundle has no Update button, from the manager's own text.** `listBundles` marks a bundle updatable only for "a third-party profile dependency saved as a registry spec under its own name"; `listVersions` asks a registry with `pnpm view <name> versions time dist-tags` and `updateBundle` installs `name@version` from the registry that answered. A repository has no version list — `git ls-remote` appears only as a reachability pre-check — so an update over git is a re-pointed spec, which is the manual model the operator asked for.
3. **House style measured before anything was written.** No official bundle in the installed tree declares `engines.dsh`; the only `engines` blocks in it are `node` ranges, `@deepseek-ai/dsh` itself at `node >=24.9.0`. Official packages gate by peer name — `@deepseek-ai/cordis ~4.1.0` plus exact-version peers on the `dsh-*` packages they import — and keep `@deepseek-ai/schemastery ~3.19.0` as a plain dependency.
4. **Why DEEPAMP cannot copy that form, measured.** It imports exactly one harness package, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (`lib/index.js:110`, `tools/index.js:31`). Cordis reaches it only as the context the Loader passes (29 `ctx.` uses, no import), and the client half imports nothing external. Peers on `dsh-*` packages this plugin never imports would be a false declaration, and peers cannot state a DSH version for a package that imports no DSH package — `engines.dsh` is the field the manager reads for exactly that case.
5. **Written, in the operator's own shape.** `"engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.2-rc.1" }` — a floor, no ceiling — plus `"peerDependencies": { "@deepseek-ai/cordis": "~4.1.0" }`, and the existing dependency moved from `~3.18.5` to `~3.19.0`, the minor the official packages carry. `private: true` stays: this release is installed by git, not published. `name` and `version` are untouched, which is what the T-519 manifest tests compare. The file went 33 lines to 39.
6. **What a declared gate does at install.** An unmet range or peer stops with `incompatible-version`, naming each unmet requirement keyed `engines.dsh` or by peer package name, and the CLI prints the exact override `dsh plugin --profile <profile> allow-version <package@version> --dsh-version <runtime> --accept-risk`. A git or tarball spec is judged after installation from these fields, and the manager restores the profile manifest and lockfile when the requirement is unmet.
7. **What is on disk and does not match the new range, stated plainly.** `deepamp-audio/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/schemastery` is a vendored pnpm symlink to `3.18.5`, installed 2026-11-03 when this tree was copied, and Node resolves the import from it — so the running host still uses 3.18.5 while the manifest now asks for `~3.19.0`. Nothing was installed to close that: an install changes a live runtime dependency, and a changed runtime dependency needs a harness restart with its own OK. It is a leftover of this host, not something a fresh install from the repository would inherit.
8. **Verification.** The manifest parses and answers the three fields written. The two suites that read the manifest pass unchanged: `tests/host.test.cjs` 2317 pass 0 fail, `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` 1034 pass 0 fail. No other suite reads the manifest, and no `lib/` or `tools/` file was touched. Copy before the change: `audio-play-cordis/scratch/deepamp-audio_package.json.bak_20261105_pre_manifest_gate`. Nothing deleted, nothing installed, no profile change, no restart.
9. **Tracker.** `TODOS.md` WM-29 item 5, the `engines.dsh` / peer question open since 2026-10-28, is closed by this card; the git-first contract and the manual-push model are recorded on `TODOS.md` WM-30 item 6.

- **What is declared** (`lib/index.js:110`, beside `apply`): `store_dir`, `specs_dir`, `ytdlp_path`, `tts_dir`, `job_timeout_sec`, `generation_ceiling_s`, `perf_log`, `import_outside_store`, `takes_limit {mode, max_bytes}`, `stt_feed {mode, rate, channels}`. Every field is optional, so a patch row with no `config:` block activates exactly as this bundle did before this card. A `config:` block goes on the `audio-play-host` row of `cordis.patch.yml`; the Loader replaces a row's `config` wholesale and never deep-merges it.
- **Measured about the schema library, tested against the installed package rather than assumed:** an absent key is accepted (a field is optional unless `.required()`); a value of the wrong type is refused and names the key (`$.job_timeout_sec expected number but got x`); an unknown key is NOT rejected; there are no numeric constraint builders (`.integer/.ge/.le/.minimum/.maximum` are undefined on a number schema); an absent NESTED object arrives as `{}`. So the schema carries TYPES only, every declared value is revalidated in code by the same checks that revalidate state.json, and an unknown declared key is named in the boot audit instead of silently doing nothing.
- **Precedence, implemented:** env > Config > state.json > code default. Env is offered only for the three paths (`AUDIO_PLAY_STORE_DIR`, `AUDIO_PLAY_SPECS_DIR`, `AUDIO_PLAY_YTDLP_PATH`), following the pattern `AUDIO_PLAY_MAX_JOBS_PER_HOST` already sets. The store root is resolved before `TTS_DIR`, `STATE_FILE` and `PERF_FILE` are derived from it. A declared `specs_dir` is put in FRONT of the candidate list and the two paths this plugin has always tried stay behind it as fallbacks. Nothing is migrated: pointing the plugin at another root leaves the old files where they are.
- **What state.json no longer records:** a key the Config or the environment holds. The eight persist rows keep the "written only when it differs from the code default" rule as their ELSE branch, and the value the file already carried is written back unchanged. Removing a Config line therefore removes the value with it, and the state file stays a record of what this plugin's own verbs were asked to change.
- **The boot audit:** one `config_declared` record, only when something was declared, refused or unknown — the keys, where each came from, what was refused, and the keys that have no knob. An instance given nothing writes nothing.
- **Tests.** `host.test.cjs` 2301 pass / 0 fail, 25 of them new T-716 cases: the schema itself, every default standing when no config is given, declared values being the values the host runs with, an out-of-range declared value held to the same gate the panel gate uses, precedence over a seeded state file, a held key not being written while a change the plugin was asked to make still is, env over Config, the specs probe order, the boot audit, and the shape the loader actually hands `apply` (measured in the installed cordis core: `resolveConfig` validates through `Config['~standard'].validate`, then `runtime.callback(this.ctx, this.config)`). ## Closed on 2026-11-03 05:2x–06:3x Berlin (1 card) — a slot that names a session now speaks that session, or says why it said nothing

### T-713  an autoplay slot was bound to a session this harness is not running and went on generating for the CURRENT session — BUILT 2026-11-03 on both planes; **the host half is LIVE since the operator's restart at 06:26 Berlin ("restart is done"); one browser reload is still owed for the client half — the same single reload already owed for T-705 and T-683, not a second one; and that slot has to be re-bound in its picker or cleared, which its binding was already dead before the restart.**
- The operator's words, verbatim: "another small bug, i had slot1 for auto play enabled, but on harness restart or reload - it seems it lost the session name - instead the dropdown shows session-e5... which seems to resulted in triggering generations for current session instead".
- **Two facts, both measured.** A slot's binding is a session id in the browser's own store (`audio-play:autospeak.slots`); it outlives a reload and it outlives a restart — what does not survive is the harness **holding** that session. And `handleLastAgentMessage` resolved a named-but-unknown id to the newest root session: `{"session_id":"session-doesnotexist123"}` answered `ok:true` with this session's last message. The dropdown printed the bare id for two states that look identical and are not ("the id is not in the list" / "the list was never read").
- **Verified after the operator's restart, 06:2x Berlin.** The refusal answers: the same request now returns `ok:false` with no session substituted; a request naming **no** id still gets the newest session; `sessions_list` still answers `session-8cd723b2-…` — the same id as before the restart, which is what makes the next line necessary. And the operator's shape was found on disk: this workspace's harness session store holds 230 `session-*` entries and exactly two begin `session-e5` — `session-e576ef88-…` (last used 2026-09-11) and `session-e5e023f6-…` (last used 2026-10-22) — both refused today. The slot was bound to an old, persisted, not-running session, and it was already unresolvable before any restart.
- **The claim this card carried at 05:2x is SUPERSEDED by that measurement**: "a harness restart ends every live session, so the session id is gone". It is false as stated, and it was written into the first version of the refusal text as well. Both are corrected in the code and in the card; the built behaviour is unchanged.
- **Host (`lib/index.js`):** a named id that does not resolve is refused — `no such session: <id> (this harness is not running that session - an id belongs to a session only while the harness has it; send no session_id to ask for the newest session instead)`. The newest-session answer stays reserved for a request that names no id, which is what the "(newest session)" option means. The corrected wording in the parenthetical goes live at the next restart; the refusal is live now.
- **Client (`lib/client.js`):** `slotSessionGone713` is the only place that decides a dead binding — it answers `""` when the list was never read, because that is not a fact about the session. The auto-poll and the slot's triangle both compare the answer's own `session` with the slot's `sid` before anything is dispatched; on a mismatch the slot's sequence baseline is DELETED rather than advanced, so a re-bind re-primes instead of comparing a number that came from another session, and the reason is stated once per (slot, id). The picker option now reads "saved session is gone" or "saved (session list not read)"; the fact goes on the existing `audio-play-slot-warn419` line, BESIDE the pin sentence and not inside `slotProblem419`, which is a statement about a PIN and returns `""` for the unpinned slot the operator was actually using. `sessions_list` is fetched on mount when, and only when, a slot carries an id.
- **The operator's ruling on the client half was "Refuse to speak, say why"** — stay silent, keep the slot armed, put it on the slot's amber line. That is what the code does.
- **Tests.** `host.test.cjs` 2276 pass / 0 fail: the old pin read the fault back to us — "unknown id -> falls back to list", `ok:true`, `session: root-1` — and now asserts the refusal, with the no-id case untouched. `ui_state.test.cjs` 1035 pass / 0 fail, +8 checks: the dead binding is labelled and the list is read on mount; an unread list does NOT claim the session is gone; a live binding is untouched; the poll guard measured over two real polls with its paired control on the same fixture (matching session → it does speak); the triangle on both sides. The suite's shared stub gained `sessions_list` and `last_agent_message` arms behind switches, both defaults behaviour-neutral for every older block. After the restart measurement one hover pin was re-pointed, with a dated comment naming the measurement it replaced. `node --check` clean on `lib/index.js`, `lib/client.js` and both test files.
- **No copy of `lib/index.js` or `lib/client.js` was taken before this change, and this card says that rather than implying one.** Nothing was measured on the audio lane and no job was placed on a fleet endpoint. ### T-684 addendum 2  the flip board's three rulings — BUILT (2026-10-29, client half, one browser reload owed)
- The operator's words, verbatim: "i think it needs to be vertically centered, the numbers are currently not
  center, that looks off"; "the number cards need a 1 pixel hoirontal line in the middle of the numbers to show
  it's a top and bottom half"; "we should add the same version in in inverted black on white setting - either as a
  4th mode or color set" — the last one scoped by their answer to **a fourth face in the walk**, not a colour
  setting on a face.
- (a) **The centring, and what was wrong with it.** `scopeFlapPrint684` placed the baseline by the ratio the
  geometry was built from — the card's middle PLUS half the cap height — and that centres the **em box**, not the
  ink. The card is sized from two ASSUMED ratios of the panel's monospace face (`FLAP_CAP684 = 0.73`,
  `FLAP_ADV684 = 0.60`), and the only way to know whether those assumptions are true for the browser rendering the
  panel is to ask the canvas. The print now measures the glyph it is about to print
  (`actualBoundingBoxAscent` / `actualBoundingBoxDescent`), sets the font BEFORE measuring — the first build asked
  for a width while the font was still whatever the last draw had left on the context, which is a measurement of
  the wrong face — fits the glyph to the card in both directions (width, and new: height, against the card's own
  cap height, which stays the authority the board is built from), and places the baseline so the middle of the ink
  lands on the middle of the card: `baseY = mid + (ascent - descent) / 2`. The ratio stays as the fallback for a
  canvas that cannot measure, and a metric that is not a plausible digit height is rejected rather than trusted.
- (b) **The seam.** `FLAP_SPLIT681` was declared once and left TRANSPARENT — `#05070800` is that colour with an
  alpha of `00` — and the line was drawn in the CARD's own colour BEFORE the print, so a glyph covering the middle
  of the card simply painted over it. That is why the operator saw no split line at all. The constant now has its
  own ink (`#394143` dark, `#8f9799` light) and the seam is drawn at the foot of the module loop, AFTER the print
  and after the flip's moving-edge lines, one pixel tall at the card's own middle — the same line the hinge nicks
  at each edge already sit on.
- (c) **The fourth face.** `CLOCK_MODES681` is now `["clock_led", "clock_nixie", "clock_flap",
  "clock_flap_light"]`, with its label ("clock — split-flap board, black on white") and its box word ("flip
  white"). It joins AFTER `clock_flap`, so the press order of everything already in the ring keeps its position and
  only the wrap moves — the same rule T-601 and T-677 used when they joined. The two boards are ONE board: the
  palette is one table keyed by the face word (`FLAP_PAL689` — a face that asks for its colours by name cannot be
  handed the other face's colours), and every question that is NOT about colour — the four modules, the drum, the
  clip, the frames, the animation gate — asks one predicate, `scopeFlapWord689`, used by the draw loop's gate and
  the router alike. A second word for the same board is exactly the shape of bug T-611 was.
- Measured: `tests/scope.test.cjs` **385 pass, 0 fail** with three new checks — the ink centring (for every printed
  digit, the middle of the ink the canvas reported lands within one pixel of the middle of the card, the ink stays
  inside the card, and when the canvas reports a face the assumed ratio does not have, the print is fitted to the
  card, the shrink measured off the recorded font); the seam (present on every card, one pixel, at the card's
  middle, in an ink that is not the card's, and drawn AFTER the print — measured off the drawing ORDER, for which
  the stub now carries a shared counter in both of its logs, since a suite that keeps a rect log and a text log
  separately cannot see a z-order across them); and the fourth face (the walk moves to `clock_flap_light`, prints
  the same four modules dark-on-white with its own seam, and draws none of the dark board's ink anywhere). The stub
  deliberately reports `0.78` of the em as the ink height, which is NOT the `0.73` the client assumes — that
  disagreement is the case the build has to survive, and it is why the centring check would have failed against the
  old arithmetic. Four older clock pins were re-pointed with dated comments (the ring literal with four words, the
  two "no clock word in this store / in the visualizer table" lists, and the wrap, now reached from the inverted
  board).
- Full client loop after the change (logs `/tmp/t689c_<suite>.log`): scope 385/0, ui_state 1022/0, transport 115/0,
  shut 68/0, stream_overlap 137/0, crossfade603 72/0, flow 89/0, endpoint_exclusivity 125/0, engine_boot 99/0,

was a white box around near-white cards. Measured: `tests/scope.test.cjs` **388 pass, 0 fail** — the fixture answers
the read through `document.body` (`#12171a`) and the new pin asserts the last full-box fill of that face is the read

## Closed on 2026-10-13 (13 cards)

### T-309 — the eject button becomes the door for local files and remote streams (long-term, TRACKED, NOT DONE)
### The user's words (2026-10-13, 06:20)
1. Eject stops being a dead button and becomes an **open** control: a small menu spawned **at the mouse pointer**,
   not centred in the panel.
2. Three choices:
   1. **Open a file from the DSH host file system** — a window to type a path.
   2. **Upload a file from the browser's own file system** — a real `<input type="file">` picker.
   3. **Open a stream and listen to it** — Shoutcast / remote MP3, with the same transport driving it.
3. "security sanitation of stream input" is the load-bearing part of 3.1.3 and must be spelled out before anything
   is built: the URL is validated (scheme allow-list, no `file:`, no `javascript:`, no loopback or link-local
   target, no credentials smuggled into the URL), the response is checked by content type rather than by the URL's
   extension, size and duration are bounded, redirects are re-validated, and nothing from the stream is ever
   written to disk or passed to a shell.
4. "should rely on existing lib (no pull into python parser)" — the playback leg is the browser's own `<audio>`
   element, which already plays a remote URL; the plugin's job is validation and the queue entry, not a decoder.
   No new audio parsing dependency is to be added.
1. The transport queue takes **URLs** (`queuePlayback(url, label, force)` ✓, [lib/client.js:5377](lib/client.js#L5377)),
   and every URL it is handed today is a plugin route (`/audio-play/<id>…`). A remote stream is not a plugin
   route, so the queue needs a source kind rather than a URL prefix guess.
2. A browser file picker gives a **File object**, not a path. The panel already has the upload leg
   (`upload_audio` ✓, used by the dictation path ✓, [lib/client.js:5530](lib/client.js#L5530)) — that is the
   existing lib this should ride, not a new one.
3. A host path is a **host-side** capability: it needs a new verb in `lib/index.js` (a read-only listing / stat
   under an allow-listed root ✓), which means a harness restart, which means its own explicit user OK.
4. The panel is a floating window with no menu primitive; a pointer-positioned submenu is a new UI shape in this
   plugin and has to respect the two rules already on the books — no horizontal scrollbar out of the panel
   (T-199 / T-219 ✓) and the panel's own z-index budget.
5. The visualizer taps the `<audio>` element, so a remote stream WOULD drive the analyser for free — the tap is
   the same tap ([lib/client.js:7412-L7422](lib/client.js#L7412-L7422)). Worth stating in the design so nobody builds
   a second analyser.

### T-314 — the eject button reverts to the pinned slot voice instead of the selected voice (user 2026-10-13 06:52, DONE)
1. The user's words: "if i use the eject button to currently schedule the agent output from current session into
   tts, it always reverts to use data instead of worf - if worf is currently selected as voice - it should use
   worf, it might be using the settings from slot1 'pinned · qwen3-tts · ent_data_ref30'".
