   ([lib/client.js:5649-L5652](lib/client.js#L5649-L5652)), so slot 1's pin (`qwen3-tts` + `ent_data_ref30`)
   shadowed whatever voice the panel was currently showing. The eject action routes through `speakLastMessage()`
   which had no way to override the pin.
3. Fix as applied: `speakNow(i, forced)` now takes a forced-settings argument
   ([lib/client.js:~5654](lib/client.js#L5654)), and `speakLastMessage()` passes the **current panel selection**
   — `selModelRef` / `selVoiceRef` / `styleTextRef` — falling back to the slot's own resolution only when no model
   is selected ([lib/client.js:5681-L5686](lib/client.js#L5681-L5686)).
4. Decision recorded: **pinning stays correct for slot auto-speak.** A slot's own "speak now" still honours its
   pin. Only the **transport eject** — a panel action, not a slot action — follows the current selection, which is
   what its hover text already promised ("with the selected TTS model").

### T-315 — a playlist row wrapped when the host tag text got long (user 2026-10-13, FIXED)
1. The user's words: "we still have playlist item line wrap if the host tag gets a longer text like 'machine
   cpu2.test at c...' -> shorten tag strings accordingly, should not bloat tag".
2. Root cause, measured rather than assumed: the machine-wait chip read `machine cpu2.test at cap` — about
   **135 px** at the panel's 9px monospace chip face, against the **132 px** cap T-307 gave every amber wait

### T-317 — the Auto-refresh setting was used but never kept (user 2026-10-13, DONE)
**Status: DONE. It is persisted now, in the panel's own guarded store, with 8 new assertions in
[tests/selection_memory.test.cjs](tests/selection_memory.test.cjs) (43 → 51). Needs a browser refresh to see it.**
1. **It is used.** `autoRefresh` keys the status poller: `if (!timer || ... || autoRefresh <= 0) return;`
   ([lib/client.js:5789](lib/client.js#L5789)), the interval is built from it
   ([lib/client.js:5814-L5817](lib/client.js#L5814-L5817)), and `0 = off` is honoured. The Settings field writes
   it ([lib/client.js:8891](lib/client.js#L8891)). So the setting is live, not dead.
2. **It was not persisted.** It was a plain `React.useState(5000)` with no `localStorage` read or write — unlike
   the panel's other preferences (`audio-play:scope.mode`, the shut state, size, position, model/voice selection,
   auto-slots). A browser refresh threw away whatever the user set and returned to 5000 ms.
3. **Applied (2026-10-13): it is persisted, under the same guard every other key uses.**
   1. New key `audio-play:autorefresh` with `autoRefreshFromStore317()`
      ([lib/client.js:607-L616](lib/client.js#L607-L616)): a value that is not a number, is negative, or exceeds
      `AUTOREFRESH_MAX317` (3600000 ms — one hour; past that a panel is stalled, not paced) is NOT applied and the
      default answers instead, exactly like every other guarded key. `0` is a LEGAL cadence and is stored as `0`,
      so "polling off" is never mistaken for "nothing was stored" (which is what a falsy test would have done).
   2. Boot reads it: `React.useState(autoRefreshFromStore317())` ([lib/client.js:4384](lib/client.js#L4384)).
   3. The Settings input writes it and clamps to the SAME ceiling boot refuses
      ([lib/client.js:9163-L9170](lib/client.js#L9163-L9170)), so what a person types and what the next page
      restores cannot disagree. Its hover and its hint line now say the value is saved.
   4. Pinned by 8 assertions: nothing stored → 5000; `12000` → restored; `0` → restored as 0; `nonsense` →
      default; `99999999999` → refused; editing the input WRITES the store; the next page starts at the typed
      number; the input clamps to the ceiling. The edit is driven on the same boot it belongs to, because every
      boot installs its own store — an edit driven later would land in a later page's store and prove nothing.

### T-323 — a playlist row can now hand its own words to the next generation (user 2026-10-13 10:2x, DONE)
**Status: DONE in `lib/client.js`. Needs a browser refresh.**
### The user's words
1. **A `reuse` button on the row** ([lib/client.js:3753-L3763](lib/client.js#L3753-L3763)), rendered only when the
   row actually HAS words. The hover names which words it is about to hand over — "this row's transcript" or "this
   row's generation text" — and how long they are, so the choice is visible before the click.
2. **The handler** ([lib/client.js:6830-L6845](lib/client.js#L6830-L6845)). A row already carries both halves the
   user named: `text` is what was sent to the engine for a generation, `transcript` is what came back out of an STT
   / diar / speaker-ASR row. Transcript wins when a row has one, because those are the words the person is actually
   listening to. It **replaces** the "Text to read aloud" field rather than appending to it: "reuse this one" is a
   substitution, and appending would silently double a line that is already sitting in front of them. A row with no
   words changes nothing and says so. It dispatches nothing — the take is still the person's decision.
3. **Wired through the same prop path as `retry`** ([lib/client.js:8968-L8969](lib/client.js#L8968-L8969)), so the
   row handlers stay one family: play, stems, cancel, retry, reuse.
The user's parenthetical "(add to redo todo of dialouge area)" is recorded here as **T-323b, OPEN**: the Text and
dialogue section (the Scene / batch composer, `SceneComposer`, T-298 / T-266 / T-297) has the same need in a
different shape. There the unit is a line with a speaker name, not one text field, so "reuse this row's words" has
to decide which speaker the line is re-aimed at before it can drop the text into the composer. That is a design
decision about the dialogue editor, not a copy of this button, so it is listed rather than guessed at.

The user's word: "later we have to update our leanings about right separation model for workflows". Recorded as an
open item so the rewrite is grounded in what was measured rather than in the older preference. What is on the table,
each of it from this session:
1. **Both roformers return exactly two named outputs** — `vocals` and `instrumental`, the second derived as
   mixture-minus-vocals (`<home>/gits/audio.cpp/src/models/roformer/session.cpp:350-351`) — which is the shape
   a voice-sample workflow wants. htdemucs is the multi-stem family and is the wrong tool for a voices/non-voices
   split.
2. **mel_band_roformer f16 is about twice as fast as bs_roformer q8_0 on these CPU engines**: 534 477 ms on a 20 s
   chunk versus a bs_roformer job cancelled at 1081 s on the same chunk without finishing. Model load is
   1554-3645 ms in both cases, so the whole cost is the separation stage. That reverses what this workspace has
   been assuming, and the assumption is what has been routing sample work to bs_roformer. **Measured later the same
   day, and better: `mel_band_roformer_q8` did the same chunk in 421 457 ms — 21 % faster than f16 and half the
   shelf footprint — so the default the guidance now carries is `mel_band_roformer_q8`, not f16.**
3. **The sample rate is a hard contract**: a 48 kHz master was refused twice with `RoFormer prepare() sample rate
   mismatch: expected 44100, got 48000`. A workflow needs a 44100 master for separation and may keep 48 kHz only
   for the samples it cuts afterwards.
4. **WRONG WHEN WRITTEN, corrected in place:** "there is no smaller roformer quant on this fleet" was true of the
   shelf and false of the catalog. Each CPU engine declared exactly four separation entries (`bs_roformer` q8_0,
   `mel_band_roformer` f16, `htdemucs_q8`, `htdemucs_f16`) because that is what the server JSON listed, not because
   nothing smaller exists. `audio.cpp/tools/model_manager_v2.py` carries `mel_band_roformer_q8_0` (251 748 928 B),
   `htdemucs_6stems_q8_0` (42 477 600 B) and `tf_gridnet_wsj0_2mix_f32` (32 792 096 B), and `mel_band_roformer_q8`
   is now installed on the shelf and configured on both CPU engines. The lesson is that "what the fleet has" has to
   be read from the install catalog plus the config, not from one running engine's model list.
5. **Cost scales with the length of the window, not the amount of speech in it**, which is why splitting a 257 s
   scene into three windows that run on two engines is the only lever that exists without new assets.
6. **Never route separation to the Vulkan lane** (`e-3` / `e-4`, `vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost` history).
7. **A model slot is not released by cancelling a job**, so a workflow that mixes separation with voice design has

### T-326 (2026-10-13, DONE, client-side): the composer can import a diarisation as a multi-speaker script
User request: "for the multi-speaker handling, it would be nice if we could re-translate the multi-speaker
transcriptions into multi-speaker scripts". Implemented in the panel, not only in the script, because the scene text
already lives in the composer and a person should not have to leave it to turn a diarisation into a scene.
1. **What it does.** A new control under the T-323b reuse block: a select over the playlist rows that carry
   diarised turns WITH words, and a button that appends them as `NAME: line`s. The names are the diar labels
   (`speaker_0`, `speaker_1`...), which pass the composer's own NAME regex, and the composer's existing cast rename
   is where a label becomes a voice. Nothing is invented: a label is never renamed to a person by guessing.
2. **The rules match `scripts/transcript_to_script.py` on purpose**, because a user can reach the same result either
   way: adjacent turns by the same speaker are joined into one line only when nothing else spoke between them and the
   gap is 2 s or less, because a diar splits a monologue for acoustic reasons and a script that re-announces the name
   on every turn reads like a stutter.
3. **Rows that cannot become a script are not offered.** A plain diarisation has spans and no text - a script needs
   words - so it is excluded. A diarisation still running is excluded even if it already carries words. The default is
   the NEWEST finished row with words, and an older row can still be picked from the select.
4. **The renderer's ceiling is stated before the import, in the hover, not discovered after it**, and importing a
   five-speaker diarisation warns and writes all five lines. A warning is not a truncation.
5. **Append, never replace**, for the same reason T-323b appends: the composer holds a whole scene.
6. **Test board: `tests/scene_composer.test.cjs` 30 -> 45 checks, all passing**, and the whole client board is green
   (actions 118, effects 4, endpoint_exclusivity 69, engine_boot 99, event_log 31, flow 78, model_library 29, render
   166, scene_composer 45, scope 103, selection_memory 51, shell_safety 31, shut 54, tooltips 12, transparency 19,
   transport 43, ui_state 403). Client-only change: a browser refresh, no harness restart.
7. **One fixture lesson recorded.** The first version of the fixtures failed 6 of the new checks for a reason that was
   the test's own bug, not the feature's: the rich four-turn row was not the newest row by id, so the default import
   source was the five-speaker row and the merge checks measured the wrong input. Renaming it to the highest id made
   all 45 pass. Also deliberate: the diarisation fixtures carry their words in `speaker_turns` and NOT in a flat
   `transcript`, so the T-323b reuse checks and the T-326 import checks each measure one affordance instead of one
   quietly stealing the other's fixture.

### T-331 (2026-10-13 12:5x, DONE client-side, browser refresh only): the read-out names the file, and a voice pick sits beside the record button
1. **The read-out is now the file's provenance while a file plays.** The line (`audio-play-lane-read`) used to print
   `selModel.tts · selVoice.tts`, which the panel itself described as "what the next dispatch would use" - a
   statement about the future, printed under a file that had already been made. It now reads the row the playing
   route belongs to and prints that row's `model` and `voice`, or its `batch_cast` for a scene part, or its
   `task_kind` for a tool row where no voice is involved. The hover says the whole thing: "what this file was made
   with: m1 · voice voy_doctor · task tts · row ap-1003 · the panel's current selection is not this file's
   provenance", and for a source or stem route it adds that the file was not generated by a voice at all. Only when
   nothing is playing does the line fall back to the selection, and its hover then says "nothing is playing, so this
   is what the NEXT dispatch would use". The two states are also coloured differently (provenance #c9d1d9,
   selection #8b949e) so a glance tells them apart.
2. **Finding the row needed one new rule, and it is a real improvement, not a workaround.** The ticker already
   resolves the playing row to print its position and its words, but it matched only on `row.route_url` / `row.url`.
   A route IS the row - `/audio-play/<id>`, with `?src=1` or `?stem=<id>` on it - so the id is now read off the
   route and matched against `row.id` as well. Without that, a row whose payload carries no `route_url` silently
   produced the fallback read-out while a file of that row was playing: a provenance line lying about the file.
3. **The voice pick.** A `<select>` sits immediately to the right of the record button, in the Winamp transport
   cluster. Its options come from the same three sources the TTS box uses (client.js:2511-2536): the per-model list
   the panel last fetched, every name in the plugin voice store, and the selected model's built-in speakers. The
   "no voice" option is present but disabled on a clone-only model, using the same gate as the TTS box's own
   dropdown (client.js:2491), so the two controls cannot disagree about what a model accepts. It writes through
   `onSelectVoice` (client.js:6870) - the very path the library and the voices section use - so it changes the
   selection and dispatches nothing. It is disabled while no model is selected, because a control that changes a
   selection no dispatch would use is not a control.
4. **Tests: transport 43 -> 50, and two other assertions were corrected rather than deleted.** The new checks are:
   the row is exactly the seven Winamp glyphs plus the pick, with the pick LAST and directly after `● Rec`; the pick
   is disabled with no model selected; its hover says whose voices it offers; the read-out while a file plays is
   that file's model and voice and not a blob; its hover names the row and says the current selection is not this
   file's provenance; reading provenance dispatches nothing; and changing the pick changes the selection the panel
   shows while asking the fleet for nothing.
   The correction that matters for the record: **two existing assertions passed only because the row was never
   resolved.** `ui_state` ("header names the auto-played row after ended") and `scope` ("once the take has peaks the
   strip stops explaining") both required the job id to appear in the status line, and it appeared there only
   because the fixtures carry no `route_url`, so the panel fell back to printing the label. With the row now
   identified from the route, the line speaks the take - which is exactly what T-307 asked for ("the line speaks the
   take, not its ordinal") - and the id lives in the hover, where T-307 also put it. Both assertions now require
   the take on the line, the id on the hover, and the FINISHED marker, and the reason for the change is written in
   the test file itself. Nothing was weakened: the same facts are required, from the places the panel actually
   puts them.
5. **Board after the change:** actions 124, effects 4, endpoint_exclusivity 69, engine_boot 99, event_log 31, flow

   since T-244 and the panel never printed it, so a lane-paused row looked like a row merely waiting its turn. It
   now carries its own chip: `tts lane paused` / `stt lane paused`, amber when a person paused the lane, red when

   machine wait beside it.

   itself: paused **by the plugin** after repeated engine failures (with the way back — press check, then resume),

   (GET / POST `prefer_primary`, a persisted flag, a queue_status readout) and the panel never exposed it, so
   placement order could only be changed by hand against the API. It sits in Settings under the machine-ceiling
   switch, reads ONCE when Settings opens, POSTs a real boolean on click, and repaints from the answer — including

   the rule and its limits: OFF is node-first with the primary competing in the same group; ON makes a free,

### T-278 PART 4 CLOSED (2026-10-14 03:4x): the Mix and Remux door — T-278 itself is now closed
1. **The ruling, asked as one question.** Where the door goes: the answer was **"one block at the bottom of
   'Text and dialogue'"** — the same shape the engine-options block took. Not row-level doors, not a new
   section. The section count of the open tree stays **7**, which is what `render.test.cjs` T-219 guards.
2. **No host half was needed, so no restart was implied.** `mix_audio` (index.js:12177) and `remux_video`
   (index.js:12305) already exist and are routed (index.js:14853, :14862). Both are **LOCAL ffmpeg steps on
   the host**: no engine, no endpoint, no queue, no new playlist row. Only `lib/client.js` was touched, so a
   browser refresh is enough to see this.
3. **The two contracts, read off the host before writing anything.** A mix takes `bed_job_id` (a playlist row),
   an optional `stem_id` (the bed stem to mix onto — left alone the host guesses by its own bed hint, or takes
   the sole stem, or refuses and names the stems it has), and `layers`: 1..`MIX_LAYER_MAX = 12` entries that are
   either an ok row's id or a safe path under the plugin output tree. Its options are `bed_gain` (0..4),
   `layer_gain` (0..4, one number for every layer because that is what the host's ffmpeg chain does), `rate`
   (0.5..2, atempo on the LAYERS only) and `delay_ms` (-600000..600000). A remux takes `video_path` (a real file
   whose extension is .mp4 .mkv .webm .mov, and the host also checks it really holds a video stream), the audio
   from `audio_job_id` plus an optional `stem_id` (or an `audio_path` the panel does not offer), and options
   `audio_codec` (`aac` re-encode, `copy`) and `trim` (`longest`, `shortest`).
4. **The delay direction is stated, not hidden.** The host cannot move audio earlier (`adelay` has no negative
   side), so a POSITIVE delay delays the layers and a NEGATIVE delay moves the bed later instead. The panel
   says this in the control's hover and reports which side actually moved, taken from the host's own
   `delay_applied_to` field rather than from what it asked for.
5. **Rows the panel offers are rows the host can open.** A bed, a layer and a remux audio source are offered only
   for a row that is `status:'ok'` AND carries an `output_path` or stems — the live `playlist_list` answer does
   carry `output_path` (measured on a live row), and a queued, running or failed row is not offered at all. The
   block says out loud how many rows it can offer, and says "no rendered row yet" when it can offer none.
6. **An untouched option sends nothing.** Every mix and remux option rides only when a person typed it, so the
   host's own default (gain 1, rate 1, delay 0, codec aac, trim longest) is what runs — the same discipline the
   T-352 knobs follow, and the reason the block cannot quietly change a job's sound.
7. **A stem id that is not a stem of the row now picked is dropped, not carried.** A stem pick belongs to the row
   it was read from. `mixStemFor353` checks the id against the picked row's own stems before it rides, for both
   verbs; sending a stale stem would ask the host to mix or dub a file that row does not have.
8. **The layer cap mirrors the host's, and it is visible.** Layer slots stop at 12 — the "add a layer" button
   disappears at the cap instead of offering a 13th the host would refuse. "drop the last layer" removes a slot

9. **A refusal arrives through the rejection path, and the wording says what the panel actually knows.** The

10. **What this block is NOT.** It creates no playlist row (a mix writes a new STEM onto the bed row it mixed and

### T-310 SETTLED and T-347 IMPLEMENTED (2026-10-14 00:4x, client-only): while dictating, the strip reads the microphone
1. **The ruling (user 2026-10-14 00:4x, verbatim):** "during dictation, we already read the microphone, so the same
   stream has to be used for the visualizer and the file creation, the dot matrix timer should turn amber-red and
   count up the time of the recording - if we do mono, highlight mono, if we do stereo, highlight stereo, the selected
   visualizer should react to the voice and the peak meter should show amplitude".
2. **The stream rule is the load-bearing one, and it is honoured literally.** `scopeArmTap300` now takes its stream
   as an argument (`scopeArmTap300(streamIn347, micIn347)`), and `scopeArmMicTap347(stream)` hands it the very stream
   `getUserMedia` already produced for the `MediaRecorder`. The panel opens the microphone in exactly ONE place in the
   whole source (`getUserMedia({ audio: true })` occurs once, pinned by a test). No second capture, no second read.
3. **One graph, not two.** The splitter, the two analysers, the auto-gain, the peak meter and the trace are the same
   objects either way; only the stream feeding them changes. The tap now carries `mic: true` so the parts of the strip
   that answer "what is this measuring?" can tell a file from a microphone.
4. **The gate changed for the microphone tap only.** A playback tap is live when the element is playing; a mic tap is
   live while the recorder is open. A file that finished five minutes ago no longer blocks the strip from following a
   voice, and a mic nobody is recording into does not keep the strip alive. When the recorder stops the tap is dropped
   **before** the tracks are stopped, and the player's own output is re-tapped if a file is still playing.
5. **The dot-matrix timer (`scopeClockBand300`).** While a recorder is open the band shows elapsed recording time from
   zero, counting up, in amber: digits in `CLOCK_REC_LIT347` (#f0883e, the panel's own caution amber) and the state
   mark as a red disc in `CLOCK_REC_MARK347` (#f85149, the panel's own alarm red), built from three bars so it stays a
   dot-matrix object rather than an arc. The "/ full length" half is NOT printed, because a recording has no length
   yet — printing a slash with nothing behind it is the lie of omission this strip has always refused. The playback
   position is not shown either, because it is not the thing being measured.
6. **The count-up has its own timepiece.** A one-second interval armed only while a recorder is open and cleared when
   it closes. The panel's refresh interval can be off, and a timer that only advances when something else happens to
   render is not a timer.
7. **Mono / stereo (`chanLit347`).** The word lit is the count of whatever is being tapped: the microphone's while
   recording (read from the live track's `getSettings().channelCount`, falling back to the strip's own measurement —
   a mono take answers exact zeros on the right channel), the take's otherwise. A recording count is lit in the same
   amber as the clock and its hover names the microphone, so one green word can no longer stand for two different
   facts. An unknown count still leaves BOTH words dark: the panel does not claim mono because a second channel was
   not seen.
8. **What the tests can and cannot prove.** The shim has no `getUserMedia` and no `AudioContext`, so the voice-follows-
   picture behaviour and the peak meter's amplitude cannot be exercised here. Six source guards were added in
   `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` pinning the four rules the ruling named: one microphone read in the whole source; the tap
   armed from the recorder's stream and recording what it taps; the recorder gate plus the hand-back to the player;
   the amber-red counting band that refuses a length it does not have; the one-second timepiece with its own arming
   and clearing; and the channel read-out lit from one helper that cannot print a recording count in the file colours.
   **The live proof is the user's: press the mic button in the browser and watch the strip.**
9. **Board:** ui_state 424 (was 418, +6 guards), transport 52, shut 54, render 169, event_log 31, flow 78, actions 124,
   scope 103, selection_memory 51, tooltips 12, effects 4, model_library 29, scene_composer 45, transparency 19,
   shell_safety 31 — all green, no host file touched, so a browser refresh is all this needs.
10. **The T-310 finding above stays as the measured record** of what the strip did before this ruling; item 5 of that
    finding ("it is NOT built, because the user has not asked for it") is now superseded by the user having asked.

### T-354 PART 1 CLOSED (2026-10-14 04:0x): the reported bug — an unfinished row could be played and got a "heard out" mark
Live screenshot report, verbatim: "current bug: looks like now the quened and unfinished items can be played
and get the heard out tag -> makes no sense".
1. **Root cause chain, read out of the code, not guessed.** `playableRows299()` (lib/client.js:8280) filtered
   the playlist on `id`, on `deadRef299` (a row the lane refused) and on kind (`stt` / `diar` / `sasr`
   excluded) — it never looked at `status`. The host's `routeForJob` (lib/index.js:13279-13284) answers
   `{ok:true, route_url:'/audio-play/<id>'}` for ANY row it has: queued, running, error included. So the
   transport walk (`walkPlayback` 8296, `playWalked` 8331) could step onto a queued row, the host handed back
   a route, `queuePlayback` put it on the media element, the heard funnel (6719-6726) recorded `out` for it,
   and `lit345` + the `audio-play-row-playing345` chip lit that row as NOW PLAYING. Every link in that chain
   was honest on its own; the hole was the missing status gate at the top.
2. **What was already correct, and why the screenshot looked odd.** Autoplay (6521-6551), the pending
   poll-then-play effect (7259-7353) and the row's own play button (4033, `(kind tts|file|task) && status
   === "ok"`) are all gated on a finished row. That is why the queued row in the screenshot shows no
   play triangle and still got played: the door was the transport, not the row.
3. **The fix is client-only — no host file was touched, no restart is implied.** Three layers:
   a. `playableRows299()` now drops every row whose `status` is not `ok`, with a comment naming the host fact
      that made the hole possible.
   b. `playJob(id)` looks the row up in the panel's own playlist and refuses an unfinished row out loud —
      "cannot play ap-1005 yet — the row is queued and there is no take to hear" — and does not ask the host
      at all. A click on a stale render cannot walk through the host's open door.
   c. `nothingPlayableMsg353()`: when the walk has nowhere to step, the panel says "the playlist holds 2
      row(s) that have not finished rendering — there is nothing to step to yet" instead of shrinking the
      playlist to "nothing this panel can play".
4. **What was deliberately NOT gated: the heard funnel itself.** The pending poll plays a row the moment
   `job_status` says `ok`, while the panel's own `playlist` copy still says `running` for it. Marking the
   funnel on that copy would have suppressed the "heard" mark on exactly the rows this panel dispatched and
   played — a honesty regression in the other direction. The gate sits on the paths that ASK for a route.
5. **`?src=1` is untouched on purpose.** A row's SOURCE file exists whether or not the render finished, and
   `playSrcNow` marks `src`, never `out`. "Play the original while I wait" stays available.
6. **HOST HALF, NOT DONE, needs its own explicit restart OK.** `routeForJob` (lib/index.js:13279) should
   refuse a row whose status is not `ok` — today the panel is the only gate anywhere in the chain. Recorded
   as an open item below; no host file was edited in this round.
7. **Tests: transport.test.cjs 52 -> 57.** The fixture's playlist became `PL_FIXED` plus a `plOverride`
   switch, so a late check can show the panel queued and synthesizing rows without pulling the fixed rows
   out from under the checks that ran earlier. The playlist is re-read through a real control (a row's
   "re-dispatch with the same parameters" button, which refreshes the playlist before anything else). Five
   new checks: the unfinished rows are drawn; pressing next never hands one to the lane and lands on a
   finished row; an unfinished row carries no "playing" chip and no "heard" chip; the empty-walk sentence
   names the unfinished rows; and the empty step asked the lane for nothing. Chips are attributed by their
   React key (`ap-1005:heard346`), so a chip cannot be blamed on the wrong row.
8. **Live check owed (browser refresh, no restart):** with a queued row in the list, press next — it should
   skip the queued row; with only unfinished rows, next should say the rows have not finished rendering.

### T-359 CLOSED (2026-10-14 05:4x): voice groups ride the voice entity (host half)
1. **The entity carries them**: a voice registry entry (lib/index.js:173, persisted as `voices: voicesReg` in
   state.json v3) gained `groups`. A restored entry revalidates its labels through the same field-by-field
   revalidation as every other field; a new entry starts with `groups: voiceGroupsFor(name)` so the labels
   survive a voice recut; `delete_voice` removes them with the entry.
2. **The vocabulary**: `VOICE_GROUP_LABEL_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9 _\-]{1,31}$/`, at most 8 labels per voice, at
   most 64 distinct labels store-wide. Labels are normalized on the way in (lower case, spaces collapsed,
   trimmed), so "Star Trek", "  STAR   trek " and "star trek" are ONE group. A malformed label is refused with
   the label named and the voice keeps exactly what it had.
3. **A group cannot exist on its own**: `voice_groups` POST with a name the store does not hold is refused —
   "a group belongs to a voice, it cannot exist on its own". A label with no voice under it is not reported by
   the index any more: groups are a filing of voices, not a shelf.
4. **One verb, two shapes**: `GET voice_groups` answers the index (label, how many voices carry it, which
   ones) plus the caps; `POST voice_groups {name, groups}` REPLACES that one voice's labels (empty clears).
   Refusals go through `logInputRefuse`, a accepted write calls `scheduleSave()`.
5. **Visible to agent and user through the same read**: `voice_registry` now carries `groups` on every entry,
   so the agent-facing read and the panel's read are the same route and cannot drift apart.
6. **It is not a dispatch input**: a grouped voice is dispatched by its name exactly as an ungrouped one, and
   `speechOptionsGate` never sees a group.
7. **Tests added (host, 12 checks)**: restore keeps and normalizes, an unfiled voice answers `[]` not a missing
   field, one write replaces, three spellings are one group, the index counts and names, the unknown-voice
   refusal, the malformed-label refusal with the voice unchanged, the 8-label cap, clearing, persistence into
   state.json, survival through a restart restore, and a grouped dispatch behaving like an ungrouped one.

   (lib/client.js:3889) and its colour is `statusColor` (lib/client.js:3678) — green `#3fb950` for an ok
   row, red for error, amber for aborted, blue for queued. So the green the user is pointing at is the take
   text's OWN colour, which has been there since well before T-330; the chip was the new thing on top of it.

   The take text keeps its status green and drops to 0.62 opacity when this panel has heard ANY media of that
   row — the rendered take, its source, or a stem — and the hover still names which media.

   "HEARD IN THIS PANEL: <each media in full> — this marks what THIS panel played, not what the lane produced;

   the title". A queued blue, an aborted amber or an error red title is already saying something else about
   that row; dimming it would merge two different statements into one shade. Such a row still names its heard
   media in the hover, so nothing is hidden.
6. The marks themselves were not touched: heard346Ref, heard346Bump, mediaOfRoute346 and dropHeard354 still
   record at queue time and still take the mark back when a play errors. The ruling was about how the fact is

### T-367 CLOSED — PPPS: the playlist clear is now two controls, "clear all" and "clear failed"
1. User words (2026-10-14): "the clear button for playlist should be split and offer 'clear all' 'clear
   failed'".
2. Measured today: ONE button in the Playlist section footer (lib/client.js:10965) calling `playlist_clear`
   POST with no body. The host clears FINISHED rows only — running and queued rows stay, files are never
   touched — and answers `{cleared, kept}`.
3. The ruling, asked as one question and answered 2026-10-14: "clear failed" means the widest set —
   **error + aborted + cancelled**. The user's own words for why: a row a person stopped counts too. So
   "failed" here means "never produced a playable take", not "the engine made an error".
4. Path, stated before the answer so it could be pushed back on, and it was not: **panel-side**, because it
   works without the restart the user is holding. `clearFailedRows367` (lib/client.js:8714-8748) walks the
   rows in the panel's own list whose status is in `FAILED_STATUS367 = { error, aborted, cancelled }` and
   issues one per-row removal each, with `delete_file: false` on every one — neither control can ask the host
   to touch a file, and that is structural, not a default.

### T-385 RULED 2026-10-14 — the eject slot becomes the import control: URL streams fetched and stored server-side, DSH filesystem files, and browser uploads. HOST-SIDE, NOT BUILT, needs a restart window
1. Ruling, verbatim: "should be able to open remote streams from URL with safe sanitation + local file play (DSH fs)
   + upload and play (browser-file select local fs for upload to DSH fs and play)". Followed by the storage decision,
   chosen from three options: "Always fetch and store server-side". So an accepted URL becomes bytes in the plugin's
   own store and a normal playlist row, not a browser-only source.
2. The three import paths and what each costs. 1) A URL: the plugin fetches it, sanitizes it, stores it, and the row
   plays like a rendered take — playback survives the source disappearing and the agent can list and replay it.
   2) A path on the DSH filesystem the plugin can already read: the player must be able to reach it, which is a
   serving route, not a client trick. 3) A browser file picker: the bytes are uploaded into the plugin store and then
   behave exactly like 1 and 2. All three need host code, so all three need a restart the user runs.
3. Sanitation I intend to implement unless the user corrects it: `http:` and `https:` only; `file:`, `data:`, `blob:`
   and every other scheme refused; localhost, loopback, link-local and private ranges refused (this is an SSRF guard,
   not decoration — the plugin would be asked to fetch an arbitrary URL); a content-type check that the answer is
   audio; a size ceiling on what is stored; and the resolved host recorded on the row so a later reader can see what
   was actually contacted.
4. What the eject button becomes, and what it must not lose: today `speakLastMessage()` rides the eject glyph. The
   `read it` button (T-384, already live beside `Generate (TTS)`) is that same function, so the swap is ready to make
   — eject's onClick becomes the import control and the glyph keeps its Winamp place. It has not been swapped yet,
   because until the import control exists the swap would leave a dead button in the transport row.
5. Pending restart work now on the shelf, both host-side: T-383 (batch failure policy: retry once on another
   endpoint, then stop the rest) and T-385 (import and instant play). Nothing in `lib/index.js` has been touched for

### T-385 seek and clock honesty BUILT (2026-10-14): a stream with no known length has no end to seek to, and no countdown either
1. The seek bar. Its `max` used to fall back to 0 whenever the length was not a positive number, and its disabled test was `!(playTime.dur > 0)`. A live media element reports an unknown length as `Infinity` or `NaN`, and `Infinity > 0` is TRUE, so the bar would have been handed `max="Infinity"` and a thumb that means nothing. Now `max` is the duration only when it is a finite positive number, `disabled` requires the same test, and the hover states which of three situations the bar is in, ending with "this stream has no known length, so there is no end to seek to. The bar stays off rather than pretending."
2. Measured live with nothing loaded: `disabled: true`, `max: "0"`, hover begins "seek the file the browser is playing. Disabled".
3. The clock band. `fmtPlayClock` already prints `--:--` for null, undefined and non-finite input, but the countdown arithmetic was not covered: `Infinity - position` is `Infinity`, and the band cannot print it. One value now decides the whole band: `durKnown388` is true only for a finite, positive duration. Unknown length means no full-length half and no countdown, exactly as T-377 already ruled for a file the browser has not measured yet.
4. The band's composition rule was the hidden half of this. The strip printed "position / length" whenever the width had room for the slash, so an empty length produced a slash with nothing after it — a claim about a number the panel does not have. The recording case already refused that; the rule is now about the LENGTH rather than about the recording: `var text = (rec347 || !fullTxt334) ? posTxt334 : ...`.
5. The lane call follows the same honesty: `fileStatsFor300` asks the host about the envelope of the FILE the lane wrote. A stream has no such file, so the panel does not ask.
6. Suites, and the fixture lesson. scope went from 111 to 112 with a new check that a countdown needs a length: with the length set (12 s of take, 6 s heard) the countdown band draws exactly one matrix glyph more than the position band and exactly 5 more lit dots — the minus, in the same dot matrix as the digits. With `duration = Infinity` the two bands are identical, glyph for glyph and lit dot for lit dot. The first version of that fixture used 12.5 s and 4.5 s heard, which made the countdown and the position print DIFFERENT digits and broke the very check it was meant to prove: 12 and 6 print the same digits, so the only difference is the minus. The fixture also restores the node's `duration` and `currentTime` afterwards, because a fixture that leaves its props changed fails the next phase for the wrong reason.
7. ui_state 537 pins the source shape: one `durKnown388` definition, the two band fields gated by it, the lane call gated by it, the slash rule, the seek `max`, the seek `disabled`, and the hover sentence that names the unknown length.

### T-385 HOST HALF BUILT (2026-10-14, needs the restart the user runs): an uploaded file becomes a row; a stream still never touches disk
User ruling, verbatim: "Streams should not be saved on disk - only playback and playlist entry, while uploading items should save the user's file for re-use in the playlist for transcription / replay / create voice from".
1. The plumbing was already there and was not duplicated. `upload_audio` has existed since 2026-09-18: the browser reads the picked file as a data-URL, the host decodes it with `base64 -d` on shell stdin — binary never crosses the JS layer — under `writePolicy(STT_DIR)`, with an extension whitelist (wav, mp3, ogg, oga, flac, m4a, aac, webm, opus, aif, aiff), a ceiling of 64 MiB measured against the DECODED bytes, and a base64 shape check. Files land in the plugin store as `stt/uploads/<id>_<name>.<ext>`.
2. What was missing was the ROW. An upload wrote a file and returned a path, and only whichever panel still remembered that path could use it. It was invisible in the playlist, unplayable from the transport, and unusable for the two things the ruling names: transcribing it, or making a voice from it.
3. A stored upload now pushes one row of the shape the rest of the host already understands: `kind: 'upload'`, `status: 'ok'`, `fn: 'stt'`, `output_path` and `file_path` both pointing at the stored file, `format` carrying the extension, and the state saved immediately. Because it is an ordinary ok row with an output path, `serveAudio` serves it (Range requests included, content type by extension), `routeForJob` routes it, and the playlist lists it like any other take.
4. It is NOT a lane job, and the boundaries say so: nothing is queued, no endpoint is chosen, no slot is held, the pump never sees it (it is not in a queued state), and `retry_job` refuses it for the plain reason that only error and aborted rows can be retried. A row whose job is to hold a file must not be mistaken for a row that owes the lane a render.
5. The restart whitelist carries the new kind. The restore path has always crushed an unknown kind back to `tts` — that is how `diar`, `task` and `sasr` were added once they existed. Without `upload` in that list, a file row would come off a restart as a TTS render of text nobody asked to render.
6. The client side of the import row gained the file half: a `file` button and a hidden `audio/*` input. It is deliberately NOT gated by the Stream input setting, because it is not a stream — the setting governs links the browser plays and the plugin never touches, while a picked file is written once and kept. After a successful upload the panel names the row, refreshes the playlist, and plays the new row immediately, which is the "instant-play" the eject was given.
7. Live proof of the client half: with the import row closed, no file control exists in the panel; pressing eject opens the row with the button and the hidden input present (`type=file`, `accept=audio/*`, `display:none`); pressing the button opened a real file chooser (`multiple: false`, `accept: "audio/*"`). No page errors. Nothing was uploaded during the proof.
8. The boundary check that keeps the ruling: the host's upload handler contains no `fetch(`, no `http(s)://` and no `route_url` — the plugin never reaches out to a URL to bring a file in. A stream is played by the browser, listed, and never written here.
9. Suites: host.test 1604 (was 1599) with five new contracts — the restore whitelist carries `upload` exactly once; a stored upload pushes exactly one row with the right shape and saves state; the answer names the row it created (`job_id`) so the panel can play it without remembering a path; the four upload guards survive the change; and the no-URL boundary above. transport 67 (was 66) with the file picker asserted in the opened import row and a separate check that it is offered while the stream setting is OFF, because an upload is not a stream.
10. Board after this round: client 1482 checks plus handlers OK (transport 67, render 203, ui_state 537, actions 172, flow 78, shut 57, scope 112, tooltips 12, model_library 36, scene_composer 60, selection_memory 62, event_log 31, shell_safety 31, transparency 20, effects 4), host 1824 (host.test 1604, endpoint_exclusivity 105, engine_boot 99, model_matrix 16). Total 3306 checks, 0 fail.
11. What is not live yet, and why: the host half of T-385 and the whole of T-383 are edits to `lib/index.js`. They are on disk and green in the suites, but the running harness still has the code it booted with. They need a harness restart, which only the user runs. The client half — the stream setting, the import row, the file picker, the canvas centring and frame, the right-edge binding, the read-out scroll, the seek and clock honesty — is live on a browser refresh and was measured live.

### T-391 BUILT (2026-10-15, live panel, screenshot): the PL button no longer drops to a line of its own — and the cause was the flex BASIS, not the minimum
User report, verbatim: "small bug: the PL button line wraps ... volume slider needs smaller minimum".
1. Measured before touching anything: at a 440 px panel the information column is 204 px wide, the EQ button is 34 px, the PL button is 31 px, and PL sat 24 px lower than EQ — on its own line. The same failure appeared expanded.
2. The first fix followed the report literally and lowered the volume slider's MINIMUM from 40 px to 22 px. Re-measured, nothing improved: the slider was still 160 px wide, PL still dropped at 440 px, and 420 px broke as well. The measurement said the minimum was not the constraint.
3. Why: a browser builds a wrapping line from each item's flex BASIS and only shrinks items inside the line it has already built. A range input with `flex: 1 1 auto` has an automatic basis, which for a range input is its intrinsic width, about 160 px. The row was therefore measured as 160 + 34 + 31 = 225 px against 204 px available, and PL was the item that did not fit — before any shrinking was allowed to happen. T-388 item 2 is what changed this basis from `70px` to `auto`, so T-388 item 2 is what introduced this wrap; its right-edge binding was kept, its basis was not.
4. The fix at lib/client.js:11975: `style: { flex: "1 1 22px", minWidth: "22px", height: "16px" }` — a small BASIS, the same floor, and grow 1 so the slider still absorbs every spare pixel when the row has room.
5. Re-measured at 360, 400, 420, 440, 460, 480, 500 and 560 px, minimised and expanded (16 measurements): EQ and PL share the line at every width. The slider grows with the row — 103 px at 420 px panel, 123 px at 440 px, 243 px at 560 px.
6. The shut mini bar was measured too, at 300, 360 and 420 px: its controls sit on one line at every width and its volume already carries an explicit basis (`1 1 70px`, min 34, max 110), so it was left alone rather than "fixed" for a problem it does not have.
7. Suite: ui_state 538 pins the basis and forbids both the old `flex: "1 1 auto", minWidth: "40px"` and the ineffective `flex: "1 1 auto", minWidth: "22px"`, so a later flex edit cannot reintroduce the wrap by changing the basis while keeping a plausible-looking minimum.
8. The lesson worth keeping: a report that names a control is not a diagnosis of the mechanism. "Volume slider needs smaller minimum" named the right control and the wrong property; only the re-measurement after the first attempt showed the basis was doing the wrapping.

### T-392 DONE (2026-10-15): the voice t2_miles is renamed to t2_arnold, through the plugin's own verbs
User report, verbatim: "also, it looks like voice t2-miles is actually t2-arnold and needs renaming". The store names this family with underscores (`t2_john`, `t2_sarah`, `t2_wife`), and `VOICE_NAME_RE` is `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}`, so the name written is `t2_arnold`.
1. What the entry held before the change: `ref_text` of 402 characters (the T2 Skynet narration passage, as the engine heard it), `ref_wav` voices/t2_miles.wav, `ref_dur_s` 25.9, `groups: ["terminator-2"]`, and `source` pointing at `yt-downloads/extracted/fullregression_20261013/samples_kitchen/t2_miles_26.wav`.
2. There is no rename verb, and `state.json` is the running host's own state — editing it under a live host is not safe, because the host holds the registry in memory and rewrites the file. The rename therefore went through the verbs: `save_voice {name:"t2_arnold", file_path: voices/t2_miles.wav, transcribe:false, ref_text:<the existing text>}`, then `voice_groups {name:"t2_arnold", groups:["terminator-2"]}`, then `delete_voice {name:"t2_miles"}`.
3. `transcribe:false` with the text carried over was a deliberate choice: re-hearing the sample would have put an STT job on the fleet for no reason and could have produced a different `ref_text` than the one every clone of this voice has been fed. The answer confirmed `text_match=true` — the new entry's transcript is character-identical to the old one.
4. The sample is byte-identical: md5 `04d9634fb320fd599d0a52055deecf89` on both `voices/t2_miles.wav` (1 244 238 bytes) and the new `voices/t2_arnold.wav` (1 244 238 bytes). The registered sample was the authoritative one, not the yt-downloads original: that file is 2 488 398 bytes with a different md5, because the registration conformed it. Copying from the original would have silently changed the voice.
5. `ref_dur_s` was re-measured by the save (step 6 of `handleSaveVoice`, ffprobe) and came back 25.9 — the same length, which is what a byte-identical copy must produce.
6. `delete_voice` answered `{"ok":true,"removed":"t2_miles","file_deleted":true,"file_error":null}` and refused nothing, because no running or queued job held the voice. The registry now lists `t2_john t2_wife skynet t2_sarah t2_arnold`, and the group index reports `terminator-2` with 4 voices: t2_arnold, t2_john, t2_sarah, t2_wife.
7. Live panel proof: the Voices section shows `t2_arnold` and the `terminator-2` label, and the family names are all present. The string `t2_miles` still appears in the panel in exactly three places, and all three are history rather than a selectable voice — the rows ap-0456, ap-0457 and ap-0458, whose labels and hovers read "qwen3-tts@q8_0 · t2_miles · 33.3s / 32.1s / 1m03". Those rows record the voice each take was actually rendered with and were left as they are. No option or dropdown anywhere in the panel carries the old name.
8. One wrinkle written down rather than hidden: `handleSaveVoice` sets `source` to the path it copied FROM, so the new entry's provenance reads `<home>/.dsh/audio-play/voices/t2_miles.wav`, which `delete_voice` then removed. The live path is the entry's own `ref_wav`. The original provenance — `yt-downloads/extracted/fullregression_20261013/samples_kitchen/t2_miles_26.wav`, the pre-conform cut — is recorded here so it is not lost with the file.
9. Docs updated: WORKFLOW_VOICE_REPLACE.md step 8 now names `t2_arnold` with the reason and the byte-identity note. The regression records under `yt-downloads/extracted/fullregression_20261013/` (including `req_14_save_t2_miles.json`, `req_15_qc_t2_miles.json`, the batch manifests and the speaker census) were NOT rewritten: they are the record of what was rendered under the old name.

### T-401 BUILT (2026-10-15): a web stream now drives the visualizer and the channel read-out
User request, verbatim: "ok i am playing a webstream for the first time in the player, the visualizers should work and display it accordingly, also the kpbs display and mono/stereo display should show stream values".
1. Why the strip could not work, measured before touching anything: the strip taps the player's OUTPUT with `captureStream()` (and `createMediaElementSource` is never used, by the standing safety rule), and a media element that fetched its resource in no-cors mode refuses to be captured. Live probe on the user's own WDR 1LIVE link: `Failed to execute 'captureStream' on 'HTMLMediaElement': Cannot capture from element with cross-origin data`. The client contained no `crossOrigin` anywhere, so every web stream was in that state.
2. The fix and its proof, same link, second probe run with the attribute set before src: the captured track reports `readyState: live`, `muted: false`, and both analysers read real signal — peak 0.555 left, 0.555 right out of 1.0.
3. Built at the panel's single src assignment site: an outside http(s) source (not a `/audio-play/ap-…` lane route) gets `crossOrigin = "anonymous"` BEFORE `a.src = url`, because setting it after a load has started does nothing. If the station will not answer a cross-origin request the element errors, and the ladder re-assigns the SAME url once with the claim removed and says so — "playing <host> without the visualizer — the station will not let the panel read its audio". One retry, guarded by a flag, so it cannot loop. The failure mode stays a flat picture, never a broken lane.
4. Measured live in the panel after the change, with the strip in oscilloscope mode and the WDR stream playing (readyState 4, currentTime 8, crossOrigin "anonymous"): canvas pixels while idle 488 lit / 5 distinct colours / max channel 185; while streaming 1505, 1048 and 1270 lit pixels with 555, 486 and 547 distinct colours and a different pixel hash on every sample. The strip is drawing the stream. The stereo word lights green `rgb(63,185,80)` and its hover reads "two channels: the strip draws both of them, in two colours" — that is the stream's own channel count, read from the player's output by the existing splitter rule (`SCOPE_STEREO_FLOOR300`).
5. The rate read-out, and the honest limit on it. `playStats300` is filled only by `fileStatsFrom300` (kbps from `bytes * 8 / duration`, kHz from `sample_rate`, both from a lane row), and a web stream has no row. ### T-403 BUILT (2026-10-15): the batch board now states what the failure policy did to a batch
Asked after the restart, with the measured facts in front of the user (the lane sends the batch keys per row but `queue_status` has no batch block), the ruling was: "Build the batch-level board now".
1. PLAN CORRECTION, and it removed a restart from the plan. The staged plan assumed a host change was needed — a batch block in `queueView`. Measured instead: `rowOf` (lib/index.js 4045-4059) already sends `batch_retry_of`, `batch_retried_to`, `batch_halt` and `batch_wait_retry` on every batch row, only when set, and the boot restore carries them too (1535-1538), so they survive a restart — which the user has just run. The batch-level fact is therefore computable from rows the board already holds. Nothing host-side was written, and no further restart is needed for this feature. `queue_status` still answers `ok, queues, machines, mgmt_disabled, prefer_primary, quality_flags` with no batch key, and that stays true on purpose.
2. What the board computes now, in `BatchBoard` (client.js, the group accumulation and the group line): per batch it counts `halted` (rows carrying a halt sentence, keeping the first sentence as the batch's reason), `waiting` (rows held while a retry is in flight, with their own reason), `retriedFrom` (rows that ARE a second attempt) and `retriedTo` (rows a second attempt replaced). The group line gains "HALTED, N parts stopped" and "N waiting for a retry"; the hover carries the host's own sentence, the line "a halted part is not queued and will not start again on their own", the waiting counterpart "held while a retry is in flight, and are still expected to run", and the two retry lists. A halted part prints "stopped: <reason>" on its own line and turns the alarm red `#f85149` — the same red a refused press and a refused request get. A waiting part prints "waiting: <reason>" and keeps its status colour.
3. The distinction the host itself insists on is kept: `batch_halt` and `batch_wait_retry` are mutually exclusive in the lane (index.js 3256-3257 clears one when it sets the other), so the board never shows both on one part, and a suite check asserts exactly that.

### T-405 BUILT (2026-10-15): what happens to a playing web stream when a new take arrives — duck (default), pause and resume, or stop
Measured before proposing anything:
1. There is ONE media element. `audioRef` (client.js 6839) is the `<audio>` in the playlist section (12425, `controls: false`), and `startPlayback(url, label, onDone)` (7781) writes `a.src = url` on it (7855). The web stream goes through the SAME function — the T-401 branch lives inside it (7852-7866). So today a new take ends a stream and starting a stream ends a take: the src swap is the whole story, and the sequential queue (`playQRef`, 7878) plays one take at a time on that one element.
2. Consequence for the duck design: keeping the stream audible under a take needs a second element for the stream, with takes staying on `audioRef`. The panel's picture is not at risk — the scope strip never uses `createMediaElementSource`, and the stream is already marked (`playStats300.stream`) so the read-out can say which element it describes.
3. Duck mode (the user's stated default): stream volume drops to an adjustable level while a take plays, restored when the take ends OR errors — `finish()` at 7787 is the single place both paths pass through, so the restore belongs there and cannot leak a ducked stream.
4. Pause-and-resume mode: `pause()` on the stream element when a take starts, `play()` on the same `finish()`. For a live station this differs from a file: a paused live element resumes at what the station is broadcasting NOW, so the ducked portion is gone, and a re-fetch may land mid-programme. That behaviour has to be stated in the setting's own hover, not discovered by the user at 2 a.m.
5. Settings that belong in the Auto-play section (it already owns "what speaks on its own"): the mode (duck / pause and resume / today's stop), the duck level (adjustable, persisted), and whether the rule applies to every take or only to arrivals from agentPlay / panelPlay / auto-speak.

### T-414 BUILT (2026-10-15) — the equalizer bars fall off faster
User, verbatim: "the equalizer bars should fall off faster, the peak markers per bar are ok, but the bars are too
slow".
A bar is drawn from the analyser's CURRENT value, so what decides how fast a bar can fall is
`AnalyserNode.smoothingTimeConstant` — a first-order smoothing across successive `getByteFrequencyData` calls.
The panel had 0.7. Measured in Chromium with one oscillator at 1200 Hz, stopped dead at a known frame, timing the
bins down to 6 % of the peak they held, 60 fps throughout:
`SCOPE_SMOOTH300 = 0.4` is now the single source for both analysers (the stereo second analyser reads the same
constant). 2.3x faster fall than the 383 ms being seen, and still smoothed enough that a 4 kHz fricative does not
make the bars jitter. The peak caps were NOT touched — `SCOPE_HOLD_DECAY300` stays at 1 px per drawn frame,
because those markers were called ok.
A second measurement, worth keeping because it changes what "turn the volume down" means: tapping a playing
media element with `captureStream()` and watching the analyser's total energy while the element's own `volume`
is set to 0 — the energy did NOT fall (baseline 20891, final 44977 over 6 s, 60 fps). The volume a media element
applies to its speakers is not what the visualizer tap is fed. Ducking a station therefore changes what the
person HEARS without changing what the strip DRAWS, and any future attempt to make the strip react to a duck has
to go through the analyser's own gain, not through `element.volume`.

### T-415 BUILT (2026-10-15) — fewer equalizer bars
User, verbatim: "we could reduce the amount of equalizer bars in the vis by 20% or 30% to reduce load and have
more fps".
`SCOPE_BANDS300` 26 -> 20: 23 % fewer bands, so 23 % less per-frame band scanning and 23 % fewer bar draws, and
each bar is wider for the same strip. Honest limit, measured on this box: after T-410 the strip already ran at
60 frames/s while a station played (measured again after this change: 121 strip frames in 2010 ms = 60/s), so
what this buys is HEADROOM, not a higher rate here — the rate is already at the browser's cap on this machine.

### T-421 BUILT (2026-10-15, later)
Measured first, in Chromium against the live strip while the WDR station played, by reading canvas pixels instead of
trusting the arithmetic. Canvas 200 x 80. The 20 bar slots already filled it exactly: bar width (200 - 19 x 1) / 20 =
9.05 px, gap 1 px, first bar x = 0, last bar x = 191 to 199. So there was no placement slack to shift right - a shift
would have pushed the first bar off the canvas and left the same hole on the right.
What the eye was seeing: lit bar columns ran 0..189, leaving 10 px of dead canvas at the right (175 lit columns, 16
runs of 9 px). The reason is the band map, not the geometry: scopeBandMap300 divided lo..nyq into 20 log bands, so
the top band covered 13.5-22 kHz, and a 128 kbps mp3 carries nothing up there. Silent spectrum, read as a gap.
Fix: the top of the band map is capped - SCOPE_HIGH_HZ300 = 16000, var hi = Math.min(nyq, SCOPE_HIGH_HZ300), and both
band edges are computed from hi instead of nyq. Every band now covers audible, present content, and the low and mid
bands get finer log resolution than before.
Re-measured the same way after the change: lit columns 0..199, 184 lit columns, 17 runs, leftPad 0, rightPad 0. The
strip is full edge to edge and the last bars carry height and peak caps.
Cost stated plainly: the panel no longer draws anything above 16 kHz. For lossy stream audio that range is empty
anyway; for a full-band local file the top 6 kHz is no longer shown.
scope.test.cjs 114 -> 115 pass, 0 fail: a source pin holds SCOPE_HIGH_HZ300 = 16000, the Math.min cap, and both pow
lines reading hi. Live probe /tmp/probe421_span.cjs, shots /tmp/strip421.png before and after.

User request, verbatim: "Now the equalizer bars are one or two pixels too wide, there should be one or two pixels
of black between bar and borders on both sides."
Measured before the change: the spectrum geometry was gapS334 = 1, fitS334 = floor((W + 1) / 3), bw = (W - 19*1)/20
and x = b*(bw+1). At the 200 px canvas with 20 bands that is bw = 9.05 and the bars span x = 0..200 edge to edge:
the leftmost bar sat against the 1 px frame, the rightmost against the 3 px frame (T-389's deliberate retro-3D
asymmetry), with no black between either.
Verified live in Chromium against the real strip with the WDR station playing (canvas read by pixels, not by the
maths): css 200 x backing 200 at dpr 1.00; scanning only the trace band (y = 25..70, excluding the clock band and
the peak meter) the lit run is x = 2..187 with 170 lit columns and 17 bar groups in that frame - left black
measured 2.00 css px, exactly the inset. The right side read 12 px in that frame only because the top three bars
were silent for a 128 kbps stream; by the arithmetic the last bar ends at 198, so the right margin is 2 px as well.
The first scan had used y from 35% of the height, which included the peak meter and reported a false left margin
of 0; the band was corrected before the number above was taken.
Suite: tests/scope.test.cjs gained a source pin for SCOPE_EDGE_INSET300 = 2, the inner428 line, the bw line built
from inner428 and the inset x line. Board after the change: 116 pass / 0 fail in scope, whole client board 1643
pass / 0 fail across 17 suites, host 1611 pass / 0 fail.

### T-436 BUILD CARD - the DL door on an imported link, measured and decided (2026-10-15, BUILT — what actually landed is under "T-436 BUILT" further down; the subtitle leg is its item 11)
The user's decision on the one open design point, asked 2026-10-15: the capability question is answered WHEN THE DL
IS PRESSED. Not at import time, not per row on open. So the button does not need a probe to exist, and a URL that
yt-dlp cannot handle is discovered by the binary at the moment a person asked for it, in the binary's own words.
Anchors measured in the current source, so the build starts from facts rather than from memory:
1. Placement. The import row is className audio-play-import390 at lib/client.js:12809. Its children in order are
   the URL input (audio-play-import-url390, placeholder "http(s) link to play"), the play button
   (audio-play-import-go390, label "play", hover "play this link now, in this browser, and keep it as a playlist
   entry. Nothing is written to disk."), and the upload button (audio-play-import-file-btn385, label "upload
   file...", renamed from "file" by T-394). The DL button goes BETWEEN the play button and the upload button, which
   is exactly the position the user named. New class: audio-play-import-dl436.
2. Import flow to reuse. submitImport390 (lib/client.js:6478) validates with streamUrlCheck390, builds a row
   {id, url, host, scheme, t}, caps the list at 40 newest-first, persists, and calls playStream395. The DL act is a
   sibling act on the SAME text field - it must not invent its own URL rules: an empty or non-http value is refused
   before the binary is ever asked.
3. Row shape to copy: handleUploadAudio (lib/index.js:12591) writes into STT_DIR/uploads/<id>_<slug>.<ext> with
   writePolicy(STT_DIR), then builds the row at 12626 - kind 'upload', status 'ok', file_path and output_path both
   set, fn 'stt', and playlist.unshift (T-393: a row pushed to the far end of the array is a row no panel can ever
   be shown), then saveStateNow(). A captured file becomes THIS shape so every consumer that already accepts an
   upload row accepts it: serveAudio serves it, routeForJob routes it, the playlist lists it, the transport can play
   it, and it can be handed to separation, chunking, diarization or voice conversion through file_path. It is NOT a
   lane job: nothing is queued, no endpoint is chosen, no slot is held.
4. Local-process shape to copy: the remux and mix steps run local ffmpeg through shellx.resolve + runx with
   sandboxPolicy: writePolicy(dirName(target)) (lib/index.js:8147, 8150, 8236, 8556). writePolicy(root) is
   { mode: 'workspace-write', workspaceRoot: root || BASE } (lib/index.js:908). The yt-dlp legs follow the same
   route: a spec per call, its own timeoutMs, its own write policy, runx, and no engine and no queue slot.
5. Settings shape to copy: limit_one_per_host is a persisted flag restored in loadState (lib/index.js:1832), omitted
   from the saved blob when it equals the default (1482), with a GET that reads and a POST that writes, and the
   client side sends a body ONLY when the caller passed a real value so a read can never look like a write
   (lib/client.js:7364). ytdlp_path follows that exactly, with a string instead of a boolean: GET reads it, POST
   sets it, an empty string clears it, and the Settings section refreshes it on open the way refreshLimitOne() does
   (lib/client.js:13371-13375).
The build, in the order it should be done:
1. Host setting. var ytdlpPath = '' persisted as s.ytdlp_path. Validation on write: it must be an absolute path,
   must exist, must be a regular file, must carry an executable bit. Refuse a bare name outright - the plugin never
   searches PATH and never guesses, per the user's rule that the path is given manually by the agent or the user.
   The GET answers the path, whether it resolves, and the version the binary reports (yt-dlp --version, cached, read
   on demand, never on a timer).
2. Host act, POST capture_url {url}. Guards in this order: path configured (otherwise 'no yt-dlp path is configured
   - Settings -> yt-dlp binary path'), URL is http or https, URL length sane. Then two calls to the binary:
   a capability call (--no-warnings --simulate --skip-download -J) and, only if that answers, the download
   (--no-warnings --no-playlist -f bestaudio -x --audio-format wav -o <store>/dl/<id>_%(id)s.%(ext)s).
3. The URL never travels on the command line. It is written to a small file and handed to yt-dlp with -a <file>,
   which is the encapsulation the user asked for ("in a thread or so (capsulated)") and it removes the quoting
   problem entirely: a URL with a query string, an ampersand or a quote is data, not shell.
4. Capability answers are read from yt-dlp's own JSON (-J gives extractor, title, duration, formats). If the binary
   answers nothing machine-readable, that is reported as the binary's failure with its exit code and the tail of its
   stderr - it is NOT treated as 'no formats', and it is never retried silently.
5. After the download: measure the landed file with the existing ffmpegDurationShell (lib/index.js:7990), create the
   row in the upload shape above with a note naming the source URL, unshift, saveStateNow, and answer {ok, id,
   file_path, duration, extractor, formats chosen}. Timeout generous but bounded (a capture is minutes, not
   milliseconds); --no-playlist is not optional, because one link must not turn into forty files.
6. Client: the DL button between play and upload. It is VISIBLE ALWAYS and DISABLED when no path is configured,
   with a hover that names the setting - a control nobody can find is the same as no control, and the gate the user
   asked for is about whether the act can run, not whether a person knows it exists. Disabled hover: no yt-dlp path
   is set. Enabled hover: asks the binary what it can do with this link, then writes the audio into the plugin's own
   store as a playlist row. Pressing it with an empty field says so in the panel and does not call anything (T-387
   item 4: a press that schedules nothing says why, in words). While it runs the button reads 'capturing...' and is
   disabled; the row appears in the playlist when it lands.
7. Settings input: a text field for the path under its own label, plus what the binary reported when it was last
   read - version and whether the file resolves. Same section, same refresh-on-open pattern.
8. Tests. host.test.cjs gets the block: refused when the path is empty; refused for a non-http URL; the capability
   spec carries --simulate/--skip-download/-J and -a and NOT the URL inline; the download spec carries --no-playlist
   and an output template inside the plugin store; a landed row is kind upload, status ok, output_path set, at the
   FRONT of the playlist. Client pins: the DL button sits between audio-play-import-go390 and
   audio-play-import-file-btn385, and its disabled state follows the setting rather than the URL.
9. The four 'never written to disk' statements (the play button hover at 12824, the eject hover, the remove hover
   at 6519, and the comment at 6448) are re-worded IN THE SAME change that makes this land. Until then they stay -
   they are true today, and editing them early would promise a door that is not there.
Open, and it needs the user's word before the first line is written: whether a capture also gets mirrored into
yt-downloads/raw/<source>/ (the workspace's own download root, whose policy says raw/ is never deleted and
manifest.json is the tracking index), or whether the plugin's own store is the only copy and yt-downloads stays
the place the skill and the scripts write to. The plugin store is required either way, because a file outside the
store cannot be served by serveAudio and cannot be a row the panel plays.

### T-449 BUILT (host half) - 2026-10-15 - the takes store limit: off by default, a named refusal, or a trim that only touches plugin takes
1. **The setting.** `mode: 'off' | 'limit' | 'auto_delete'`, default `off`; `max_bytes` in BYTES, default
   `2147483648` (2 GiB), floor `1048576` (1 MiB — "a line smaller than this is a typo, not a limit"), ceiling
   `1099511627776` (1 TiB — "a bigger number is a missing unit, not a plan"). Persisted in state.json only when it
   differs from the code default, restored BEFORE anything can dispatch, and revalidated: a state file naming a mode
   this plugin does not have, or a line outside the floor and ceiling, leaves the default in place rather than
   inventing a limit nobody asked for. Door: `GET|POST /api/audio-play/takes_limit`.
2. **The number it works from is measured, not claimed.** `measureTakes449()` walks the takes directory with the
   SAME bounded walk `storage_status` uses (node builtins when present, `du -sb` when they are not, symbolic links
   never followed), so the number a refusal quotes and the number the panel shows are one number. Live measurement
   on this host after the restart: **1 423 079 003 bytes over 981 files** in `<home>/.dsh/audio-play/tts`.
   The cached reading is a FLOOR, not a live reading — takes are added by renders and removed only by this feature,
   so an old measurement never overstates the store; and every refusal says how old the reading was and how it was
   taken (`measured 12 s ago by walk`).
3. **`limit` mode refuses, in words.** The gate sits on the three doors that write a take — `enqueueTtsJob`,
   `handleDispatchTask`, `handleDispatchBatch` — and runs BEFORE the row exists, so a refusal costs no playlist row,
   no endpoint call and no queue slot (the same reason enqueueTtsJob was split out of handleDispatchTts in T-130).
   The refusal names the current usage, the limit, the age of the reading, the directory, and the four things a
   person can do about it. It is recorded twice: as a `dispatch_refuse` and as a `takes_limit_refuse`.
4. **`auto_delete` trims, oldest first, and says what it removed.** It runs when the mode is chosen (a person who
   chose auto_delete asked for the store to come under the line, not for a promise about later) and after every take
   lands (`takesAfterWrite449`, fire-and-forget: a trim that failed must never turn a rendered take into an error
   row and never delays delivery). Candidates are files DIRECTLY in the takes directory whose NAME is a plugin take
   (`ap-NNNN_…`), oldest mtime first, and the newest 20 takes are never candidates at all. Never removed: a take a
   playlist row points at, a stem, a batch part, the source a resample was made from, the sample of a registered
   voice, or a file that is not a plugin take (a person's own file in that directory is outside this feature, and it
   still COUNTS toward the measured number). Each removal is a `takes_trim_remove` perf event naming the file, its
   size and what was left; each protected file is a `takes_trim_keep` naming the reason; and a trim that ends STILL
   over the line says so as `takes_trim_nothing_left` rather than pretending it made room.
5. **What the bound does not touch, stated in the answer itself:** transcriptions, uploads and clips (they count
   toward the number), voices, texts, the playlist row cap, and any file in the takes directory that is not a plugin
   take. `dispatch_stt` is not gated: a transcription is not a take.
6. **A moved takes directory moves the number.** `set_save_path` (both the set and the reset branch) calls
   `takesUsageReset449()` — the old directory's bytes are not carried across the move.
7. **Tests.** 24 new pins in `tests/host.test.cjs`, and the round-4 fixture is real: a directory under `/tmp` of
   real files with known sizes and mtimes, the plugin's takes directory moved onto it through its own
   `set_save_path` door, and one fenced seam in the harness's shell stub that EXECUTES `rm -f` for that fixture path
   only — so "the four oldest are gone from disk" is asserted against files that really disappear. No file under the
   real store is removed by any test. Host suite: **1736 pass / 0 fail**.

### T-463 BUILT, client side, needs a browser refresh (2026-10-15) - the Advanced options board follows the form in use and says which one it followed
The ruling, verbatim answer to the question round: **"should also follow stt model, depending on selection , but
needs visual implication"**. Both halves of that sentence are built: it FOLLOWS, and it SAYS.
1. **The resolver (`capActive363`).** The FORM ON SCREEN decides first: when the kind the section is showing is a
   tool kind, the render form is not on screen at all (the tool form replaced it), so the board cannot be bound to a
   render model nobody can dispatch from here. With a render kind on screen, the picker this person last touched
   breaks the tie between the render form and the transcription form — `onModelChange` now records which picker was
   touched (`tts` → text, `task` → tool, `stt` → transcription). If that form's own picker is empty the board falls
   back in a stated order (the other half of this section, then transcription) rather than claiming a model nobody
   picked. Lane mapping is unchanged: a tool job rides the tts lane (T-242), transcription rides the stt lane.
2. **The visual implication is the board's first line.** `these options belong to <model> · the tool / generate form
   · tts lane · record read from primary` — model, form, lane and endpoint, in that order, coloured blue when the
   record on screen really is that model's and amber when it is not. A board that follows a selection silently is a
   board that sends another model's knobs into a job, and that is exactly the failure this line exists to make
   visible before anyone types.
3. **The second half of the visibility.** When a record IS on screen but belongs to a different model or endpoint,
   the board says so before the person touches it: "the record on screen belongs to controlfoley on primary, not to
   clon1 — press read the record for this model, and until you do, nothing typed here is sent with a job for it".
4. **The send is now described by the JOB, not by the board.** `capSend352(lane, listKey, modelId)` is called by
   `dispatchTts` with its own model and by `dispatchTask` with the tool model it is dispatching; the guard compares
   the record's key AND its model id against the job. Before this the guard re-derived "tts + selModel.tts" from
   inside itself, which is why the board could only ever ride a speech render. Merge order on a tool job is a rule,
   not an accident: the record's values go first and the tool form's own three fields (duration_seconds,
   guidance_scale, num_inference_steps) are laid over them, because a field you can see on the form is a stronger
   statement than a name in a generated list. Untouched controls still send no `options` key at all.
5. **The transcription half is honest about what the host can carry today.** `dispatch_stt` has no general
   engine-options door — the only options it reads are diar knobs (`lib/index.js:11483-11590`, `knobGate.options`
   → `job.diar_options`). So while the board is bound to a transcription model it READS and DISPLAYS that model's
   record (the read goes to the stt endpoint: `GET model_capabilities?fn=stt&id=primary&family=…`, pinned) and says

### T-470 BUILT, client side, needs a browser refresh (user 2026-10-15) - "imported streams" is now collapsible, and a live station holds it open

   links it is hiding, so a closed block says what is behind it. DOM order is label, count, arrows and flex `order`
   prints arrows around them, which is the trick `Collapsible` uses (lib/client.js:1113) so a suite that finds a
   header by the text its subtree begins with still finds "imported streams" at the front.
2. **The state rides the section machinery, not a private flag.** It persists as `__streams` through the same
   `toggleExpand` the eleven top-level sections use (it persists any key beginning with `__`), and `__streams: true`
   was added to `SECTION_DEFAULTS` (lib/client.js:790) for the reason that table's own comment gives: `toggleExpand`
   computes the CURRENT value as `nx[fn] === undefined ? !!SECTION_DEFAULTS[fn] : !!nx[fn]`, so a key that is open by
   default but missing from the table computes `!undefined = true` on the first click and never closes - the exact
   "click twice" bug that comment names. Open by default: an imported link is visible until a person says otherwise.
3. **The parenthetical is a safety rule and it is an OR that cannot be overridden**: `var streamsOpen470 =
   sectionOpen("__streams", true) || streamLive470;` with `streamLive470 = !!(streamNow395 || streamAudible395())`
   (lib/client.js:12545-12546). While the panel holds or plays a station the block is forced open, the control reads
   `not-allowed`, the hover says why ("the play / pause and stop controls for the station the panel is playing or
   holding live on these rows, and the transport in the strip belongs to the take, not to the stream"), and the click
   answers out loud instead of doing nothing. A HELD station counts as live, because it is one keypress from audible.
