### T-441 BUILT (2026-10-16, user ruling "Default stays linear, log is opt-in") - the volume slider now has a named curve, and it is a Settings switch
1. **What it was.** Since T-300 the panel wrote the slider straight onto `HTMLMediaElement.volume`: position IS
   amplitude. Half the slider is half the amplitude, which is -6 dB, and that is audibly quieter than the middle of a
   real volume control — the reason the card was opened.
2. **What it is now.** One Settings line, `Log volume taper (off = linear)`, default OFF, so nothing changes until it
   is switched on. The curve is one pure function, `volAmplitude441(v, logOn)` (lib/client.js:845): the hardware-pot
   taper `(100^v - 1) / 99`, which spans 100x in amplitude (40 dB) across the travel and keeps the ends exact — 0 is
   silence, 1 is full. Measured at slider positions: 0.25 -> 0.021841 (-33.2 dB), 0.5 -> 0.090909 (-20.8 dB),
   0.75 -> 0.309321 (-10.2 dB), against linear at the same positions (0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 -> -12.0 / -6.0 / -2.5 dB).
3. **One setting governs both sliders** — the player strip (`audio-play-vol`) and the mini header (`audio-play-vol312`)
   share one volume state, and both hovers now state the active curve in words and dB rather than leaving it implicit.
   Both call sites run through the same function; the state variable keeps the POSITION, so the two sliders cannot
   drift apart.
4. **Switching mid-play is audible at once:** the stored position is re-applied through the new curve, so flipping the
   switch at half the slider changes the element from 0.5 to 0.090909 without touching the slider. The setting is
   persisted (`audio-play:vol.log`), so a reload keeps the curve it had.
5. **Seven new pins** (tests/scope.test.cjs) that read the amplitude the media element ACTUALLY received off the host
   node the panel holds a ref to — not the slider's own value: default linear; the Settings line exists, is off, and
   explains both curves in its hover; switching re-applies at once and persists; the taper survives a reload; 0.25 is
   0.021841 not 0.25; both sliders are wired to one handler and one curve flag; and the curve is one door, not a
   per-look tweak. Suite **166 pass, 0 fail**.
6. **Live when:** client-side, browser refresh.
7. **MEASURED ANSWER to the user's question "already in place?": YES - it was built on 2026-10-16 under the ruling "Default stays linear, log is opt-in".** The user's word: "volume linear vs log: -> should have nothing todo with gain value usually - also - already in place ?". It is in place: the taper exists (`volLog441` at lib/client.js:11476-11504, the amplitude mapping at lib/client.js:911-918, the Settings control at lib/client.js:15691), its default is OFF (the linear mapping the panel has always used), the choice persists (`LS_VOL_LOG441`), and flipping it mid-play changes what is audible NOW. On the user's point: the stored value is the SLIDER POSITION (0..1) and the taper changes how that position maps to amplitude - no gain value is stored, which is exactly the shape the user described. No new work: the card's own BUILT block above is the record, and the user's question is answered by it. Refresh-only.

### T-447 BUILT - what landed (the client half is refresh-only; the host half needs a harness restart)
HOST (lib/index.js). storage_status now answers a second question inside the SAME read, because a second request for
the same panel opening is how a diagnostic turns into load. A bounded walk of the plugin's own store - at most 20000
files, eight levels deep, symbolic links never followed, an unreadable subdirectory skipped rather than fatal -
produces a `store` object: the store path, its bytes, its file count, a truncated flag when either cap was hit, the
store's direct children as parts sorted largest first, and a per-root number for each of the four roots. The root
records were left untouched on purpose: the host suite freezes them to exactly {path, exists, writable, free_bytes,
total_bytes, error}, and a diagnostic should widen its own output rather than break a pinned contract. In a realm
without node builtins the same answer comes from `du -sb --max-depth=1`, one bounded call, and that route reports
null for file counts instead of inventing one - a missing number that is labelled is honest, an invented one is not.
Two facts that came out of measuring rather than assuming:
1. The store total is the store, not a sum of its parts. Three of the four roots live INSIDE the store directory, so
   adding the root numbers to the store total would count them twice. The payload therefore carries the tree and
   never a summed figure, and the client never adds anything.
2. These are file sizes, not disk usage. The texts folder measured 2 672 bytes here against 16 K from du, because
   du counts allocated blocks and this walk counts the bytes the files hold. The filesystem rows above answer a
   different question again - what the filesystem has - so the panel now shows three kinds of number and says which
   is which.
3. A size-sorted list loses the folder the request actually named. Parts come back sorted largest first, and on the
   real store that order is takes, transcriptions, voices, perf log, state file, state backups - texts is eighth of
   eight. Show six of them by size and the texts folder never reaches the line, even though the user named it. The
   client now puts the four named folders first, in that order, and lets the leftovers fill in behind: order on this
   line is meaning, not magnitude. The test fixture was rebuilt from the real measured store for the same reason - a
   fixture made only of the four folders asked about cannot catch the failure mode the feature actually had.
CLIENT (lib/client.js). Under the storage rows in Settings, one line. Rendered from the store measured above it reads
exactly: "this plugin's own files: 1.4 GB in 1445 files - takes 1.3 GB (954), transcriptions 79 MB (459), voices 19
MB (20), texts 2.6 KB (3), perf_log.jsonl 4.2 MB (1), state.json 39 KB (1)". Directory spellings are replaced by the
plugin's own words for the four folders a person actually thinks about, a raw byte string never appears on this panel
(the readability rule T-199 established), a count stopped at the cap says so, and the line carries a hover that
states what it measures and when. It is its own line rather than another number in the same row because the rows
above answer what the FILESYSTEM has while this answers what THIS PLUGIN holds. The low-space warning stays exactly
where it was and no second alarm was added.
PINS. Five added to the host suite, which now reports 1616 pass 0 fail: the store arrives as its own object while the
root records keep their pinned shape; the store is measured, with bytes, a count and parts naming the folders asked
about; every part is smaller than the whole and the whole is smaller than the filesystem it sits on; the takes folder
is the largest part today; and measuring the store still writes NOTHING - no probe file, no policy request. Five
added to ui_state, which now reports 553 pass 0 fail: a host that answers without a store object renders no store
line and leaves the storage rows exactly as they were, which matters because the client half ships before the host
half does; a host that answers with a store gets exactly one line and the filesystem rows are untouched; the line
uses the plugin's words and counts and never a raw byte string; and a truncated walk says so instead of presenting a
smaller number as the whole. Writing the ui_state pins caught two things about this panel: changing what
storage_status returns has to be followed by asking again, because the panel keeps the answer in its own state and
re-rendering alone only re-shows what was already fetched; and the fixture had to be rebuilt from the real store
before it could catch the ordering bug described above. Full client board after the change: 1657 pass 0 fail.
WHAT IS NOT VISIBLE YET. The running harness is the process started at 07:44 UTC today, before this edit, so the live
panel right now answers without a store object and therefore shows no store line. That is the pinned backward
compatibility behaving correctly, not a missing feature. The line appears at the next harness restart, which joins
the host-side queue already waiting on that restart: the voice_ref fix and its re-test, T-436, T-441, T-422's host
half and T-431's host half.

That settles which half of the disagreement is the accurate statement for these families: the DISPATCH gate is the

be offered for a family the engine declares a clone task for — decision (b) in the card above — and the retry rows

### T-489 BUILT (2026-10-16) - a transcript row now reports the length of the audio it transcribed
1. **Measured on the live store before the change:** of 35 `stt` / `diar` rows, **34 answered
   `duration: 0`** (ap-0639, ap-0645, ap-0598 … all 0; ap-0596 was the exception at 147). The panel showed `--:--` on
   every transcript row, the length was missing from `playlist_list` / `job_status`, and nothing in the store could say
   how much audio a transcription pass had actually covered.
2. **Why it happened, in one sentence:** the only length this plugin ever probed was a rows OWN output file, and a
   transcript row writes a `.txt`. The boot backfill (2026-09-19) had the same blind spot by construction - its filter
   accepted only `.wav/.mp3/.ogg` outputs - so restarting never fixed it.
3. **The fix, in the one place every job ends.** `finishJob` (lib/index.js) now measures a finished transcript row from
   the row's own `file_path` - the audio the engine was given - through the existing `probeDurationShell`, guarded by
   "no length yet" so a diar row that already has one is not re-probed, and a probe that answers nothing leaves the row
   reporting no length rather than inventing one. Helpers: `TRANSCRIPT_KINDS489` (`stt`, `diar`) and
   `transcriptAudioSource489`, which refuses a non-audio or unsafe path outright.
4. **The boot backfill covers them now.** Its filter accepts a transcript row whose input is audio, the probe target is
   chosen per row (own output for an audio row, `file_path` for a transcript row), the bound went from 30 to 60 because
   this store measured 34 rows needing it, and each probe now has a rejection handler (the old code had only a fulfilled
   handler, so a rejected probe could leave the save never scheduled).
5. **Pinned six ways** in `tests/host.test.cjs`: the finished row carries the probed number (30.0 s answered, 30 on the
   row, kind `stt`); the probe ran against the INPUT path and never against the `.txt`; `job_status` answers the same
   number the row carries; when both probes fail (`noDurationAtAll`) the row keeps reporting no length; and two source
   pins place the hook in `finishJob` and the widened filter in the backfill. Measured: host **1778 pass, 0 fail**
   (1772 before). Client board spot-checked green after the change: render 207 (0 throw), actions 203, ui_state 612,
   transport 107, tooltips 12.
6. **A test that was wrong, not the code.** The first negative case used `probeDur: '0'` and the row came back 4.3 s:
   `probeDurationShell` falls back to `ffmpegDurationShell` when ffprobe answers 0, and the harness ffmpeg seam answers
   `Duration: 00:00:04.25`. The honest negative is `noDurationAtAll`, which fails both probes - and that is what is
   pinned now.
7. **What is live when.** Host-side, so it needs the next restart the user takes. Until then the 34 existing transcript
   rows keep answering 0, and the backfill fixes them at that restart (60 rows per boot, and this store has 34). The
   panel needed no change: its time cell already draws `duration > 0` for any row kind and already says "no audio length
   reported for this row" when there is none.

1. **The blind spot, measured.** The engines own `/v1/models` answer carries a `loaded` flag per model. The plugin read

   nobody owned any more looked identical to an idle one: `online:true http:200`. The engine offers nothing richer:
   `/health` answers `{status, backend, models, ui, ui_management}`, and both `/v1/ui/models` and `/v1/status` answer
   `unknown endpoint` (measured on cpu2 2026-10-16).
2. **The change.** `loadedModelIds490` reads the flag out of the model answer the `endpoint_models` door already has in
   hand (no second request), for the primary and for a registry entry alike. The value is carried on the endpoint
   (`loaded_models` / `loaded_at`), surfaced additively in `primaryEndpointView` and `registryEntryView`, and recorded
   in the perf log as `loaded` plus up to 8 `loaded_ids`. A fresh session that has not read an endpoint answers
   `loaded_models: []` with `loaded_at: 0` - "not read yet", never a claim that the engine holds nothing.

   engines are holding the diar model from the windowed runs, and nothing in the plugin has a job on either of them.
4. **Pinned six ways** (tests/host.test.cjs): the not-read-yet state, the primary answer, the registry exposure without
   a second probe, the perf-log record, the registry-entry path agreeing with the door answer, and a source pin. The
   T-243 key-parity guard was extended on BOTH sides at once (its hardcoded list grew `loaded_at` / `loaded_models`)

### T-497 BUILT (2026-10-16, user request) - the voices tree gained the bucket it could not name: hardcoded "ungrouped"
1. **The request, verbatim:** "in voices selection tree, add hardcoded group 'ungrouped' under 'all groups'".
2. **What was missing, and why the tree could not produce it itself.** The group axis (T-361) is DERIVED:
   `gIdx361` counts the group labels the rows already carry, and the shelf offers only labels that exist —
   "a group with no voice under it is not offered at all". That rule is right for filed groups, but it left the
   opposite case unnamed: a voice carrying **no** group had no chip, so the only way to see those voices was to drop
   the filter and scan the rows. With no filing made at all, the shelf showed only "all groups" plus the empty-state
   line, and the whole store was ungrouped with nothing to click.
3. **What it is now.** A hardcoded chip directly under "all groups": `ungrouped (N)`, counted from the same rows
   (`rows.filter(isUngrouped361).length`), offered whether or not anybody has filed anything. Clicking it narrows to
   exactly the voices carrying no group; clicking it again drops the pick; the store counts in the tree do not move,
   as with any other group pick.
4. **The pick id is a sentinel (`"__ungrouped__"`), not the word.** A person who files a REAL group and names it
   "ungrouped" gets its own chip and its own count from `gIdx361`; the label helper renders the word for display only.
   Neither bucket can shadow the other, and the hover on the hardcoded chip says so out loud.
5. **One door for the filter.** The group line in the row predicate became `groupRowMatch361(p, group361)`, which
   answers a filed group and the hardcoded bucket in one place, so the "ungrouped" case is not a special branch
   bolted onto the render. The count line and the empty-state sentence read the same door (`groupCount361`,
   `groupLabel361`), so the sentence no longer risks printing the sentinel id.
6. **Two older pins had to move, and that is recorded rather than smoothed over.** The T-361 pins asserted those
   exact source lines (`if (group361 && (p.groups || []).indexOf(group361) < 0) return false;` and
   `gIdx361[group361] !== undefined`); the door rename made them red before they were updated. They now assert the
   door and both of its arms, and the second one also pins that the hardcoded chip exists and is counted from rows.
   The rule they guard is unchanged.

   invisible: the chip says `ungrouped (3)`; clicking it shows exactly those 3 rows, states `showing 3 of 3`, and moves

### T-502 BUILT 2026-10-16 (host half needs the next restart) - a paused-but-enabled endpoint could not be brought
back from the panel: the first verb of the click was a no-op and the host refuses no-ops (user report 2026-10-16:
"some endpoints still show as paused in endpoints settings and i can't unpause them")
1. **Measured live, on the running host, before touching anything.** `GET endpoint_registry?fn=tts` answered
   `e-10 gpu1.test:8963 enabled:true paused:true paused_by:none`; `fn=stt` answered the same for `e-9`. The panel's
   `enable` press sends two verbs (T-300 U-7): `endpoint_update {fn,id,enabled:true}` and then, when the row was
   paused, `endpoint_resume {fn,id}`. Replaying the first verb by hand answered:
   `{"ok":false,"error":"nothing to change — pass url, route, enabled, batch_allowed, paused or models"}` — because
   `enabled` was ALREADY true, so the write touched nothing (`touched` stays 0 at lib/index.js:16940-16955, and the
   primary branch has the same rule at :16918).
2. **Why that becomes "I can't unpause it".** `call()` rejects on `ok:false`, and `endpointAction`'s chain is a
   promise chain (`lib/client.js`, the `wasPaused299` branch): the rejection goes to the `catch` at the end of the
   chain, so **the second verb is never sent**. What the person sees is the red toast
   `endpoint_update refused: nothing to change — …` and a row that still says `paused`. A DISABLED row works, because
   there the first verb is a real change; a paused-but-enabled row has no first verb that changes anything, so it can
   never be reached from the panel. Measured the other half too: `POST endpoint_resume {fn:"stt","id":"e-9"}` alone
   cleared the pause and it was still clear 8 s later with nothing re-applying it, so the host's resume path was never
   the problem — the click never got that far. The pause was restored to exactly the state the user had ruled.
3. **The rule the host needed, and where the line is.** An idempotent press is not an error, and a press that names
   nothing to do is not a press. So the handler now counts two things instead of one: `asked` (a recognised key was
   present in the body — url, route, enabled, batch_allowed, paused, or a models list) and `touched` (a value actually
   changed). `asked > 0 && touched === 0` answers `ok:true` with `changed: []`, the endpoint view, and a note that
   names the state it found; `asked === 0 && touched === 0` keeps the old refusal word for word, on both the primary
   branch and the registry branch. Nothing about a malformed body became quieter.
4. **The panel half.** `endpointAction` no longer sends a verb that changes nothing: `enable` sends
   `endpoint_update {enabled:true}` only when the row's own host answer says `enabled === false`, and goes straight to
   the resume verb when the endpoint was already enabled and only held. The update call is also tolerant of an
   `ok:false` answer the way the unload verb already is (T-498), so a refusal on the first verb can no longer swallow
   the second one.
5. **Pins.** Host: a no-op `enabled:true` on an enabled endpoint answers ok with `changed: []` and the endpoint view;
   the same on the primary; a body with no recognised key still refuses with the unchanged sentence; a real change
   still reports `changed` with the key named. Client: pressing the state control on a paused-and-enabled row sends
   ONE verb (`endpoint_resume`) and not an update; pressing it on a disabled row still sends the update; the refusal
   on the first verb no longer cancels the second.
6. **This card is also the door T-503 walks through.** The refusal existed to catch a press that asked for nothing;
   the collapse T-503 removes the second verb entirely, and a press that asks for one state is one verb.

### T-527 CLOSED 2026-10-17 (the question was asked, answered, and built in T-536) - the static waveform's take bars collapse to 1 px whenever a bucket's max and min are the same size

1. **The measurement, taken off the drawing and not off the reading of the code.** In the static mode, with the lane's peaks answer in hand (the suite's own fixture: 120 buckets, `min = -a`, `max = +a`, `a = 0.05 + 0.75*|sin|`), the frame paints 67 bars and EVERY one of them is 1 px tall, at y values that do track the amplitude: 22.85, 17.52, 12.71, 8.89, 7.48, 5.81, 5.60, 6.44 … The picture is a row of one-pixel marks that rise and fall, not a min-to-max bar picture.

2. **Why, at the source.** `scopeStaticFrame300` computes `var hi = mid - scale346(mx334) * amp;` and `var lo = mid - scale346(Math.max(-1, mn334) < 0 ? mn334 : 0) * amp;` — and `scale346` takes `Math.abs` of its argument — so BOTH excursions are pushed the SAME way, above the midline. The next line, `if (lo < hi) lo = hi;`, is what turns the resulting negative bar length into 1 px. A bucket whose positive and negative excursions are equal in size therefore draws a bar of zero length, and the guard paints one pixel.

3. **What T-509 did about it, and what it deliberately did not do.** The live station window this card built could not live with that collapse (an analyser frame of a running stream is an AC excursion whose top and bottom are the same size, so the collapse would have drawn a row of dots and the request would not have been served), so the live bar spans what it measured: `hi = mid - scale(max)*amp`, `lo = mid + scale(min)*amp`. The TAKE path was left untouched, byte for byte, and its 1 px collapse is pinned nowhere — no suite asserts bar heights in the static mode today, which is why this went unnoticed for as long as it did.

4. **Why it is a question and not a fix.** The static waveform is a display the user has tuned more than once (T-333 play head, T-334 aggregation and the 2 px floor, T-307 the strip's size), and "make the bars span min to max" changes what every take looks like in that box — including the ghost layer T-509 just added behind the live window. That is the user's call, not a code detail, so under the standing ruling of 2026-10-16 (no question rounds; skip what needs a decision and record the skip) it is recorded here rather than acted on.

5. **What the fix would be, if the answer comes back yes.** One expression in `scopeStaticFrame300` (`lo = mid + scale346(...) * amp`), the same guard kept for the asymmetric case, and new pins on bar HEIGHTS in the static mode — the existing static checks count rects (scenario K asserts `fillRects` grew by at least 100) and would not notice either way, which is exactly the gap this card is recording.

6. **State:** not built, no code changed for it, question pending. Discovered while building T-509; the full measurement trail is on the T-509 card, item 6.


7. **The question was asked and answered (2026-10-17 question round).** It went out as: "Should the take picture draw
   each bar from its measured minimum to its measured maximum, the way the live window already does?" with the
   alternatives being to leave the take path alone or to give the collapsed bar a minimum height. The answer was
   **"Both variants span the excursion"**. Item 5 of this card predicted the fix exactly — one expression and new pins
   on bar HEIGHTS — and that is what was built, on the T-536 card.
8. **What proves it now.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` mounts a symmetric sine (240 buckets, `max = +a`, `min = -a`, loud
   half 0.72, quiet half 0.18) — the shape the collapse ate — and reads the bars of the last frame the panel drew:
   67 bars, none of them 1 px tall. Before this card there was no pin anywhere on static bar heights, which is what
   let the defect survive from T-334 to 2026-10-17.

### T-536 BUILT 2026-10-17, CLIENT HALF (browser refresh, no restart) - the take waveform and the station waveform are one instrument: same bar geometry, one colour choice, no ghost, mark where the sound is

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "The new stream-waveform plotter is nice, but now it clashes with the re-design you did for
   the file-based variant vs stream-based variant -> should be harmonized - with the position marked (red line being
   removed during stream play) and file-based variant showing the waveform in white again - the current 'green
   dots'-variant is not usable -> ask to refine". Four refining answers came back from the 2026-10-17 round: both
   variants span the excursion; the colour becomes a toggle in the visualizer settings between white, DotMatrixGreen
   and Flames, "with Flames making the color dependant on the amplitude"; "The mark should show current position on
   the waveform that is being heard"; and the ghost behind the live window — "i guess: drop it, see 1".
2. **The green dots, and why they were dots.** `scopeStaticFrame300` put BOTH excursions above the midline
   (`mid - scale(max)*amp` and `mid - scale(min)*amp`, and `scale()` takes the absolute value), so a bucket whose top
   and bottom are the same size produced `lo > hi`, and `if (lo < hi) lo = hi;` turned it into 1 px. Measured on the
   suite's own symmetric fixture before this card: 67 bars, every one 1 px tall. That is the whole T-527 card, which
   this card closes by doing the thing it asked permission to do.
3. **The take bar now spans what it measured:** `hi = mid - scale346(mx334) * amp`, `lo = mid + scale346(mn334) * amp`,
   the guard kept for the asymmetric case. The live window already drew this way since T-509, which is exactly why the
   two pictures looked like two instruments.
4. **The ghost is gone** (see the note appended to the T-509 card). `scopeStaticFrame300` lost its `ghost309`
   argument, the dim colour `SCOPE_GHOST309` is no longer painted, the play-head suppression that only existed for a
   ghost is gone, and the live branch draws one thing. The peaks read is NOT skipped: the same mode shows a take at any
   moment. Four pins were re-pointed to the new state rather than deleted.
5. **The mark.** During stream play the red line is gone — no `#f85149` is painted anywhere in a live-window frame,
   measured. The mark moved from the fixed middle of the window (T-509's reading of an older ruling, a reference the
   picture travelled across that pointed at nothing) to the NEWEST bar at the right edge, because on a live window the
   position being heard is the newest frame. Its colour is the scheme's OTHER colour, so a mark is never the same
   colour as the bars it marks. In the take view the play head stays where it has been since T-333, still red: the
   user removed the red line "during stream play", not from the panel.
6. **The colour choice.** `audio-play:scope.schemes` (constant `LS_SCOPE_SCHEMES536`), one value per mode, three
   values: `white` (`SCOPE_CAP300`, the strip's own near-white), `green` (`SCOPE_TEXT300`, the dot-matrix green this
   strip has drawn a waveform in since the beginning), `flames`. Default for the waveform mode is `white`, which is the
   "in white again" of the ask. The control is a third cell on the waveform row of the visualizer table, built like
   the level box beside it — same box, same size, press cycles the value, the word on the box is the value in use — and
   its hover names what the current value means.
7. **The flames thresholds, stated rather than inherited halfway.** Yellow at `SCOPE_YELLOW_AT300` = 0.66, which is
   the point the strip's peak caps already turn at. Red at `SCOPE_FLAMES_RED536` = 0.9, which is NEW: the panel's bar
   ramp has only ever had one turning point, so the second one is chosen by this card and written into the constant's
   comment and into the control's hover, where a reader can check it against the picture. A bar's colour and its height
   are computed from the same number (`Math.max` of its two excursions), so a tall bar cannot be coloured as if it were
   quiet — pinned at source level.
8. **Scope, deliberately narrow.** The scheme is wired to the waveform mode only. A stereo trace is two colours because
   it is two measurements, and a VU face's green, amber and red ARE levels; repainting those under a colour switch
   would take meaning away from a picture to satisfy a setting the user asked for next to a waveform. Extending the
   choice to the other modes is a question, not an assumption.
9. **The refresh limiter is on the next card (T-537), built the same day.** The level list the user gave was "120/ 60
   (default) / 30 /20 /12 /0 fps". Two entries needed a word first: 120 is above what a browser draw loop hands out on
   this display (about 60), and 0 reads two ways — the strip drawing nothing, or drawing every frame with no cap. Both
   were asked in the 2026-10-17 round and both were answered: **"Cap only: 60 (default) / 30 / 20 / 12"** and **"Drop 0
   from the list"**. What was built, and the shape the cap takes, are on T-537.
10. **Suites.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` 215 / 0: nine pins added by this card (no bar is 1 px on a symmetric wave; white
    by default and the green absent; one control, on the waveform row only, naming its value; the hover explains the
    value and the press; the press cycles and stores; a mount stored on green draws green; a mount stored on flames
    puts the loud half at 0.72 in yellow and the quiet half at 0.18 in green with no red below nine tenths; the flames
    hover states both turning points; and the source pin above), plus the six re-pointed T-509 pins. Full sweep green:
    ui_state 787, render 209, transport 109, actions 203, flow 80, shut 62, transparency 22, event_log 35,
    stream_overlap 133, scope 215, batch_board 29, tooltips 12, shell_safety 31, model_library 45, model_matrix 16,
    scene_composer 83, selection_memory 62, engine_boot 99, effects 4, endpoint_exclusivity 105, handlers OK.
11. **Three harness facts learned while writing those pins, each of which changed how the pins read the drawing.**
    1. `br.frames(1)` draws nothing once the mock has run a take to its end and the panel has stopped its draw loop —
       measured three times before this paragraph was written, and it is why the first version of these pins reported
       `bars: 0` while the log held 1036 real rects.
    2. A fixed tail slice of the rect log crosses a frame boundary: `slice(-80)` measured 80 bars where one frame holds
       67, which is how a pin starts disagreeing with itself.
    3. What is used instead: walk backwards from the end of the log while x keeps decreasing — that is the seam between
       two frames — and mount a page with the value already stored, which is how this suite tests every stored choice
       (the level table above is tested the same way). A stored value is what a reload hands the panel.
12. **Refresh debt:** every change on this card is client-half. No harness restart is needed; the browser has to be
    refreshed for any of it to be visible.

### T-537 BUILT 2026-10-17, CLIENT HALF (browser refresh, no restart) - a global draw cap for the visualizer, and the playlist row's control named `clr` because it no longer deletes anything

1. **Two asks, one round.** The first, verbatim: "the 'visualizer' settings options should get another dropdown to set
   a global 'refresh timer' to limit or increase desired frame rate vs cpu usage in maybe 5 levels". The second came as
   the answer to the delete question this card's other half answers: "do 1 - and re-label those buttons from 'del' to
   'clr' in playlist", where option 1 was "Del becomes entry-only now, no file branch".
2. **The levels, and the two that were taken out.** The user's list was "120/ 60 (default) / 30 /20 /12 /0 fps". Asked
   what 120 should mean (the strip re-arms with `requestAnimationFrame` and this display offers about 60, so a 120
   option is a label over a picture that cannot have it) the answer was **"Cap only: 60 (default) / 30 / 20 / 12"**.
   Asked what 0 should mean (the strip drawing nothing, or drawing every frame uncapped) the answer was **"Drop 0 from
   the list"**. So the control offers four values, 60 is the default and is what the panel does today, and the cap can
   only slow the strip down. That is honest arithmetic: a limiter cannot hand out frames the display does not draw.
3. **What the cap gates, and what it deliberately does not.** `audio-play:scope.fps` (constant `LS_SCOPE_FPS537`), read
   into a ref at mount and on every change. In the draw loop: `var ratio537 = scopeFpsRatio537(scopeFpsRef537.current);
   if (ratio537 <= 1 || (n % ratio537) === 0) { try { scopePaint300(); } ... }` — the ratio is counted against a
   nominal 60 Hz display (30 → every 2nd frame, 20 → every 3rd, 12 → every 5th), and on a display offering a different
   cadence the ratio holds and the rate scales with the display. The re-arm, the `scopeLive300()` liveness check and
   the tap self-heal keep running every frame on purpose: the heal counts quiet frames, and a cap that also slowed that
   clock would hide a second behaviour — when a dead tap gets thrown away — inside a setting about CPU. Nothing is
   drawn when nothing is playing, which was already true and is said on the control.
4. **The cost of a lower rate is stated, not hidden.** The analyser is sampled when the strip draws, so a capped strip
   reads less of the wave, and the live window's 67 bars cover more seconds of a station. That sentence is in the
   dropdown's hover and in the constant's comment, because "fewer frames for less CPU" is only half of what it buys.
5. **The control is the one the ask named.** `h("select", …)`, class `audio-play-scope-fps537`, in the visualizer group
   of Settings above the per-mode table, with its own heading "Visualizer — how often the strip draws", because it is
   one number for the whole strip and not a per-mode choice. The user asked for "another dropdown" and got a dropdown;
   a cycling box would have been this card inventing a second idiom for a value with four known states.
6. **A refused value changes nothing.** The first version of the setter ran the incoming value through the same reader
   the mount uses, so `999` was quietly rewritten into 60: a broken setting restored by an act that never happened, and
   the store rewritten along with it. The setter now rejects anything outside the four options and touches neither ref
   nor store. A corrupt value already in the store is a different case and still falls back to the default at read
   time. This was found by a pin written for this card, not by reading the code.
7. **The row control.** `Del` on a playlist row asked "Remove file from disk? OK = row AND file, Cancel = row only".
   It is now `clr`, it asks nothing, it always sends `delete_file:false`, and its hover says the saved file stays on
   disk. The name went with the act, on the user's word: a control named Del that never deletes a file is a word the
   user has to un-learn at every reach. `deleteJob(id, deleteFile)` keeps its second argument and the host still
   honours `delete_file` for any caller that asks — this card is about who may ask from a playlist row, and the answer
   is nobody. The voice row's `Del` (a voice entry and its WAV, confirm-gated) and the Output section's delete-all
   (the takes store, confirm-gated) keep their names and their confirms: neither is a playlist row.
8. **Suites.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` 221 / 0: six pins for this card (one dropdown with exactly 60/30/20/12, no 120
   and no 0, showing 60; the hover naming the cost; a choice stored and shown; a value outside the four refused with
   the cap unmoved; a page stored on 30 showing 30; and a source pin on the gate and the ratio function).
   `tests/actions.test.cjs` 202 / 0: the three pins that measured the confirm dialog (yes → `delete_file:true`, no →
   false, and the label `Del`) were replaced by two that measure the new ruling — one `clr` per playlist row and
   nothing named `Del` carrying the "stays on disk" promise, and a press that never reaches a confirm that is installed
   and would answer YES. The voice Del pins and the delete-all pins are untouched.
9. **How the cap is pinned, and why it is not pinned as a frame count.** Measured while writing these pins: the mock
   runs a take to its end while a press is being flushed, the panel stops its draw loop when the element says "ended",
   and a later `frames(n)` draws nothing — so a pin counting rects across frames measures whether a take is still
   playing, not whether a draw was skipped. The control is measured by what it offers, what it shows and what it
   stores; the gate itself is read at source.
10. **Not built, still open:** the on-demand "remove unreferenced takes now" verb (host-side, needs a restart OK), and
    the per-row format menu from the download-format ruling (T-468 items 31 to 34).

11. **The shared Settings box caught this card, by measurement.** `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` T-510 counts the controls
    in the Settings section off the DRAWING and reads each one's own drawn style. The first version of the new dropdown
    carried `inputStyle` plus a bespoke `width: "150px"` and its own padding, and three T-510 pins failed: the count of
    dropdowns, a deviation list naming `padding="4px 6px"`, `height=undefined`, `fontSize="12px"`, and the widths rule
    that allows only 70 / 86 / 140 plus `auto` plus the unset ones. It now takes `selectStyle510` like every other
    control in that section, and the counts moved 4 → 5 dropdowns, "all ten controls" → "all eleven", and the source
    pin's adopted count 11 → 12, each re-point written with the card that moved it. This is the pin doing the job its
    label claims: a control added later without the shared box fails there rather than looking fine.
12. **A wording rule this card ran into:** T-236 guards the panel against printing a raw host error with a blunt test —
    no rendered text may contain the substring `raw `. The caption under the new dropdown said "a draw cap", and `draw `
    contains it, so the pin failed on a sentence about frame rates. The guard is left blunt on purpose (it is cheap and
    it catches the thing it was written for) and the sentence moved to "a cap on drawing". Recorded because it is a rule
    about WORDING that applies to every control built after this one, and nothing in the code says it.

### T-539 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - the spectrum analyser's switch is dB / log, and the spectrum has its colour choice with flames rendering

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "about vis settings: 'spectrum analyser' - change switch dB / amp to switch between 'dB and
   log' - the current 'amp' seeting is too low, add second option to switch between grren/flames colors, and add the
   flames rendering option".
2. **What is being said about `amp`.** The spectrum's second level option is a linear normalized amplitude, and the
   user's reading is that it sits too low — quiet bands are barely visible next to loud ones. `log` is asked for as the
   alternative, which is a compressed scale: the quiet end gets room, the loud end stops owning the whole box. The exact
   mapping (reference point, how many decades of level the box spans, and whether the peak-hold caps follow the same
   curve) is the open part, and it is asked about rather than guessed.
3. **Colour, for this mode.** The user's answer to the scope question was: "spectrum analyser, oscilloscope and VU faces
   should get another color option, too, I will give information below". For the spectrum the named pair is green /
   flames (white is not named for this mode), and flames has to be RENDERED here, not just reused from the waveform: a
   spectrum bar is a frequency band, and the amplitude that decides its colour is that band's own level.
4. **What this card does not decide:** the oscilloscope and the VU faces' colour options, which the user says they will
   describe, and whether the existing two-colour stereo trace keeps a colour per channel under a scheme (T-536 item 8
   recorded why those modes were left alone; this card reopens it on the user's word).
5. **Depends on:** T-536 (the scheme machinery this extends) and the user's colour information.
6. **What `log` was defined to be.** Asked directly, the user's answer was: "the current 'amp' is not to 'slow' it's
   not enough amplitude - the mapping should favour fast changes and peaking - same spacing and sizes for now". So the
   band count, the bar widths, the inset, the gaps and the peak-hold caps are untouched; only the height mapping
   changed. The curve is `log10(1 + 9a)` over the amplitude `a`: 0 at silence, 1 at full scale (so a peak still
   saturates the ladder, which is the peaking half of the request), and its slope at silence is 9 / ln(10) = 3.91
   against 1 for a straight amplitude line - a small change near silence moves the bar, which is the "favours fast
   changes" half written as a number.
7. **Measured against the two spacings the mode has been offered** (the mock analyser's window is -100 dB to -30 dB,
   and the strip's own ladder floor and top are -70 dB and 0 dB): a bin reported at 200 of 255 (-45 dB) lights 5
   segments on dB spacing and 1 on log spacing; the same bin at the ceiling (255, -30 dB) lights 8 segments on dB and
   2 on log. The quiet pair is reported as what the DRAWING shows rather than as a victory for either mapping: a
   ladder cut in 4 px steps (3 px segment plus 1 px gap) cannot separate these two curves at -45 dB, where they
   differ by a fraction of one segment. That limitation is stated in the pin, not smoothed over.
8. **The colour control, and a vocabulary per mode.** The spectrum row now carries the same toggle box the waveform
   row has, cycling that mode's two words: `green` (the bargraph bands this mode has always worn - green body, yellow
   upper third, red tip, unchanged) and `flames` (every segment of every bar takes its colour from the shared flame
   ramp at its own height). A mode's own list is what its control cycles AND what a stored value is checked against,
   so `white` cannot leak from the waveform's vocabulary into the spectrum's, and the spectrum's default is `green`.
   `scopeBar300` gained an OPTIONAL palette argument: every caller that does not name one paints exactly what it painted
   before, so the modes the ruling did not name are untouched, and "green" and an absent palette are deliberately the
   same painting - the word names what already happens rather than changing it.
9. **A real bug a pin caught, recorded because it is the reason the pins exist.** The first version of the spectrum
   cell printed the WAVEFORM mode's colour word on the spectrum row: the box's label was still read from the static
   mode while its hover correctly described the spectrum's value. `T-536, re-pointed by T-539` is what found it - the
   control existed, its hover was right, and the word on the box was wrong. A screenshot of that panel would not have
   shown it, because both rows would each have looked like a plausible word.
10. **What is still open on this card.** The oscilloscope and the VU faces still have NO colour control: the user's
    word was "spectrum analyser, oscilloscope and VU faces should get another color option, too, I will give
    information below", and the information for those two has not arrived. A colour invented for someone else's meter
    before that word is a guess, so the rows are left alone. Also still open: whether the oscilloscope's two-channel
    trace keeps a colour per channel under a scheme (T-536 item 8 left it alone; this card reopens the question on the
    user's word and does not answer it).
11. **Pins** (`tests/scope.test.cjs` 225 / 0, from 221 at the start of this build). The mock learned `b.hotBinValue`,
    which names how loud a hot bin is rather than only which bins are hot - without it the mapping difference is
    invisible to a 4 px ladder and a pin would have been written about a number it could not see. `T-506b` was
    re-pointed rather than deleted (its switch-honouring point survives; only its second word changed), the hot-bin
    pair and the mapping's source pin are new, and the table pin now measures two controls on two named rows.

### T-540 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - the waveform flames ramp is a continuous flame gradient, not three bands

1. What exists today (T-536): three flat colours chosen from the bar's own excursion — green, yellow past two thirds
   (`SCOPE_YELLOW_AT300` = 0.66), red at nine tenths (`SCOPE_FLAMES_RED536` = 0.9, chosen by that card and stated).
2. "Better" is the user's word and it is not yet defined here: it can mean a continuous gradient instead of three
   bands, more turning points, different thresholds, or a different hue range (amber toward white at the top). Asked
   rather than guessed, because a ramp is exactly the kind of thing this panel's user has tuned more than once.
3. What is measurable regardless of the answer: the ramp must stay a function of the number that sets the bar's height,
   so colour and height cannot disagree about how loud a bar is. That rule is pinned at source level since T-536.
4. **The user's answer, verbatim** (asked what was wrong with the three bands): "I was imagining a 'flames like
   optical effect with a fluent conversion into the color change-not mapped to defined levels' - louder=hotter color".
   So the thresholds are gone, not moved.
5. **What was built.** One shared ramp, `scopeFlameColour540`, four stops linear between them: a deep ember
   `rgb(122,31,10)` at the bottom, orange `rgb(255,122,0)` at 0.45, the strip's own yellow `rgb(255,216,0)` at 0.75,
   and a near-white `rgb(255,244,200)` at the top. It is used by the waveform's `flames` value (one colour per bar,
   from that bar's own excursion) and by the spectrum's `flames` value (one colour per SEGMENT, from that segment's own
   height, which is what makes a bar read as one flame rather than three stacked bands). The stops are named constants
   in one place, because the shape of a flame is a taste decision and a taste decision has to be re-tunable without
   hunting through a drawing function.
6. **The bottom stop is an ember, not black, and that is a decision worth knowing.** On the strip's dark canvas a bar
   that fades to black is a bar that is not there, and a quiet passage is still audio. If the user wants the flame to
   die to black at the bottom, it is one number in the stop list.
7. **What was retired.** `SCOPE_FLAMES_RED536` (0.9, the red point T-536 invented and stated in the open) is gone from
   the file, and the history of why it was invented and why it was retired is written where the constant used to be.
   `SCOPE_YELLOW_AT300` and `SCOPE_RED_AT300` stay, because they belong to the bargraph bands of the modes that were
   not given a flame palette - the waveform ramp no longer uses them, the bargraph bars still do. The live window's
   position mark keeps T-536's rule that a mark is never the colour of the bars it marks: in `flames` the bars wear
   the ramp, so the mark goes back to the strip's dot-matrix green, which is the one colour a flame ramp never
   produces.
8. **Pins** (`tests/scope.test.cjs` 225 / 0). The hover pin was re-pointed from "states the two turning points" to
   "states the ramp and says it is continuous", and it now asserts the OLD wording is absent. The bar pin measures the
   ramp as a ramp: in one frame of one test wave (loud half 0.72, quiet half 0.18) the strip carries many distinct
   flame colours - at least six - with at least eight bars in the hot region and eight in the ember region, and NOT
   one bar painted in any of the three band hexes the old variant used.

### T-541 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - a new visualizer mode: level against time against frequency

1. Not built, not designed. The shape a waterfall implies is the spectrum's bands stacked over time — a third mode whose
   picture is a history rather than a frame, which is a different thing from T-509's scrolling window of amplitudes.
2. What has to be settled before code: whether it is the analyser's frequency bins drawn as rows of pixels (a real
   spectrogram, which needs a colour ramp and a scroll direction) or the existing bar grid painted per band over time;
   where its level switch sits in the visualizer table; and what its colour scheme is under the T-536 machinery.
3. It is a new mode in `SCOPE_MODES`, which means the mode cycle, the table, the strip hover, the note text and every
   mode-counting pin in `tests/scope.test.cjs` move with it. That is the cost of a mode in this panel, and it is why
   this is queued rather than squeezed in beside another card.
4. **Designed 2026-10-17, the user's own words:** "waterfall spectru[m] analyser with different options of color
   mapping, … the full canvas should be used (hide timers) like for the VUs … should have option to go bottom->up or
   top->bottom (setting) - frequency waterfalls, maybe with later '3D' option". So: a real spectrogram painted from
   `getByteFrequencyData`, not the bar ladder painted over time.
5. **The settled shape.** Frequency axis: **log**, matching the mapping the spectrum already uses (fftSize 1024 gives
   512 bins, 23.4 Hz each on a 24 kHz lane; raw linear bins put nearly all resolution in bass, which is why the
   panel's spectrum is log-mapped in the first place). Bass at the bottom, treble at the top. Default direction:
   **newest frame painted at the bottom, history pushed upward**; the opposite direction is a stored setting, because
   the user asked for the option rather than for a preference buried in code.
6. **Full canvas, by joining the gate that already exists.** VU modes already skip the dot-matrix clock band
   (`if (!vu445) scopeClockBand300(...)` and the same gate on `g.translate(0, SCOPE_CLOCK_H300)`,
   `lib/client.js:14494` and `:14500`). The waterfall joins that gate instead of inventing a second way to hide the
   timers, which is what "like for the VUs" means in code.
7. **Colour mappings the switch will offer** (the user picked all four): `green` and `flames` (the two ramps that
   already exist and are already pinned), plus two new ramps defined in code — `ironbow` (black → deep purple → red →
   orange → yellow → white, the classic spectrogram) and `cold` (black → blue → cyan → white). They live in
   `SCOPE_SCHEME_OPTS_BY_MODE539` as a per-mode vocabulary beside `spectrum: ["green","flames"]`, so the T-536
   machinery is extended, not rebuilt. No ramp is fetched; each is a list of stops in the file, like
   `SCOPE_FLAME_STOPS540`.
8. **The cost, stated before writing:** a seventh entry in `SCOPE_MODES300` moves the click cycle, the visualizer
   table (`SCOPE_MODE_WORDS300`), the strip hover, the note text, `SCOPE_LEVEL_MODES346` (the waterfall carries the
   dB/log switch — it is a level picture), the full-canvas gate, and every mode-counting pin in
   `tests/scope.test.cjs`. The fps cap (60/30/20/12) applies to it like to every other mode.
9. **"3D" is a later extension, tracked here so it is not forgotten and not assumed.** A waterfall already has a time
   axis; a 3D view is a different projection of the same frames. It gets its own card when it is asked for.
10. **Three rulings answered 2026-10-17, all three chosen by the user:** the visualizer code stays in the single
    `lib/client.js` (T-554 closed: single client file, as recommended, no build step and no drift pin machinery); the
    history is packed as **one canvas row per frame**, which makes the fps cap the time control (about 1.3 s of history
    at 60 fps, 2.7 s at 30 fps, 4 s at 20 fps on the 80 px canvas); and the waterfall uses the **whole canvas** — the
    dot-matrix clock band AND the peak strip are both hidden, exactly as the VU faces do.
11. **A contradiction in my own option wording, caught before any code.** I offered "log frequency, bass at the
    bottom" together with "newest frame at the bottom, history rising". Those two cannot both be true: if history
    moves up the canvas, the vertical axis is TIME, and frequency has to lie along the horizontal axis (bass at one
    side). The two coherent arrangements are (A) time vertical, frequency horizontal — a waterfall; and (B) time
    horizontal, frequency vertical — a scrolling spectrogram, which is the arrangement that actually puts bass at the
    bottom. The user's own words ("bottom->up or top->bottom") fit (A). The axis arrangement is asked and settled
    before the renderer is written.

12. **BUILT 2026-10-17, client half only.** `lib/client.js` carries the mode, the renderer, the setting and the
    colour ramps. No host change, so no restart is involved; a browser refresh is what shows it.
13. **What the mode is in the tables.** `SCOPE_MODES300` gained `waterfall` BEFORE `off` (`lib/client.js:379`), so
    the click ring is off, spectrum, oscilloscope, static, vu_led, vu_needle, waterfall, off. `SCOPE_LABELS300`
    names it "waterfall — spectrogram history" for the strip hover. The per-mode level table gained a row with the
    analyser's own two words (`dB` / `log`, default `dB`) and the colour box gained a third row, the waterfall's,
    offering `green, flames, ironbow, cold` with `green` as the default — the panel's identity first, the classic
    spectrogram ramp one press away.
14. **Full canvas, by joining the gate that already existed.** `scopeFullCanvas541` (`lib/client.js:385`) is the VU
    predicate plus the waterfall, and the clock band, its `translate`, the peak-strip reservation and the clock's
    click target all ask that one predicate instead of carrying a second way to hide the same two things. The
    per-frame background clear is now gated per mode (`if (m !== "waterfall")` at `lib/client.js:14573`), because a
    waterfall whose canvas is cleared every frame has no history at all; the frame function paints the background
    itself when it is starting fresh.
15. **The renderer, and why the history lives in the canvas.** `scopeWaterfallFrame541` copies the canvas onto
    itself shifted by one row (`drawImage` with the transform reset to identity and the source rect in DEVICE
    pixels, because the source rect is measured in the bitmap's own pixels while the destination is measured in the
    transformed space), then paints one new row of 196 one-pixel columns (200 px less the 2 px of black T-428 keeps
    inside the frame). One row per DRAWN frame, which makes the fps cap the time control. The column map is
    `scopeBandMap300` given a column count — the same log chain the bargraph uses, with its no-bin-shown-twice rule
    intact — cached in a ref so no arithmetic runs inside a frame. Silence paints a row in the ramp's floor colour,
    because quiet and nothing-playing must not look identical (T-511's rule).
16. **Four faults, all found while building this and all fixed in the same act.**
    a. `cycleScopeScheme536("static")` was hardcoded at the render site for every row of the per-mode table, so the
       colour box on the SPECTRUM row printed the spectrum's colour word and changed the WAVEFORM mode's scheme.
       Found by writing a third row that had to cycle its own colour. Now `cycleScopeScheme536(mode346)`. This was a
       live fault in the shipped panel, not a fault in the new mode.
    b. The waterfall asked the ANALYSER for the sample rate. An AnalyserNode does not carry one — the rate belongs
       to the context the node was made from — so the column map came back empty and the mode scrolled a canvas it
       never painted into. The harness showed it as zero one-pixel rects. The bin width is now computed once where
       the context is known and carried on the tap as `t.binHz`, and the bargraph bands read the same number.
    c. The component's state tuple was named `scopeWfDir541`, shadowing the module-level validator of the same
       name, and the `useState` initializer calls that validator — the first render would have called an array as a
       function. Caught while writing; the tuple is `scopeWfDirTup541`. `node --check` cannot see this class of
       fault, which is why the suite is the check that matters.
    d. A standalone `if` for the history reset was first written in the middle of the mode cycle's `if / else if`
       chain, which would have re-parented every `else if` after it and silently changed what the cycle does. Caught
       before it was written; the reset now sits after the chain.
    e. My own caption tripped the panel's blunt wording guard. T-236 forbids the substring `raw ` in anything the
       panel renders (so a host `health_error` can never leak into a phrase), and the caption I wrote — "how far
       back you can see is the **draw cap** times the canvas height" — contains it inside "draw cap". The suite
       caught it; the wording moved to "follows the drawing rate and the canvas height" and the guard stayed blunt,
       which is exactly the outcome the T-537 comment beside that control describes.
17. **What the new pins measure** (`tests/scope.test.cjs`, scenario E541, 253 pass / 0 fail): the ring position
    (five presses from the mounted `off` land on the moving-coil face, the press after them lands on the waterfall);
    a fresh start paints one background fill and copies nothing, and across a run the copies equal the frames minus
    one; a continuing frame paints no background; 196 one-pixel columns per frame; the newest row at y=79 in the
    default direction with a translate offset of zero, and at y=0 in the other; the copy geometry in both
    directions (source rect and destination rect read apart); no clock glyph in the clock green anywhere in the
    mode; the axis direction measured by moving ONE hot bin from index 2 to index 400 and watching the lit column
    move from the left half to the right half, one column only; the direction select carries both words the user
    named, stores `audio-play:scope.wfdir541`, and its hover says which end is now and that the setting affects the
    waterfall and no other mode; four presses on the colour box produce four different colour sets and return to
    green; a column at the top of the analyser window gets a colour that is neither of the two stops it lies
    between, which is the interpolation rather than a band.
18. **Pins that had to move, and why each move is honest.** The no-Web-Audio ring pin: six clicks became seven and
    the label says seven modes. T-421's source pin: the band chain's loop bound is now `nBands541` with no third
    argument still meaning 20, and the pin says that out loud. T-536 / T-539's colour-row pin: two rows became
    three, and the oscilloscope and VU faces still have no colour control because the user's information for them
    has not arrived. The T-307 / T-334 "off reads the analyser no more than before" pin was re-baselined, because
    the waterfall between the old baseline and `off` legitimately reads the analyser and that is not a fault in
    `off`. The suite's fake context gained `drawImage` with all eight numbers recorded, because a mode whose whole
    act is a self-copy cannot be pinned any other way.
19. **`tests/ui_state.test.cjs` re-pointed (798 pass / 0 fail).** The Settings inventory is a measured count, and a
    control was added: the section now holds **five** dropdowns (the draw cap, the queue knobs and the waterfall
    direction) and seven numeric boxes, all eleven wearing the shared box, so `adopted510` went 12 → 13 and the
    outside `inputStyle` count is still 37 — which is the point of that pin and the reason the label names the card
    that moved it. The "all N controls carry the same box" label went ten → eleven. No new ui_state pin was written
    for the waterfall: the direction control is measured where the mode is measured, in the scope suite.
20. **What is NOT claimed.** The history lengths quoted in the design (about 1.3 s at 60 fps, 2.7 s at 30, 4 s at
    20 on the 80 px canvas) are arithmetic from the canvas height and the draw cap, not a measurement taken in a
    browser. No browser refresh was performed by the agent and no screenshot was taken. "3D" is not built. The
    oscilloscope and VU colour options are still unbuilt for the same reason as before: the user's information has
    not arrived. The ramp stop values are the agent's taste decisions, named as constants so they can be re-tuned
    without touching a drawing function.

### T-541 amendment (2026-10-17, same day) - the waterfall's level choice is gone and its direction is now a switch

1. **The ruling, verbatim:** "for waterfall vis: remove \"log\" option, keep only dB option and replace with a
   switch to invert top->dawn direction of the \"waterfall\"".
2. **What the level cell became.** `SCOPE_LEVEL_OPTS346.waterfall` now holds ONE word: `words: ["dB"], def: "dB"`.
   The table renderer was extended rather than special-cased away: a mode with two words gets the cycling press it
   always had, a mode with one word gets the word printed in the same box, with the note "fixed reading" where the
   "dB / log" pair used to be. A button whose only possible action changes nothing is a button that looks pressable
   and does nothing when pressed, which is what T-537 exists to stop. The row itself stays, so the waterfall keeps
   its name press and its colour box.
3. **The log curve was not removed from the panel**, only from this mode. The spectrum mode still offers dB and log,
   and `scopeBarLogFrac539` is untouched.
4. **A stored "log" from before the ruling needs no migration.** The reader compares the stored word against
   `words[0]` and `words[1]`; `words[1]` is now undefined, so a stale "log" resolves to the default exactly the way
   an unknown word always has. No cleanup verb was invented for a case the validator already handles.
5. **The direction is a switch, not a dropdown.** Same class name (`audio-play-scope-wfdir541`), now on the label,
   with an `input type="checkbox"` inside it, which is how the volume-taper switch in the same section is built.
   OFF is "up" - newest along the bottom edge, history rising - which is the default the operator's own phrase
   "bottom->up" describes. ON is "down". **The stored key and the two stored words are unchanged**, so a panel that
   already stored a direction keeps it; what changed is the control that writes it.
6. **Suite fallout, measured rather than asserted.** The visualizer suite went 277 -> 278: the direction pin now
   measures a checkbox whose OFF state is the default and the word beside it names the inverted state; the level pin
   now measures a span with no press handler that prints "dB"; and a new pin measures the whole level table - seven
   cells, six pressable, one read-out, exactly one "fixed reading" note - so a second mode losing its choice by
   accident would fail here. The UI suite stayed at 806 with three pins re-pointed: Settings dropdowns 6 -> 5, the
   shared-box adopters 14 -> 13 (the retired dropdown wore the shared box), and the name-button hover wording.
   Tooltips 12 / 0, full sweep green.
7. **One hover sentence was reworded** because it had become false for this mode: "this mode keeps its own level
   choice" is now "this mode keeps its own level reading".
