### T-542 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - the dancing llama: a silhouette that hops on the bass and steps on an onset, standing in front of a horizontal spectrogram

1. Not built, not designed, and deliberately not guessed. The name says a llama that moves; it does not say what it
   reacts to (level, spectrum, a beat, the peak meter, both channels), whether it is drawn in the same canvas or an
   overlay, or whether it replaces a mode or sits beside the existing five.
2. What the panel already has that such a mode would use: the strip's own measured facts — a smoothed wave, a peak meter,
   both channels, the tap's liveness, and a draw loop that stops when nothing plays. A mascot that animates while nothing
   is audible would be a lie about the audio, and this panel has a standing rule against that (T-511).
3. Needs the user's description before it can become a build.

4. **Designed 2026-10-17, the user's own words:** "1 and 2 - the spectrum should generate the background and the beat
   and base and bps should influence the llama (but just a suggestion, can be optimized / overruled by you)" and, on the
   artwork, "1 - but might be nice to have standalone file/lib to reduce file sizes - adjust as needed".
5. **What that means for build order.** The llama is not a separate picture beside the strip: it rides on the
   spectrogram as its background, so **T-541 is built first and T-542 sits on top of it**. Building the mascot before
   the renderer it stands in front of would mean drawing the stage after the actor.
6. **What drives it in v1, and what is deliberately not claimed.** Bass-band energy (the low bins of the same
   `getByteFrequencyData` read) bobs the body; an onset detector — the jump in total spectral energy between frames —
   triggers a step. **No tempo number is shown anywhere in v1**, because no tempo is measured anywhere in this panel,
   and painting a guessed BPM would be the exact kind of claim T-511 exists to stop. Rhythm measurement as a real
   feature is tracked outside this plugin at workspace `TODOS.md` **WM-15**, which is where the user asked for it:
   "track a bps detection as new long term integration todo for global usage".
7. **Artwork: drawn in code, in the canvas**, in the strip's existing palette, from rectangles and lines — no image
   file, no fetch, nothing external. The separability the user asked for is answered on the card about file layout
   (T-554), not by loading something from disk.

8. **Built 2026-10-17, client half.** `llama` is the seventh entry of `SCOPE_MODES300` and `off` stays last, so the
   ring is eight wide: spectrum, oscilloscope, static waveform, VU ladder, VU coil, waterfall, llama, off. The press
   that leaves the llama lands on `off`, and the mode is persisted under `audio-play:scope.mode` like every other mode.
   The name in the Settings table reads `llama - dancing on a horizontal spectrogram`.
9. **The canvas is split, not shared, and the reason is a fault avoided rather than a layout taste.** The history is
   the canvas (T-541's self-copy), so a copy over the whole 200x80 box would drag the llama's own pixels into the
   spectrogram's history and smear the animal into its own trail. Measured geometry at dpr 1: inset 2 leaves 196x76 to
   draw in; the llama's region is 66 px (a 30x34 grid at 2 px = 60 px, plus 3 px of play either side for the step); a
   2 px black gap; the spectrogram gets the remaining 128 px starting at x 70. The recorded shift is
   `drawImage(cv, 70, 0, 127, 80, 71, 0, 127, 80)` - source and destination both start at x 70 - and the silhouette's
   right edge is x 65. A fresh entry paints exactly one 200x80 background and copies nothing; every frame after it
   copies exactly one column and fills nothing. History length is arithmetic, not a measurement: 128 columns, about
   2.1 s at 60 fps and 4.3 s at 30.
10. **Time runs downward, frequency runs across the column, and bass sits at the BOTTOM** - the axis is vertical in
    this orientation, so the low bins are painted along the bottom edge of the column and the newest column is painted
    at the edge the llama faces. Measured with the harness's band instrument (one hot bin at a time, the same
    instrument T-429 built): bin 2 (46.9 Hz) lights y 72, bin 400 (9.4 kHz) lights y 5, on a 76-pixel column spanning
    y 2..77 at x 70. The chain is the shared `scopeBandMap300` asked for 76 rows, so the bars, the waterfall and this
    mode read the same ladder.
11. **Two measurements drive the body, and only two.** 1) The hop: the loudest byte over the 8 lowest rows of that
    same chain, put through `scopeBarFrac300`, worth at most 3 cells. Measured: 4 px of rise (2 cells) between a
    silent bass and the loudest byte this harness can produce - the mock's ceiling byte 255 reads as -30 dBFS in its
    own window while the panel's ladder runs -70 to 0, so 0.571 of the ladder is the most the fixture can hand the
    mode, and the pin says so instead of asking for a third cell the fixture cannot deliver. 2) The step: spectral
    flux against the PREVIOUS frame, `fluxMean = flux / drawn`, mean bytes risen per row, threshold
    `SCOPE_LLAMA_ONSET542 = 24`. A step runs for 6 frames and alternates a one-cell lean with one hop cell, measured
    as x 5 at rest, x 7 on the frame after a rise, x 3 on the frame after that.
12. **The threshold was moved by measurement, not by preference.** It was written as 40. The suite measured 134 mean
    for a rise across 40 of the 76 rows, 36.9 for a rise across 11 rows, and 3.4 for one bin firing at the same
    level. 40 would have stepped on a broad rise and ignored a moderate one; 24 sits between a broad rise and a
    single flickering bin, and both sides are pinned: the sparse case is asserted NOT to step, because a mode that
    stepped at one bin would be dancing at noise.
13. **No tempo, no BPM, no beat count is painted anywhere in this mode.** The user asked for "the beat and base and
    bps" as an influence and accepted the answer that this panel measures no tempo; the two influences above are
    measurements of the audio, and a guessed BPM is a lie (T-511). Rhythm measurement as a real feature stays at
    workspace `TODOS.md` **WM-15**, where the user asked for it to be tracked for global usage. The frame function
    contains no `fillText`, no clock glyph and no 3x3 cell, and that is pinned against the drawing log rather than
    against the source text.
14. **The artwork is the traced mask, and the trace is on record.** `SCOPE_LLAMA_MASK542` is 34 rows of 30 bits,
    419 lit cells, produced by `scratch/trace_llama.py` from `assets/llama-winamp.png` (the operator's own supplied
    silhouette, 274x274 RGBA): threshold mask 19651 px, kept to the largest 8-connected component at 19384 px, animal
    bbox 202x232, aspect 0.871, contour walk 1045 points, Douglas-Peucker at eps 2.5 down to 79 points, and the
    filled 79-point polygon measured against the source mask at IoU 0.946 before anything was inlined. Mirrored to
    face right, which is the operator's own instruction ("small orientation help - mirror it if needed"). The suite
    re-derives the lit-cell count from the constant in the client and asserts 419, and the drawing log itself is
    asserted at 419 cells per frame, 30 columns wide and 34 rows tall.
15. **Why 34 rows and not the 38 an earlier sampling of the same mask produced.** A 38-row mask at 2 px is 76 px, which is exactly the
    inner height: a body that fills floor to ceiling has nothing to hop into. 30x34 at 2 px is 60x68, which leaves
    8 px (4 cells) of headroom, and the hop's 3 cells fit inside it. The mask was regenerated at that size rather
    than the drawing being scaled into a corner of the canvas.
16. **A fault the suite found that reading the file did not.** The frame function referenced `SCOPE_WF_RAMPS542`, a
    name that exists nowhere in the file. The mode drew one background fill and stopped, because the animation loop
    catches the exception and stops the loop - so the symptom looked like an idle mode, not like a crash. Fixed to
    `SCOPE_WF_RAMPS541`, the same table the waterfall reads, and the reason this is written down is that "the source
    looked right" is not a check: the drawing log is.
17. **Colour.** The silhouette is one colour per frame, taken from the top stop of the ramp the mode was given -
    `SCOPE_WF_RAMPS541`, the same four ramps the waterfall background uses (green by default, flames, ironbow, cold),
    not a colour invented for the animal. Measured: four frames across four ramps, four distinct colours, none of them
    the canvas colour. The spectrogram behind it obeys the mode's own level word (dB or log) and its own ramp, in the
    same Settings row the waterfall's controls live in.
18. **What v1 deliberately does not do.** No direction control (newest column fixed at x 70, the animal fixed facing
    right), no choice of which edge is newest, no upload of operator artwork, no per-channel llama, no tempo. A llama
    with no tap draws no cells and no column: the body moves on measured bands, and a llama standing on invented
    silence would be this mode lying about the audio.
19. **Suite.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` 260 -> 277 pass, 0 fail (17 new pins in scenario F542). Re-pointed rather than
    deleted: the ring is eight wide, the click walk to reach the waterfall is six presses, three T-541 source regexes
    (the shared clear now excludes two modes, `scopeFullCanvas541` is three lines, `SCOPE_MODES300` has eight
    entries), the T-535 body window widened to 3000 characters, and the T-536 colour table is four entries including
    `audio-play-scope-scheme536-llama`.

### T-542 amendment (2026-10-17, same day) - the split canvas is gone: the spectrogram owns the whole width, the history runs right to left, and the llama is wiped every frame

1. **The operator's words, verbatim.** After seeing the first build and a screenshot: "keep llama vis direction
   fixxed, but invert the spectogramm from current variant, also currently it's not interacting and the spectogram
   should fill full canvas length - also, lama is not animated currently". Asked which axis "invert" meant:
   "direction, currently it looks like lama is running backwards - needs to move right to left, while lama is facing
   right - so it looks like a running lama, also, it looks like the lama frames are not removed and only ever added
   resulting in static picture of the lama overlay".
2. **The 66 / 2 / 128 split was removed.** The spectrogram now owns all 196 drawable pixels; the newest column is
   painted at x 197, the far edge - which is the edge the llama faces. `SCOPE_LLAMA_GAP542` is deleted, because a
   constant nothing reads is a fault waiting for someone to believe it.
3. **The shift now moves LEFT.** Measured from the drawing log at dpr 1 on a 200 x 80 canvas with the 2 px inset:
   source (3, 2, 195, 76), destination (2, 2, 195, 76) - the destination starts one pixel to the left of the source,
   so a column painted at the far edge today sits further left in every frame after it and leaves through the left
   edge. The first build ran the other way (newest at x 70, history extending right), which is what read as running
   backwards.
4. **The wipe is what makes the full width safe.** The shift now starts at x 3, which is INSIDE the animal's box
   (x 2..67), so the animal's own pixels ride the copy. After the copy and before the animal is painted, the frame
   fills the box (66 x 76 at the inset) with the canvas colour. Without that fill each frame adds a silhouette on
   top of the last one - the accumulation the operator named. The proof that the wipe works is drawn, not argued:
   three consecutive frames each paint exactly 419 silhouette cells, never 421, never 838.
5. **What did not change:** the llama's own direction (no direction control - "keep llama vis direction fixxed"), the
   mirrored silhouette facing right, bass at the bottom of the column, the onset threshold 24, the six-frame step,
   the hop cap of three cells, the shared ramp table, and the rule that this mode prints no number because the only
   number it could print would be a guess about tempo.
6. **Visible history, measured off the geometry:** the columns that stay visible run from x 68 to x 197, which is 130
   columns - about 2.2 seconds at 60 fps, 4.3 s at 30 fps. Arithmetic on the drawing rate, not a measurement of what
   a person perceives.
7. **A weak pin found while re-pointing the strong ones.** The "this mode paints no text" pin extracted the frame
   function with a brace pattern capped at 4000 characters; the function is 6897 characters today, so the match
   returned an empty string and the pin passed on nothing at all. It now extracts the function by position and
   refuses to assert anything unless the slice is longer than 6000 characters. Same lesson as the undeclared constant
   on this card: the source looked right is not a check.
8. **Suites:** visualizer 277 -> 278, UI state 806 / 0, tooltips 12 / 0, full sweep green.
9. **Still open on this mode, in the operator's own words** ("I would have expected some more artwork and interaction
   between spectogram and lama"): the silhouette's colour is the ramp's brightest stop, and on the green ramp that
   stop is rgb(244,250,244) - near white - which is exactly what the screenshot shows. That was my decision, it is
   written here rather than left to be rediscovered, and the artwork question is the next one being asked.

### T-542 amendment 2 (2026-10-17, same day, second ruling) - the llama is centred and the history moved out of the visible canvas

1. **The ruling, verbatim:** "from the current view i first suggest we center the lama in the canvas and let the
   spectogram fill the full width".
2. **Why the wipe from amendment 1 had to go.** A centred animal and a full-width spectrum cannot share a canvas that
   stores its own history: the animal's box would have to be wiped out of the MIDDLE of the picture, which is a hole
   in the spectrum rather than an animal standing in front of it. The columns therefore moved into a bitmap of the
   mode's own (`scopeLlamaHist542`, built with `document.createElement("canvas")`, never shown). Each frame shifts
   that bitmap, paints the new column into it, blits the whole bitmap onto the visible canvas, and paints the animal
   last, on the visible canvas.
3. **The accumulation fault is now structural rather than patched.** The animal is never painted where the history
   lives, so it cannot be dragged along with the history or pile up inside it. Measured three ways: the history
   bitmap contains no 2 x 2 silhouette cell, the visible canvas receives exactly one whole-canvas blit per frame, and
   three frames running each draw 419 cells.
4. **Centred by arithmetic, not by a box:** `x = inset + floor((innerWidth - gridWidth) / 2) + lean` = x 70 at rest,
   72 and 68 across a step. The pin proves centring rather than asserting a number: the black margin to the left of
   the grid (68 px) equals the black margin to its right (68 px). `SCOPE_LLAMA_PLAY542`, `SCOPE_LLAMA_REGION542` and
   `SCOPE_LLAMA_GAP542` are gone from the file; a source pin asserts that none of them survives.
5. **The harness grew a second canvas.** `document.createElement("canvas")` in the suite now returns an offscreen
   bitmap whose drawings are logged SEPARATELY (`histRectLog`, `histImageLog`). Without that separation "the newest
   column is at x 197" and "the animal is centred" would both be read out of one log, and a mode that painted the
   right thing in the wrong place would pass.
6. **Two faults made while re-pointing, both recorded because both looked fine.**
   - A line comment placed in the middle of a multi-line boolean expression commented out the rest of that line. The
     pin kept passing while one of its clauses was dead. That pin has since been rewritten; the lesson is that a
     passing check is not the same as an intact check.
   - A splice whose range was one line too long swallowed the first line of the neighbouring check and left its tail
     dangling. `node --check` caught it before anything ran. Splice ranges are now taken from the file line by line,
     and the splices run bottom-up so earlier line numbers stay true.
7. **Suites:** visualizer 278 / 0 (11 pins re-pointed, 5 new helpers, one harness capability added), UI state
   806 / 0, tooltips 12 / 0, full sweep green.
8. **What is still open on this mode:** the artwork and interaction question the operator raised ("more artwork and
   interaction between spectogram and lama") is unanswered beyond the layout, and the silhouette is still painted
   with the ramp's brightest stop - near white on the green ramp. The double-click shortcut is T-556.

### T-543 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - during web-stream-only play the read-out shows the rate this browser decodes at, and no bitrate's own numbers are available to show

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "currently during web-stream-only play, the kbps and KHz display are grey: should show stream
   information if easily available".
2. **What the grey means today:** the strip's clock band prints the sample rate and the bitrate it was TOLD. With a take
   those come from the peaks read and the row's own file. With a station the panel has no such read — the lane never saw
   the file — so the fields sit at their unset look, which reads as a broken display rather than as an honest absence.
3. **"If easily available" is the ruling's own limit, and it is the right one.** What a browser hands a panel about a
   stream it is playing is limited and partly unreliable: the element knows its duration (often `Infinity` for a live
   stream) and its buffered ranges, and an analyser gives sample rate of the OUTPUT graph, not of the station's encoder.
   A bitrate is not something the element reports. So the honest options are the analyser's own sample rate, the fact
   that this is a live stream rather than a file, and nothing else — and a field that shows an output-graph sample rate
   as if it were the station's encoder rate is a claim the panel cannot support (T-511: never paint a value the host
   did not answer).
4. Needs a decision about which of those facts to print, which is asked on this card rather than decided in code.
5. **The decision, as the user made it** (asked which facts may be printed): "kHz from the graph we already have, kbps
   left blank". The other offered options — trying the station's own announced ICY bitrate, dropping both numbers for a
   live marker, or pairing the graph rate with the download container — were not chosen. The ICY option would have
   needed a new kind of read from the station being played, and that is a network decision the user has to make, not one
   the panel makes on their behalf.
6. **What was built.** One helper, `streamDecodeHz543()`: it answers the `sampleRate` of the AudioContext the panel
   already builds to feed the visualizer, and it answers 0 unless the tap is a LIVE STATION tap, so a take's own header
   numbers are never replaced by a graph rate and a graph that has been thrown away (the strip is off) answers nothing.
   The read-out prints `24 kHz decoded here` in the strip's ok green. Whole rates print whole, the way the take
   read-out already prints them, so a stream and a take do not wear two number styles for one kind of fact; a rate that
   is not whole prints one decimal rather than being rounded, because rounding a rate is inventing a number.
7. **The bitrate half is left out, not dashed.** `-- kbps` in a rate read-out is read as "zero kilobits" by people who
   read rate read-outs, and this panel has never measured one for a stream. With a station playing and no graph open the
   span says `live stream` in grey rather than printing dashes for two things it does not know; the hover for that state
   is the sentence this card already carried, which says outright that the page is told nothing about a stream's
   bitrate or sampling rate and the panel does not ask the station.
8. **The naming is the point, not the number.** The unit reads "decoded here" rather than "sampling", and the hover
   states three things: the number is the rate this browser decodes the station at, read from the graph the panel built
   for the visualizer; no bitrate is printed and why; and a station's own declared rate, if it declares one, is not
   read here. A number that is true but mislabelled is the failure mode T-511 exists to stop.
9. **Pins** (`tests/scope.test.cjs` 226 / 0). Measured in the scenario where a station is what the graph is fed from:
   the read-out is exactly `24 kHz decoded here` (the mock context decodes at 24000 Hz), it contains no `kbps` and no
   dash, its hover carries both clauses, and its colour is the ok green rather than the unset grey. The take-path pins
   on this read-out (`384 kbps  48 kHz`, and the dashes while the lane has not answered) are untouched and still pass,
   which is the proof that the stream branch did not reach into the file branch.

### T-544 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - the time read-out during stream-only play sits centred in the canvas, keeping the dot-matrix drawing

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "time display during stream only play should be 'centered' within canvas (keep dot-matrix
   allignment)".
2. What is true about that clock today: it is drawn as a 5x7 matrix of glyphs, sized to what fits the strip's width
   (T-334's rule: the band is a matrix of the glyphs that FIT, so the floor is a matrix and not a fixed count), and it
   carries the position read-out. A live stream has no position in a file, which is what the band prints differently in
   that state.
3. Centring is a layout decision inside a matrix that is currently laid out from an edge. Keeping the dot-matrix rule
   while centring means the matrix is built from the middle out (or measured and offset), not that the glyphs are
   stretched. Small, client-half, and it has to keep the existing pins on the band's matrix shape.
4. **What was built (2026-10-17).** The band measures the run it is about to print (`text.length * 6 * cell` — the
   same cell and the same 5-dots-plus-one-gap advance as always), works out the space left between the state mark's
   advance point (x 20) and the right edge (W - 6), and offsets the start x by half of it. Nothing else about the
   drawing changed: same cell size, same glyph matrices, same refusal to draw a partial digit, same state mark hard
   against the left edge. The offset is applied only when BOTH conditions hold: the band is printing the position
   ALONE (T-385's rule — a live stream has no length, so there is nothing after the slash) and the tap is a live
   station tap. A take with a length keeps the layout T-334 gave it, byte for byte.
5. **Where the line is drawn, and why.** "Stream only play" was read as the source, not the mode: the centring follows
   the station tap, so it holds in every visualizer mode that draws the band. It was NOT extended to a take whose
   length happens to be unknown, because that is a take with a missing number, not a stream, and the user's words named
   the stream state. If a take with an unknown length should also centre, that is a one-condition change and it needs
   the user's word.
6. **Pins** (`tests/scope.test.cjs` 223 / 0, from 221). The centring is measured off geometry, not off a colour a
   second element could be wearing: the band's dots are the only 2x2 rects above the 24 px band line (bars are drawn
   below it, the state mark is built from 1 px and 6 px rects). Pin one: in a station frame the MIDDLE of the glyph run
   lands on the middle of the space the mark leaves (within one cell) and the run moved off its old start at x 20 —
   measured run 62..150 in a 200 px band, centre 106 against the space centre 103. Pin two, the counterpin: in a take
   frame the digits still start at exactly x 20. A first version of the pin compared the two pads directly and failed by
   1 px, because the glyph advance carries a gap cell AFTER the last glyph as well as before it; the pad comparison was
   replaced by the centre comparison, which is what centring actually claims.

### T-551 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - a ducked stream stayed ducked after a play act interrupted the take that ducked it

1. **The report, verbatim:** "i have the feeling that the playback of voice samples from the playbutton in the voices
   section OR the playlist, WHILE playing a stream doesn't restore the stream volume after playback, it stays ducked -
   the vol slider shows 100% but setting it to 100% makes it louder , forcing an update of the play volume manually, so
   i guess we are missing the 'restore previous stream volume' after the 'overplay by voice samples' -> needs analysis".
   The feeling was right, and the diagnosis in the report was close: the restore is not missing, it is **closed off**
   before it can run.
2. **The mechanism, read out of the code.** `startPlayback` (client.js:9746) is the one door: it calls
   `applyOverlap395()` before assigning the new take's resource, and its `finish()` - attached as the element's
   `onended` / `onerror` - is the ONLY place `releaseOverlap395()` is called for a take that ends on its own. The three
   play-now acts (`playJob` 12505, `playSrcNow` 12536, `playVoiceNow448` 12548) all interrupt in the same shape: empty
   the client queue, clear the busy flag, `queuePlayback(..., force:true)`. `playJob`'s own comment already states the
   dangerous fact: "replacing src mid-playback never fires 'ended' for the old file, so the flag is cleared here". The
   flag is cleared; the duck token is not handed back. So the interrupting take ducks a station that is **already
   ducked**, remembers that ducked level as its own `prev`, and the level the person had set is lost together with the
   token that held it. When the second take ends, the station is restored to the duck level. That is exactly what the
   user hears: quiet stream, slider still reading 100 %, moving the slider makes it louder.
3. **Reproduced before it was fixed**, in `tests/stream_overlap.test.cjs`, by writing the pin as the correct behaviour:
   station at the duck level after the first take (0.25), a second play act pressed while that take is still playing,
   the take ended - expected 1, measured **0.25**. The suite's existing single-take pin (the station gets its volume
   back exactly) passes, which is why this went unnoticed: the leak needs an interrupt, and no pin interrupted anything.
4. **The fix, in one place.** `applyOverlap395()` now releases an outstanding overlap **before** it takes a new duck:
   it restores the element the previous token ducked (or resumes the one it paused), clears that token, and only then
   reads the station's level as its own `prev`. It is a narrow restore rather than a call to `releaseOverlap395()`,
   because the panel's readings are about to be owned by the new take a few lines later and handing them to the station
   in between would be a flicker nobody asked for; what must not be skipped is the element's own level. One fix covers
   all three doors because all three walk through `startPlayback`.
5. **Pins** (`tests/stream_overlap.test.cjs` 137 / 0, from 133): the duck does not compound (the station sits at the
   duck level once, not at the duck of a duck), the hand-back after an interrupt is measured, and a source pin asserts
   that the release happens inside `applyOverlap395` before the station is read - and that the row press, the source
   press and the voice-sample press still reach the station through the one funnel, so a later edit cannot give one of
   them a private path past the door. The ordering claim is measured against the function body, not the file:
   `var a395 = streamAudioRef.current;` appears in other functions too, and a whole-file comparison would have
   compared the pin against the wrong line.
6. **What this does not claim.** The panel's play-volume slider drives the TAKE element, not the station element; the
   user's observation about the slider is consistent with the leak and is recorded as an observation, not as a second
   measurement. If a stream is still quiet after a refresh with this fix in place, the next thing to look at is a
   station element that is re-armed while a take is ducking it, which this fix does not change.

### T-552 BUILT 2026-10-17 (HOST HALF goes live at the user's restart; CLIENT HALF needs a browser refresh) - the generation-limits switch became a number field, and it moved in Settings

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "in settings, change option 'disable generation limits generation ceiling 300 s - limits ON'
   to be a textfield like the others so user can set limit with default 300 - or 0 for disabling the limit, and move
   between read-aloud chunk limit and generation timeout".
2. **What exists today.** The host owns a constant `GEN_DURATION_CEILING` (300 s) and a BOOLEAN switch
   `disable_generation_limits` (default false = limits applied), persisted in the settings store and read/written by
   `GET|POST /api/audio-play/disable_generation_limits`, which answers `limits_apply` and `ceiling_seconds`. The panel
   renders that as a switch plus a read-only sentence naming the ceiling. The refusal a capped request gets is a host
   error naming the ceiling (index.js:13956).
3. **Why this one needs the user's restart, and why that is said up front.** Turning a host constant into a stored
   number is a host-half change in `lib/index.js`. The panel half (a number field, in the position the user named) can
   be built and pinned without a restart, but the new number only takes effect for real audio when the host module is
   reloaded, and a restart is the user's act and this agent's never.
4. **What the change has to settle, and what this card proposes rather than guesses:** the ceiling becomes one stored
   integer in seconds, default 300, with **0 meaning no ceiling**; the boolean switch is retired rather than kept
   beside it, because two controls for one limit is the clutter the user has been removing elsewhere; a person who
   already stored `disable_generation_limits: true` must be read as ceiling 0 rather than losing their setting; the
   refusal sentence a capped request gets has to name the number the person actually set, not a constant; and the
   control moves between the read-aloud chunk limit and the generation timeout, which is a Settings-order change the
   T-510 control-count and width pins will have to be re-pointed against.
5. **Depends on:** the user's restart for the host half to go live, and the T-510 Settings harmonization rules (this
   field takes the Settings number style like its neighbours).
6. **The two rulings that settled the open questions (asked 2026-10-17, both answered):** build it now, host half
   included, rather than shipping only the panel half; and **retire the switch, migrate it** — one control for one
   limit, with a stored `disable_generation_limits: true` read as ceiling 0 so nobody silently gets their limit back.
   The alternatives offered and declined were "panel half only, host half later" and "keep the switch as a read-out".

7. **Host half (`lib/index.js`), what it now is.** `GEN_DURATION_CEILING` (300) stayed as the DEFAULT; beside it came
   `GEN_CEILING_NONE552 = 0`, `GEN_CEILING_MAX552 = 3600` and the live `generationCeiling552`. The gate reads the live
   number (`if (tk === 'gen' && generationCeiling552 > 0)`), so `> 0` is the whole of the old switch and there is no
   second state that could contradict it. The live boolean `disableGenLimits` is GONE, not kept beside the number.
   The store now writes `generation_ceiling_s` (only when it differs from the default) and no longer writes the
   boolean at all — the boolean is still READ on load, which is what makes the migration real rather than claimed.
8. **The new door.** `GET|POST /api/audio-play/generation_ceiling`. GET answers `ceiling_s`, `default_s`, `max_s`,
   `limits_apply`, the two description sentences the old verb carried (kept verbatim — what the ceiling governs did not
   change when the control that sets it changed), and a `note` that says in one shape what a 0 means. POST stores one
   whole number 0..3600 and refuses anything else naming the range and the meaning of 0. **3600 is a guard this card
   chose, not the user's number:** a "generation ceiling" above an hour is not a limit on generation, it is a hang, and
   the host refuses to be told one. Say so if it ever gets in anyone's way.
9. **The retired door stays open as a mapping.** `disable_generation_limits` still answers: `enabled:true` maps to
   ceiling 0, `enabled:false` maps to the default, and every answer carries the resulting `ceiling_s` plus a `retired`
   sentence naming the verb that owns the number now. It is not a second control — nothing that walks through it can
   put a limit beside the one number. The PANEL no longer speaks it: the client contains zero occurrences of the name.
10. **Panel half (`lib/client.js`).** The checkbox and its read-only ceiling line are gone. In their place is a number
    field, `audio-play-gen-ceiling552`, in the position the user named — between the read-aloud chunk size and the
    generation timeout — carrying the shared Settings box (`numStyle510`, the 86px unit width like the timeout beside
    it). It is debounced like the timeout (typing 300 would otherwise post 3, 30 and 300 to the host); blur and Enter
    commit at once. It is EMPTY until the host answers, and its note line then says either "not read from the host yet"
    or "0 = no ceiling · now capping gen takes at N s". Out-of-range values are refused before they are sent and the
    field goes back to the number the host holds; a host refusal is reported with the host's own sentence (the write
    asks `call()` to keep `ok:false` answers rather than rejecting them, so the sentence a person needs is the one that
    is shown) and is followed by a read-back of what the host actually holds.
11. **Measured, not asserted.** Host suite **1944 / 0** (was 1935): a 121 s request against a stored ceiling of 120 is
    refused naming 120, a 120 s request dispatches; POST 0 then a 1800 s request dispatches; five out-of-shape values
    (-5, 3601, 1.5, "abc", missing) are all refused and none of them changes the stored number; state.json carries
    `generation_ceiling_s: 0` and no longer carries the boolean; and the migration is proven by seeding an OLD state
    (`disable_generation_limits: true`) into a fresh process, which answers `ceiling_s: 0` and dispatches a 900 s take
    with no POST made by anyone. Client suite **798 / 0** (was 791): the field carries the host's number before anyone
    touches it, sits between the chunk field and the timeout field in draw order, has the same width as the timeout

    adopted controls, 37 outside) and the toggles-count floor moved from nine to eight because a checkbox left the

    `genLimitsFromAnswer456` to `refreshTakesLimit449` and swallowed seven functions that lived between them
    (`importOutsideFromAnswer458`, `refreshImportOutside458`, `flipImportOutside458`, `takesBytesText449`,
    `takesLimitFromAnswer449`, `takesLimitMib449`, `takesLimitLine449`). The suite threw on
    `takesLimitLine449 is not defined` and they were restored verbatim from the pre-edit copy. A slice that names only
    the functions it means to replace still has to check what else it covers.
13. **What is NOT claimed.** The 3600 guard and the 700 ms debounce are this card's choices. The migration is proven
    for a stored `true`; a state.json carrying BOTH an old boolean and a stored number reads the number, which is the

### T-557 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - the spectrum's reflection as the floor the llama runs on; GEOMETRY REOPENED BY T-564

**Status correction written 12:30 the same day.** This card was written as QUEUED at 08:3x and BUILT later the same
morning by scratch/t557_P1..P4; the 20-row floor, the 1:1 mirror, the 45deg flare and the animal standing in the floor
band all pass in the run recorded on T-558's amendment (284 pass / 8 fail, every T-557 check green). What is open on
this card now is not the build, it is the geometry: T-564 asks the wall to reach both canvas edges, and the numbers
this card's pins quote (wall x 22..177, deepest floor row x 3..196) are the numbers that would move.

The operator's word, verbatim: "with the current offset of the bottom line of the spectrum within the canvas, it looks
like the black space is the 'floor' the lama is running on, if we could mirror the spectrum at the current bottom line
and shift the bottom mirror part by 45° it would give a nice 3D effect, and be the floor - as an idea".

**What is measured today, before anything is designed.**

1. The strip canvas is 200 x 80 CSS px with a 2 px inset, so the drawable band is 196 x 76.
2. The llama grid is 30 x 34 cells at 2 px = 60 x 68 px, centred at x 70..129, and at rest its lowest cell's bottom
   edge sits at y 78, which is the bottom edge of the drawable band. **The animal's feet are already exactly on the
   bottom of the canvas.** There is no floor band today.
3. The black the operator is reading as a floor is the quiet end of the spectrum: a row with nothing in it paints at
   the ramp's floor colour `rgb(10,58,14)`, and near-silence at the lowest frequencies reads dark against the loud
   columns above it. So the "floor" the screenshot shows is partly the inset and partly the mode's own silence.
4. A mirrored, sheared band therefore needs height the spectrum has today. The three shapes that would pay for it are
   (a) the spectrum keeps the upper part of the band and gives the lower rows to the floor, (b) the floor is drawn
   over the spectrum region and the animal stands in front of both, or (c) the floor is drawn only where the spectrum
   is quiet, which is what the screenshot already looks like and needs the least new drawing. Which one is a decision
   about what the mode should show, not a detail.
5. Two things this needs before it can be measured rather than drawn blind: the harness has no `transform`/`scale`
   mock, so a sheared `drawImage` cannot be pinned today; and the reflection has to come from the history bitmap, not
   from the visible canvas, or the animal's pixels would be reflected too.
6. This is also the "3D" the operator asked for on the waterfall earlier ("frequency waterfalls, '3D' later"). It is
   one mechanism for both modes, so it is recorded once here and not twice.
7. **Not started.** It needs the operator's word on the height split in item 4 before any drawing is worth writing.

8. **What the fault actually was, and it was not the layout.** The wall's history was a bitmap the size of the WHOLE
   canvas, addressed in DEVICE pixels by its blits and in CSS pixels by the column pixels painted into it. At
   devicePixelRatio 1 the two agree. At any other ratio they do not: the columns land at CSS numbers inside a
   device-sized bitmap, so the wall covers 1/ratio of the space it owns. Measured on the operator's own screen (canvas
   226 CSS px, ratio 1.25, bitmap 283 px wide): the wall's newest column sat at bitmap x 203, which is canvas x 162 --
   **41 px short of its own far edge** -- and its rows stopped at bitmap y 57 of 100, canvas y 45 -- **12 px short of
   its own bottom**. That is "too short on the right side and not tall enough", and the black void beside the wall,
   and it was invisible to every pin the suite had, because every llama pin ran at ratio 1 where the two spaces agree.
9. **The build, all of it derived from W, H, inset, floor and the ratio -- nothing read off a screenshot (the
   operator's method ruling for this card, verbatim: "do NOT read pixel from screenshots to hardcode them, think about
   the allignment to generate the pixel dynamically to get the 3D-effect of the 'box view' we want - it can all be
   dynamic to adjust to size changes").** The history bitmap now holds **THE WALL ONLY**, sized in whole wall pixels:
   `cellD542 = max(1, ceil(dpr))` bitmap px per wall px, band = `specW * cellD` by `specRows * cellD` (156 x 57 at
   ratio 1, 312 x 114 at ratio 2). A wall pixel is a `cellD x cellD` cell at the band's far column, so the wall TILES
   its band at every ratio instead of painting 1 px dots at CSS coordinates. The visible canvas is drawn in CSS space
   under the transform the panel already set: the ground fills `0,0,W,H` once per frame, the band is laid on the wall's
   own rect `specX, inset, specW, specRows`, and the floor's mirrors are destination-in-CSS / source-in-wall-pixels.
   One space per surface, no mixing anywhere in the mode.
10. **The shared horizon row (the ruling, verbatim: "Wall bottom row = floor top row, one shared horizon row").**
    `axis542 = inset + rows - floor` (58) and `specRows542 = axis - inset + 1` (57): the wall owns the horizon row as
    its own bass row, painted once, out of the union of channels T-558 kept. The floor mirrors rows k = 1..floor-1
    (19 copies), source band row `56-k`, destination `58+k`, so the shared row IS the hinge. The floor's band is now
    fed exactly those 19 rows and no more -- a right-channel copy of the shared row would be a row nothing reads.
11. **T-564's line is gone (verbatim ask: "the newly added horizontal single line should be removed again -> the
    bottom border line of the wall-spectrum NEEDS to be adjusted to have the same length and vertical position as the
    top border of the floor-spectrum").** No copy is laid at 58 at all. The horizon's length is the wall's length, x
    22..177 at 200 px, because the horizon is the wall. What the same operator asked for in the same breath -- "the
    floor spectrum lower border can be extended to the full horizontal length of the canvas first (~3% too short on
    the left side currently)" -- is carried by the DEEPEST floor row instead: x 2..197 at 200 px, x 2..297 at 300 px,
    inset .. W-1-inset exactly.
12. **The flare's slope is computed, and the angle it implies is stated rather than hidden.** `flare = (specX - inset)
    / (floor - 1)` = 20/19 at the default size, because a slope pinned at 1 (T-557's `SCOPE_LLAMA_FLOOR_SLOPE542`,
    tan 45 = 1, kept in the file as the record of the decision it replaced) reaches the inner edge one row PAST the
    last row the floor has -- that is the 1 px of black at each side edge the operator measured as ~3%. The side edges
    are therefore about 46deg and not exactly 45deg. The operator's two instructions -- full width, inset wall kept --
    cannot both hold at tan 45; the extension is the one that was written down, and the constant is marked superseded
    where it stands.
13. **The pins. 15 re-pointed, 3 added, no claim loosened.** `tests/scope.test.cjs` 298 checks, 0 fail. The re-points

### T-563 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - dragging the canvas's right edge no longer switches the visualizer mode

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "small todo: if i change the canvas by dragging the right border, it should not also switch
   the visualizer which is currently also triggered".
2. **The intent is already in the code, and it is right.** T-333 gave the strip two jobs with one element
   (client.js:16134-16137): a press anywhere but the right edge cycles the mode, a press ON the right edge (within
   SCOPE_GRIP331 = 9 px, :418) starts a width drag. The guard written for the collision is at :16140 —
   `if (scopeDrag331.current && scopeDrag331.current.moved) { ... return; }` — so a drag that moved must not fall
   through to cycleScope300() at :16147.
3. **The fault, measured from the handler order in the same element.** onPointerUp at :16178 sets
   scopeDrag331.current = null, and pointerup fires BEFORE click. By the time the click handler at :16139 reads its
   guard, the drag object is already gone, `moved` is never seen, the guard cannot fire, and cycleScope300() runs.
   Resizing the display therefore also changes what it draws — exactly what the comment at :16137 says the guard was
   written to prevent. The guard is dead code, not a wrong threshold.
4. **The shape of the fix, with a test that fails against today's file:** the "this press moved" fact has to outlive
   pointerup — a moved flag (or a timestamp) the click handler reads and clears on its own terms. The pin asserts BOTH
   halves: a drag that moved leaves the mode where it was, and a press that did not move still cycles the mode, which
   is the T-333 behaviour the operator chose.
5. **Same element, so it belongs on this card:** the clock band is a second element with its own handler (T-376,

### T-566 BUILT 2026-10-17 (CLIENT HALF - browser refresh, no restart) - the row carries the whole instruction and the model chip is the item that gives way

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "the playlist shows the Text instruction field too small compared to modelname".
2. **Measured: there are two truncations, and the first one is not a width problem at all.** At lib/client.js:5272-5275
   the row's main string is built as `j.text.slice(0, 60) + "…"` — and a transcript is cut at 60 the same way. So the
   row never holds more than 60 characters of the instruction, whatever the column width is.
3. **The second is the squeeze.** The text cell at :5490-5499 is `flex: "1 1 0", minWidth: 0` with ellipsis — basis 0
   means it claims nothing up front and takes only what is left. The meta cell at :5526-5534 carries
   `model@quant · voice · duration` (built at :5276-5288), has no flex basis of its own, and is capped at
   `maxWidth: "130px"`. In a wrapping flex line a basis-auto cell is packed by its hypothetical width before a
   basis-0 cell is given anything, so the model chip is served first and the take text is what gets cut. That is
   precisely the comparison the operator is objecting to.
4. **History this fix must not quietly undo.** The basis-0 choice is T-307's answer to "now it looks like every
   playlist item has 2 rows" (the comment at :5487-5489 records the mechanism: flex-basis:auto on a wrapping line
   moves long text to a second line instead of cutting it). T-373 added the hover slide that shows the cut part on
   hover. T-306 fixed the id column at 48 px and the lane tag at 26 px. Any ruling that gives the text more room is
   allowed, but it is a ruling about the same row those cards shaped, and the pins they left behind move with it.
5. **The open ruling, four shapes:** (a) raise or drop the 60-character cut and let the flex squeeze decide how much
   shows; (b) give the text a floor and cap the meta chip harder, so the model name is the thing that ellipsises;
   (c) put the text on its own line — a deliberate reversal of T-307, which was written to stop exactly that; (d) keep
   the row as it is and widen the column. Which one is chosen says what the list is for: reading the words, or
   reading which model made the take.
6. **Client only.** Not started. Cross-references: T-306, T-307, T-373, T-300 U-3, and T-559 (both are decisions about
   how the playlist behaves).

1. **Where it fires.** `pumpPlayback`'s completion door - the one place every lane take passes through when it ends -
   and only when the queue is EMPTY, which is what leaves a chunked read-aloud playing its own parts in order instead
   of being walked off into unrelated rows. Three gates: the toggle ON; the queue drained; and not a press-stop
   (`playStopped307`, the pause/stop distinction T-307 had to build because a browser cannot tell the two apart).

   order, oldest first, keyed on the row's own `created` stamp - the row AFTER it, not the row below it on screen.
   That is the order the operator's own example names (ap-0665, then ap-0666, then ap-0667). Three things are NOT
   copied from the transport walk, on purpose: it wraps (this one stops at the end); it refuses a row that is not `ok`
   and steps past it (this one WAITS for a row that is still rendering); and it is driven by a press (this one is
   driven by a take reaching its end).
3. **The wait half of the ruling.** A row that is queued or rendering sets a wait and the panel says so out loud
   once ("fast forward: ap-0603 is still rendering - it will play when it is ready"). The wait is resolved by the
   panel's own cadence read of the playlist - the same read that first learns a row settled - so it costs no request
   and no timer of its own. Rendered: it plays. Failed: it is stepped over and the walk carries on from the row after
   it. Gone from the list: the wait is dropped rather than chasing a row that is not there. Turning the toggle off
   drops a wait it had left standing.
4. **What it refuses to walk on.** A route with a query is not a take: a row's ORIGINAL source (`?src=1`), one of its
   stems (`?stem=...`), or a download copy (`?dl=1`) ending does not start a walk through the list. The route is the
   honest source of the row id (queuePlayback's own lesson, T-334), not the label.

### T-571 CLOSED 2026-10-17 (NO CHANGE - the field stays exactly as it was, by the operator's ruling after the analysis) - "steps" is a real option on both audio models, so the field stays and no slider is invented

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "sfx: 'steps' should be no input window, right ? -> analyse, discuss if unclear".

   both audio-generation models, not a leftover: controlfoley - int, default 25, "Euler flow inference steps";
   stable audio - int, default 8, "Diffusion steps" (`model_specs/controlfoley.json`, `model_specs/stable_audio.json`,
   read 2026-10-17). Taking the field away takes away a knob both models document.

   panel's bare "steps" placeholder names no default, so it reads like a required field next to two that are not.
4. **RULING GIVEN 2026-10-17 (operator, verbatim):** "if we load the advanced tab, it should already be imported, ? so
   i guess keep as is but change input text box for steps ?!? analyse". Read as: the field stays VISIBLE - a value
   living behind a closed panel is a value a person cannot see they are sending - and what changes is the CONTROL.
5. **The analysis, measured today across the model specs that declare these options:** every model that accepts
   `num_inference_steps` declares a FLOOR (min 1) and almost none declare a ceiling - only `audiosr` (1000),
   `kugelaudio` (1000) and `zipvoice` (64) do. So a slider here has an honest low end and an invented high end, which
   is exactly the kind of guess T-567 was just built to remove. The honest change is a number input carrying the
   model's own floor and its own prefilled default, with both named in the hover, instead of a free-text box that
   invites any number.

   ux and values are known , see above , otherwise skip".** For steps the values are NOT known - no ceiling is declared
   for controlfoley, stable audio, minimax_music3 or heartmula - so the control change this card proposed is SKIPPED. The
   field stays a text box exactly as it was; the only thing that changed beside it is the hover, which now tells the
   truth about the defaults and the floor (built under T-570).
7. **Not started as a control change, deliberately:** a slider with an invented top end is what the operator's own rule
   now forbids.

### T-572 BUILT 2026-10-17 (HOST HALF live since the operator's 2026-10-17 20:13 restart, CLIENT HALF on a browser refresh; the per-root listing bound is appended in item 23) - the preset store is the text store, the list is the filesystem, and the picker reads it

5. **RULING GIVEN 2026-10-17 (operator, verbatim): "plugin store so we can preseed defaults".** Presets live in the

   than starting empty. That also settles the agent question in item 3: the agent can read them, and write them when

6. **RETHINK REQUESTED 2026-10-17 (operator, verbatim):** "hmm, rethink - compare with existing text store - can we
   re-use existing stores ? - can we combine those in form of a subfolder structure with txt or md or jsonc files - in a

   prompts is dynamically generated from the fs ? - might need some redoing, do backup before".
7. **Measured today, and there IS an existing store to reuse.** `~/.dsh/audio-play/texts/` with an `index.json`
   (`version: 1`) and one file per saved text. Host side (`lib/index.js:11825-11826`, `:12016-12210`): verbs
   `batch_text_list`, `batch_text_load {path}`, `batch_text_save {name, content | from_path}`; accepted extensions are

   (`textRoots298`, `:11880`); save refuses to overwrite and caps size. A saved file already IS the uniform header format
   the operator described: `schema_version: 2`, `saved_at`, `saved_by`, `title`, `outDir`, `format_detected`, `source`,

9. **The shape to confirm or correct before any build:** reuse `texts/` rather than inventing a preset store; allow a

     `bash scripts/backup_snapshot.sh` -> `the workspace backup directory/snapshot_20261017_150550_snapshot.tar.gz`, 3.9 G,
     `RC=0` (tar's "Removing leading '/' from member names" is its normal noise, not a lost file). Nothing was deleted
     anywhere in this card; the old behaviour is kept as a labelled fallback rather than removed.
11. **Host half: the list is a walk (`lib/index.js`).** `handleBatchTextList` (`:12066`) now walks `textRoots298()`
     through the fs service's own `listDir` seam. The bounds follow the T-447 store-walk rule, because a listing that
     can hang the panel is not a listing: `TEXT_LIST_MAX572 = 300` offered entries, `TEXT_LIST_DEPTH572 = 3` levels
     below a root, `TEXT_LIST_SCAN_MAX572 = 4000` things examined (`:11908-11910`); symlinks and oddities are not

     and named in `unreadable[]`, and a truncated walk reports `list_truncated: true` instead of quietly reporting a
     smaller number. `texts/index.json` is not offered as a text (`:11925`).
12. **The index was demoted, not deleted.** Where the walk finds a file the index also knows, the index supplies what
     only it knows - title, cast, lines, chars, `saved_at`, `source_name` - and the row carries `in_index: true`. Where
     it does not, the row is still listed, with `bytes` from the listing seam, `folder` (its sub-path under the root)

13. **Subfolders (`lib/index.js:11901-11907`).** `batch_text_save` gained `folder`: up to `TEXT_FOLDER_MAX_PARTS572 = 3`
     plain names joined by `/`, each validated by the SAME rule a file name is validated by (`TEXT_NAME_RE`), so
     `presets/music` is accepted while `../..`, `a/../../b` and `oh $(id)` are refused before anything is written. The
     target is still re-checked against the root afterwards, and the directory is created with the plugin's own
     idempotent `ensureDir` (`:12253`, `:12371`) - the same primitive the older save paths already use.
14. **A preset is a shape of its own, not a scene with one line in it.** A music prompt names no speaker, and the
     dialogue parser refuses a text that names no speaker - correctly, because a prompt is not something someone says.
     Pushing a preset through that parser would either refuse the save or invent a voice. So `batch_text_save {prompt}`
     writes a preset document (`handleTextPresetSave572`, `lib/index.js:12238`) carrying the uniform header the batch
     documents carry - `schema_version: 2`, `saved_at`, `saved_by`, `title` - plus `kind: 'preset'`, `preset_for` and
     `prompt`. `batch_text_load` believes the header and answers `kind: 'preset'`, `format: 'preset'`, `prompt`,
     `lines: []`, `cast: []` (`:12221`), with `content` still carrying the raw file. Never-overwrite, the size ceiling
     and the index entry apply to a preset exactly as they apply to a chapter.
15. **Client half: the picker IS the store (`lib/client.js`).** The panel keeps no preset list of its own
     (`:7726-7776`): `loadPresets572` asks the host and keeps the rows whose `format` is `preset` or whose folder starts

     dropped into `texts/presets/` by hand appears without a panel change. The row is one `select`

     says "nothing has been rendered yet" - Generate is still the thing that renders.
16. **A prompt is not a file name, and the card keeps both.** The store wants a name (letters, digits, space, dot,
     dash, underscore, starting with a letter or digit); "rain on a tin roof, distant thunder" has a comma. The name is
     DERIVED (`presetNameFrom572`, `:7733`) and the full prompt is kept as the `title`, which is free text: the picker
     shows the prompt, the file name stays boring, and nothing the person typed is thrown away. An empty field is

17. **The bug the pin found, kept because it is the interesting part.** `call()` builds request bodies from a per-verb
     whitelist (`lib/client.js:9544-9556`), and `batch_text_save`'s whitelist knew only `{name, content, from_path,

     content}`, path still absent, and the T-298 pin on that shape still means what it says.

        form, plus a check that the old form is gone), and the harness seam itself - the fake fs gained `listDir`,

   rewritten with only the part BEFORE it, the caret clamped to the end of what was left, and the rest of the sentence

   I could make a broth. | ` and after `N` it read `... | N` - both correct - and after the rest of the burst it read

   collapsed into ONE dialogue row on disk (`s01.json`: 1 row, cast `Janeway`, every other speaker's words inside it).
   This is not a tool artefact: the same sequence with real Playwright keyboard events into the located field
   reproduced it, and the fix below is what stopped it.

   instead of re-deriving it from a parse, the field's value comes from the region, `onBlur` releases it, and a reorder
   or a delete drops it. The serializer is untouched - a line that begins with a NAME is still a new turn, which is
   what T-462's ruling asked for and what the file format has always been. What changed is that the split no longer
   happens under the person's own caret. Re-measured on the live panel after the fix: the same burst left the field
   holding exactly what was typed (`I could make a broth.
Nelix: Second broth line.`), and a four-turn scene typed

### T-519 BUILT 2026-10-16 (client half needs a browser refresh, host half needs a host restart) - the Log section's top row prints the version at its right end, read from package.json by the host

User request, verbatim: "the top row of the log section should show the version number on the right side of the deepamp plugin, taken from SSOT value (not hardcoded)".

1. **Measured - there is no version in the panel today.** The Log section's top row is `lib/client.js:1405-1411` (`audio-play-log-page-head`, holding the `audio-play-log-src` span and the count sentence), and `grep -n "version" lib/client.js` finds only two unrelated things: the yt-dlp BINARY's version (`lib/client.js:10466`, read off the host's `ytdlp_path` probe) and a tool label at `lib/client.js:2763`. Nothing anywhere prints this plugin's own version.
2. **Measured - what the SSOT actually is.** `package.json` carries `"name": "@mepaw/audio-play-cordis"` and `"version": "0.0.1"`, and its `exports` map ALREADY exposes `"./package.json": "./package.json"`, so the manifest is reachable from both faces without a path guess. The HOST has no version route: there is no `about` / `plugin_version` verb, and the only `version` keys in `lib/index.js` are the yt-dlp probe's and a state `version: 3` at :1525.
3. **The two honest shapes, and the card's own bias.** (a) Both faces read the manifest through the exports map - client-only cost, no restart, and the value has exactly one home. (b) The host reads its own manifest once and answers the version on a read route, and the panel prints that answer as UNKNOWN until it lands (the T-511 / T-515 rule). (a) is cheaper and keeps this card refresh-only; (b) is the shape that also gives an AGENT the version. Which one is chosen is a build decision taken with a test in front of me, not a guess in chat - and a version string typed into `lib/client.js` is the hardcode the user named, so it is out.
4. **One value, two places (xref the user's own ruling).** T-508 item 7: when no info url is set, the `i` button's hover carries "version number of plugin from SSOT". Two surfaces must not each carry their own copy. Whichever shape wins, both read the same value.
5. **Layout fact to respect:** the version goes at the RIGHT end of a row that already holds the source label and the event-count sentence, and that row already uses `flexShrink: 0` on its parts. Reserving the right end is a layout change the render suites have to re-read, not a string append.
6. **The version number itself is a release decision, not a code decision.** `0.0.1` is a placeholder. Setting it is part of the pre-release plan (T-524), and T-522 (the SSOT / hardcode review) is where a wrong or duplicated version would be caught.
7. **State:** QUEUED. Client half under shape (a); shape (b) would add a host read and join the restart debt.
8. **Shape (b) is what got built, and item 3's option (a) is now measured to be impossible.** The card leaned to (a) — both faces reading the manifest through the exports map — and the measurement killed it: the browser half of this plugin is loaded as inline text through `window.__DSH_BOOT__` / `__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`, and the `require` inside that factory resolves REGISTERED client modules only (measured: it resolves `react`, and nothing else the plugin ships). There is no file access, no exports-map resolution and no manifest read on the client side, and no shipped `@deepseek-ai/*` client file reads its own package.json. A version the browser half cannot read is not a design choice, so the host reads its own manifest and the panel prints what it is told.
   **Built, host half (`lib/index.js`, needs the restart this card joins):** `GET /api/audio-play/plugin_version` answers `{ ok, version, name, source, via, read_at, note }`. It tries the module-import door first (`import('../package.json', { with: { type: 'json' } })`, which node 24.20.0 accepts — probed before writing, not assumed) and falls back to the ctx filesystem door (`fsx.resolve(...).then(fsx.readText)`), naming which door answered (`module import` / `ctx fs read` / `neither door`, the last carrying BOTH failure strings). The manifest path is derived from `new URL('../package.json', import.meta.url)`, never typed. A SUCCESS is cached — a manifest does not change under a running host — and a FAILURE deliberately is not, so a host that could not read its manifest once may answer on the next ask. POST is refused 405. The op is logged (`logQueueOp('plugin_version', { via, source, ok })`).
   **Built, client half (`lib/client.js`, needs a browser refresh):** one read per panel, asked at mount because the Log section is open by default (`React.useEffect(function () { if (sectionOpen("__log", true)) readPluginVersion519(); }, []);`) and asked again when the person opens a closed Log section (`if (willOpen) readPluginVersion519();`); never re-asked once an answer is in hand, and never polled. The mark is `pluginVersionMark519(ans)` under the same UNKNOWN discipline T-511 / T-515 established, and the three states are three different sentences: no answer yet -> `version: not read yet`; the host refused -> `version: not read` carrying the host's own words on the hover plus the sentence that a host restart is what lands the route; an answer -> the host's string printed VERBATIM (`0.0.1` today), no prefix, no padding, no re-formatting, with the manifest path, the door and the read time on the hover.
   **Layout, as item 5 demanded — and the render suites did have to re-read it.** The head row became a flex line (`display:flex, flexWrap:wrap, alignItems:baseline, gap:8px`) with the label given `flexShrink:0` and the mark carrying `marginLeft:auto` so it is pushed to the far right end. Two collisions were found by the suites, and both were resolved by strengthening rather than loosening. (1) The T-219 rule fired — a flex row whose children refuse to shrink must be a row that can WRAP — so `flexWrap` went in with its reason written beside it, because a version is never truncated to fit. (2) The T-219 pin IDENTIFIED the lane chip row by a style fingerprint (display:flex + gap:8px + fontSize:10px), and the new version row legitimately uses the same compact shape, so the fingerprint matched two rows and `.pop()` measured the wrong one; the lane row is NAMED now (`audio-play-lane-chip-row311`) and the pin points at the name, with every assertion after it unchanged.
   **Pins.** Host suite (`tests/host.test.cjs`, now **1889 pass / 0 fail**, was 1883): the answer's `version` is compared against `package.json` read INDEPENDENTLY by the test at test time — that comparison is the difference between an SSOT and a string that happens to match; `source` must end in `package.json`; `via` must be one of the two named doors; a second call returns the SAME `read_at` (one read, kept); POST is refused 405 with the plugin's own named method refusal; a FAILED read is not cached. Client suite (`tests/ui_state.test.cjs`, now **735 pass / 0 fail**, was 726): a normal mount asks exactly once; before the answer lands the mark says `version: not read yet` and carries the unknown class; after it lands the mark is exactly the host's string with `marginLeft:auto` and `flexShrink:0`, sitting as the second child of the head row beside the `panel log` label (T-520's label) and not inside the count sentence, so T-300's placement rule still holds; a refusal says `version: not read` with the host's words and the restart sentence on the hover; closing and reopening the section does not ask again; and no quoted semver-shaped string exists anywhere in `lib/client.js`.
   **The no-hardcoded-version half of the request is pinned on BOTH faces,** which is the part of it that was a rule rather than a layout: the host suite asserts that neither `lib/index.js` nor `lib/client.js` contains a semver-shaped quoted string (the pattern `['"] digits.digits.digits ['"]` matches zero occurrences in either file today) and that the manifest path is derived from the host module's own URL. Item 6 stays open exactly as written: `0.0.1` is a placeholder, and choosing the real number belongs to the release plan (T-524), not to this card.
   Two harness facts worth recording because each cost a cycle: the host suite's fake response object reports `code`, not `status` (tests/host.test.cjs:846), and the import attribute in the file is quoted `'json'` rather than `"json"` — the pin now accepts either quoting instead of freezing the file's accident.

## Closed on 2026-10-18 (fifth pass, 2 cards: the two double-click shortcuts, both built client-side and measured in the real browser)

### T-556 QUEUED 2026-10-17 (user, verbatim) - double-clicking the visualizer canvas opens Settings and scrolls to the visualizer settings

1. **The request, verbatim:** "todo - add double klick fuction shortcut to visu-canvas to open settings and scroll
   to visualizer settings".
2. **Status:** queued, not started. Recorded before the current visualizer work continues, so it is not lost.
3. **What has to be settled before it is built, and what is already known from this panel:**
   - The strip already owns a press that changes mode (the strip press cycles the ring), and a double-click on the
     same element arrives as two single presses plus a dblclick. A shortcut that also moves the mode under it would
     be two acts from one gesture, which this project does not do. The design question is therefore whether the
     strip press stays a press and the double-click is recognised before the second press takes effect, or whether
     the mode press moves elsewhere.
   - "Open settings" and "scroll to the visualizer settings" are two acts. The panel's Settings sections are already
     reachable and the visualizer group has named controls in it, so the scroll target exists; whether the shortcut
     also expands a collapsed panel is not decided.
4. **Open question for the operator (to be asked one at a time, not assumed):** what should happen to the mode press
   that a double-click necessarily includes first.


### T-545 MID-TERM, QUEUED 2026-10-17 (user, verbatim) - double-clicking a playlist row plays it, and the row is highlighted

1. **The ask, verbatim:** "add as mid-term-todo: for playlist table items: - add a double-klick functionality with same
   functionality as the play button (or src play button for src entries) -> should result in instant play and highlight
   of that row entry".
2. What already exists to build on: the row's own play control, the SRC play control for rows whose audio is an input
   file, and the panel's notion of which row the transport is on (the control that plays "the row the transport is on"
   exists and its hover says it falls back to the first playable row). A double-click is a second route to the same act,
   so it must land on the SAME state the button lands on — one act, one implementation, the rule T-535 applied to the
   visualizer name.
3. What "highlight" has to be decided against: the panel already distinguishes the row the transport is on, the row that
   is playing, and a row that was walked to. A highlight that is a fourth visual state would need to say which of those
   it means. Marked mid-term by the user, so it is not built in this stretch.
4. **The open question is answered** (asked 2026-10-17, the user chose "The existing NOW PLAYING lit row"): a
   double-click produces the row's own play act and the lit state that act already produces. There is no fourth visual
   state, no flash, and no separate selection mark. What is left to build, and it is a build decision rather than an
   open one: the double-click must reach the SAME handler the row's play button reaches (T-535's rule — one act, one
   implementation), and for a source entry that is the SRC play button's act, not the take act. Still mid-term, still
   not built.

### T-360 CLOSED (2026-10-14 05:5x): the model table's own voice names are read, not only the family's

1. **Measured on the live lane (2026-10-14 05:0x-05:2x)**: `cpu2.test:8963` and `cpu1.test:8963`
   `/v1/models` answer n=54 entries carrying `id, object, owned_by, family, task, mode, loaded, path` and NO
   voice field. The served page (`GET cpu2.test:8963/`, 200, 1 823 379 bytes) carries `builtin_voices` 18
   times: once per family spec (`kokoro_tts` 54, `kitten_tts2` 47, `kitten_tts` 8, `kugelaudio` 4,
   `pocket_tts` 1) and again per model entry in the bundled model table (`kugelaudio` entries name
   default/clear/english_female/english_male with `default_voice:"default"`; `lfm2-audio-s2s` declares
   `builtin_voices:[]`). `refresh_voices` answered `builtins:[] builtins_source:'none'` for every primary model
   on this lane except the two pocket_tts builds (`1`, `'capability'`).
2. **The disagreement this closes**: the FAMILY spec and the MODEL entry do not always say the same thing. A
   checkpoint that declares no built-in voices was being offered its family's speakers, because the reader only
   ever looked at the family spec.
3. **The harvest**: `capFindModelVoices(page)` (anchored on `{"id":"` entries, capped at 400 entries,
   `CAP_MODEL_KEY_RE` for the model id, projecting only `family, task, builtin_voices, default_voice`) records
   per model `{voices, default_voice, family, task, declared_empty}`. `builtin_voices: []` is a DECLARATION
   (`declared_empty: true`); only an entry naming neither key is skipped. The first draft skipped empty
   declarations, which discarded exactly the case the feature exists for — recorded here as a fix, not a
   footnote.
4. **What the answer carries**: `model_voice_scan {scanned, named, dropped}`, `model_voice_entries`, and
   `model_voices` filtered to the requested family when a family is asked for. `capCachedModelVoices(fn, id,
   modelId)` reads the same cache and TTL as the family read, so the model-level read costs no extra fetch.
5. **`refresh_voices` order is now model -> capability(family) -> mirror**, answering
   `builtins_source:'model'` when the checkpoint spoke for itself.
6. **Fixture facts** (`artifacts/t248a_capability_reader_20261007/fixture/engine_index_20261007.html`, pinned
   1 672 292 bytes / md5 e5738b3e8e3131afba729a80bd3cbf7d): exactly THREE model entries carry voice fields —
   `lfm2-audio-jp-tts`, `lfm2-audio-s2s`, `lfm2-audio-jp-s2s`, all family `lfm2_audio`, all declaring an EMPTY
   list. Its `lfm2_audio` family spec declares no built-in voices at all, so the test page gets one surgical
   injection — the four speakers the 2026-10-14 primary page declares for that family — into that family's own
   `ui` block, and a check proves the injection landed on exactly one `ui` block and added exactly one
   `builtin_voices` occurrence. Nothing else in the captured page is touched.
7. **Tests added (host, 6 checks)**: the injection integrity, three model declarations found on the same single
   page read, family answer and checkpoint answer side by side (family declares four, `lfm2-audio-jp-tts`
   declares none), `refresh_voices` answering `builtins:[] builtins_source:'model'` for that checkpoint,

   of it.

### T-518 DONE 2026-10-16 (client half, needs a browser refresh) - the report after switching the primary endpoint was a wall of text; it is now two short lines

User request, verbatim: "optimise the long log text after switching primary endpoint for TTS or SST - the current wall of text is too long and not helpful this way".

1. **What it printed before (measured in `lib/client.js:10770-10784` before the patch).** ONE toast line carrying: the new primary, the verb name (`endpoint_promote`), the entry that left the registry, the displaced endpoint's new id and route, the claim that its flags / health answer / model answer were "carried over", the re-stamp split with both numbers, the guarantee that every row keeps the endpoint url it was placed on, and "no row changed machine" - 250+ characters, for both TTS and STT.
2. **What it prints now.** Two short lines holding the facts a person acts on: `primary is now cpu2.test:8963 (TTS1)` then `e-1 left the tts registry · cpu1.test:8963 survives as e-4 · 1 row moved`. The pin measures the whole report at under 120 characters and at most 2 lines.
3. **What was dropped, and why dropping it is safe.** The verb name (the panel sends exactly one call; the panel's U-18 rule is that UI text names the ACTION a person can take, not the call behind it), the carried-over-flags sentence, and the "keeps its url / no row changed machine" guarantees. Those are the HOST's guarantees, and the same handler re-reads the registry rows, the machine board and the health lights (`refreshRegistry` / `refreshMachines` / `probeHealthAll`), so the person sees the state on the rows instead of reading a paragraph about it.
4. **What still gets its own line, on purpose:** a warning that changes what you can do next. When the host reports the demoted entry has NO model answer, the report says `e-4 has no model answer yet - press models on its row before placing work on it` (3 lines max). That is actionable, not explanatory, so it survived the compaction.
5. **The re-stamp COUNT is still the host's, not a client guess (T-238 unchanged).** The compact form says "2 rows moved", and the pin proves the pinned row is counted too - which is only possible from the host's `restamped` answer, not from the panel's own lane count.
6. **The pre-action confirm line is NOT compacted.** The armed row still spells out what the second click will do before an irreversible step is taken; the user's complaint was about the report AFTER the switch, and a warning read before pressing has a different job.
7. **Verified:** `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` **693 pass / 0 fail** (the T-235 toast pin, the T-238 re-stamp-split pin and the T-238 no-model-answer pin re-pointed to the compact form; one new pin asserts the wall is gone - no verb name, no carried-over sentence, no "no row changed machine", <= 2 lines, < 120 chars). `render 208 / 0`, `actions 203 / 0`, `transport 107 / 0`, `batch_board 29 / 0` re-run after the change.
8. **State:** DONE, client half. Needs a browser refresh together with the refresh debt listed on T-503 / T-505 / T-506.
