### T-604 BUILT 2026-10-19 - ONE speaker-name rule across the plugin, the diar label it now admits, and the turn marker an engine was being told twice
- Built on the operator's ruling, verbatim: **"do a full analysis and implement uniform fix across all relevant parts including test so we can clear open todos"**. It answered the open question T-581 item 11 had opened hours earlier — should the host read `SPEAKER_00:` as a speaker at all — and it was built on both halves at once, which is why the restart debt is stated up front instead of discovered later.
- The analysis found three answers to "who is a speaker" and one question answered too late: the author reader's rule (`speakerNameOk298`, strict by design, widened by T-591 to a registry lookup), the plugin-shape reader (`.json` branch of `parseTextDoc298`, which applied **no** rule and took a saved document's `voice` strings verbatim), the composer's looser row parser (`NAME_RE381`), and the render-side question — *can a lane clone this name?* — answered only by `normalizeBatchDoc` at dispatch time, after the panel had already shown the scene as ready. The evidence was read off disk: two probe documents whose dialogue text begins with its own `[S1] ` marker, and one whose voice slots hold human names no engine can clone.
- The rule is now one function: `speakerNameOk604` = a human name, or a voice id the live registry holds, or a **diar label** (`DIAR_LABEL_RE604 = /^(speaker|spk)[ _-]?\d{1,3}$/i`), with front matter winning over all three. Both readers (`speakerLine298`, `batchScript585`) and the panel's mirror (`speakerLine594`) go through it. `speaker:` / `speakerhood:` (no number), `S1:` (the tag namespace), `part_2:` / `take_3:` / `chapter_7:` (the shapes the strict rule exists to keep out) are pinned as still refused; `speaker_0`, `Speaker 2`, `SPK-3`, `SPEAKER_00` are read as speakers. The refusal sentence names the three classes it checked.
- **The boundary that keeps it safe, pinned:** a diar label is a speaker and never a voice. `VOICE_NAME_RE` still gates every dialogue voice, so a scene keyed by `SPEAKER_00` is refused at plan time (`line 1 voice "SPEAKER_00" is not a voice name`) exactly as a scene keyed by `Tom Paris` is, and neither refusal created a row. Renaming onto registered voices is what makes such a scene renderable — measured end to end, including the plan accepting the renamed file.
- **Two defects the analysis found and fixed on the way.** (1) A comment written 2026-10-18 claimed `renamed_from` was kept in a saved document "so the author's own names are not lost"; measured, it was dropped by the document build, so a file saved with a cast lost the names it came from and the mapping existed only in the browser session that made it. It is kept now. (2) `planBatchParts` writes each take's `[Sn] ` markers from the part-local cast, so a marker already inside a line's text reached the engine **twice**: measured on the suite's own fixture, `script_chars 444 / part_chars_sum 459` before, `429 / 444` after, and the dispatched request body now carries exactly one leading marker per line, in that line's voice slot, while a marker written inside a sentence stays in the sentence.
- **The two text shapes now agree about a turn that spans lines.** The tagged reader walked only tagged lines and dropped every untagged one, so a saved turn whose text carried a newline lost the rest of the turn on read-back. It now follows the author shape (an untagged line belongs to the turn above it; lines before the first marker are notes) and takes the marker out of the line text, because the speaker of a line lives in its voice. Save → file → load → save again measured with every word intact.
- **The asymmetry the uniform rule keeps, on purpose:** a TEXT shape that names no speaker is refused at the load, because there is nothing there to fix; a saved DOCUMENT whose voice strings are not speakers is kept loadable and its offenders are named (`speaker_kinds` plus the shape notes), because refusing that load would lock a file the operator can only repair by opening it — the situation T-581 item 5.3 was about. The dialogue grammar stays the gate at plan and dispatch time for both shapes, so nothing unspeakable reaches an engine either way.
- **What the host now answers, not only accepts:** `batch_text_load` and `batch_text_save` carry `speaker_kinds` (every distinct speaker, in order of first appearance, with `speaker`, `front_matter`, `human_name`, `registered_voice`, `diar_label`, `voice_ok`) plus shape notes naming the speakers that own no voice and the fix that fits them; the save computes them *after* its own cast rename so the answer describes the file it wrote. `cast_preview` answers the same facts beside its voice-side `kind`, and a diar label gets its own sentence instead of the generic one.
- **The panel half:** the mirror admits the diar class and says which class decided it; a diar row carries an amber "diar label — rename it onto a voice" marker whose hover names the speaker; the load's shape notes are printed on the file line the panel already had and never showed; the import message that said the labels "cannot be speaker names on this host" now says what is true (renamed for reading, owns no voice, rename it onto one in the cast rows). The anti-drift pin compares the connective list, the front-matter key list, the voice-id grammar **and the diar regex** read out of both source files. The summary line under the composer was made honest about the heading it carries: it says "voices", and until now it printed every row's value under that heading — a front-matter name included, and a diar file reading `voices: SPEAKER_00, SPEAKER_01`, which is the exact claim this build's rule rejects. A name the plugin does not read as a speaker no longer contributes one, an unrenamed diar label is named in its own clause as a label with no voice behind it, and the voice list says "none behind this scene yet" when nothing has one. The take ceiling still counts a diar label on purpose, and the comment at the count says why (six labels must be renamed onto five voices or fewer, and excluding them would hide the ceiling from exactly the file that needs it).
- Tests: `host` **1991 / 0** (was 1982; 9 new pins, 3 re-pointed with their reasons written where the old clause stood — the chars arithmetic, the source pin's call sites, and "the tags stay INSIDE the text", which measured false for the batch route), `scene_composer` **156 / 0** (was 151; 5 new pins, 2 re-pointed — the diar LIMIT pin became a success pin with the limit written into its place, and the marked-row pin now measures 2 refusals + 1 diar marker), `tooltips` **12 / 0** (U-18 clean on every hover this build wrote; run separately, because `npm test` does not run it). Full battery, all 23 suites, every one `rc=0` and 0 fail, run twice (before and after the summary-wording change): actions 223, batch_board 29, effects 4, endpoint_exclusivity 105, engine_boot 99, event_log 35, flow 89, handler OK, host 1991, model_library 45, model_matrix 16, render 212, scene_composer 156, scope 312, selection_memory 62, shell_safety 31, shut 63, stream_overlap 137, tooltips 12, transparency 22, transport 109, ui_state 821, verb_contract OK — the run to act on is `scratch/npmtest_20261019_t604_full2.log`; the steps that got there are kept as `scratch/npmtest_20261019_t604_host1.log` (1979/3), `_host2.log` (1989/2), `_host3.log` (1991/0), `_composer1.log` (153/3), `_composer2.log` (153/1), `_composer3.log` (154/0), `_composer4.log` (154/0) and `_composer5.log` (156/0). One of my own measurements was caught by its own pin (a marker count that looked anywhere past position 4 instead of at the front of the line) and corrected.

## Built and closed on 2026-10-20 (one card, tests only — no host code, no client code, no restart, the live host never touched) — the fixture that had made every restart claim unmeasurable

### T-593 BUILT AND CLOSED 2026-10-20 — the empty voice registry was the fixture asking a host before its boot's state restore had landed
- The card was opened on a measurement that looked like a plugin fault and was written down as a fixture fault: a host booted through `fsSeed` answers `{"ok":true,"voices":{}}` although the state handed to it carries the voices in full. It stayed open because the card refused to guess a cause, and because the whole class of claims it blocked — "a restart does not re-run ffmpeg for a number the plugin already has", "a hand-written `state.json` is restored", "a bad value is dropped and the rest of the voice survives" — could not be pinned while the fixture answered empty.
- **What it was not, measured out over three passes.** The saved state's shape: bisected key by key, nothing wrong with it, and a host booted from the plugin's OWN saved state restored both voices (`scratch/t593_repro_20261020.cjs`). The fs seam being clobbered: instrumented, the seed was read once, intact, never overwritten (`t593_repro2_20261020.cjs`). The trigger is **when the fixture asks**: one seed, one host, asked in the tick `apply()` returns in answers an empty registry, asked one macrotask later answers both voices with every stored field (`t593_repro3_20261020.cjs`). `voice_registry` is a synchronous read, so a request that arrives before the restore has run is served from an empty `voicesReg`. That also explains the card's own paradox — the hand-built seed that "answers correctly" had simply been asked after a chain of probe requests, while the seed that looked broken was asked as the boot host's first request.
- **The fix is one boot settle inside `tests/host.test.cjs`, and it is paid once per host at that host's first request.** The fs seam now records the promise the host chains its state restore from, so the wait is for the host's real read rather than a guessed sleep, followed by two macrotask boundaries for any clamped boot timer; `call()` awaits it before the first dispatch and nothing after. No call site was edited, and `lib/index.js` and `lib/client.js` were not touched at all — their mtimes are still the ones from before the operator's restart, so there is no restart debt from this card and the running host was never involved.
- **Blast radius measured rather than assumed.** The card's breadth claim ("17 suites boot hosts through this fixture") is corrected: only **three** suites seed `state.json` — `host`, `engine_boot`, `endpoint_exclusivity` (`ui_state` names the path in a file listing and seeds no state). The two non-host suites were re-run as settle-patched copies and came back with counts identical to their baselines — **99 / 0** and **105 / 0** (`scratch/t593_eb_copy_20261020.cjs`, `t593_ee_copy_20261020.cjs`) — so nothing in them had been measuring an unrestored host and they are left as they were. Inside `host.test.cjs` the settle changed exactly two pins: the two tripwires this card and T-581 5.4 had planted. The other 1989 pins did not move.
- **The tripwire was replaced by the claim it was guarding, and the trap stayed pinned beside it.** A host booted from the state the plugin itself saved answers both voices with `speech_s 7.4 / speech_file_s 22.8 / silence_s 15.4 / tail_s 15.4 / ref_dur_s 22.8`; that boot issued **neither silencedetect nor ffprobe**; and `voice_speech_probe {all:true}` on that restarted host answers both voices from what it restored with `measured_now:false` and still **zero** silencedetect runs — the number survives the restart, so there is nothing to measure. Alongside them, a counter-example pin: a host asked **without** the settle from the very same seed still answers an empty registry, so the settle cannot be quietly removed and the next author learns why a host must never be asked in the boot tick.
- **T-581 5.4's open question answered, and its pin re-pointed with the reason where the old clause stood.** No `voices` block is rejected and no voice is lost: a settled boot of the smuggle state restores **all three** voices and drops only the values the probe could not have produced, each on its own — a negative `speech_s` goes while the `speech_file_s` behind it stays, a `speech_s` with no `speech_file_s` behind it goes, a non-numeric `tail_s` goes while `speech_s` / `speech_file_s` / `silence_s` stay. The 2026-10-19 reading "this host answers NO voices at all" was the early ask, and the card's alternative — "the restore rejects the block" — is now recorded as measured against, not chosen.
- **What this card does NOT fix, stated so it is not mistaken for settled:** the plugin still serves a synchronous read that arrives before its own state restore has completed. In the fixture that was the ask; on the live host no such ask has been observed (the panel's first request comes seconds after boot). Whether the plugin should refuse to serve until its store is loaded is an ordering question for the operator, not a change a tests-only card makes. **And the claim itself now has a live reading beside the fixture pin:** `GET voice_registry` on the running host (the operator's restart, `pid 87210`) answers **19 voices, and all 19 carry `speech_s`** — while the plugin's own `perf_log.jsonl` holds no `voice_speech_probe` record at all since that boot (its two probe records are timestamped 08:16 UTC, hours before it). The numbers came back from the store; nothing re-measured them.
- Tests: `host` **1994 / 0** (was 1991; one tripwire pin became four). Full battery, all 23 suites, every one `rc=0` and 0 fail: actions 223, batch_board 29, effects 4, endpoint_exclusivity 105, engine_boot 99, event_log 35, flow 89, handler OK, host 1994, model_library 45, model_matrix 16, render 212, scene_composer 156, scope 312, selection_memory 62, shell_safety 31, shut 63, stream_overlap 137, tooltips 12, transparency 22, transport 109, ui_state 821, verb_contract OK — log `scratch/npmtest_20261020_t593_full1.log`. The steps that got there are kept: `scratch/npmtest_20261020_t593_host1.log` (1989 / 2 — the two tripwires failing exactly as designed, and nothing else moving), `scratch/npmtest_20261020_t593_host2.log` (1994 / 0), `scratch/npmtest_20261020_t593_eecopy.log`, `scratch/npmtest_20261020_t593_ebcopy.log`. Diagnostic drivers and patched suite copies are all in `scratch/` (`t593_harness_20261020.cjs`, `t593_repro_20261020.cjs`, `t593_repro2_20261020.cjs`, `t593_repro3_20261020.cjs`, `t593_repro4_20261020.cjs`, `t593_probe_host_20261020.cjs` — the whole suite with prints at the pin, which is what proved the seed intact and the boot answer empty at the 1991 / 0 baseline). Nothing was deleted.

### T-605 BUILT 2026-10-20 - ONE voice ceiling, adjustable and persisted, read by the take path, the batch, the plan, the cast answers and the panel
- Built on the operator's ruling, verbatim: **"I KNOW that ttsd can handle 5 speakers with clean results - we just have to diagnose LATER why our implementation doesn't work as expected -> during regression testing... for now limit to 5 voices, but make the limit adjustable"**, and on the range asked back and answered: **"1 to 5, default 5, and the take-side default moves from 4 to 5 (Recommended)"**. The two rejected shapes were recorded: a range up to 8, and a separate take-side default of 4.
- It became a knob instead of a constant because of a measurement, not a guess (T-580 item 10, re-run under T-582 6.3, same 3-slot scene text, both TTS endpoints): 3 voices rendered 16.56 s with 2.8 s silence and 13.7 s of speech (83% yield); 4 voices rendered 30.08 s with 28.7 s silence and 1.3 s of speech (4.3%); 5 voices rendered 30.08 s with 28.4 s silence and 1.7 s of speech - the `max_frames 375` ceiling. 5-voice `gen_ms`: 721 435 on the primary (`ap-0732`), 786 390 on `e-11` (`ap-0733`).
- **What it replaced: three answers to "how many voices fit in one take" in three places** - `MAX_DIALOGUE_SPEAKERS = 4` as the take-side default, a hard constant in batch resolution, and the panel's own composer count. There is now one stored ceiling, `voiceCeiling605`, default 5, bounded 1..5, read by all five places.
- **The verb and the persistence rule.** `GET|POST /api/audio-play/voice_ceiling` answers `{voices, default_voices, min_voices, max_voices, at_default, applies_to, what_it_does_not_touch, note}`; a POST outside 1..5 is refused with the range named. The default is not stored: at the default the key is absent from `state.json`, which is the standing rule for every set-only value in this plugin. One `perfLog` line (`ev: voice_ceiling`) records a change.
- **The plan and the cast ANSWER the number instead of letting it be inferred:** `cast_max`, `voice_ceiling`, `voice_ceiling_default`, `voice_ceiling_max` beside the cast, and `cast_preview.cast_over_ceiling` when a scene asks for more than the ceiling. Two different warnings are kept apart: a **clamp** sentence fires only for a number somebody actually NAMED (`ceilingClamp605` requires `spkNamed605`), so an inferred cast is never reported as if the operator had asked for it; an **over-ceiling** note is emitted for any cast above the ceiling, named or inferred.
- **The client half** (`lib/client.js`, lands on a browser reload): a Settings row between the generation ceiling and the job timeout - "voices per take", a numeric box bounded 1..5 wearing the shared box at the unit width (86 px), debounced commit, revert-on-refusal - and the composer's own take ceiling, which now reads the same number instead of carrying its own.
- **What this card does NOT fix, said plainly:** the engine truncation measured above is untouched. A 4- or 5-voice take still renders mostly silence; the mechanism question T-580 asks is deferred to regression testing on the operator's word. This card changes only how many voices are allowed, and where that number lives.

### T-607 BUILT 2026-10-20 - a queued row's endpoint is PROVISIONAL: the pump asks "can the lane this row carries take it NOW?" every pass, instead of stamping a placement once and treating it as a promise
- Built on the operator's live report, verbatim: **"shows 0668 waiting for TTS3 slot instead of using TTS1 - the 'fix to an endpoint for jobs' seems to happen to early ? investigate and fix accordingly aswell"**, and on the fix shape asked back and chosen, verbatim: **"Place at start time, re-decide every pass (Recommended)"**.
- **Measured, read-only, before any code.** `ap-0065`..`ap-0068` were submitted inside 1.2 s of each other and all four were stamped onto `e-11` in ONE completion pass (`assigned_at` 1792453812321 for one row, …322 for the other three). The head row `ap-0065` then parked at the T-236 pre-flight gate (`perf_log` `endpoint_preflight` at 1792453812676, model load `"st":"cached"`) and **never took a queue slot**. The primary went idle at 1792454066796; `ap-0066` started on `e-11` at 1792455339729 - **21 minutes 13 s later**. A later read showed `slots {max: 2, used: 1}` with `primary.running_job_id null`: nothing was short of capacity, the rows were stuck on a name.
- **The mechanism.** `pump()` stamped a placement on EVERY still-pending row it walked; `startQueuedJob` can park at a gate WITHOUT taking a queue slot, so the whole-queue capacity stop never fired and the walk kept going; `endpointSlotBusy` counts RUNNING rows only, so the rows behind a slotless head row kept seeing the same lane as free; and `rowLaneOf` made the welded lane permanent - a row carrying an `endpoint_id` never asked again. Nothing marked whether a lane was the caller's choice or the plugin's guess, so an automatic placement and an operator pin were indistinguishable.
- **The rule now:** per row per pass, ONE availability question - does the lane this row carries still exist, is its runner slot free (T-231), is its machine under the soft per-host cap (T-208)? Yes: keep it, no churn, `assigned_at` does not move. No: place it again now among the lanes that can take it; if none can and it was never placed, park it unassigned with the reason `parkRow` can name; if it does carry a lane, keep the lane and let the existing gates name the wait (`endpoint_slot_wait` naming the holder, `machine_wait`, `endpoint_boot_wait`, `batch_order_wait`).
- **Two boundaries that had to be found by measurement, not assumed.** (1) The pass-level claim map gates PLACEMENT only - a row parked on a lane takes nothing there, so it must not reserve that lane, and the first draft's version churned the T-255 (b) batch parts and the held-lane rows (five T-255 pins failed; they were re-thought, not re-pointed). (2) **Capability is never re-decided at pump time**: the first draft did, and it stranded rows the plugin had accepted itself - `known voice gets reference_text attached` and the T-188 paused-endpoint pin failed, then the suite aborted on an undefined candidate at `tests/host.test.cjs:6304`. A single usable primary is accepted with no catalog answer at all (T-188 / T-198), so re-asking capability would un-place rows this plugin took on its own lane. Availability is the pump's question; capability was the dispatcher's.
- **The usage clock moved from placement to slot-taking:** `stampEndpointUsed(fn, laneId)` is called once, in `startQueuedJob` right after `takeQueueSlot`, and is addressed by LANE ID (the object `endpointForJob` returns for a primary-lane row carries `id: 'primary'` with no `.primary` flag, so the old candidate-based stamper would have skipped every primary-lane row silently). Two pins were re-pointed with the reason written where the old clause stood - T-203's LRU pin and T-238 (C)'s clock pin, whose seeded 5000 / 9000 clocks are now legitimately overwritten by real slot-taking.
- **A pin is now marked, so the panel can say which kind of waiting this is:** `endpoint_pinned` is set only when the CALLER named the endpoint (plumbed through seven submit sites; the pump's own stamp never sets it), round-trips through the saved state, and is projected onto queued rows in `playlist_list` / `job_status`. `parkRow` also gained `only_hold_bar` and a second scan: an operator hold is a HARD bar (T-503), so the first scan skipped the held candidate and the row looked "unassigned for no reason"; now the hold is named.
- **The panel says who decided (client half, plain browser reload).** A queued row the caller pinned wears a violet marker `pinned by you`, whose hover names the endpoint, the machine, and what a pin does NOT do (it never moves the row, so if it waits, it waits HERE); the lane tag of a queued row the PLUGIN placed says the opposite - chosen by the plugin, re-checked every pass, a lane that can takes it, and if none can it keeps this one and says why. Both are gated on the row still being queued, the only state where the sentence is true and the only state the host marks; violet rather than the wait chips' amber because it answers WHO chose, not WHAT it waits for, and a pinned row can and does wear both. The comment that implied an auto row's endpoint is picked once and never moves was amended in place.
- Tests: `endpoint_exclusivity` **125 / 0** (was 105: 14 behavioural + 6 contract pins, nothing relaxed) - the held-lane shape (three rows welded to a plugin-held endpoint KEEP it, one carries `endpoint_wait`, the two behind carry exactly one key naming the row ahead, and not one request reached an engine while another lane sat idle), the head-row shape (a row at the pre-flight gate takes no slot, keeps its lane, says `waiting_for_model`, and is not stamped onto the lane the same pass took), the completion pass (two free lanes -> two rows, one per machine, third row left `endpoint_pending` with no lane), the clock (0 while rows sit placed; moves at slot-taking), and the pin marker followed through row view, playlist view, `state.json` and a restarted host. `host` **2022 / 0** (was 2021). `ui_state` **846 / 0** (was 837: 2 source + 7 behaviour pins for the marker and the two hover sentences, each row addressed by the key its element carries because the tree the suite reads is flat; the T-380 non-vacuity pin counting gated row markers was re-pointed 6 -> 7 with the reason where the old clause stood). `tooltips`, `transport`, `transparency`, `scope`, `selection_memory`, `scene_composer`, `verb_contract` re-run against the changed row, unchanged and green. Full battery, 23 suites, every one `rc=0`: **4645 / 0** across the 21 suites that print a count (the T-605 close: 4624 - the +21 is exactly this card's pins).
- **What this card does NOT fix:** why a row can sit at the pre-flight gate long enough to matter (the T-236 / T-580-adjacent mechanism question, deferred by the operator to regression testing); it does not move a row off a lane a person or the plugin is holding (T-188 / T-503 stand - what the pump now refuses is placing a row that has NO lane onto such a lane); it does not change submit-time placement, the pin refusal sentence, or the batch-order gate. The marker and both hover sentences are built, but the panel half is pinned by fixtures and has not been read live yet.
- **Restart debt:** the `lib/index.js` half is inert until the operator restarts `dsh web` - the same single approval this day's lane carries for T-605; the `lib/client.js` panel half lands on a plain browser reload, no restart. Live verification owed after it, all read-only: a queued row's `endpoint_id` follows a freeing endpoint instead of staying welded; `endpoint_pinned` appears only on rows whose submit named an endpoint; `queue_status`'s per-lane `queued_rows` counts the rows currently headed there.
- **Restart debt CLEARED the same day, 2026-10-20 08:26 Berlin, by the operator hand:** the host half is running (proved by the ceiling verb answering at all). What the live read confirms: the three TTS slots are as the registry says, the incident rows are all `ok` and none carries the pin flag (correct - they predate the code that writes it), and the two usage clocks still hold the values the old code wrote at placement time, which is exactly what the clock move predicts: they refresh when a row takes a slot. ### T-613 BUILT 2026-10-20 — pressing the same row again no longer lengthens the multi-speaker editor: a reuse write is checked against the scene it is about to be written into
- **The operator's words, verbatim, and what they interrupted:** "skip that for now, fix the \"reuse\" of TTS-D jobs first - current problem is that the text \"is added\" on top of existing rows, so the mult-speaker editor content gets longer with every klick". The fix was put in front of the two design topics recorded on T-608 item 34 (voice selection by dropdown instead of typed names; what the reuse affordance is for and what a diar row should hand over). Those stay recorded and unplanned.
- **Four write paths, all of them appending, none of them looking:** the composer's reuse control for a multi-speaker row (`lib/client.js:8183`), its single-line branch for a row that is not multi-speaker (`:8211`), the import picker (`:8409`), and the hand-off a board row's reuse button leaves for the render phase (`:8653`). Appending is T-323's rule that a whole scene is not replaced — the right rule, and not the same rule as appending the same lines a second time.
- **One function now owns every reuse write** (`appendSceneBlocks613`, `:8101`), with `sceneTextLines613` (`:8079`), `blockInSceneText613` (`:8087`) and `alreadyInSceneClause613` (`:8114`): a block already in the scene is not written again, a row that is partly there contributes only its missing lines, a row wholly there writes nothing, and the note says which of the three happened.
- **"Already in this scene" is a whole line, never a piece of one:** `A: hi` is not present in a scene that says `A: hi there`; a multi-line block matches only as the same run of consecutive lines; trailing whitespace is ignored on both sides of the comparison and the written text keeps the block's own words; an empty block counts as present. All four rules are pinned.
- **The check is on the scene text, not on a memory of which rows were taken:** a cast rename maps a speaker onto a voice at save time and does not rewrite the `NAME:` lines, so what this control wrote is still what it can recognise; take the lines out of the text and the same row can be written again. A per-row flag would be wrong the first time a person deleted a line by hand. What it cannot do is recognise a line edited into a different line — that is a new line, and it is written as one. Nothing here deletes, replaces, or reorders a line.
- **The panel counts what arrived instead of claiming an import:** "1 of that row's 8 line(s) were already in this scene and were not written a second time", or "nothing was written: all 8 line(s) that ap-0006 carries are already in this scene … so pressing this control again did not lengthen the scene. Take them out of the scene text if you want them written again. Nothing was dispatched."
- **A board row's press keeps its other half:** the write is guarded, and the chapter editor is opened anyway when nothing was written, because that press was made to reach the editor, where each speaker gets a voice for every line that speaker owns; the cast read still runs after a skipped write, and the sentence is written after it because `checkCast` clears the note when it answers.
- **Both hovers were rewritten to promise what the act now does** (T-459): "all 8 of those line(s) are already in this scene, so pressing this writes nothing and the scene does not grow", or "3 of those 8 line(s) are already in this scene and would not be written again" — computed on the lines the act actually writes, which for a diar row means the relabelled `dialogueLines584` output and not the raw `SPEAKER_00` labels the hover lists.

## Built on 2026-10-21 (first build of the day: 1 card, HOST HALF only - restart owed and not asked for, no restart performed, nothing downloaded, nothing dispatched, no engine contacted; plus 2 cards opened by the operator's own requests, both still open)

### T-620  BUILT 2026-10-21 - the DL button could not answer a real link; the cause was this plugin's own stdout bound, not YouTube
- THE ACT THAT FAILED: the operator pasted `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YwDVtf7-KWc` into the player's url bar and pressed DL. The panel answered "download failed: yt-dlp could not answer for this link: …" with the message cut in the middle of a JSON document.
- BEFORE, measured: the lane log already held it - `ap-0141`, `capability_failed`, **exit 0**, `timed_out false`, version 2026.08.19, **empty `err_tail`**, `out_tail` ending inside a JSON string. Re-running the plugin's exact capability call by hand, read-only: exit 0, empty stderr, **11,618,735 bytes on stdout** (182 formats, `duration 1408`, automatic captions in about 150 languages). The lane did `JSON.parse` over the whole stdout of the shell seam, and the seam caps captured stdout - a bound this plugin names in its own comment at `lib/index.js:10676-10679` ("The executor default stdout cap (64KB) would truncate the body into 'bad json'") and raises to 200 MB on the engine tasks route for exactly that reason. The capability call never got the raised bound. Not a YouTube block, not a bot check, not the binary's version, not ffmpeg.
- THE RULING (operator, recorded 2026-10-21 between 03:15 and 03:21 Berlin, chosen from the options offered): "Fix the DL lane first, then use the panel's DL button" - chosen over downloading by hand, over converting the whole 23-minute clip, and over recording the finding for a later session.
- AFTER, built in `lib/index.js`: the capability question asks for the facts this lane acts on as one bounded template line - `--no-warnings --simulate --skip-download -f bestaudio --print` over id, extractor_key, duration, format_id, ext, acodec, filesize and title, separated by `@@|@@`. Measured on the same link: **127 bytes**, eight fields, empty stderr. The title is printed LAST so the split is bounded to seven fields that cannot contain the separator, and a title carrying a separator or a newline survives intact.
- THE FAILURE PATH, deliberately unchanged: an empty stdout is no answer, not a small answer, so `info` stays null and the refusal branch reports the binary's own words read from the END of what it printed. Measured with the new shape on a dead link: exit 1 and `ERROR: [youtube] nope_missin: This video is unavailable` on stderr. The rule T-436 insisted on survives the change.
- FIXED ALONG THE WAY: the capability pass now resolves the format the download leg will actually ask for, so a link with no audio-only format is named before the download instead of after it. `formats: <count>` became `format: "251-20 webm opus 22085194B"` in the row answer and in the lane record.
- MEASURED FACTS KEPT: `n_formats` prints `NA` outside a playlist, so a template cannot carry a format count. `bestaudio` on this link is `251-20`, webm/opus, abr 125.46, 22,085,194 bytes, 1408 s; the lane's `-x --audio-format wav` turns that into about a quarter of a gigabyte at 48 kHz stereo, which is what a conversion job would be asked to stage. Artefacts: `scratch/diag/capJ.json` (the 11.6 MB answer), `scratch/diag/capT.txt` (127 bytes), `scratch/diag/badP.err` (the dead-link words), `scratch/diag/url.txt` (the link, handed in a file exactly as the plugin does).
- TESTS: five pins in `tests/host.test.cjs` named the old `-J` shape - the stub seam's answer, the call-shape assertion, the call-ordering index, the source-shape count, and the answer's `formats === 2` field. All five name the bounded template now, and the stub answers the way the binary answers that call. `node tests/host.test.cjs`: **2023 pass, 0 fail**, kept at `scratch/diag/host_test_20261021.log`.
- OWED: this is a host half, and the live host runs `main: lib/index.js` from a `link:` bundle, so the change is on disk and not in the running process. It needs the operator's per-restart OK for the `dsh web` restart. None was asked for and none was performed.

### T-622 opened (operator request, verbatim, 2026-10-21 03:21 Berlin) - the OmniVoice instruct vocabulary, ANALYSED, decision still the operator's
- Read the current playlist: **118 rows, 16 not ok** - 7 qwen3-tts cancelled before dispatch, 5 omnivoice instruct refusals, 1 kill-requested, 1 qwen3-tts 503 busy, 1 index_tts2 missing `--voice-ref`, 1 kokoro-tts UniDic resources not bundled. Counted honestly: two engine-side faults, one request the plugin should have refused before dispatch, eight operator cancels, five the vocabulary wall.
- The five OmniVoice rows carried "Loud shouting" (ap-0136/137/138), "loud shout" (ap-0140) and "male voice, thirties, dry delivery" (ap-0098), all under `voice_mode: "no_voice"`. The engine's `resolve_instruct` (`src/models/omnivoice/prompt_builder.cpp:374` in the reference checkout at `650b6370`) checks every comma-separated item against a CLOSED set - the twelve attributes of `instruct_en_to_zh` (:311-325) in English and Chinese, plus the ten accents and the dialect list (:337-346) - and offers "did you mean" only within edit distance `max(2, len/3)` (:295-309).
- THE FINDING: the spec's own description of the option ("speaker attributes, accent, style, or delivery") is wider than the code accepts. There is no loudness, emotion or delivery item in the vocabulary, so "angry and loud" - the phrase this project has aimed at since T-471 - is not expressible through OmniVoice instruct items. Calling OmniVoice a design model is correct (the spec declares `capabilities {"design":["voice_design"]}`, and this plugin's family row at `lib/index.js:7455` says `tts clone design`); the mismatch is that the panel's free-text style field hands the engine prose where the engine expects one of its listed items.

## Built on 2026-10-21 (eleventh build of the day: 1 bug fixed, CLIENT HALF ONLY - lands on a plain browser reload, no host file touched, no verb change, no restart owed) - T-627: a play press on a PAUSED title now resumes it; a fresh start is what an already-playing, finished, or stopped file gets

- THE REPORT (operator, verbatim, 2026-10-21 11:38 Berlin): **"i just found another bug, if i have a title paused, if i hit play it starts fresh instead of unpause. play button should only start fresh if already playing, if paused it should unpause please investigate and fix across playbacks - must also word 'during stream play' or crossfade edge cases"**.
- THE CAUSE, IN ONE LINE: the pause button already resumed (`togglePlaybackPause299` calls `a.play()` and touches no resource), but the play side had no resume path at all - every play control ends in `startPlayback`, and `startPlayback` re-assigns the element's resource (`a.src = url; a.load(); a.play()`), which is precisely what rewinds a media element to 0. The transport's ▶ was the clearest case because **T-407 had already built the resume rule for a paused STATION only**: `playWalked` carried a station-only branch and let a paused TAKE fall straight through to `playJob`. That fall-through was the bug.
- THE FIX IS ONE RULE, NOT SEVEN PATCHES: `resumeHeldPlayback627(a, url627)` (lib/client.js, beside `playbackIsHeld299`) resumes when the file is **held** - paused, not ended, not stopped by a press, holding a resource - and refuses otherwise, which is what keeps the operator's other half ("only start fresh if already playing") exactly as it was. It touches `play()` and nothing else: no `src`, no `load()`, no seek. `resumePresented627()` is the transport's version of the same question, asked against `controlEl395()` - the element the pause button, the volume slider and the position bar already agree on (T-407 / T-504). The old station-only branch in `playWalked` was taken out and its case now lives inside the one rule.
- "ACROSS PLAYBACKS" IS LITERAL: the rule is asked at every door that plays something - the transport ▶, a row's own play button, "▶ src", a stem button, a voice sample, prev / next, and an imported station (`playStream395`, the one path that used to RE-FETCH a paused station, which on a live broadcast means jumping to the live edge). Each asks **before** it interrupts, so a resume never destroys the queue or the busy flag of the run it is resuming.
- A PRESS NEVER RESUMES THE WRONG MEDIA: `mediaHeldMatches627` compares the pressed route with the resource the element actually holds (exact, or after stripping the origin - a browser reports absolute, the panel hands a lane route). A paused source file does not answer the press that asks for that row's main output, a paused stem does not answer a press for another stem, and another row is a fresh start. Both directions are measured.
- THE WORDING THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR: the answer names the act and the position - "This file was PAUSED - play resumes it from 0:12 of 0:40 instead of starting it again" - and for a broadcast, where a position would be a lie, "The station was PAUSED - play resumes it from where it stopped instead of starting it again". A take resume then words the stream it sits on, in the mode it is in: pause mode "the station is still paused under this take and plays on when the take ends", duck mode "the station keeps playing under it, at the ducked level", stop mode "there is no station under this take". The ▶'s own hover carries the whole ruling before the press, on both mounts.
- THE CROSSFADE EDGE THAT NEEDS A REFUSAL, NOT AN ANSWER: a station whose pause belongs to a TAKE (pause mode stepped it back for the length of the render) is not a person's pause. A press targeting the station in that moment says so - "the station is paused BY THE CROSSFADE while a take is playing - it plays on when that take ends (the crossfade setting is 'pause the stream'; the station's own stop button ends it now)" - rather than fighting the setting. `stationPausedByTake627()` reads `overlapRef395.current` for it, and the suite proves the sentence: when the take ends, `releaseOverlap395()` hands the station its playback back.
- WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT CHANGE: a STOPPED file starts fresh (T-307's stopped-is-not-paused distinction, measured); `pauseStream395` stays the imported line's own toggle (T-407's ruling); a press on a file that is NOT the held one still drops the queue - that is what those controls have always been for; an auto walk (`ffStepForward559` / `fastForwardAfter559`) is not a press and got no guard.
- TESTS, AND THEIR NEGATIVE CONTROLS: new suite `tests/pause_resume.test.cjs`, **48 checks, 0 fail**, added to the standing `npm test` gate in `package.json`; the full gate runs green (`/tmp/npmtest_20261021_t627.log`, EXIT=0). Resume and fresh are measured on the element: resume = `play()` ran with the same `src`, no new `load()`, no new lane ask; fresh = the resource was re-assigned. `/tmp/neg627/a/client.js` (guards taken back out - the panel as it was when the bug was reported) fails **23** of the checks, including the operator's own case; `/tmp/neg627/b/client.js` (guards in, identity test off) fails **5**, which is what proves the "right media only" checks bite.
- THREE OLDER PINS RE-POINTED IN PLACE, WITH THE REASON WHERE THE OLD MEASURE STOOD: `tests/transport.test.cjs` pinned nine panel-scoped prefixes in the panel stylesheet where the honest count is now **eleven** - two arrived with **T-594**'s speed-slider track rules, and that pin was already stale before this build because the suite is not in the `npm test` list; the claim it guards (every rule panel-scoped, nothing unscoped) is unchanged. `tests/shut.test.cjs` T-375 and `tests/stream_overlap.test.cjs` T-551 both compared against the literal `queuePlayback("/audio-play/" + encodeURIComponent(id) + "?src=1", id, true)`; the source press and the stem press now spell that route into a local name first, because a press has to know which file it is asking about before it drops the queue. Same route, new position - both pins now measure the call.
- OWED FROM THIS BUILD: the same plain browser reload the other client-half builds are owed. On that reload: pause a take, press ▶, and it plays on from where it stopped with its position named; press ▶ again while it is playing and it starts fresh; press "▶ src" on a paused take and it does not resume that take; pause a station with the transport and press ▶ and the station plays on; press the same live link again while the station is paused and it is not re-fetched.

## Built on 2026-10-21 (thirteenth build of the day: 1 ruled open item built, CLIENT HALF ONLY - lands on a plain browser reload, no host file touched, no verb change, no restart owed) - T-613 item 15: a reuse press writes a row's lines OVER the block this scene already carries for those speakers, in place, instead of refusing

- THE RULING, VERBATIM (operator, 2026-10-21 02:22 Berlin, answering the open question T-613 item 13 left): **"can't the second press just overwrite it, like the first press would ? do not overcomplicate"**, and its shape question answered **"By speaker name"**. What that rules out is on the card: no provenance record in the scene, no stored list of which block came from which row, no separate remove control.
- THE GUARD RENAMED WITH THE ACT IT PERFORMS: `appendSceneBlocks613` (refuse a repeat, append the rest) is gone from `lib/client.js` and `writeSceneBlocks613(blocks)` (:8490) stands in its place - the old name appears nowhere in the file. It reports `{ total, added, replaced, taken, put, leftRuns, same, changed, textUnchanged, names, addedNames, replacedNames, presentNames, newNames }`, and `setText` runs **only when the text actually changes**.
- THE RUN, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: `blockName613` reads a block's first line with the composer's OWN name rule `NAME_RE381` (:8053); `sceneTurns613` (:8466) walks the scene text into `[{ name, start, end }]` line ranges with that same rule - a continuation line and a blank line belong to the turn they follow, a leading unattributed line is a turn with `name: ""`. The press finds the first scene turn whose speaker name one of the row's blocks carries, extends while every following turn also belongs to the row's names, and writes the row's blocks - in the row's order - into the place that run occupied. A speaker the row does not speak for ends the run. `endLine613` is the line the first turn outside the run begins on, or the end of the text when nothing is left.
- WHY IT IS THE WHOLE RUN AND NOT THE FIRST TURN OF EACH NAME: the first attempt replaced only the first turn of each name, and a repeat press of the 8-line 3-speaker row grew the scene **526 -> 705 characters** - the exact fault T-613 was opened for. A later, separate turn under one of those names is counted in `leftRuns`, left exactly where it sat, and said out loud: "this scene carries 1 more turn(s) under voy_janeway and they were left where they are".
- THE SLICE FAULT, MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED: slicing with a turn's own `end` index instead of the line the next turn begins on silently ate the next speaker's line (`B’Elanna Torres: Try the left one.` disappeared from the authored fixture) and threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'end')` when the run reached the end of the text.

## Built on 2026-10-21 (seventeenth build of the day: 1 operator request built, HOST + CLIENT halves - the host half needs an operator-run `dsh web` restart, the client half one browser reload) - T-626: the engine build number is visible in the endpoint section, as a value a person RECORDED on the node

- THE ASK, verbatim (operator 2026-10-21): "the buildnumber should be visible in our endpoint section (track as small todo)". It came in the same message as the node updates, and the node updates are what made it meaningful: both CPU lanes were moved to `0125a991` = `v0.9.2-drama3-base-small-26-g0125a991` today (cpu1 `<home>/gits/audio-cpp`, cpu2 `/opt/quickrobot/audio.cpp`, 126 spec JSONs each, `BUILD_RC=0`, logs `<home>/build_20261021.log`), and until today nothing in the panel said which build a slot is running.
- WHAT WAS MEASURED FIRST, because it decided the whole design: **the engine does not serve its own build.** `GET <engine>/health` answers `{"status":"ok","backend":"cpu","models":59,"ui":true,"ui_management":true}` and the served UI routes carry no version or build route; in the reference checkout the build info exists only for `--version` (`app/server/main.cpp:170-171`, `app/common/build_info.cpp` used at `app/cli/main.cpp:665/801`). So a plugin that "shows the build number" by asking the engine would show nothing, and a plugin that inferred it would be inventing it.
- THE DECIDED ROUTE, and it is the honest one: the plugin RECORDS what a person read on the node (the value of `git describe --tags`) with the time it was recorded, reports it as recorded, and never as measured. The panel says so in the hover: "The plugin cannot measure it".
- THE HOST HALF. One store keyed by lane id with `primary` included, so there is ONE code path for a primary slot and a registry entry: `endpointBuilds626`, `buildRecordOf626`, `setBuildRecord626` (it returns true only when something actually MOVED, which is what makes the T-502 `changed` / `unchanged` answer honest for this field too), `endpointBuildsSnapshot626` (undefined when nothing is recorded, so a fresh install writes no key). `cleanEndpointRouteInput` validates `build` in the SAME gate as `url` / `route` / the flags / `models`, so a bad build string rejects the WHOLE update rather than silently dropping one field; `endpoint_add` carries it, `endpoint_update` counts it in `asked` and pushes it into `changed` only when it moved, and `registryEntryView` / `primaryEndpointView` answer it as `build` plus `build_at` on every entry and on the primary view. Persisted under the additive key `endpoint_builds`, and the restore REVALIDATES rather than trusts: an id that is neither `primary` nor `e-<digits>` is dropped, a build string that fails the shape gate is dropped, and a timestamp that is not a number is read as 0 (recorded, date unknown).
- THE STRING GATE, and why it is that shape: `BUILD_TEXT_MAX626 = 96`, `^[A-Za-z0-9._+\-()/ ]+$`, CRLF and tabs folded to spaces. It accepts what `git describe --tags` prints (`v0.9.2-drama3-base-small-26-g0125a991`) and nothing that could smuggle markup or a control sequence into a row. `""` clears the record. A refused field goes through `logInputRefuse`, so it lands in the perf log as an `input_refused` record naming the verb and the reason - the same record a bad url has always produced, not an endpoint-state refusal.

## Built on 2026-10-22 (first build of the day: 1 operator fix-up on yesterday's control, CLIENT HALF, one browser reload owed) - T-629 item 19: the speed readout is pinned to the SLIDER, and a release hides it

- THE FIX-UP, verbatim (operator 2026-10-22 00:14 Berlin): "The Value of speed % looks nice, but should be pinned to the slider, not the mouse pointer movement , and should hide as soon as mouse is released after slide". Yesterday's control worked; its PLACEMENT was wrong, and the operator found it by using it.
- TWO SEPARATE FAULTS, two separate fixes. First: the box chased `ev.clientX` / `ev.clientY`, so the number moved when the HAND moved and not when the VALUE moved. Second: `onPointerMove` opened the box on a plain hover, so a release could not hide it - a move would just show it again the moment the cursor came back.
- THE PLACEMENT NOW READS THE CONTROL. `sliderReadoutAt629` takes the held element's own rect plus its `min` / `value` / `max` and puts the box on the THUMB: a range input maps its value onto the track minus the thumb's own width (`SLIDER_READOUT_THUMB629 = 12`), so 0.75 on a 45 px strip sits at 6 + 0.75 × 33 = 30.75 px from the strip's left edge, and the 46 px box is centred there with `SLIDER_READOUT_GAP629 = 4` of air above. When the strip is against the panel's top edge the box goes UNDER it rather than being clipped. `clientX` / `clientY` are not inputs to the placement anywhere in it. min / max are read off the element, so a slider whose range is 0..100 (the volume) places correctly too - the placement still knows nothing about playback speed.
- A READOUT BELONGS TO A HOLD, NOT TO A HOVER. `sliderReadoutHeld629` tracks `pointer` and `key` apart (a keyboard hold has no press to end it; a press a browser cancels must not leave a box behind): `onPointerDown` opens, `onPointerMove` is gated by the held flag, and `onPointerUp` / `onPointerCancel` / `onKeyUp` / `onBlur` all go through ONE `hide629()` that clears the flag AND the box. `onInput` recomputes the whole position from the control while a hold is active - it no longer carries the old coordinates over. A keyboard hold lands the box in exactly the same place a press does: one placement, no pointer branch.
- TESTS. `tests/ui_state.test.cjs` **909 -> 916 pass, 0 fail**. FOUR T-629 pins RE-POINTED IN PLACE with the reason written where the old measure stood: the press pin (was `left 178px / top 74px` off a pointer at clientX 500; now `left 8px / top 14px` off the strip's own rect), the drag pin (was "the box follows the pointer to 298px"; now the cursor travels 120 px with the value unchanged and NOTHING moves), the in-flight pin (was `left 298px` carried from the press; now the value moving to the far end moves the box 8 px right to stay on the thumb), and the keyboard pin (was `top 10px` from a different fallback; now `top 14px`, the same place a press puts it). SIX new checks: the same value pressed at a different place on the strip lands the box in the SAME place; a hover with no press held shows no box at all; a strip against the panel top gets the box UNDER it at `top 24px`; and three source pins - the placement reads the control and contains no `clientX`, the move handler is gated by the held flag with every release path going through `hide629()`, and the paint puts the box where the placement computed it instead of re-deriving a position from a raw pointer offset. ## Built on 2026-10-22 (second build of the day: 1 operator report built, CLIENT HALF, one browser reload owed) - T-630: a fresh start says the playback speed again at the door that plays

- THE REPORT, verbatim (operator 2026-10-22 Berlin): "Fresh starting play actions do not seem to respect the speed setting ?!?".
- WHERE THE OLD CLAIM STOPPED SHORT. T-594 put the speed on the take's element in `queuePlayback`, and its comment says "on every arrival" - but a queue is not a start. What a start does is `a.src = url`, `a.load()`, `a.play()`: an assertion made before the load is not the assertion at the moment the file begins. And a resume press - T-627's `resumeHeldPlayback627`, or the transport pause button letting a paused take play on - never goes through the queue at all, so those starts carried no assertion whatsoever.
- THE FIX: `applyRateAtPlayDoor630` (lib/client.js:15717) is asked at three doors - in `startPlayback` immediately after `load()` and before `play()`, in `resumeHeldPlayback627` before its `play()`, and in `togglePlaybackPause299` when the pause button resumes. It reads the speed from `playRatePosRef630`, a ref next to the state that the setter moves in the same act, so a door built in an older render slice still reads the CURRENT speed. The queue-time assertion T-594 introduced is KEPT: this is an addition at the last moment, not a replacement.
- WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED, stated plainly: the root cause was not measured - this harness renders props, not pixels and there is no browser in reach from this session. Two candidate causes are named and both are covered: a browser that puts the element back at normal speed when a new resource loads (what the report describes), and a play door whose closure carried an older speed. The fix does not depend on which one it was.
- T-594 RULING (2) IS ENFORCED BY THE DOOR'S GUARD: the function returns unless the element is `audioRef.current`, and the T-627 resume door asks it only when the element is not a station. A pin proves the station element is never even ASKED for a rate.
- TESTS. `tests/pause_resume.test.cjs` **48 -> 56 pass, 0 fail**. The mock media element now models the reported symptom instead of assuming the browser kept the speed - its `load()` puts the element back at 1x - and every rate the PANEL asks for is recorded in `_rateSets`, so a pin can tell "the panel asked for 1.41x" from "the mock left it at 1". Six new behaviour checks (a fresh start from the transport control asks the element it just started for 2^0.5; a second fresh start asks again after the load; the pause button's resume plays on at the held speed; the row's own control is a third door and the pin names the one lane ask that door needs because T-627 matches on the full route; a station is never asked; the queue-time line is still there) plus three source checks. One older T-627 source pin RE-POINTED in place: "the resume touches play() and nothing else" now reads "play() and the speed on the element it already holds" - no src, no load, no seek, still refused.
- THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, one per door: `/tmp/neg630a/lib/client.js` (the `startPlayback` door off) fails **3**; `/tmp/neg630b/lib/client.js` (the T-627 resume door off) fails **2**; `/tmp/neg630c/lib/client.js` (the pause-button door off) fails **2**. ## Built on 2026-10-22 (eighth build of the day: HOST HALF, and it went live with the operator's own 08:14 Berlin restart after the backend crash, no restart asked for by this work) - T-596 item 7's extension: `batch_text_delete` and `batch_text_update`, and neither one deletes

- THE RULING, verbatim (operator 2026-10-21 00:53 Berlin, answering the "list" button question): "remove the button, re-read on open - and extend the todo: Add 'delete' and 'update' functionality for the preset prompts". The button half landed on 2026-10-21. This is the delete and update half, built 04:54-06:52 Berlin.
- NOTHING IS DELETED. Both verbs `mv -n` the file that was there into `BASE + '/texts-trash'` under a dated name (`2026-10-22T04-52-07Z__quick house.json`) and answer with `deleted: false` plus the path it moved to. A replaced preset is still on disk one directory over with its name and its timestamp on it. The workspace trashbin rule (move it, never delete; nothing in this tree is under git) and this plugin's own never-overwrite ruling of 2026-10-12 are the two sources of this rule, and neither was invented for this verb.
- THE TRASH IS A SIBLING OF `texts/`, NOT A FOLDER INSIDE IT, and the reason is the picker: `batch_text_list` is a walk of the filesystem since T-572, so a `.trash` inside `texts/` would be walked straight back into the dropdown. Outside `texts/` it cannot be listed, and the same containment rule that protects every other path is what keeps a retired file out of these verbs' reach.
- A VERB THAT DESTROYS ANSWERS BEFORE IT ACTS (T-589, the operator's word after the 2026-10-18 incident). Without `confirm` naming itself, delete reports the file, its bytes, its title and where it would go; update reports the old and the new character counts and where the current version would go. Both answers carry `would_move` / `would_replace`, and both change nothing.
- PRESETS ONLY, refused by name. The file is read back and must parse as `kind:"preset"` with a string `prompt` before either verb touches it; a dialogue batch file is refused with its reason stated and stays on disk. The format is read from the file, never assumed from the folder it happens to sit in.
- THE LISTING KEEPS THE TRUTH: the index entry that named the old path is replaced by one with `format:'retired'`, `retired_from` naming where it came from and `retired_at` stamping when, pointing at the trash copy. An update re-lists the path once with the new byte count. No entry is left naming a path that no longer exists.
- TWO FINDINGS, both from running the verb rather than reading it. (1) Asked for `texts/x.json; rm -rf /` the host first answered "no file at that path": `isSafePath` refuses quotes, backslashes and control characters but says nothing about `;` or a glob, so the characters the save door already refuses in a NAME are now refused here by name instead of being trusted to `sq()`'s quoting. (2) The gate's own "already in the trash" refusal was dead code, because the containment rule always fired first; it is gone and its sentence is now part of the containment refusal, which is the only place a person is told where a retired preset went and that it is restored by hand.
- TESTS: 10 new checks in `tests/host.test.cjs` and a new opt-in shell seam (`opts.moveSeam596`) that EXECUTES `mv -n` inside the fake fs, because "nothing is deleted, the file went to the trash" is a claim about a filesystem and cannot be proved off a recorded command. `node tests/host.test.cjs`: 2068 pass, 0 fail (was 2057). Full `npm test`: EXIT=0, 0 FAIL and 0 THREW lines (log `/tmp/npmtest_20261022_t596_verbs.log`). Negative control `/tmp/neg596del/` (both `confirm` gates forced open): 2062 pass, 6 fail, and the six are the gate's own checks.
- LIVE, PROVED THE CAREFUL WAY: a POST to each new verb with no path answered `path is required (a preset file under <home>/.dsh/audio-play/texts, as batch_text_list reports it)` - the refusal that fires before any filesystem is touched. No preset has been deleted or updated live yet; `texts-trash/` does not exist and will not until a person asks for a move.
- STILL THE OPERATOR'S CALL: the panel-side control shape. Nothing was built in `lib/client.js` for it, deliberately - a button calling a verb the host does not answer is worse than no button, and the host half only became live at 08:14 today. The two shapes worth choosing between are a delete glyph on the preset picker row, and a "replace" beside "save" that writes the edited prompt onto the selected preset's own path while the previous version moves to the trash.

## Built on 2026-10-22 (ninth build of the day: HOST HALF, and it is NOT live yet - one `dsh web` restart owed, its own explicit OK) - T-596's confirmed move was broken by its own sandbox policy, and a conversion row now names the voice it converted to

- THE FAULT, in the host's own words. The dry answers worked live (`would_move` with the path and bytes, `would_replace` with `old_chars:72` / `new_chars:52`, nothing touched). The CONFIRMED pair both failed: `the move failed: mv exit 1 - the preset is still where it was` and `the current version could not be moved aside: mv exit 1 - nothing was written, the preset is unchanged`. Both are in the lane log as `ev:"input_refused"`. `texts-trash/` was created and left empty; the probe preset is unchanged and still listed. The verbs kept their promise under failure: nothing else moved.
- THE CAUSE IS ONE LINE OF POLICY. `mv` wrote at two ends and the per-call `sandboxPolicy` named only the end the file LEAVES: `writePolicy(dirName(p596))` = `texts/presets`, while `writePolicy` is ONE `workspaceRoot` and the runner binds only that writable. `mkdir -p texts-trash` had succeeded seconds earlier because ITS policy named BASE. A move needs a root that contains both ends. Both legs now carry `writePolicy(BASE)` (:13312, :13381) with the measurement written above each one - BASE is what `writePolicy()` already defaults to, and the path gate still keeps the command inside `texts/`.
- WHY 2 068 GREEN CHECKS MISSED IT, and what changed. The suite's `moveSeam596` executes `mv -n` inside the fake fs, so it proves the effect of a move and is blind to a policy the real shell refuses. A new check reads the recorded spec and pins the move's `workspaceRoot` to BASE - not the source directory, not the trash - with the live `mv exit 1` in the label. Host suite: **2 072 pass / 0 fail** (`/tmp/host596e.log`).
- THE CONVERSION LANE LANDED, MEASURED ON BOTH CPU NODES. From one short real take (ap-0133, 2.39 s): **ap-0163** chatterbox `vc` aimed at the registry voice `bijan` came back **ok, 2.40 s, 115 244 bytes** on cpu2 with the T-625 mechanism visible in the log (`task_kind_override` wire `clon` vs asked `vc`, then `load ... "task":"vc"`); **ap-0162** rvc_f16 with `target_voice` was **refused before the row existed** (rvc declares no speaker reference) and the version naming rvc's own `options.voice_id` was accepted and came back **ok, 2.38 s, 190 444 bytes** on cpu1 with the note that the engine chose the target and with no reference staged (`in_bytes:0`).
- AND THE ROW COULD NOT SAY WHO IT CONVERTED TO. Both rows answered `voice:""` and so did `ev:"job_outcome"`. A `vc` row now carries `vc_target_voice`, its file is named `ap-<id>_<model>_vc_to_<voice>.wav`, and the outcome log carries `vc_target`. The name is a SEPARATE key from `voice` on purpose: `voice` becomes `req.voice_id` on this lane, and a plugin registry name is not an engine voice_id - the measured seed_vc refusal of 2026-10-15 ("unknown Seed-VC request option: target_voice") is what confusion between those two costs. Three new checks pin the row key, the absence of the name on the wire, and the log field.
- ONE LIVE DELETE PROOF, DONE WITHOUT TOUCHING THE OPERATOR'S AUDIO. `resample_audio` on an existing short row made a throwaway copy (**ap-0164**, 222 784 bytes in `tts/`); `playlist_delete {job_id, delete_file:true}` answered **`file_deleted:true`** and the file is gone. The `DL_DIR` half of that guard (the capture store, which is what T-623 item 17 added) is still unproven live: the only capture row on the lane is the operator's. The same policy shape is named on the T-623 card: the delete's `rm` names one directory while its target list can hold several.
- OWED FROM THIS BUILD: one operator-run `dsh web` restart. Until it, the running host still has the broken move policy, and the next conversion row still cannot show `vc_target_voice`.


## Built on 2026-10-22 (eleventh build of the day: HOST HALF, and it is NOT live yet - one `dsh web` restart owed, its own explicit OK) - T-606: a converted mp3 / ogg copy carries the six tags its row can answer

A wav is never tagged: the builder returns an empty argument list for any container other than mp3 and ogg.
- The six values, read off the row and nothing else: title is the prompt on a generated row and the spoken text on a speech row, cut at 100 characters with the whole line then travelling in `comment`; artist is the voice on a speech row and the model family on a generated row; album is `batch_title` on a batch part and absent otherwise; year travels under the key `date`; comment carries the job id, the model and the vetted options map.
- Genre follows the operator's ruling of 2026-10-22 - a generated row whose model family declares BOTH music and effects (stable_audio) carries **no genre frame at all**, "Leave the genre tag off in that case"; a music-only family tags Music, an effect-only family tags Sound effect, a speech / vc / s2s row tags Speech, and a separated take carries no genre either.
- Measured on this host with the ffmpeg this plugin runs, over a copy of a real stored take in `/tmp` (nothing synthesised, nothing in the store touched): `-id3v2_version 4` writes ID3v2.4 (read back at byte level as version 4 revision 0); title / artist / album / genre land as TIT2 / TPE1 / TALB / TCON; `date=` lands as the native TDRC frame while `year=` lands as a user-defined TXXX frame, which is why the render date is written as `date`; `comment` lands as TXXX[comment] on mp3 (no spelling of it writes COMM on this ffmpeg) and as the Vorbis DESCRIPTION on ogg; and this host's `ffprobe` reports the ogg comments on the STREAM, not on the container.
- `tests/host.test.cjs`: a new T-606 block of 12 checks, and four existing command-shape pins re-pointed with dated comments rather than relaxed (the T-468 conversion seam, two mount filters, the twin call-site source pin). The suite caught a fault in this card's own scanner - it mis-read sq()'s `'\''` idiom and reported a quoted `$(whoami)` as loose - fixed in the test; the command it was scanning was correct.
- Suite totals for this batch: 24 suites, 4 962 checks, 0 fail, 0 throw, every suite EXIT=0 (host 2 084 - 2 072 before plus the 12 new T-606 checks; ui_state 944; scope 332; scene_composer 215; render 220 pass 0 throw; actions 229; stream_overlap 137; endpoint_exclusivity 125; transport 110; engine_boot 99; flow 89; shut 66; selection_memory 62; pause_resume 56; model_library 45; batch_board 29; event_log 35; transparency 22; shell_safety 31; tooltips 12; verb_contract 12; handler 4; effects 4; model_matrix 0 checks, exit 0).

## Built on 2026-10-23 (first build of the day: HOST HALF, and it went live with the operator's own 07:57 Berlin / 05:57 UTC restart) - the playlist id sequence gets a persisted floor, and the save-voice gate gets the mark the operator's ruling picked

So the plugin gains a stored switch, default OFF, and it is its own value: the read-aloud chunking in Settings (`audio-play:chunkSize`, a browser value in CHARACTERS, default 600) is a different mechanism in a different unit and the host half never reads it - a source pin says so.
- WHY "three times higher" was not the fix, measured on the code and on a live row: the seconds wish is clamped to 600 s inside `secondsBudget` and the text budget to 4 000 characters, and the number an unnamed caller really gets is not the 45 s the constant names - with `job_timeout 3600` and the default pessimistic cost (200 s of compute per second of audio) it is **18 s**. ap-0174, read live while the card was open, is the same arithmetic: `part_chars 135`, 3 speakers, `frame_seconds 150`, `frame_source derived`. "Do not cut a chapter" is not a bigger number, it is a flag - which is what was built.
- THE SWITCH: `BATCH_AUTO_SPLIT633 = false` as the code default plus a live value, written to state.json **only when it differs from the default** and restored in `loadState` - the shape `limit_one_per_host` uses. `GET|POST /api/audio-play/batch_split`: GET answers `enabled` beside `part_seconds`, `min_part_seconds`, `max_parts`, `chars_per_second`, `job_timeout_sec` and `seconds_budget` (the 45 s wish against the 18 s the timeout pays for, now readable from the plugin); POST needs a real boolean and refuses anything else with `enabled must be true or false`.
- THE SEAM, and what the switch does NOT touch: `planBatchParts` gained a seventh argument, and only the two LENGTH rules - the seconds budget and the character budget - sit behind it. The CAST rule stays outside it, because a take cannot carry more voices than the voice ceiling (T-605): with the switch off a wide scene is still cut where a new voice would not fit. Frame arithmetic is untouched - a part is never given less room than it estimates unless `job_timeout / cost_per_second` caps it, `over_budget` and `truncated_risk` still fire, and T-173's runaway guard and T-203's truncation notice still do their job.
- BOTH ANSWERS SAY WHICH RULE MADE THE PART COUNT. The dispatch answer says "Automatic part-splitting is OFF on the batch path (batch_split, T-633): ... cut only where a new voice would exceed the speaker ceiling (N), never for length", or the ON wording with the number it cuts at; the dry-run `batch_plan` answer carries `split_switch` and `split_rule` in its own object, and its per-part over-budget warning adds "the part-splitting switch (batch_split) is OFF, so nothing was cut for length; turning it back on is the other lever". A plan that shows one part without saying why hides the rule it followed.
- THE COST OF CHANGING A LANE DEFAULT, recorded because it was not small: 26 pins failed and one suite aborted until seven fixtures were told to ASK for the cut - the T-173/174/175/176 block, T-179, T-251, T-217, the T-203 / T-205 factory, T-258, T-262 and T-266 / T-298 now seed `batch_auto_split: true`, each with a dated RE-POINT comment. Not one claim was relaxed: every pin carries the same number it carried before, and what changed is that the split is something a fixture asks for instead of something it inherited. The T-251 pure-planner pins needed nothing, because the new argument is additive.
- TESTS: 18 new host checks (planner OFF against ON, the ceiling still cutting with the switch off, the frame room coming from the part's own estimate under a timed cost and `over_budget` firing under the default cost, the shipped default on a fresh store, the boolean-only POST, the plan wording OFF and ON, and three persistence pins). ## Built on 2026-10-23 (evening) - the voice-capable mark belongs to the PLACEMENT, not to the dispatcher alone (T-631 items 27-28)

- THE PROOF ROW FOUND THE GAP ON THE LIVE HOST. ap-0184 (gen, `controlfoley`, a family the engine record names `sfx` only) rendered ok - 8.01 s, 706 604 B, on `primary` - and stayed `voice_capable:''` with no `voice_capable_mark` line in the perf log, so the panel would have offered that take the save-voice door the gate exists to refuse.
- THE CAUSE, READ OUT OF THE CODE. The mark had one call site - the dispatcher - and its guard is `if (!url) return;`. A row accepted while no lane can take it is submitted `deferred` (`chooseEndpointAtSubmit` returns `endpoint:null` whenever more than one candidate exists; the T-188 short-circuit applies only to a LONE primary), so the row carried `endpoint_pending:true` and no node, and when the pump chose its node later nothing marked it again.
- THE FIX. `pump()` now calls `markVoiceCapable631(job, String(job.family || job.model || ''), placed.endpoint)` on the same branch that stamps the lane (lib/index.js:5127), with the reason written beside it. The dispatch call stays, the pump adds the second one.
- IT IS LIVE. The operator restarted the harness at 23:01 Berlin after a machine crash (pids 70040 / 70053), so every host edit written today is live and no restart is owed for this one.
- A FIXTURE SEAM HAD TO BE ADDED to make the state reproducible: `speechHoldMs` (tests/host.test.cjs:154-161) holds the first render of a fixture - speech route or `/v1/tasks/run` - for a real beat, so the only qualified lane is still carrying a row when the next row is accepted. Three attempts did not reproduce it first, and the reason is on the record: a LONE primary always takes the row whatever it is doing, and `AUDIO_PLAY_MAX_JOBS_PER_HOST=1` does not help because a busy endpoint is still a submit candidate - only a second registered endpoint makes submit answer `deferred`.
- TESTS. `tests/host.test.cjs` **2120 pass, 0 fail** (2116 pass, 0 fail before this change): the row is reproduced as accepted with no node, the mark lands when the pump places it, the perf line names the record read, and a source-shape pin holds the pump's stamp branch to marking on the family the row carries. No other suite was re-run for this change, per the operator's ruling of 2026-10-22.

## Built on 2026-10-24 (morning) - the voice list is read from the engine that renders it (T-614, host half)

- Measured before any line was written, on both CPU nodes: the engine's own `voice_id` parameter is served per model on `/v1/models?include_params=1` (`qwen3-tts` and `qwen3-customvoice` 9 values with no default, `supertonic` 10 with default "M1", `kokoro-tts` 54 with default "af_heart"), while the plugin's own `GET voice_modes` said this engine has no built-in speaker. The gap was one request wide: the plugin had always read the capability record harvested out of the engine's served page, and never the parameter the engine validates.
- `GET voice_modes?fn=…&model=…` now carries `model_voice_params` — `present`, `values`, `count`, `default`, `source`, plus `stale` when the answer is a carried-over one — read from the endpoint the caller named, cached 60 s per endpoint URL (10 s after a failure), on demand only: no timer, no poller, no fetch at module load, no log record on any path.
- Where the family record said "no built-in voices" and the engine's own parameter names some, `preset_speaker` joins the mode list, and the sentence that was wrong in `no_voice_reason` is corrected in place: the old claim stays visible, the correction is appended.
- Three cases are kept apart, because collapsing them is how a wrong answer gets made. An empty `values` array is the engine declaring that this model takes no built-in speaker, and the answer says it renders on its own voice (the operator's ruling of 2026-10-23). A model with no `voice_id` parameter says the parameter is absent. A read that failed says it failed and marks the voices unknown — never a refusal, and never a limit.
- The first live check of this reader caught a fault in the reader itself, and it is recorded rather than hidden. The build read through `getJson`, a stdout read: 116 892 bytes of answer (118 131 on cpu2) through a seam that caps stdout at 64 000, so the body parsed to nothing and the answer claimed the engine had declared no `voice_id` parameter for a model that has nine. It is the fault T-252 exists for, met a second time on a second route. The read now uses the file transport — `curl -o`, `capReadTmp`, `--max-filesize`, a size check against what the server announced so a short body answers "truncated at N bytes of M" and is never parsed, guarded removal on every exit path.
- The engine's default is carried as the engine's value; the plugin does not adopt it. No voice name appears in the reader's code. The dispatch gate is untouched (its refusal is family-level, today's fact is model-level, and changing it changes what is sent to a remote engine), and `endpoint_models` stays names-only.
- Tests: 10 new host checks, and a new mock seam that writes this answer to the `-o` target instead of answering it on stdout — a mock that answered it on stdout would have kept the bug invisible. **host suite 2120 -> 2130 pass, 0 fail.** Host half built; `lib/index.js` changed after the operator's 09:35 Berlin restart, so this needs a second restart with its own explicit OK. Client half (the dropdown built from this answer) not started.

## serveAudio could not serve a big capture row (T-624 follow-up), 2026-10-24 — host half built, its restart owed

- The operator pressed play on ap-0141 on the live panel and the route answered `404 {"ok":false,"error":"cannot read file"}` on a row that is `ok` with its file on disk. The cause was this plugin's own read: the route pulled the WHOLE take into memory against an inline 100 MiB bound, and ap-0141 is 270 382 890 bytes, so a servable row was reported unreadable.
- The suite had never shown it because its fs stub hands back a buffer of any size; the real `FsService` refuses a read over the cap its caller passes. An opt-in door for that rule (`opts.fsReadCapEnforces624`, with `opts.fsSize624` declaring a size rather than allocating one) is what made the wall visible in a test, and it is a finding about the harness as much as about this route.
- Built: the bounds are named (`SERVE_MAX_BYTES624` 100 MiB, `SERVE_RANGE_WINDOW624` 8 MiB — the window this plugin already proves through the byte-range seam), a `range:` request reads only the window and answers 206 with a `Content-Range` that says what was sent and where the file continues, an open-ended window is cut rather than attempted, a suffix range is honoured, an unsatisfiable range answers 416 with `bytes */<size>`, and a whole-file read over the cap answers 413 carrying both numbers (270382890 asked, 104857600 allowed) plus the route to seek it by — deliberately not 404. The T-468 download twin is removed on every one of those early answers so a refused read leaves no scratch file behind. The in-memory whole read stays as the branch for a host without the byte-range seam.
- Tests: 16 new host checks; first run 2138 pass / 8 fail, all eight caused by the fixture writing a capital `Range` while `serveAudio` reads `req.headers.range` and `fakeReq` does not lowercase; after that **2146 pass, 0 fail**. Host half only — `lib/index.js` — so it is not live until a restart OK is given.
